items.quote: While stagnant ethanol prices have continued to put some pressure on profitability, we remain quite optimistic as I said earlier about the sector outlook. We are also expecting that the much-awaited revision in ethanol prices will come about.

items.quote: The chemical prices across the board, they were much higher than what anybody anticipated. So we will definitely focus on reducing our consumption of chemical, steam, energy.

items.quote: We continue to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities across our businesses, even as we continue to adopt digital solutions across our businesses to improve our efficiency and streamlining our processes.

items.quote: You will be happy to know that Simon India has recently patented a tech tool, copyrighted a tech tool. So I'm very happy to see that Simon India is developing in-house tech products to improve their own productivity and quality of work.

items.quote: Looking ahead, I think the macroeconomic situation, of course, is a concern to all of us. It is affecting capex plans both in India and the Middle East. So that's a concern. It has also increased the input prices even for our sugar business.

items.statement: Expecting long-overdue ethanol price revision; government pushing higher blending (E27, E30, E85, E100 notifications)

items.statement: Rupee depreciation beneficial for Dubai project inflows; monitoring currency, may take forward covers if needed

items.quote: So now since we are 100% sold out, we have sold it on a payment plan wherein 50% was collected during construction and 50% will be collected post getting BCC, which is a building completion certificate.

items.quote: It will reduce, but not drastically because this time also, it is high because as I told you, it is because of the debtors, increase in the debtors.

items.statement: Current capacity with planned expansions adequate to support growth to INR1,000 crore by FY28

items.quote: And in fact, as we speak, currently the percentage of occupancy in our hotel is about 65% from Marriott Bonvoy members. That is a good sign. And the target for them, I believe, should at least should be to take that up to 80%-85% and significantly reduce what the OTAs are contributing.

items.statement: Debt increased for Marriott Executive Apartments acquisition (INR 215 cr consideration); consolidated borrowings INR 264 cr as of 31 Mar 2026; no further debt increase expected; healthy cash flows to fund renovations
items.quote: As of 31 st March 2026, our borrowings are at INR 264 crores(on a consolidated basis). That's it. They are not in thousands.

items.statement: Finance cost rose from Rs 64 lakh to Rs 530 lakh in Q4 FY26 due to acquisition debt; no further increase anticipated; comfortable with current leverage
items.quote: We don't see any further increase. We have healthy cash revenues and healthy cash balances to fund our ongoing renovations.

items.statement: Board discussed dividends; expects to initiate dividend payout from next year (FY27) post convention center renovation completion
items.quote: By the end of this year, we will be completing the renovation of the convention center where a lot of capital has been reinvested in the property to uplift it. So, mostly the board also discussed this issue several times, and we expect to give you a good outcome from next year.

items.statement: Phase 1 renovation completed at Courtyard Hyderabad; new rooms achieving 95-99% occupancy; spa revenue more than doubled; rooftop restaurant launched
items.quote: We have already finished our phase one of our renovations. And we see that there's a big impact on it because the new rooms have come into play. And we see the new rooms being occupied almost all the time. That is close to 95% to 99% occupancy because these are new rooms that are offering.

items.statement: Convention center expansion to 20,000 sq ft under renovation; expects 2x EBITDA increase post completion
items.quote: The first thing is the biggest contribution we will see is the adding of the new convention center and the renovation of the old convention center in Marriott. We are going to see a substantial twofold increase in the EBITDAs because of this addition.

items.statement: Outsourced laundry now running at 60-65% of previous cost; invested in HVAC equipment lowering HLP costs; exploring shared non-customer-facing HR functions across three hotels for cost reduction
items.quote: One of the first things that we had done after we took over was outsourcing the laundry, for example. But now our laundry is running at 60% to 65% of the cost that it used to run before. So, there was a big saving made there. We have also recently invested into, like, our HVAC equipment which has then lowered various HLP costs for the company where, again, we are saving costs.

items.statement: 25 new star hotels planned in Hyderabad by 2032 adding ~5,000 rooms; management believes actual supply will materialize post FY30-31 and less than half of announced projects typically open; demand expected to outpace supply
items.quote: But we see that the demand will still go up during this period and will catch up, or it will be even more than what the supply is. So, we see that in no way affecting our ADRs, and our ADRs are still going to be strongly improving because the supply will be less. And second thing, in hotel projects, the planning and the execution and the capital allocation and the time management is very crucial,

items.statement: Actively evaluating NCLT/distressed asset opportunities; submitted expressions of interest but nothing materialized yet; assessment based on asset quality, location, and future yield potential
items.quote: Yes, there are many opportunities that we keep looking for in NCLT and other distressed scenarios. Currently, the hospitality sector for the last two years has experienced tremendous growth and has outperformed many other industries. And this distress is a little lesser. But for us, the analysis is based on how the asset is built, what's its performance, and what location is it at, and what can it

items.statement: Q4 FY26 combined ADR Rs 7,605; combined RevPAR Rs 4,931; Marriott ADR Rs 7,423, Courtyard ADR Rs 8,010; FY26 Marriott ADR +6.8%, Courtyard occupancy +13%
items.quote: For Q4 FY '26, ADR stood at INR 7,423 at Marriott and INR 8,010 at Courtyard, with combined ADR at Rs 7,605. Combined RevPar for the quarter stood at Rs 4,931, which was primarily impacted by softer occupancy trends during the period.

items.statement: Courtyard occupancy dropped from 72.6% to 52.2% in FY26 due to renovation; already back to normal levels
items.quote: So, the temporary dip in this year, you have seen it because of the massive renovation that happened to courtyard. That's why you see the dip in the occupancy, but it's already back to normal. And you can see it being back to normal this year.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and West Asia conflict impacting near-term travel sentiment and ADR; inflationary pressures on commodities, energy, operating costs
items.quote: The hospitality industry witnessed a relatively softer operating environment during the later part of the quarter, particularly in March, impacted by geopolitical tensions, the ongoing West Asia conflict and temporary disruptions in travel sentiment. The sector also continued to face inflationary pressures across commodities, energy and operating costs during this period.

items.statement: Exploring shared non-customer-facing HR functions across three hotels post Marriott Executive Apartments acquisition to reduce costs
items.quote: Now, the additional thing that we are intending to do is after we had acquired the third hotel, is that even from a human resource standpoint, to see how much we can leverage and, you know, reduce costs where, you know, some of the departments that are not customer facing could be common to all the hotels.

items.statement: Targeting 10-15% sales growth for FY27 base business
items.quote: We hope we can continue between 10% to 15% again this year. That's our target.

items.statement: Targeting ~12% EBITDA margin for base business in FY27
items.quote: Yes, Sagar, we are targeting something around that. We are targeting a good sales growth as well, but we have to see how the market reacts.

items.statement: Merger expected to contribute 1-2% EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: As these synergies begin getting realized over time, we internally estimate that the merger itself can potentially contribute nearly 1% to 2% EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Fill-finish capex estimated at INR50 crores as part of Cefiderocol facility
items.quote: So the total capex we are estimating is around INR50 crores, which includes equipment and capability but one size. So and filing dossier, so all of that is included.

items.statement: 7ACA project on track for Q1 CY2027 commissioning
items.quote: We are still committed to the commissioning in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Cefiderocol facility on track for end of CY2026 commissioning, launch Q2/Q3 CY2027
items.quote: The Cefiderocol facility remains on track for commissioning by the end of this calendar year. Subject to regulatory approvals and registrations, we expect product launch during Q2 or Q3 of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Exblifep commercialization early stage, selling in India and Europe with 4x QoQ growth
items.quote: Currently, we are at an early stage commercialization. The product is currently selling in only India and Europe. We now have Q1 numbers emerging from Europe. And while still not financially meaningful, they are encouraging and represent multiple orders. It is about fourfold improvement over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Exblifep commercial discussions active in US, Russia, Latin America, Southeast Asia with term-sheets and definitive agreements under discussion
items.quote: Commercial discussions continue across multiple geographies. Currently, we are actively discussing opportunities in the United States, Russia, Latin America and Southeast Asia. In some of these markets term-sheets, all definitive agreements are under discussion.

items.statement: Exblifep lifetime sales maintained at $1-2 billion, peak in year 4-5 post-launch
items.quote: We still maintain the lifetime sales would be between $1 billion to $2 billion overall during the life of the patent. And the peak should be reaching fourth or fifth year of the launch, not three years.

items.statement: Plan to launch 5-6 large sterile products covering ~2/3 of US Cephalosporin market ($1.2B opportunity) over next 5 years
items.quote: Over the next few years, Orchid plans to launch approximately five to six large sterile products catering to nearly two-thirds of the U.S. Cephalosporin market opportunity. This overall opportunity size is estimated at approximately $1.2 billion.

items.statement: First two US ANDAs (Ceftazidime-Avibactam, Ceftaroline) to be filed via CMO, then shift to own facility post-FDA approval
items.quote: So Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline would be the first two candidates. They will be filed through a CMO.

items.statement: April price increase due to war anxiety and higher solvent/input costs; weekly price reviews to pass on costs
items.quote: So you see the pricing did increase in the month of April, due to the war. People were a little anxious about covering their materials. And obviously, the cost has also increased since you all know the solvents and all the inputs are more expensive.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margins recovered from Q2/Q3 lows of 31-32% as lower-priced inventory replaced high-cost stock
items.quote: Our Q2, Q3 gross margins were around 31%, 32%. So here we were carrying high price inventory and forced to sell at a lower value. Towards the end of Q3, we decided we need to sell at the current market prices rather than hold inventory. That's what led to the recovery of Q4 and we also starting getting lower priced inventory.

items.statement: AMS platform remains ~INR8 crore annual EBITDA drag but strategically important for Cefiderocol market entry
items.quote: The platform currently remains an EBITDA drag of approximately INR8 crores annually. But strategically, we believe it is extremely important. It positions Orchid not merely as a manufacturer of antibiotics, but as a long-term participant in responsible anti-infective healthcare solutions.

items.statement: Regulated markets 30%, ROW 70% of FY26 revenue; regulated mix hard to predict due to exclusive long-term contracts
items.quote: Our trend has been one-third, two-third, broadly fluctuating 5% here or there. For this year, whole year, 30% is regulated and 70% is ROW. That's what the end of year number, Loveleen.

items.statement: Exblifep treated ~30,000 patients in last year
items.quote: So about 30,000 patients we would have treated in last year.

items.statement: Non-Cephalosporin portfolio from Dhanuka merger is non-antibiotics, will remain <10% of business for next 5 years
items.quote: But as alluded in the presentation, even for the next five years, 90% is still going to be Ceph.

items.statement: Merger order reserved in March hearing, formal written order expected shortly after court vacations
items.quote: During the March hearing, the order was reserved. We are still awaiting the formal written order. We expect this to be received shortly after the court vacations.

items.statement: US FDA facility approval needed for own-site manufacturing; will file ANDAs via CMO first to derisk timeline
items.quote: So currently, the plan is that we will try and file the ANDA from an alternate CMO. And as we approach the U.S. FDA for our inspection and when we get the approval, then we can use our site as an alternate manufacturing site.

items.statement: Dhanuka Labs FY26 revenue INR450 crores (down ~10% YoY), EBITDA/PAT under audit
items.quote: Yes. The revenue numbers are INR450 crores, which was INR500 crores last year, so almost same 10% reduction. EBITDA numbers, I don't have at this point of time. The audit is going on.

items.statement: Pricing recovery uncertain due to war, supply chain costs, global competitive intensity, geopolitical situations
items.quote: Going forward, we still need to monitor the impact of pricing due to the war, supply chain costs, global competitive intensity and geopolitical situations. However, from a business standpoint, it does not appear -- it does appear that the worst phase of the pricing cycle may now be behind us.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam out-licensing deals in advanced stages for Japan, Russia, US, LatAm, SE Asia; hope to announce one this quarter
items.quote: We are in multiple stages of discussion in Japan, Russia, U.S., Latin America and Southeast Asia. Some are in term-sheet space, some are in definitive agreement space. We wanted to announce one deal before the call. Unfortunately, it's not signed so we cannot. Hopefully, within this quarter, we should announce one.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement for INR 300 crore fund raise at INR 4,650 crore equity valuation from EAAA Alternatives
items.quote: And today, I'm proud to announce that Cyient Semiconductors has signed a definitive agreement for its first external funding route, a total of INR300 crore s with equity valuation at INR4,650 crores from EAAA Alternatives who were formerly known as Edelweiss Alternatives

items.statement: Fund raise structured as INR 200 crore debt and INR 100 crore equity at competitive rate
items.value: INR 200 crore debt, INR 100 crore equity
items.quote: So, the deal is a combination of debt and equity, debt at 200 crores, equity at 100 crores. It's a competitive rate. We can't disclose the rate because we're still not close to deal.

items.statement: Cyient committed to original $100 million investment thesis, $30 million already invested, $70 million remaining
items.quote: Cyient remains committed, like I said, to the $100 million. We've already put in about $30 million. So, rest of the money is available.

items.statement: Completed Kinetic Technologies acquisition for approximately $85 million in March 2026
items.quote: To accelerate this vision, in March 2026, we completed the acquisition of Kinetic Technologies for approximately $85 million.

items.statement: Kinetic acquisition funded through debt raised at Singapore entity
items.quote: We funded Kinetic through debt raised at Singapore entity because we got pretty good rates and we felt like that's a good use of our capital.

items.statement: ASIC pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities
items.quote: And finally, commercially, our ASIC pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities, and we were selected as the L1 bidder on the SCL semiconductor modernization initiative.

items.statement: Power ASSP including Kinetic is 50-60% of business, rest split between services and ASIC turnkey
items.quote: So today, Power ASSP s including Kinetic is roughly 50% to 60% of our business. The rest of the business is split between services and ASIC turnkey

items.statement: ASSP revenue share expected to increase over next 3-4 years as products commercialize after 2-3 year R&D cycle
items.quote: As we progress and we develop our own products which we are working on, we do believe that ASSP revenue share will increase in the next 3-4 years, because there is an R&D development cycle of almost 2 years to 3 years for the product to commercialize.

items.statement: ASSP gross margins typically 50-60%, followed by custom ASIC turnkey, then services
items.quote: From a gross margin standpoint, ASSP given it is product and IP driven will have the highest gross margin typically in the 50% to 60% range, depending on which customer segment you sell, followed by custom ASIC turnkey followed by services.

items.statement: Custom ASIC turnkey expected to grow faster near term, ASSP to remain significant long term
items.quote: Now in the near term, we do believe that custom ASIC turnkey will grow faster compared to the other segments. But in the longer term, ASSP will continue to remain a significant portion of our business.

items.statement: Targeting breakeven late FY27 or early FY28, may shift by a quarter or two given significant opportunity set
items.quote: So, for now, we are still looking at a breakeven late FY27, early FY28. But based on the investor conversations, we'll come back.

items.statement: Board willing to accept slight breakeven delay to capture significant opportunity, fund raise creates investment dollars
items.quote: But I would just say maybe a quarter or two shift, we wouldn't worry too much or I wouldn't worry too much as an investor because just the opportunity set is also here and now, and we don't want to lose out because we don't have any investment dollars.

items.statement: Launched 7 new GaN products with Navitas targeting Indian market at 650 volts
items.quote: In partnership with Navitas as well, we launched 7 new GaN products, specifically targeting the Indian market.

items.statement: Actively working on 800-volt to 50-volt power architecture with GaN as component, part of Open Compute Project
items.quote: We are working on the 800-volt to 50-volt power architecture, and GaN will be one of the components of that architecture.

items.statement: ASIC and ASSP pipeline primarily targeting industrial and medical applications
items.quote: So, our ASIC and ASSP pipeline is usually targeting industrial and medical applications, that's where bulk of our pipeline is based out of.

items.statement: Hired India sales head from Arrow and Texas Instruments, evaluating distribution companies for India ecosystem
items.quote: we just recently hired someone to head our sales in India as of last week. He hails both from Arrow as well as from Texas Instruments. The gentleman is actually evaluating distribution companies right now to work through the India ecosystem

items.statement: Filed 4 patents on high-voltage DC architecture and advanced delivery systems for AI data centers with NVIDIA, Google, Meta and hyperscalers
items.quote: And during the year, we filed 4 patents focused on high-voltage DC architecture and advanced delivery systems for AI data centers along with NVIDIA, Google, Meta and other hyperscalers and infrastructure companies.

items.statement: Contributing member of Open Compute Platform (OCP) shaping next-gen AI data center power architecture standards
items.quote: we're also contributing members of the o pen compute platforms, (OCP), helping shape the next -generation AI data center power architecture and infrastructure standards

items.statement: Addressable market opportunity for power semiconductors approximately $8.5 billion
items.quote: Third, power semiconductors represent one of the fastest-growing segments of the semiconductor industry today. With our acquisition and internal investment in low- and high-voltage product strategies, we're positioning Cyient semiconductors to participate in the addressable market opportunity of approximately $8.5 billion.

items.statement: Data center power share growing from 2% in 2025 to 8% in 2030, power is single biggest bottleneck for data centers
items.quote: The share of power for data centers is going up from 2% in 2025 to 8% in 2030.

items.statement: Total semiconductor balance sheet debt $100 million: $80 million foreign currency (Kinetic) + $20 million India (new fund raise)
items.quote: That's right, 80 plus 20, 100 in total on semiconductor balance sheet.

items.statement: Won Semiconductor Complex of India modernization program, landmark for India's semiconductor self-sufficiency
items.quote: We won the semiconductor complex of India modernization program, which is a landmark program for India's semiconductor self-sufficiency.

items.statement: Built robust leadership team across senior and mid-management with deep semiconductor expertise
items.quote: Second, we have built the first set of robust leaders across senior and mid management with deep expertise to execute in semiconductors.

items.statement: Onboarded key industry veterans across semiconductor industry as advisers
items.quote: We also onboarded key industry veterans across the semiconductor industry as our advisers.

items.statement: Valuation at 6-7x revenue (FY26/FY27) aligned with global semiconductor comparables trading at 5-15x revenue
items.quote: This valuation roughly works out to be 6x revenue to 7x revenue, depending on which revenue we consider, FY26 or '27. The way to think about it is along these 3 lines: trading comparables with global semiconductor companies. Most semiconductor companies today are trading anywhere between 5x to 15x revenue depending on their profile.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 top line growth at 15% to 20% rate with potential for stronger growth in coming years
items.quote: Further, we continue to see robust opportunities across all three product segments in the defines market and therefore reaffirm our FY27 top line growth at 15% to 20% rate, with a potential for much stronger growth over the coming years.

items.statement: Standalone order book at INR2,141 crores as of 31st March; consolidated order book at INR2,600 crores
items.value: INR2,141 crores standalone, INR2,600 crores consolidated
items.quote: Yes, we have order book of INR2,141. This is order book standalone order book of Astra. Management: And consolidated goes up to I mean consolidated is INR2,600

items.statement: Q4 fresh orders of approximately INR530 crores; PNC of INR300 crores more orders expected in next couple of months
items.value: INR530 crores fresh orders, INR300 crores PNC
items.quote: In Q4 alone, we secured fresh orders worth of approximately INR530 crores, taking our total order book to a robust INR2141 crores as on 31st March, and concluded PNC of INR300 crores more orders which are expected to be received in next couple of months.

items.statement: Expect to book sales of INR1,300 crores to INR1,400 crores in FY27, around 15% to 20% growth compared to FY26
items.quote: Regarding execution front, we have planned to book sales of INR1300 crores to INR1400 crores, that is around 15% to 20% growth compared to FY26, covering 40% of R&D and 60% from the production area.

items.statement: Expect to nearly triple turnover over next five years (FY30-FY31) based on five to six major programs
items.quote: We believe that Astra is structurally positioned to nearly triple its turnover over this period, while simultaneously improving the quality of earnings, cash generation, and long-term shareholder value creation.

items.statement: Clear visibility of approximately INR1,600 crores plus orders which can be booked in FY27; 25% from R&D programs, balance from production orders
items.quote: Going forward, we have a clear visibility of approximately INR1600 crores plus orders which can be booked in the current year, that is FY27. Around 25% of this expected to come from R&D programs, while balance are basically driven by the production orders.

items.statement: Export margins improved to close to 40% gross margin due to higher value addition from co-development with Rafael
items.quote: So, because of that, the value add is much higher than the regular exports that were recorded in the previous periods. Therefore, generally these carry good amount of value add. I would say the gross margin will be close to about 40% kind of thing in these exports.

items.statement: Management indicates current margins (55%) are probably at top end; suggests factoring in slightly lower numbers on margin front
items.quote: Okay, amid from a guidance perspective, I think we should very clearly state , this probably is the top end, you can actually you should factor in slightly lower numbers only on the margin front, so that there is no disappointment coming in at a later date.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR40-50 crores to continue; no additional major capex beyond normal requirements for revenue tripling
items.quote: Yes, in terms of the capex, as you know every year, we are augmenting the existing requirements by spending close to about INR40 crores, INR50 crores. So that will continue. Therefore, there won't be an additional capex beyond this what we are doing normally.

items.statement: Significant improvement in working capital cycle in FY26; operating cash flow of INR370 crores vs minus INR99 crores last year; expect continued improvement in receivables realization
items.quote: FY26 has been another strong year for the company, characterized by consistent growth, effective execution, margin expansion driven by favourable revenue mix, and improved working capital cycle, resulting in operating cash flow of INR370 crores compared to minus INR99 crores as of last year.

items.statement: Board in-principle approved demerger of space, meteorology, and hydrology business to create sharper strategic focus; detailed scheme expected in next few weeks
items.quote: On a strategic front, the Board of Directors have in -principle approved demerger of our space, meteorology, and hydrology business. The objective of this move is to create sharper strategic and operational focus for business segments.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2.40 per equity share (120% of face value) for FY25-26, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of INR2.40 per equity share, that is about 120% of face value for the year FY25-'26, subject to approval of shareholders at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Radar segment ~60% of revenue; space and meteorology ~16%; FY27 expected mix: radar 45%, EW and missile 25%, space and meteorology 25%, others from strategic areas
items.quote: Segment-wise, radar segment is again expected to contribute around 45%, electronic warfare and missile together around 25%, space and meteorology around 25%, and the remaining other from strategic business areas.

items.statement: ARC (JV) expects minimum 50% growth in both order booking and sales in FY27; visibility of INR200 crores order book, expected to cross INR600 crores sales
items.quote: Going forward in FY27, we expect to outperform and we expect the minimum growth of 50% both in terms of order booking and as well as sales. As on date, we have visibility of INR200 crores order book in FY27 for ARC and also expected to cross INR600 crores sales.

items.statement: ARC projected EBITDA 18-20% on INR600 crores top line; Astra's share of profit at least INR20 crores for FY27
items.quote: EBITDA, I think around 18% to 20% is what is being projected by the company. So, basing on that, on INR600 crores top line, at least about INR20 crores plus of will be our share of p rofit for the entire year

items.statement: Key Q4 orders: SDR programs, radar subsystems from BEL, Gaganyaan checkout hardware from ISRO; completed shipborne radar delivery to DRDO
items.quote: Key orders received during the quarter, which is in Q4, including SDR programs, subsystems of various radar projects from BEL, and the checkout hardware for prestigious Gaganyaan mission from ISRO.

items.statement: Multiple Astra-owned IP branded products expected to launch before Diwali; first NCNC demo planned this quarter
items.quote: This financial year itself, hopefully before Diwali, you will have multiple Astra products where we own the complete IP, they are o ur branded products and solutions for global markets , India first, global markets

items.statement: Su-30 upgrade: Virupaksha radar AAAU development completion in 2-3 months, radar qualification expected FY28, production orders in 2-3 years; Angad EW pod jammer development completion in ~1 year
items.quote: For the radar, the AAAU which we have taken up development, that is on I think next two to three months we should be in a position to complete the development and hand over to DRDO. And in all probability, I think in maybe FY28, DRDO will be ready to qualify the overall radar.

items.statement: Uttam AESA radar negotiations with HAL at final stage, order expected Q2 or Q3; QRSAM FOPM orders started, main orders 3-4 months after BEL contract (expected by June)
items.quote: I think we are expecting, you know, this particular order sometime in the Q2 or Q3 and as the process is more like, you know, to place the order. So, but as far as today's position, as on today, negotiations are on for Uttam radar with HAL.

items.statement: MMIC division producing active devices in-house for most subsystems; no supply issues encountered; promoting MMICs to domestic and international players
items.quote: If you look at the overall MMIC thing, as of now we have not encountered any issue and that production and as well as development is going very smooth. And second thing is as far as the dependency like yes, in all our subsystems, we are most of the active devices we are sourcing out from our in-house MMIC division.

items.statement: Total addressable market remains INR28,000 crores between FY26-FY28, but timeline may extend to FY30-FY31 due to program delays
items.quote: Well, Sanjeev, the total accessible market remained same, but only there is a shift in the year as you know there are many programs got delayed for various reasons as these are all government-driven programs.

items.statement: Developed and delivered complete systems: Mobile Multi-Object Tracking Radar, Phased Array Telemetry, Doppler weather radars, counter-drone radar D4, wind profiler radars
items.quote: Mobile Multi-Object Tracking Radar to SHAR and ISRO, complete; Phased Array Telemetry, that's PATM system to ITR and DRDO; Fixed Head Doppler Radars to ITR, DRDO; Radiation Mode T& E facility to same, to DL RL and DRDO.

items.statement: Revenue tripling is rear-ended (FY29-FY30) driven by 5-6 major programs; excludes export potential and other BEL programs which provide upside buffer
items.quote: Yes, you're right, absolutely. It is going to be rear -ended. There are basically five or six major programs which are driving this as I think I alluded a couple of times now. We have QRSAM, we have Uttam radars, we have Su -30 Virupaksha, we have Su -30 Angad, and we have regular business which we do for our JV and also maybe, you know, electronic mines, for example, is a big area for us, okay?

items.statement: Exports now IP-driven/co-developed with Rafael (SDR RF portion) vs earlier low-margin build-to-print; export margins ~45% vs single-digit in BTP
items.quote: Here although it is BTP, but our value addition is more and the margins as Mr. SGR had already mentioned, it is around 45% as compared to the single-digit figure in the BTP business.

items.statement: ARC JV share of profit after tax ~INR8 crores for FY26 (down due to $2M forex provision); R&D expenditure ongoing
items.quote: Yes, during the current year, of course R&D expenditure is always there. In addition to that, there is a foreign exchange provision which the company has to make. So, because of that, close to about $2 million of provision was made in the books of accounts.

items.statement: Space business: delivered complex defence satellite subsystems; expecting repeat orders from ISRO and defence for satellite constellations
items.quote: we have deliv ered the subsystems for a defence satellite program, which is a very main like complex subsystems which we made in over a period of one year, that would completed in last quarter and that has a decent contribution. And we are expecting similar subsystems going forward as the user is plan ning to go for constellation of those satellites

items.statement: Evolved from tier-2 subsystem supplier to tier-1 systems manufacturer and DCPP for strategic programs; horizontal technology stack across domains creates moat
items.quote: We have in reality evolved from a component manufacturer to a deeply integrated, IP -driven systems manufacturer to now becoming a development-cum-production partner for strategic national programs.

items.statement: Declared higher dividend of INR 3.50 per share for FY26 versus INR 3.00 last year
items.quote: We have declared a higher dividend overall for the year, INR 3.50 per share against last year's INR 3.00.

items.statement: Guides double-digit group revenue growth and consolidated EBITDA margin of 12% to 13.5% for FY27 inclusive of SCS
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA, we are guiding for a 12 % to 13.5% range for the year. And this is inclusive of SCS, which will now be part of the (GCM ) Global Cables and Mechatronics Division.

items.statement: GCM division targets double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 10% to 12% in FY27 versus 6% last year
items.quote: GCM as a consolidated division last year, if you consider SCS part of it, it was at 6%. And we are expecting that this year to the EBITDA margin to be 10% to 12%.

items.statement: ICM division expects double-digit revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins in FY27
items.quote: We again see double -digit growth here, despite the single -digit sector outlook. This is mainly going to be driven by gains in market share and Beyond Cable project ramp ups that we have already won.

items.statement: SED division expected to maintain comfortable double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27
items.quote: I think we will be in a comfortable double digit. I think that is all we can say for the coming year. That is exactly what we have also guided in our forecast.

items.statement: Consolidated operational EBITDA grew 10.5% to INR 443 crore in FY26
items.quote: The consolidated operational EBITDA for the year ended March 2026 was INR 443 crores, as against INR 401 crores for the corresponding previous year, recording a growth of 10.5%.

items.statement: SCDR division EBITDA margin reached double-digit 11% for first time in FY26
items.quote: SCD revenue grew by around (+10%) and EBITDA, for the first time margin, went to double digit. We ended the year at 11% there.

items.statement: SES turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26 after restructuring, trajectory from -20% in Q1 to +2% in Q4
items.quote: So, just to let the quarterly trajectory, which happened in FY26 was in Q1, we were at almost (-20%) EBITDA. From there, in Q2, we moved to (-6%), Q3 to almost (-2%), to Q4, (+2%).

items.statement: FY27 capex allocated at INR 200 crore covering AURIC land purchase, STC building, SAL Chennai Plant-2, SCD capacity expansion
items.quote: We have a CAPEX allocated for about INR 200 crores. This is covering AURIC Maharashtra land purchase, STC building completion, SAL Chennai Plant -2, and the SCD capacity expansion.

items.statement: Capex split: ~INR 80 crore India operations, ~INR 50 crore global operations, ~INR 50 crore STC, ~INR 15-16 crore corporate IT
items.quote: Out of the total, what we are looking at INR 200 crores, we would be approximately allocating to India operations close to INR 80 crores. And about INR 50 crores will go to global operations. And about INR 50-odd crores would be going to STC. And there would be a tail of around INR 15 crores to INR 16 crores coming to corporate, primarily into IT infrastructure and those kind of stuff.

items.statement: Electronics Division building redevelopment estimated at INR 30-40 crore over two years, half allocated in FY27
items.quote: For the Electronics Division alone, I think it will be spread over two years. I think this building, if I am not mistaken, is about INR 30 crores to INR 40 crores of the investment, but it will be spread over two years. So, this year allocation may be half of that.

items.statement: Morocco factory operating at one shift, comfortably meeting current requirements, no capacity utilization issue
items.quote: I think we don't have a capacity utilization issue in most of our places. I think, for example, in Morocco, we operate mostly in one shift. So, I don't think there is an issue at all. Executing the businesses and capacities are in place in most of the places.

items.statement: Electronics Division gained momentum in digital clusters and electronic throttle controls, set to supply complete clusters, throttle, switch assembly for premium EV motorbike and digital clusters to US off-highway customer
items.quote: SED is now set to supply complete clusters, throttle, switch assembly, for one of the premium EV motorbikes. And we will also be supplying digital clusters to a key off-highway customer in the USA.

items.statement: Signed Technical Collaboration Agreement with global brake system supplier for two-wheeler brake caliper development under testing with key customer
items.quote: This quarter, with the support of STC, we signed a Technical Collaboration Agreement, or a TCA, with a global brake system supplier for designing and developing a two-wheeler brake caliper for some of our customers. This is now under development and is also under testing with one of our key customers.

items.statement: Sunroof cable launch under testing with multiple Indian and global customers
items.quote: And we are also progressing well with the Sunroof Cable launch, which is now under testing with multiple Indian and global customers.

items.statement: PLD executed first orders for US largest retailer, awarded significant additional business becoming meaningful new channel
items.quote: Another big positive thing that happened in PLD was we successfully executed the first set of orders of US largest retailer. And we feel that this retailer has awarded significant additional businesses coming forward. And this is going to become a meaningful new channel for PLD.

items.statement: World's largest halogen lamp manufacturer declared insolvency, active discussions with multiple new customers for low-cost India manufacturing
items.quote: And also, the fact that one of the world's largest halogen lamp manufacturers – in fact, the largest halogen lamp manufacturer has declared insolvency. The insolvency means there are a lot of active discussions now underway with multiple new customers who are looking to utilize our low-cost manufacturing in India.

items.statement: Expects full resolution of tariff-related matters within next few months; customers obtaining licenses to avoid new tariffs on US imports
items.quote: On the tariff side, I think both from the customers and from the government, the recoveries are ongoing. We expect a full resolution for all the tariff -related matters, hopefully within the next few months.

items.statement: Total debt INR 785 crore as of March 2026; surplus cash invested in mutual funds INR 235 crore
items.quote: The total debt level was INR 785 crores, as on March 2026. The surplus cash balance invested in the mutual funds was INR 235 crores, as on March 2026.

items.statement: DCD growth dampened by year-on-year price concessions passed to customers with lag when commodity prices fall
items.quote: Our revenue grew by around 9%. But what happened was the growth rate was a bit dampened by the year -on-year price concessions that we had passed on to the customer. You know, we always have a lag. So, when the commodity price goes down, with a lag, we pass on that.

items.statement: PLD margins pressured due to inability to pass on commodity price increases in Moly, Tungsten; expects recovery as top line grows
items.quote: The revenues declined by around 3% and EBITDA also declined. And this happened primarily because we were not able to pass on the price increases that happened in the commodity markets like Moly, Tungsten, etc. and also the volumes, did not grow to that extent.

items.statement: Will push customers for compensation on commodity price increases from Middle East crisis; expects most to be passed on
items.quote: But the point with all these things is that how the world is operating, right? So, if there's going to be any for example, if XYZ customers are launching a project promised in August, but it goes to October or next January, then there is a delay in the launch. These kinds of things are not in our hands. We are looking at what currently customers are saying when the launch is and at what time and w

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical headwind and commodity price volatility are key risks to FY27 outlook and margin guidance
items.quote: Of course, this is subject to what happens in Middle East or the commodity prices, which are the standard caveats, I would say.

items.statement: Completed major restructuring in North America: consolidated Mexico factories to single Matamoros facility, expanded Brownsville warehouse, closed El Paso warehouse
items.quote: We said that we have one too many factories in Mexico, we need to consolidate them. Therefore, we embarked upon that, and we completed the Juarez shift to Matamoros. So, now instead of having two factories in Mexico, now we operate under a single consolidated facility, which me ans it serves both for automotive and non- automotive purposes in North America. While we were doing it, we also had to d

items.statement: Completed SES restructuring: shut Poland, moved manufacturing to Morocco, warehouse Germany to Hungary, right-sized Germany operations, moved tool room to Morocco, integrated Canada into SED
items.quote: Basically, what happened was our SES restructuring got completed. We shut down Poland. We moved all the manufacturing to Morocco. We moved the warehouse from Germany to Hungary. We right sized the operations in Germany. There was a tool room in Germany. We moved that also from Germany to Morocco. And as we are doing all these things, we went into the tranche-2. Jiaxing transfer was under turmoil.

items.statement: Completed 16 plant SAP go-lives in DCD in April; four SAP implementations in last year, moving group to SAP HANA
items.quote: We had DCD plants going live in the beginning of this month. All 16 plants went live in April, and that went very successfully. It also ends the year full of SAP implementations. We have done almost four SAP implementations just in the last year, and one starting this year. And there will be a couple more going through this year as well as we move completely towards SAP HANA across the Suprajit Gr

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY27 expected at 27%, same as FY26
items.quote: For FY26 it was 27%. Then there is no change in the structure for the year '27 also. It will be the same.

items.statement: Phoenix Lamps margin dropped ~200 bps due to flat top line and inflation; expects recovery to last year's level or better by year-end.
items.value: ~200 bps drop; target: last year level or better
items.quote: Phoenix Lamps division, yes, last year has been, I would say, yes, you are right about 200 basis point drop in the margin is very true. This is largely because the top line did not grow. Obviously inflationary pressure keeps pushing up.

items.statement: DCD margin drop due to higher team costs at Suprajit Technology Centre and corporate office for global ops and SAP, not operational weakness.
items.quote: when you see the drop, it is not that the operations of DCD has drawn. It is as strong as ever. So, that is as far as the DCD is concerned.

items.statement: SAL-2 plant at Vallam near port approved for capacity expansion as existing SAL capacity is fully utilized.
items.quote: SAL-2, that is purely capacity building because we are running out of capacity in terms of physical infrastructure building, etc. Therefore, we have to have an SAL-2.

items.statement: SCD business is vast majority cable; actuator business from LDC acquisition is small but targeted for growth.
items.quote: if you are asking me from our SCD division, how much of it is cable and non-cable, I would say a vast majority of it is cable. Having said that, when we went in for LDC, one of the key things which attracted us towards LDC Kongsberg was their actuator business.

items.statement: Unrecovered tariffs absorbed ~$1-2M in P&L in FY26; Mexico tariffs ongoing and will continue in FY27.
items.quote: Net of recovery for the year, there may be an additional charge of last year, may have been probably a million plus into the P&L. It would be $1 million to $2 million as an additional charge, which is charged to the P&L, yes.

items.statement: $6M 301 tariff recovery from US Federal Government in final court stages; decision expected in 3-6 months; not included in margin guidance.
items.quote: we have disclosed about the case with the Federal Government on recovery of a 301 tariff, which is about $6 million. That $6 million is still an ongoing tussle between us and the Federal Government. We are in the final stages of coming to a resolution by the Court, which I am hopeful that in the next three to six months, we will hear from.

items.statement: US non-auto (agri/off-road) demand recovery still slow; some production relocated to China.
items.quote: The recovery of this non-automotive side of the business in US is still slow. There are two parts to it. Some of them have got relocated to smaller handheld grass cutters, etc., relocated to China, most of it.

items.statement: TRIFA brand lost ~$3M sales in Middle East; Indian OEMs shifting halogen purchases to Suprajit after competitor exit.
items.quote: I think TRIFA lost business. I mean, I am giving just a thumb rule off -the-cuff answer to this. Maybe about $3 million probably because of the loss of business of TRIFA brand.

items.statement: Phoenix Lamps rebranded to Lighting & Electricals; launched horns as first internally manufactured product; more new products coming.
items.quote: if you see the re-nomenclature of Phoenix Lamps division, it is now also electricals, so lighting and electricals. So, all I could say is that as a team, we are working on other projects. In an appropriate time, we will get to know about it. As a first step, as you probably may be knowing that we launched our horns as a part of our internally manufactured product into the market, it is a first ste

items.statement: Phoenix already sells LED bulbs; strategy is 'Last Man Standing' to sweat halogen assets while competitors exit; expects slow sunset not sudden death.
items.quote: Are there any plans to now get into LED? I think I have to answer that in past tense. We have already got into LED. So, that is the past tense. We are already having Phoenix brand LED bulbs available. Okay. So, that is a drop-in solution.

items.statement: Targets 20% share of key China EV customer's cable business within 2-3 years; currently 3-4 of 20+ projects commercialized.
items.quote: I would say over a period of time, I think maybe in China, at least if we do not get, let us say, 20% of that customer's share of business in the next two, three years' time, maybe we would think that we have not been very successful.

items.statement: China Jiaxing operations resolving initial issues; US Juarez consolidated into Matamoros; Europe warehouses moved from Germany to Hungary in two tranches.
items.quote: The issues within Europe of relocating all the warehouses to Hungary from high-cost Germany, the scaling down of G erman team and two tranches, the multiple things have happened. The effect of that will be seen in this year

items.statement: Actuator motors shifted from China to Indian supplier, eliminating tariff risk for US/Mexico supply chain.
items.quote: It was shifted to an Indian supplier, that is now what is going on. So, that had helped us in reducing the tariff risks and now the tariff risk is completely off because our customer assembles with our motors, which is in India origin.

items.statement: Actuator portfolio: high-force for premium SUVs (US/EU), medium-force in development for India/global (samples in months, 2-year pipeline), small actuators for 2W India already commercialized.
items.quote: we are expecting to have samples of those now with a lot of our customers in the coming few months, where we have redesigned an actuator for having a lower force and of course, in terms of cost and quietness for the cabin, we have tried to develop an actuator that is better than our competition.

items.statement: Electronics Division (SED) commercialized: digital clusters (Supra 1.0/2.0/2.5/3.0), seat-lock & charging gun actuators, throttle position sensors (ferrite magnet-based, non-rare earth); new non-auto cluster project in North America startin
items.quote: The first and foremost thing is the actuator. So, I would say seat-lock actuator or when you put a charging gun for an electric vehicle, you need to charge the electric chargers, then you need to have a lock there. So, we have started supplying it.

items.statement: No fixed order book with volumes; orders are price-based on SAP portal, quantities depend on OEM production schedules.
items.quote: Our order book is what is there on the SAP portal on that day, and the volumes are depending upon how that particular, let's say, model works out. There is nothing like a fixed order that has been awarded by the customer with volume.

items.statement: Employee cost-to-sales ratio peaked above 25% in FY26 due to restructuring costs; expects improvement to 21-22% base in FY27 as restructuring completes.
items.quote: last year as we had done some restructuring and reduction of people and that cost has hit the P&L. So, the cost of that restructuring would be sitting there in the employee cost somewhere. So, from that point of view, I would expect that by this year's number should be an improvement.

items.statement: Consolidation continuing in cables and lamps; largest European halogen lamp maker now insolvent; Suprajit gaining share as competitors exit or get acquired.
items.quote: one of the biggest, largest halogen lamp manufacturer s has gone insolvent in Europe just now. So, these are all parts of the game and consolidation will be the key. Those who are not efficient, who are not value for money will have difficulty going forward

items.statement: Tariff recovery timing uncertain: duties paid by customers may need refunding if recovered via US portal; net P&L impact unclear.
items.quote: if the customer has paid for the duty and we are recovering through this portal, then we have also an obligation to pay it back to the customer who has paid us. So, in a sense, there is a lag and some amount of that lag of that duties and tariffs may have a positive impact on this year. But it is very difficult to say because quite a bit of it has to be refunded to customers back.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY28 at INR1,600-1,700 crore; EBITDA margin target 18-20%
items.quote: FY27, it will be like about INR1,400 crores to INR 1,500 crores and then gradually inch up to INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: Annual production volume target of 230,000 tons (40-50% increase from current ~163,000 tons)
items.quote: We should be manufacturing and selli ng about 2,30,000 tons. So that's the kind of increase that we are expecting, which is about between 40% to 50

items.statement: Remaining capex of INR125 crore to be spent in FY27; no new capex planned after current expansion
items.quote: On that front, we have already the remaining capex of around INR125 crores, which will be expensed out during this year.

items.statement: PM2 rebuild completed March 2026, capacity enhanced to 75 tpd; DDS project commissioning targeted by mid-June; PM3 upgrade deferred to mid-June
items.quote: Paper Machine 2 rebuild was completed in March 2026, enhancing its installed capacity to 75 tons per day through major upgrades.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization above 92% post expansion of PM4, PM1, PM2; targeting 95%+ utilization
items.quote: So on the utilization front, if we talk of the OE levels, so they are above 92%, and this is post expansion of all the 3 machines, PM 4, PM 1 and PM 2.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.90%, up 234 bps QoQ; FY26 EBITDA margin 14.80%
items.quote: EBITDA margins impro ved significantly to 15.90%, representing an expansion of 234 basis points on quarter-on-quarter basis

items.statement: Current NSR stable at INR69,000-70,000/ton; Q4 NSR INR3,700/ton; FY26 NSR down ~INR2,000/ton YoY
items.quote: We are being able to maintain our pricing at a healthy level of about between INR69,000 and INR70,000 per ton, and it's working well and stable for us.

items.statement: Wheat straw prices up 50-60% YoY but expected to normalize by early June; wood chip prices stable; pulp prices $600-700/ton globally
items.quote: Wheat straw pricing is higher by about 50%, 60% compared to last year in a similar period. And so yes, that impact is there.

items.statement: Chemical costs up 3-5% for some chemicals; caustic soda recovery 95%; key chemicals: filler, AKD, chlorine dioxide
items.quote: So this is a bit of a temporary stage where we see the input chemical cost has risen in some chemicals, not all by around 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Long-term debt INR720 crore (Mar 2026); peak debt INR650-675 crore by end FY27; annual repayment INR170-180 crore; avg cost of funds 8.5%
items.quote: As on 31st March, we have a long-term debt of INR720 crores. And it will be reduced by almost INR 100 crores by repayment of existing debt.

items.statement: Notebook paper share reduced from 22% to 7-8%, targeting exit; specialty paper target 25-30% of production; copier and high-end printing growing
items.quote: We are already down to about 7% to 8%. And after the upgradation of this -- all our machines tha t happens, we will be looking at an option of not serving the sector at all

items.statement: Anti-dumping application filed (1.5-2 year timeline); anti-subsidy application filed, expected resolution by FY26 end; MIP for paperboard extended 1 year
items.quote: We've also submitted an anti-subsidy application, which works faster. And we are expecting that to be processed and come to fruition by, let's say, this year-end or by this financial year-end.

items.statement: Lean season expected next 2-3 months with pricing pressure; reversal expected around September; FY27 operations expected better than FY26
items.quote: I think this is a lean season, the next 2, 3 months. And historically also, we see dampening in pricing. And this is what we're going to have an impact on our operations also.

items.statement: Advances to capital suppliers reduced from INR83.6 crore to INR30.6 crore as projects capitalized; some regular supplier advances recovered
items.quote: These are actually not trade suppliers. These are capital asset suppliers. So obviously, the project was under implementation over the last two years.

items.statement: Risk of Chinese/Indonesian paper dumping via trade diversion due to West Asia conflict; industry engaging policymakers for safeguard measures
items.quote: The West Asia crisis has also created the risk of trade diversion with export-oriented paper producers from China and Indonesia potentially redirecting surplus inventories to India at predatory pricing.

items.statement: Social farm forestry added 854 acres in Q4, total 18,300+ acres benefiting 19,100+ farmers; new eucalyptus varieties (P29, E2) and Subabul, Melia, Casuarina introduced
items.quote: We added 854 acres of social farm forestry during the quarter, taking the total area under plantation to more than 18,300 acres and benefiting over 19,100 farmers in the community.

items.statement: Tissue paper project deferred until debt under control; not shelved, will be next investment
items.quote: The plan for tissue project only stands deferred. It's not shelved. It's deferred for a certain point of time until we get our entire operation in control and as debt u nder control

items.statement: AI/Industry 4.0 Project Nirmaan expected to reduce total manufacturing cost 5-8% by FY28; MACS Blend Control implemented on PM4
items.quote: So overall, on the operational cost, if you see, having through and through AI implemented on all the machines. So, this is partly we have done on one of our biggest machines, and at the back end once we have everything in place, we look forward at around 5% to 8% of total cost of manufacturing coming down from the existing levels.

items.statement: Order backlog at INR 17,200 crore, up 26% year-over-year
items.quote: Today we have INR17,200 crore of order backlog.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 15-20% CAGR; achieved ~20% in FY26
items.quote: 15% to 20% CAGR of revenue, this year we did almost 20% on the higher side of the band.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 13-15%; achieved 13.3% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA 13% to 15%, we've firmly remained in that band not just this year, but over the last 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: ROCE target over 20%; reached 19.4% in FY26
items.quote: ROCE over 20% we are getting closer to that and I'm sure in the next couple of years we wi ll surely cross 20

items.statement: O&M revenue share target 20% in 3-5 years; currently at 17%
items.quote: O&M at 17% we said that our medium-term 3 to 5-year outlook is to take it to 20% and we are working and on track from that perspective.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 13.3% and PAT margin at 9.4% for FY26
items.quote: These are the key performance metrics: EBITDA at 13.3%, PAT at 9.4%.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 950 crore (excluding HAM investment); gross debt ~INR 100 crore
items.quote: Our net cash, excluding the investment in HAM, is INR 950 crore, because our borrowing is less or more or less close to INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 5 per share, up from INR 4 last year
items.quote: In line with the performance, the board recommended a final dividend of INR 5/- per share, up from INR 4/- last year.

items.statement: Order intake of INR 7,500 crore in FY26 vs INR 5,700 crore in FY25
items.quote: Our order intake we closed with INR 7,500 crore almost that is year-over-year. Last year we did about INR 5,700 crore this year we have done INR 7,500 crore.

items.statement: Core market opportunity $75-100 billion over next 5-7 years across India, Saudi, Africa, Europe, SE Asia, CIS
items.quote: If you put all this together, this is almost 75 billion to 100 billion in next five to seven years is the opportunity.

items.statement: Future energy sectors (solar, semiconductor, data centers, green hydrogen, AI) add $4-6 billion opportunity
items.quote: The future energy sector, which I told you solar, semiconductor, data centers and all, this is further 5 billion to 6 billion.

items.statement: O&M market opportunity $10 billion over next 5-7 years from long-term contracts
items.quote: And then we have another vertical, you know very well, is operation and maintenance, which is a predictability in this which brings because these are long-term contracts, 10 years, 15 years, 20 years contract and that is another $10 billion in next five to seven years.

items.statement: Perur desalination plant (SE Asia's largest) nearing commissioning by next year
items.quote: Next year around this time we should be commissioning this plant.

items.statement: Al-Haer project in Saudi at 83% physical progress, on track for commissioning
items.quote: The construction is o ver, we have achieved 83% of physical progress, the latest progress what last month we had posted and we are keeping up on it, we are on track and we should be commissioning this

items.statement: Targeting higher industrial mix in Saudi beyond municipal; registered with Aramco for industrial opportunities
items.quote: We are seeing a lot of traction in industrial, especially as we said earlier, AI and mining is a field that we see will bring in a lot of growth in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: Currency and raw material volatility from geopolitical events (Ukraine-Russia, Gulf crisis) can affect business
items.quote: Currency and raw material volatility, this is also something which is an effect of geopolitical situations. First, we saw Ukraine-Russia war, now we see Gulf crisis.

items.statement: Team development critical for 20% growth; reinforcing team across geographies including senior hire in CIS
items.quote: The kind of growth what we are talking about will not work without this, so this remains on the management focus.

items.statement: Order book at 4x revenue (target 3x); O&M backlog INR 6,500 crore with 5-20 year contracts
items.quote: We said we will k eep our order book at least 3x of revenues. We are at over 4x of revenues, giving a robust revenue visibility

items.statement: Net working capital days ~100 days
items.quote: Net working capital days hovering around 100 days.

items.statement: Technology focus adds value for clients (positive IRR) and WABAG; ceramic membranes, radium removal capabilities
items.quote: We have given our client a lot of positive IRR, increase in IRR through technology. For us also it's beneficial. For him also it's beneficial.

items.statement: Selected as one of five finalists for Global Desalination Company of the Year; won Wastewater Project of the Year
items.quote: We got selected for the desalination company of the year. Unfortunately, a bigger developer who is in a developer stage won it, but we were one of the five that got selected.

items.statement: Only pursue sovereign-guaranteed or MDB-funded projects; avoid state/municipal funded projects due to payment risk
items.quote: We don't take projects which are funded by state government or municipalities because we consider that as a big risk.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 15-20% with EBITDA margins 13-15%
items.quote: But broadly the guardrails remain, that we will grow at a 15% to 20%, continue to grow profitably. Our EBITDA margins will remain 13% to 15%.

items.statement: Order book at INR 17,300 crore
items.quote: You have an order book of INR 17,300 crore.

items.statement: Expect INR 10,000-12,000 crore order book addition in next two years
items.quote: with another INR10,000 crore to INR 12,000 crore of order book in the next two years

items.statement: Asset-light model with minimal gross/net block investment
items.quote: we don't invest in real assets, real estate, buildings, offices. We don't invest in equi pment; we don't invest in manufacturing

items.statement: International revenue mix currently 50%, targeting growth in Middle East and Africa
items.quote: Today we are at 50 % and 50%, we're looking at Middle East, Africa, you've seen the sizes that are there, so this will provide an opportunity for better margins as well as better working capital profiles.

items.statement: O&M target 20% of revenue as high-margin recurring business
items.quote: And third is, of course, our medium-long term objective of taking O&M to 20%. O&M is a high margin-accretive business, very close to the customer which can allow us to access new business as it comes, a lot of repeat business can come when we are more closer to the customer.

items.statement: Hire ~200 fresh engineers annually with 1.5 years training program
items.quote: We almost take 200 fresh engineers from the colleges every year. We have a both classroom training and on-the-job training for almost year and a half, train them and then put them on the job.

items.statement: Bhupesh Chowdary joined as Deputy Managing Director with 30 years experience
items.quote: I will take this pleasure to introduce our senior colleague, Mr. Bhupesh Chowdary Nagineni, who joined us at the senior management level as Deputy Managing Director. He joined us very recently, only a few weeks back

items.statement: Desalination water cost at 8 paise per litre vs bottled water at INR 20 per litre
items.quote: a desalination water is 8 paise a litre. I repeat, 8 paise a litre. It's affordable.

items.statement: Recycled water cost at 5-6 paise per litre
items.quote: this water is used for industrial purpose, for irrigation, for agriculture, for commercial in stitution, and the water which is released goes back to the domestic users. So that's the second source we have, which is even cheaper than desal, maybe 5 paise to 6 paise a litre

items.statement: Investing in ceramic membranes for longer life and lower lifecycle cost
items.quote: ceramic membranes have a huge advantage being ceramic you can put it in the furnace and fire it and all the junk which is settled on it or clogged it they burn out and then you bring the membrane back and load it they are fresh membranes.

items.statement: AI partnership with Pani Energy showing reduced chemical consumption and better water utilization
items.quote: There is an expectation or what we are realizing: reduced chemical consumption, better utilization of water. There are very many other parameters on which result is positive, we are enthused.

items.statement: Recent order wins: BWSSB, BPCL, two Chennai orders, DJB project
items.quote: There was BWSSB, BPCL, two Chennai orders, you have DJB. All these orders will again start bringing in revenues.

items.statement: Municipal platform development underway, asset-light model, pilot studies positive
items.quote: We are on the verge of getting closer with whatever that we need to agree. And it will be a vision for creating a platform where we can b id for multiple municipal projects and we don't have to scout for new partners every

items.statement: Open to bolt-on technology acquisitions globally
items.quote: Now are we looking at a small maybe bolt -on acquisition for the technology globally where it can add or help our technology prowess? Rajiv Mittal: Definitely. Short answer is yes

items.statement: No diversification outside water segment planned in near future
items.quote: is no need, and we are not looking at in the near future of any diversification which is outside water. We call ourselves pure -play water company and in the near future we don't see that changing

items.statement: Price variation clauses cover 70% of costs in large Indian projects, not in international
items.quote: In international, generally we don't have those clauses. But in most of the large Indian orders, we have a price variation clause where we are covered by any fluctuation which happens. But still, it only covers 70% of our costs, not 100% of the cost.

items.statement: Indian segment profitability varies quarterly due to project phases, blended margins better indicator
items.quote: See, to look at it as only for the quarter will not be the right way to see because projects are at different phases, right? Today we have two or three large projects which are in construction phase. And you know construction is more or less a pass-through for us.

items.statement: Bio-CNG plant to serve 3,500 homes or 400 vehicles daily, first of 100 planned
items.quote: The volume what we are going to generate is going to serve per day around 3,500 homes can get their cooking gas or 400 vehicles. That's the magnitude we are talking.

items.statement: Five-year strategy blueprint being developed by new Deputy MD
items.quote: I am also started working in a way to say that , we have a strategy plan for the next five years that will be also as a blueprint will be drawn, and the short gaps, and also the capabilities that need to be b uilt for the organization and the structure, that would also get in place

items.statement: Order backlog is around 50% higher than last year, showing robustness for upcoming execution
items.quote: And that shows the complete robustness in terms of what we have on the hand to execute in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Gross margin dropped 1.5-1.6% in FY26 vs FY25 due to commodity impact and revenue mix shift
items.quote: The gross margin, when you look at, it's slightly dropped. If you look at in terms of margin, it is close to 1.6%, 1.5% drop.

items.statement: Copper and aluminum prices rose 30%+ and steel rose ~10% in the year April 2025 to March 2026
items.quote: Just to give you like copper, aluminum in last 1 year, I'm talking about the year, which is between April '25 and March '26, has seen an upward movement of 30% plus. And so is steel, which is another component which we use extensively in our products, whi ch has seen close to 10% increase in the last 12 months

items.statement: Commodity hedging covers 50-60% of exposure; forex hedging done on PO and net ARAP basis
items.quote: So commodity hedging is completely covered up to the 50% to 60%. And forex hedging for any dependency on the import, we do 2 type of hedging. One is also the PO hedging particularly on order by order and then we also have a net ARAP forex hedging.

items.statement: Large infrastructure projects (>6 months) use variable price contracts to pass through commodity increases
items.quote: Mostly what we try to do the large infrastructure project, which is more than 6-month delivery period, which always with the customer with some variable contract. It means what it means we make sure that we give the price today. But if price may go up, we try to negotiate that differential has to be recovered from the customer.

items.statement: Data center IT load estimated at 1.5 GW currently, ~3 GW in advanced stage for next 1.5-2 years, targeting 8 GW by 2030
items.value: 1.5 GW current, ~3 GW pipeline, 8 GW target
items.quote: We -- with the best of industry estimates are sitting close to about 1.5 gigawatts of IT load. There are a set of people who say that we should be close to about 8 gigawa tts by 2030. And this is a reality because what we understand is there's about 3 gigawatts, which have been already in a very advanced stage of sort of getting signed up and getting rolled out in the next 1.5 to 2 years' time

items.statement: Data centers represent ~10-12% of current order backlog, expected to increase
items.quote: Maybe if under control of my CFO, maybe typically about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Energy storage (BESS) capacity expected to grow from ~1 GWh to 210-240 GWh by 2030-2032 per government plans
items.quote: Now what we have done, if you look at this, what we have done and we are trying to bring in all solutions of from Schneider side, which are either power distribution, power management, software, the structure, the design. We are trying to give a combination of this, and we are working, especially with all those clients who are really looking for one of the best -of-breed solutions fully automated,

items.statement: Capex approved and capitalization started from end of Q4 FY26, driving depreciation increase
items.quote: The dep, if you look at increase in Q4 is largely you all approved the capex to invest, and we have started capitalizing from Q4 end of the Q4 and then impact is coming.

items.statement: Q4 gross margin 36.6% impacted ~2.5% by commodity and sales phasing; full-year margin drop largely commodity-driven
items.quote: Margin largely, as we said, that's largely impacting because of the commodity. Almost 2.5% is coming from commodity and is coming from the sales.

items.statement: Service revenue grew to 15% of sales but modernization projects (lower margin) grew faster than spares/AMC
items.quote: And then we also have a modernization projects where we say that either more on revamp where we call projects mostly what happened the third category is growing compared to other 2. Other 2 has better margin than third one, which is modernization and RA.

items.statement: Selective order booking in Q4 due to commodity uncertainty; only accepting orders with variable price clauses
items.quote: The Q4 order intake because of uncertainty in commodity market, we were very, very selective. Were only selecting the orders where we can get certain leverage in terms of whether I can realize the price even with the price increase, so variable clause.

items.statement: Government capex up 11.5% to INR 12.2 lakh crore; power utilities' financial outlay up ~20% for FY27
items.quote: The capex planned and which is getting rolled out by the government is about 11.5% higher than what it was last year, whi ch is typically about INR12.2 lakh crores. And the power central utilities have been actually having a lot of declaration on the financial outlay, which will be -- they will be doing in FY27, which is roughly up by about 20

items.statement: Launched dry-type transformers (Trihal design, E4 C4F1 class, seismic compliant) for data centers, metros, commercial buildings
items.quote: And we have actually supplied close to 170,000 units worldwide across 100 countries. And what specifically which this brings in is, if you notice, is E4, C4F1 class, which is one of the -- I would say, is one of the most stringent, more robust endurance class made in dry type transformers.

items.statement: Launched One Digital Grid AI platform for DISCOMs with fault detection, asset management, and chatbot assistant
items.quote: Now in very simple layman terms, this is a tool which advises guides and interacts with the DISCOMs in terms of telling them how do they make the grid work most efficiently. So what it actually does using AI is it not only captures as to where the fault is, how do you bring it back, what is the lease cost of bringing it back, where -- which asset geographically is placed where, how to attack it.

items.statement: Management expects minimum 10-12% revenue growth in FY27 and aims to return to pre-investment EBITDA margin levels of 14-15%
items.quote: 10%, 12% is the bare minimum we should be hitting, and we are confident of doing that for this year. And yes, if things go well and some things go in favor, maybe more than that as well.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR34 crores; FY27 budget is INR10-15 crores for maintenance and additional machinery at Sanand and Chandipur
items.quote: this year, we did around INR34 crores. And for the current year, we have a budget of around INR10 crores to INR15 crores.

items.statement: Sanand Protec unit running at ~50% utilization; targets INR40 crores minimum annual revenue at existing capacity
items.value: 50% utilization; INR40 crores annual revenue target
items.quote: Sanand, we have just -- it was more of capex into infrastructure building, and we have started with a small SME there. And with this setup, as of now, we are running at around 50% capacity, and we are trying to improve it gradually. And for the year, we target in the range of anything with the existing capacity should be in the range of INR40 crores minimum, INR40 crores on annual basis, yes.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.34% (-185 bps YoY); FY26 EBITDA margin 11.21% (-130 bps YoY) due to higher raw material costs, lower realizations, increased employee expenses
items.quote: EBITDA margin came in at 9.34%, reflecting a decline of 185 basis points year-on-year, primarily on account of higher raw material costs during the quarter.

items.statement: Domestic business grew ~20% YoY in FY26; exports faced headwinds from US tariffs and weak EU demand; Q4 domestic growth slowed due to cautious sentiment and gas shortages
items.quote: Despite the challenging external environment, our domestic business continued to be the growth engine, expanding by approximately 20% year-on-year, while exports faced headwinds that we are actively working to overcome.

items.statement: Raw material costs increased across textiles, leather, polymers, synthetics due to petro-based inputs, currency impact, freight and energy costs; price pass-through lags in both OEM export and domestic markets
items.quote: we've seen increase in mostly, I think across the board, we've seen an increase due to whatever is happening globally. A lot of these products are petro-based. So, that's where we've seen increase. Some of these raw materials also have to be imported. So, we have seen increase in the prices increase in the exchange rate difference, which is hurting us, and increasing freight costs.

items.statement: US tariffs were prohibitive for most of FY26; Europe demand bleak; South America, Australia, Russia, Africa performed well; Middle East okay; UAE marketing arm established for MEA region
items.quote: South America has done well for us. Australia, Russia has done well. These are our OEM markets in our own branded markets. Middle East has been okay. I wouldn't say great. Africa has done well. But yes, Europe is not so well. U.S., we all know the situation.

items.statement: New in-house manufacturing of PU Coated Gloves and PVC Gumboots started as import substitutes; PU gloves import market ~INR80-90 crores; both categories target domestic and export revenue
items.value: INR80-90 crores PU gloves import market
items.quote: PU gloves in India, yes, at least would like the import figure, if it is to be trusted, probably India imports roughly around anywhere between INR80 crores to INR90 crores of these gloves or maybe more.

items.statement: Working capital debt ~INR110-115 crores; no term loan except INR5 crores for Sanand subsidy eligibility; expect debt to decline over next 4 years with lower capex and cash generation; finance cost could approach zero in 3-4 years
items.quote: with the current level of operations and current outstanding, which we have, INR110 crores, INR115 crores, that is definitely with most of the major capex happening. And in that situation, we can pay most of the debt in next 4 years.

items.statement: Labour code formalization and stricter BIS standards seen as positive for organized players; expected to expand PPE market and benefit Mallcom
items.quote: the more formalization there is in -- with respect to labour, I think it's better for organized players like us. And it will definitely make it into a much bigger market for PPE as well.

items.statement: Export sales are white-label/OEM; domestic is branded; LatAm relationships >15-20 years; strict payment terms (LC/advance) with no credit beyond goods transit time
items.quote: So, that way, we are very strict with our payment terms. Most of -- either we work on LCs or we work on some advance or we secure our payments. We don't offer any sort of credit to them
