items.statement: Chinese competitors have local raw material advantage reducing currency/freight pressure; domestic competitors also raising prices or stopping orders; unorganized players struggling with input cost volatility
items.quote: China, because a lot of the materials, they are able to buy locally. So, they face this pressure lesser, at least for the currency devaluation and the freight, they don't face as much pressure as we do.

items.statement: Major raw materials: textiles, leather, polymers, synthetics (PU, PC, NBR); petro-based, partly imported; facing price increases, currency impact, freight costs, energy cost increases
items.quote: major raw materials for us are largely in 4 different categories. These are textiles, leather, polymers and synthetics like PU, PC, these kind of NBR, these kinds of chemicals.

items.statement: Distributors stock inventory and pre-buy ahead of price hikes; some work on back-to-back orders; price list revised twice in Q4 but lag exists due to pending orders and rate contracts
items.quote: In fact, in the last quarter, we've revised our price list twice to be able to pass on the prices. But still, you have to respect some of the previous prices, some long-term rate contracts that you have.

items.statement: FY26 operating revenue INR540 crores (+11% YoY); EBITDA INR61 crores; PAT INR30 crores (5.5% margin, not comparable to FY25 due to INR25 crore one-time land sale gain)
items.quote: For the financial year 2026, operating revenue stood at INR540 crores, registering a growth of approximately 11% year-on-year. EBITDA for the year stood at INR61 crores, while EBITDA margin came in at 11.21%.

items.statement: Eligible for INR10 crores capital subsidy for Sanand project under state policy; will apply in FY27; INR7 crores subsidy already received for Chandipur project (INR14 crore machinery cost)
items.quote: as per tax side policy there in the range of INR10 crores, we should be getting.

items.statement: Invested in fresh hiring to support new manufacturing facilities and growth; expanded distribution network and marketing team including 8 traveling export salespeople
items.quote: the company kept investing in creation of talent pool by fresh Mallcom ( hiring needed to drive growth as well as has continued to participate in both domestic and international fairs, organizing technical seminars, investing in brand

items.statement: FY27 domestic branded generics growth guided at 100-150 bps above market, implying double-digit growth
items.quote: if you ask me domestic, I've already called out that we should be 100 to 150 basis points higher than the market, which means that maybe a double-digit kind of growth is what we are looking forward to.

items.statement: FY27 US pharma growth guided at high single-digit on dollar-to-dollar basis plus forex gain and H2 new launches
items.quote: U.S. market from a currency-to-currency basis, the dollar to dollar, we are looking at a high single -digit margin and the currency gain would add up to that.

items.statement: FY27 ROW markets guided at higher teens growth
items.quote: From the ROW markets, we have looked at a higher teen's kind of growth. And we assume that, that is going to be the trend even in the coming year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 20-21% range, subject to geopolitical and cost clarity by H2/Q3
items.quote: we have touched a 20.4% kind of growth like-to-like, we would -- we should be within the range of 20% to 21%.

items.statement: Tax rate guidance revised to 27-29% from FY27 due to move to new tax regime from April 2026
items.quote: we want to revise our guidance on tax rate. The number will be around 27% to 29% going forward.

items.statement: R&D spend guided at 4-5% of revenue for FY27, consistent with FY26 at 4.2%
items.quote: we expect it to be similar between 4% to 5% even in the coming year.

items.statement: Other expenses (ex-Occlutech) guided to increase 7-8% in FY27
items.quote: Other than that, the other expenses can increase by 7% to 8%, not beyond that.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 20.4% from 19.4% in FY25, driven by mix improvement and cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA was INR3,052 million, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 20.4% versus 19.4% in FY '25

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 14.4% vs 12.4% in Q4 FY25, up 200 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA was INR5,174 million, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 14.4% for the Q4 FY '25 versus 12.4% for Q4 2 025

items.statement: India branded generics grew ~10% YoY in FY26, outperforming IPM by ~100-150 bps; chronic segment grew 16.1% vs IPM 13.6%
items.quote: branded generic business growth, that has been close to 10% and international sales were INR12,223 million with a Y-o-Y growth of 25.4%.

items.statement: Semaglutide launched March 2026, achieved ~11% unit market share in latest IQVIA report, expected to rise further
items.quote: in the most recent IQVIA re port, we could garner a market -- unit market share of around 11% and we expect it to go up even further in the coming months.

items.statement: Chronic share of branded generics reached ~22%, improving ~1% per year over last 3-4 years
items.quote: today, our chronic business as far as branded generic business is concerned. We are close to 22% of our business is from chronic

items.statement: API and packaging material costs rising due to geopolitical environment; impact expected in Q1 FY27 and beyond if situation persists
items.quote: we can see the raw material prices are increasing, the packing material prices are increasing and we have been cautiously watching the prices

items.statement: Forex policy hedges 80% of exposure; raw material and packing material procurement managed weekly with inventory build on price dips
items.quote: we have a forex policy, and we generally cover 80% or we hedge 80% of our forex exposure.

items.statement: Occlutech acquisition to close in 45-60 days; full consolidation from Q2 FY27; no further acquisitions foreseen for next 12 months
items.quote: Occlutech is one of our biggest investment in last 10 years and we don't foresee any further investment into acquisitions at least for the next 12 months.

items.statement: Enzene US biologics plant commissioned recently; India business at early double-digit EBITDA margin; US plant loss-making, nearing breakeven this year
items.quote: India is around -- is in breakeven, much more than breakeven. We are in late -- early double digits, you can say teens EBITDA. U.S., we will lose money

items.statement: Denosumab (Prolia/Xgeva) biosimilar US approval expected by Q1 FY28; European approval received for Prolia, partner in place; Xgeva EU launch not imminent
items.quote: if we are good, maybe by next quarter -- I mean, next year's first quarter. So, there's still some time.

items.statement: Tolvaptan US launch targeted September-October 2026; limited competition market
items.quote: our expected launch is around September or October, somewhere around that time. And it's a limited player launch.

items.statement: Field force at ~14,500 MRs; attrition reduced to 18-19%, well below industry average; recent additions focused on chronic therapies
items.quote: our number of MRs at a group level is around 14,500. The other -- what was the attrition was the other question, right? We are at 18% to 19% kind of attrition currently

items.statement: CEO search initiated with top global headhunters; will take few months; promoters to run business interim; CEO to oversee core pharma, other businesses report to other promoters
items.quote: we will look for a CEO. We have engaged with the top 3 global head and up for this. And that would be in place. It would take a few months

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO revenue <INR100 cr in FY26; meaningful scale (INR200-300 cr) expected in couple of years
items.quote: Last year, we recognized some CDMO from U.S. that was like less than INR100 crores. So, it's pretty small. It would take time for us to get like meaningfully like INR200 crores, INR300 crores.

items.statement: Dividend payout 25-30% of PAT; absolute dividend unlikely to reduce in FY27 despite higher tax rate; payout % may rise
items.quote: currently, I think we actually declare 25% to 30% of our PAT as dividend. In next year, since we'll be coming out of MAT, definitely, the PAT, you will see that -- and we have actually discussed this in a few of our previous calls also that our tax rate will significantly go up from FY '27. So definitely, there will -- if we maintain the same dividend which we have declared in the last few years,

items.statement: Geopolitical instability and supply chain dynamics increasing logistics, API and packaging costs; near-term headwinds expected; inventory built up to mitigate disruptions
items.quote: the current geopolitical environment and evolving global supply chain dynamics have resulted in increased logistics costs along with some pressure on APIs and the packaging materials. We are continuously watching these changing trends. These external factors may lead to some near-term headwinds.

items.statement: Trade generic growth 4.3% in FY26 due to restructuring and sales cutoff issues; focus on margin improvement over top line; growth expected to improve in FY27
items.quote: Trade generic, this year, we had carved out a separate entity, and during that transition, we have had certain challenges. So, this year, the growth has been lesser as far as trade generic is concerned, it's close to around 4.3% on an annualized basis.

items.statement: India acute segment grew 10% vs IPM 7.7%; chronic grew 16.1% vs IPM 13.6% (250 bps outperformance); outperformed in 6 key therapies
items.quote: Acute segment reported a growth of 10% versus IPM, which grew by 7.7% and chronic segment reported 16.1% versus the IPM growth of 13.6%, which is almost a 250-basis point outperformance.

items.statement: Management declined to give specific numerical guidance for FY27 but expects a better year after a difficult phase
items.quote: So, Mr. Varun, again for next year we are not giving any specific number on the guidance part.

items.statement: FY26 was an average year with adverse weather impacting sales in key regions and crop segments
items.quote: As a business year for the Indian agrochemical sector, FY'26 was an average year with some unexpected and adverse weather conditions.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin percentage improved to 30% from 29% despite revenue decline
items.quote: However, gross margin percentage improved to 30% compared to 29% in the previous year, supported by product mix improvement and calibrated pricing actions.

items.statement: Branded segment gross margin averages around 40% while B2B segment is at 15-20%
items.quote: For branded depending upon product but since our portfolio of patent is going up, we are on an average at around 40% whereas on the B2B we are at around 15-20%.

items.statement: Target branded EBITDA margin of 18-20% and B2B EBITDA margin around 8% for next year
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the branded should be anywhere from 18-20% and on the B2B it should be around 8% or so.

items.statement: Two rounds of price increases implemented in April and May 2026 to mitigate rising input costs
items.quote: To mitigate rising input costs, t he Company implemented two rounds of price increases during April and May 2026

items.statement: Conscious decision to hold back ₹50-70 crore of sales in March 2026 to avoid low-realization sales
items.quote: While this prudent decision impacted near-term revenues by approximately ₹50 –70 crore, we believe it was necessary to protect medium-term profitability and maintain channel discipline.

items.statement: Patented product portfolio increased from 30% to 40% of branded sales
items.quote: presently our patent product portfolio has gone up from 30% to 40% of our branded, which almost entire formulation everything is done in our own factory.

items.statement: Launched 3 patented products in FY26 and plans 4 new launches in FY27 including Fluzam, Midcotin, Cubax Power Extra, and Trishanku
items.quote: FY'27 will see us launch Fluzam, Midcotin, Cubax Power Extra, and Trishanku. These patented products are expected to further strengthen our positioning in the specialized crop protection market.

items.statement: Introduced 5 new bio-stimulant products in FY26: Sprink, Richgrow Gold, Emprole, Tornet & Punctual
items.quote: The new segment of bio products includes Sprink, Richgrow Gold, Emprole, Tornet & Punctual.

items.statement: Postponed new capex for existing plant, keeping it on hold
items.quote: we are postponing the newer capex which we are supposed to do in our existing plant. So, that we are keeping it on hold.

items.statement: Capacity utilization 80-90% during season and 50-60% off-season; existing capacity sufficient
items.quote: We see our capacity utilization going up to 80-90% during the season and off season we are at around 50-60%. So, just to answer if our existing manufacturing capacity is sufficing, if that is the question, yes.

items.statement: 4 new off-patent molecules to be produced at Gajraula facility in FY27, already in production in Q1
items.quote: I had mentioned also that, you know, there were around four new off patent molecules that we had been working on for the whole of last year. And R&D was able to succeed in the synthesis methods of these four molecules. These four molecules will be in production. In fact, they are already getting produced in this particular Q1.

items.statement: Inventory reduced from ₹958 crore in FY24 to ₹651 crore as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: I am pleased to share that inventory levels have reduced significantly from approximately ₹958 crore in FY24 to ₹773 crore in FY25 and further to ₹651 crore as of March 31, 2026.

items.statement: Branded inventory days 120-150 and receivables 120 days; B2B inventory 90-120 days and receivables 90 days
items.quote: inventory days for the branded is little higher, anywhere between 120 to 150 days and for the B2B business it is 90 to 120. With respect to receivables, again on the receivable side it is around 120 days and B2B side it is 90 days.

items.statement: Sales return percentage reduced from 20-30% to 20-21%, targeting below 20% next year
items.quote: Presently we are at around 20-21% of sales return and we are pretty comfortable at this and continuing we will try to go down less than 20% for the next year.

items.statement: Bank facility utilization at 85-90%, with 10% headroom available plus government 20% additional funding
items.quote: even at this present time if you see our utilization of the bank facilities it is at around 85-90%. That means still 10% facilities we have which we can avail and we can utilize. Plus, this additional help which has come from the central government those also we will take.

items.statement: Loan balances have been constantly reducing over last 3 years; FY26 operating cash flow positive at ₹90 crore
items.quote: If you see my last 3 years loan balances we have been constantly reducing it. So, we have been and if you see my cash flow for the year FY25-26 even though we have made a profit of 8 crores. After tax my cash flow from operations is 90 crores.

items.statement: No fund raise or rights issue planned; relying on internal accruals, bank facilities and government funding
items.quote: We are in a full-fledged production time. So, our capital requirement is higher. So, even at this present time if you see our utilization of the bank facilities it is at around 85-90%. That means still 10% facilities we have which we can avail and we can utilize. Plus, this additional help which has come from the central government those also we will take.

items.statement: Registrations progressing in Mexico (2 in final stages), Sri Lanka (fast track), Thailand (first registration received), Vietnam (expanding portfolio)
items.quote: Our registrations abroad are ongoing with 2 registrations in Mexico in the final stages of approval. In Sri Lanka, the registration of our patented molecules is in progress on a fast track, while we successfully received our first registration in Thailand. In Vietnam, we are expanding the registration portfolio with our local partners.

items.statement: Shipping consignments to Sudan; final stages of starting subsidiary in Brazil; interest in patented Nano Urea formulation abroad
items.quote: Regarding orders, we continue to ship consignments to Sudan where our products are being well accepted. We are in the final stages of starting a subsidiary in Brazil. We also are continuing to see interest in our patented Nano Urea formulation abroad.

items.statement: Facing counterfeit surge for popular products like Ronfen; introducing high-security holograms on key products
items.quote: We are experiencing a surge in counterfeits especially for our popular products such as Ronfen. To tackle this, we are introducing high security hologram on our key products to help our customers differentiate genuine products from counterfeits.

items.statement: New labels will display mode of action based on IRAC, HRAC, FRAC classifications to prevent pest resistance
items.quote: Our new labels will display the mode of action based on IRAC, HRAC and FRAC. We believe this transparency will help the farmers choose the right products.

items.statement: R&D spend maintained at around 1% of revenue; filed 100+ patents, expecting 2-3 new patents annually for next 5 years
items.quote: the general percentage what we spend on our R&D and the patents will continue which is for our industry the percentage doesn't look very high but we continue to do it between around 1% or so. So, we have already filed close to 100 plus patents and we are hopeful to see at least 2 to 3 new patents coming at least for the next 5 years.

items.statement: OPEX reduced by close to 15% in FY26
items.quote: Also, other two which we have planned was the OPEX reduction. There also we reduced close to 15% of our OPEX.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR400 crores, EBITDA margin 14%, gross margin 49-50%
items.quote: Yes. We assume that the margin will be high as the premium product will sell more. And also there is an increase in the ASP also.

items.statement: Steady state target of around 200 COCO stores post cleanup
items.quote: Around 200 COCO stores.

items.statement: FY26 challenging with muted consumer demand and pressure on discretionary spending in mass and value segments
items.quote: FY '26 continued to be a challenging year for the footwear industry, with muted consumer demand and continued pressure on discretionary spending, particularly in the mass and value segments.

items.statement: Demand recovery driven by both ticket size and footfall improvement
items.quote: Both. Ticket size also has an impact and also the footfall. Both of the factors are important.

items.statement: Blended gross margin declined due to price cuts in sub-INR500 products; Q4 margin improved with new season ASP increase
items.quote: Blended gross margin has declined last year because we have taken a price cut for the last 1 or 2 years, we have taken some price cut in our product s less than INR500

items.statement: Expect 50 basis point gross margin improvement in FY27 from premiumization and ASP increase
items.quote: I think we can expect another 50-basis point improvement in gross margin.

items.statement: TFM portfolio grew 46% YoY in FY26; British Walkers grew 6% YoY; Skechers showing sequential growth
items.quote: Our TFM portfolio delivered a strong growth of 46% year -on-year during FY '26, reflecting improving acceptance across customer segment and continued traction in premium and semi -premium categories.

items.statement: Premium products (above INR1,500) contribute 15% of revenue; deliver 2-3% higher gross margin with less discounting
items.quote: No, one thing is that this premium product has given the gross margin somewhat 2%, 3% more than the normal mass market product. And also the discounting of this product is comparatively less compared to the lower category product.

items.statement: Athleisure structurally limited due to small store format lacking changing rooms; will not expand beyond men's range
items.quote: It's limited. Because we don't have that much space to keep all the athleisure like tracksuit, pants and everything. We are only keeping men's thing because the ladies thing, we cannot keep because we don't have change room and all this.

items.statement: Asset-light expansion strategy; franchisee (FRM/TFM) requires only stock investment vs COCO needing capex and stock
items.quote: Our asset-light expansion strategy continues to remain central to our long-term growth plans.

items.statement: Closed ~60 stores in last 2 years; no further closures planned; focus on profit-making stores and e-commerce
items.quote: See, we have closed around 60 stores in the last 2 years. So that means , we are focusing on opening some strategic store, which will give us more sales. But we'll not keep the store which are making losses.

items.statement: Inventory reduced ~40% YoY; lost some Q4 sales due to understocking; now rebuilding stock for spring-summer season
items.quote: See, when you take some calls in the working capital thing, because we have taken a call to reduce the inventory days. Yes, in the fourth quarter, we have lost some sales because of lower inventory.

items.statement: Inventory correction done; will increase inventory to required level for new season, focusing on full-price stock over discounted
items.quote: Already, the inventory correction has been done. Now this year, we'll increase the inventory to the extent that is needed. We'll not go overboard on inventory.

items.statement: Deliberately reduced purchases in Q3-Q4 to pay down creditors; trade payables fell from INR196 crores to INR111 crores partly due to demerger
items.quote: So one part has reduced because of our demerger because las t year's figure is comparing with both the company. But still considering that also, we are able to reduce the creditors of Khadim India Limited because we -- for the last 2 quarters in Q3 and Q4, we deliberately reduced the purchase and paid our creditors so that the creditors balance has also come down.

items.statement: Will correct franchisee debtor levels in FY27 after inventory correction in FY26
items.quote: Like last year, we have corrected the inventory. This year, we'll make correction in the debtors also.

items.statement: Target net debt INR110-115 crores post restructuring
items.quote: INR110 crores to INR115 crores.

items.statement: Working capital limits available but not fully utilized; comfortable with cash flow management via EBO collections

items.quote: Another U.S. bid order is expected to contribute close to INR10 crores annually.

items.quote: The successful launch of our proprietary hydraulic gear pumps after nearly five years of focused R&D efforts is another important step in that direction and reflects our long-term product development capabilities.

items.statement: Quality Control Order (QCO) effective August 2026 expected to deter furniture imports, a key competitive advantage
items.quote: Furniture imports, which represent our primary source of competition, are currently under pressure due to the foreign currency fluctuations, the supply chain and logistics disruptions, and the regulatory measures, (QCO) the Quality Control Order coming into effect from August 2026.

items.quote: But today we will say that I think most of our stores are about 85% to 90% completely made by us. We have expanded our facility to add different products such as beds, mattress, dining table, so we are a complete solution provider.

But when you look at it as a complete mixture, we have still grown at 4% when you look at same store sales growth.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target of 11% to 13%
items.quote: So, if you look at EBITDA, I think with a disciplined approach and maintaining operational efficiency, we should be this year able to deliver anywhere between 11% to 13% in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: FY26 trips grew 29% YoY to 5.23 million; stable IT/ITES demand, strong GCC demand in ETS; diversified CCR demand growth

items.statement: Top 200 clients churn minimal at 2-3%; long-tail clients vary with needs
items.quote: But our major clients if I were to say are top 200 clients, the churn is minimum, there may be 2% or 3% is what's over there.

items.quote: EBITDA for FY26 stood at INR939.29 million. Margin during the year was influenced by higher manpower cost, expanding leadership bandwidth, investment in tech, and competitive pricing environment, especially in the ETS segment.

items.statement: Employee cost growth budgeted at 13-16% for FY27; other expenses growth at 8-9%
items.quote: So, in our in terms of our HR cost, we would expect approximately, you know, anywhere between a 13% to 15% or 16% growth in the employee cost. That is what we are budgeting for in the latest AOP.

items.statement: Fuel cost pass-through in most contracts after 5% threshold; lag of few days to weeks

items.quote: So, unless we see a so what your -- the first question about EV investments, if we see those conditions developing where, you know, EVs are a very much a norm and they are sustainable financially, we will see a larger investment in EV capex over there. items.statement: Cash and investments INR1,373M as of March 31, 2026; low leverage, healthy cash flow

items.statement: No demand impact yet from PM work-from-home appeal; clients have matured WFH policies post-COVID

items.statement: Expanding leadership bandwidth in senior positions in FY27; manpower cost growth muted vs FY26
items.quote: This year what we are seeing is we'll be seeing a much more muted growth in our manpower cost, which should give us some operating leverages over there while we are looking at also expanding our leadership bandwidth in senior positions this year.

items.statement: Growth drivers: ~60-65% from new client acquisitions, rest from organic wallet share expansion and vendor consolidation

items.statement: Captive recycling plant gave 0.5% margin benefit in Q4; battery breaking operation expected to stabilize next quarter for further benefit, but RML price increases creating headwinds
items.quote: Last quarter, we have seen about 0.5% benefit coming from the recycling plant because predominantly, it was a refining operation that we are currently operating in. We are expecting our battery breaking operation to stabilize in the coming quarter.

items.statement: New Energy strategy shifting: earlier 80% EV / 20% ESS long-term, now ~2/3 EV, 1/3 ESS (or higher ESS share); ESS accelerated due to renewable drive
items.quote: Earlier, our projections are more about like 80% coming from EV long term, 20% from ESS. I think long term, while EV will still be the larger component, today, we believe it's going to look something more like 2/3, 1/3, maybe even depending on how successfully ESS continues to roll out, it can even be higher.

items.statement: Telecom market share remains robust ~50% despite lead-acid to lithium transition; supplying packs to 2W/3W/LCV OEMs; engaged with passenger vehicle OEMs (long lead times)
items.quote: We continue our market leadership in this segment through the technology transition, and the first exports of lithium systems in this segment has also taken place.

items.statement: Gotion LFP technology licensing hindered by Chinese government restrictions; Amara Raja now self-driven on R&D for NMC/LFP/future chemistries; LFP plant likely 2028 or later
items.quote: Since that time, I think all of you would have also been seeing in the news that sharing of technology, licensing technology is something that's been largely discouraged by the Chinese government.

items.statement: Expecting localization mandates for energy storage (like solar ALMM) to help domestic cell makers; EV side may see duty increases on imported components as local capacity builds
items.quote: A couple of other areas that localization may start getting mandated in phases in the energy storage, especially at the utility scale, where the government is directly the buyer.

items.statement: Export volumes muted in Q4 due to geopolitical issues, Middle East tensions, North American tariff barriers; exports 11% of Q4 revenue, 12% of FY26 revenue
items.quote: During the current quarter, with the ongoing geopolitical issues, we have seen a muted growth in the export volumes of Automotive business. And we hope in the next coming quarters, the momentum will revive.

items.statement: Infused INR100 crores into Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies in Q4 FY26; cumulative investment in subsidiary now INR1,500 crores
items.quote: And in this current quarter, we have also infused about INR100 crores further into Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, our new energy subsidiary. With this, the overall investment into this subsidiary is about INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: New Energy revenue INR280 crores in Q4 FY26 (1.5x YoY); FY26 consolidated revenue INR13,814 crores (+7.5% YoY); Lead Acid revenue growth 12% YoY in Q4
items.quote: The New Energy business clocked a revenue of about INR280 crores from the sale of battery packs and chargers.

items.statement: Lubes business reached INR50 crores per quarter sales revenue scale
items.quote: The lubes product also have shown reasonable growth in numbers, and we have now reached a scale of about INR50 crores per quarter as a sales revenue from this segment.

items.statement: Chinese visa limitations for equipment commissioning engineers creating challenges for Giga 1 timeline; mitigation via CQP experience and partial visa success
items.quote: The bigger challenge that we've been facing is not so much that we don't have access to equipment, but we have a little bit of limitations in terms of getting the engineers from China to come and help to actually commission the equipment.

items.statement: Lead-acid capacity redundancy risk assessed as low: strong tubular demand (solar/home), ICE vehicle parc growth, auxiliary battery demand, hybrid vehicle solutions provide long runway
items.quote: We don't foresee an immediate problem with respect to our tubular batteries. As Harsha mentioned, the home application might offer more runway with the solar systems, et cetera, coming in. The tubular batteries will continue to be on demand.

items.statement: R&D teams moving into E Positive Energy Labs (final commissioning phase) over next month in phased manner; consolidated teams and upgraded equipment to accelerate R&D backlog
items.quote: E Positive Energy Labs, our R&D center is undergoing the final commissioning phase. Our teams are starting to move into the facility over the next month in a phased manner.

items.statement: Achieved 12x water positive and zero waste to landfill at manufacturing locations; continuing sustainability efforts on energy reduction and renewable share increase
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that though our plants are located in distressed water situation areas, we've been assured 12x water positive in these locations and continue to work very steadfast in our sustainability goals. We're also zero waste to landfill, which is also a significant achievement this year.

items.statement: CPG business targets break-even within 6-8 quarters and single-digit EBITDA margin by end of decade
items.quote: The intent is to break even within the next 6-8 quarters and exit this decade with a good single-digit percentage EBITDA on this business.

items.statement: Only capex planned is new jaggery facility of about Rs 45 crore
items.quote: The only CAPEX that we are doing this year is largely the new Jaggery facility. That is about a 45-odd crore CAPEX which we are doing.

items.statement: Ethanol production capacity utilization may increase to 17 crore litres if blending percentage rises
items.quote: We have, as Muthu pointed out earlier, produced about 16 crore liters. We would probably tend towards 17 crore liters if there is an improvement in ethanol blending percentage.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu cane planting expected to increase 10-15%
items.quote: We have planted roughly about we are looking at about 10-15% increase in the planting.

items.statement: CPG value-added products target 30%+ gross margin level
items.quote: Lot of these value-added products move the business into the 30+% gross margin level.

items.statement: Cane cost increased to Rs 4,087/MT from Rs 3,768/MT due to FRP hike of Rs 150/MT
items.quote: Cane cost for the current quarter is Rs. 4087 per metric ton (MT) as against the Rs. 3768 per MT of the corresponding quarter of the previous year. This increase is mainly on account of the increase in FRP, which was about Rs. 150 per MT, announced by the Central Government.

items.statement: Government shared intent for E30 blending through BIS; higher allocations expected in new ethanol year
items.quote: The good development has been the government sharing their intent through the BIS aspect for E30. We have been telling this for the last 4 to 5 quarters. We expect positive action from the government. It will become visible during the allocations that will come up in the new ethanol year.

items.statement: No significant action expected on ethanol pricing; focus on blending percentage increase
items.quote: Our last read of the situation was that there may not be too much action on pricing but there will be an action on increase in blending percentages.

items.statement: MSP for sugar unlikely given inflationary pressures
items.quote: Not really. I think given the inflationary pressures it is unlikely.

items.statement: PSRIPL loan obligations to be completed by June 30, 2026; EID infused Rs 600 crore by May 15
items.quote: With these two tranches of the investment, EID has infused so far by 15th May was about Rs.600 crores into the payment obligations of the PSRIPL. So, another $1.4 million scheduled for the payment in June 2026. This will be funded through internal receivables from the PSRIPL. With the above, all the loans obligations of PSRIPL will get completed by 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Exploring entry into ethnic snacking and culinary convenience segments; conversations ongoing
items.quote: We are talking about ethnic snacking and culinary convenience. These are segments which we are looking at further. In terms of how to enter these segments, these are conversations which we are having as well.

items.statement: CPG recalibration focuses on jaggery, brown sugar, premium whites and newer sweet products
items.quote: We are focusing on those products only in sort of few channels. But in terms of the margin accretive products and value-added products, they will be more on the browns line, which is jaggery, couple of variants of brown sugar, premium whites. So, this is all in the realm of sweeteners. And newer product launches also in the realm of sweet products which are being planned for later in the year.

items.statement: Sugar recovery improved 0.5% in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka due to good weather
items.quote: We had a good upside on recovery. If your question is relevant to Tamil Nadu, we had about a 0.5% improvement in recovery and that, I think, is endemic across multiple sugar units in TN because we have had good weather, diurnal weather. Karnataka also had a good upside in recovery.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu planting constrained by competing crops like paddy; expects some recovery upside
items.quote: Tamil Nadu will be constrained because of attractiveness of the other crops. The government has been focusing on paddy per se, as you are aware. Having said that, we look at the portion of improving from where we are in terms of planting and also expect some upsides on recovery.

items.statement: Refinery closure addressed; TN and AP cane dwindling remains a drag on profitability
items.quote: The refinery was of course a constraining element. We have addressed it. There were some conversations around the TN operations and I would put AP into that as well where cane has been dwindling. This has been a drag.

items.statement: Focus on improving working capital management to stem losses in TN/AP operations
items.quote: So, we are running very tightly on cost and efficiency. So, over time, I think we will have to manage this piece better, bring costs down, improve our working capital management to stem the losses which are coming from this segment.

items.statement: No timeline given for dividend resumption; focus on strengthening business operations
items.quote: as I said, I think it's in our endeavor to strengthen the business operations of the company going forward. I can't really give you any timelines on this

items.statement: Valensa has stronger operating team in place after management restructuring
items.quote: We have also had some organisation and management restructuring. A stronger operating team is in place right now and they are driving this mandate forward.

items.statement: Nutra exports to US increased after tariff settled at 10%
items.quote: The increase is due to the more exports to the US, as the US tariff got settled at 10%.

items.statement: Sugar sales volume 97,000 MT including 6,000 MT exports in Q4 FY26
items.quote: As far as the sugar volumes are concerned, we sold about 97,000 MT, which includes about 6,000 MT of the exports, as against 73,000 MT of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Refinery loss widened to Rs 293 crore from Rs 99 crore in Q4 FY26
items.quote: for the current quarter, E.I.D.- Parry ( after accounting other costs, is about Rs. 293 crores, against the loss of Rs. 99 crores in the corresponding previous year quarter

items.statement: Sugar realization flat at Rs 39.28/kg vs Rs 39.22/kg YoY
items.quote: As far as the sugar realization is concerned, for the current quarter, it is Rs. 39.28, as against, Rs. 39.22 of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Distillery average realization declined to Rs 64.25/litre from Rs 66.98/litre YoY
items.quote: As far as the price realization is concerned, the average realization is at Rs. 64.25 for the current quarter, as against the Rs. 66.98 per litre, as compared to the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Co-gen power tariff improved to Rs 4.57/unit from Rs 4.38/unit YoY
items.quote: As far as the power tariff is concerned, we were able to realize Rs. 4.57 per unit for the current quarter, as against the Rs. 4.38 per unit in the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Global sugar surplus of 196.7 MMT production vs 193.8 MMT demand in 2025-26 pressuring prices
items.quote: This reflects improving global supplies with total production of 196.7 million tons (MMT), exceeding demand of 193.8MMT in 2025-26, led by higher output in India and Thailand, partially offsetting mixed trends in Brazil and the EU.

items.statement: Sugar exports banned till September 30, 2026
items.quote: Further exports have been banned till September 30, 2026.

items.statement: India sugar production net of ethanol diversion at 27 MMT as of March 31; Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 20%+
items.quote: Domestic sugar trends indicate a recovery in production led by key states, with an all-India output net of ethanol diversion reaching 27 MMT as of March 31, driven primarily by Maharashtra and Karnataka, which grew in excess of 20%, while Uttar Pradesh remained flat.

items.statement: PSRIPL SEZ exit formalities commenced; expected completion by September 30, 2026
items.quote: The unit is located in the SEZ. We have obtained an in-principal exit letter from the SEZ authorities on the 20th of April. Exit formalities have commenced and are expected to be completed by 30th September 2026.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue target ₹9,400-9,500 crore, ~24-25% growth
items.quote: Overall, in Lighting and Steel, the revenue will be around ₹7,200 crores from the Steel Division and around ₹2,200 crores from the Lighting Division. So, the overall revenue will be ₹9,400 crores to ₹9,500 crores this year.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated EBITDA target ₹680-700 crore, ~25-26% growth
items.quote: Similarly, in EBITDA, it will be around ₹480 crores in the Steel Division and around ₹200 crores in Lighting. So, this will be around ₹680 crores. In this also, there will be a growth of 25-26%.

items.statement: FY27 Steel volume target 11 lakh tons, ~21-22% growth over FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we are targeting overall volume of 11 lakh tons, representing growth of nearly 21% to 22% over FY26, supported by improving utilization levels, phased commissioning of new capacities and strong contribution from value-added products.

items.statement: FY27 Steel EBITDA target ₹470-480 crore, may cross ₹500 crore
items.quote: And where our EBITDA was ₹385 crores this year (FY26), we will do ₹470 crores to ₹480 crores this year (FY27), and it can even cross ₹500 crores.

items.statement: FY27 Lighting EBITDA target ~₹200 crore
items.quote: That's why we will do around 480 to 470 crore in the Steel Division and around ₹200 crores EBITDA in the Lighting Division.

items.statement: FY27 Wire & Cable revenue target ₹260 crore, on track for 3-year ₹500-600 crore goal
items.quote: Our FY27 revenue target for the Wire and Cable business is ₹260 crores, firmly on track with the three-year guidance of ₹500 crores to ₹600 crores business.

items.statement: Lighting & Consumer Durables medium-term value growth target 22-25% annually
items.quote: Overall, we are targeting value growth of 22% to 25% annually in Lighting and Consumer Durables segment overall -- over the medium term, supported by deeper distribution penetration, premiumization and continued investment in brand building.

items.statement: FY27 Steel export volume target >2.5 lakh tons, nearly double FY26
items.quote: Exports stood at 1.36 lakh tons for FY26, and we are targeting to cross 2.5 lakh tons in the coming year.

items.statement: Steel order book ~₹1,000 crore plus, led by exports, spiral, domestic API; strong H1 FY27 visibility
items.quote: The current order book of the Steel Division is about ₹1,000 crores plus, led by exports, spiral, and some domestic API orders, providing strong visibility for H1 FY27, which is expected to be the highest-ever half year for value-added product sales.

items.statement: Professional Lighting order book ₹160 crore at end Q4 FY26
items.quote: The Professional Lighting business achieved double-digit revenue growth at ₹473 crores for the full year, being a 26% share in the total revenue of the Lighting segment and ended Q4 FY26 with an order book of ₹160 crores, providing healthy near-term execution visibility.

items.statement: North America export order book ~₹1,000 crore including spiral, 65,000 tons booked, 10,000 tons/month from current month
items.quote: Already 65,000 tons of material is booked, and from this month, 10,000 tons per month is already added. So, you must have heard one thing in my commentary, last year where our exports were about 1.4 lakh tons, we will be exporting more than 2.5 lakh tons this year, almost double the growth in volume. And this North America order book we have is about ₹1,000 crores, including some spiral.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 7.9%, sequential improvement from better realization and mix
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹170 crores with margins of 7.9%, reflecting sequential improvement driven by better realization and improved product mix.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 Steel EBITDA ₹5,121/ton; FY26 full year ₹4,553/ton
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹126 crores with EBITDA per ton to ₹5,121 per ton. For the full year FY26 for the Steel business, the business reported revenue of ₹5,731 crores, reflecting stable year-on-year performance. Overall volume stood at 9.04 lakh tons, a growth of 3% year-on-year on volume terms. The capacity utilization of 78% to 80% was maintained throughout the year, even in a challeng

items.statement: FY27 Steel EBITDA/ton assumed ~₹4,700 due to oil & gas pressure, labor/fuel cost increases
items.quote: We are assuming there will be some pressure in oil and gas. The oil and gas segment is a very substantially high-margin business domestically. So, we are assuming there will be some pressure there. That's why we expect the EBITDA per ton to be around ₹4,700 for the whole year.

items.statement: Export EBITDA/ton expected ₹9,000-10,000, will lift overall Steel EBITDA/ton
items.quote: And in this, the entire segment that we are exporting, we will have an EBITDA of about ₹9,000 to ₹10,000 per ton. Because of this, your overall EBITDA per ton will also improve, and the quantity of value-added products will increase, leading to overall company growth.

items.statement: Capacity increased ~2 lakh tons in last 1.5 years; will reach 1.6 mt in FY27, 1.9 mt by FY28-29
items.quote: In the last one and a half years, our capacity has improved by about 2 lakh tons. And in the next one year, we will reach around 1.6 million from 1.4. And after that, our capacity will increase by about 3 lakh tons. So, in FY28 - FY29, our capacity will be around 1.9 million.

items.statement: FY26 capacity utilization 78-80% maintained despite challenges
items.quote: The capacity utilization of 78% to 80% was maintained throughout the year, even in a challenging operating environment.

items.statement: Domestic demand supported by Har Ghar Jal, city gas distribution but government spending low (₹3,000 crore disbursed vs ₹55,000 crore budget)
items.quote: In FY26 where the government budget for the Jal distribution program is there, Amrut, Har Ghar Jal program, Jal Jeevan Mission program is there and the government budget was about ₹55,000 crores, but the government distributed money was only ₹3,000 crores. Because of this, there was an impact throughout the year, particularly for companies like ours.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 net working capital cycle 58 days; FY26 full year 66 days
items.quote: In Q4 FY26, our net working capital cycle was 58 days with a return on capital employed, ROCE of 20.76% and a return on equity, ROE of 15.23%. And on a yearly basis, the net working capital cycle was 66 days with a return on capital emp loyed, ROCE of 15.93% and a return on equity of 11.21

items.statement: Zero-debt company with net cash surplus ₹337 crore as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: We remain a zero-debt company with a net cash surplus of ₹337 crores as of March 31, '26.

items.statement: Final dividend ₹2.50/share declared; total FY26 dividend ₹5.00/share (interim + final)
items.quote: We have declared a final dividend of ₹2.50 per share, demonstrating our ongoing commitment to delivering shareholder value. This is in addition to the interim dividend of ₹2.50 per share already distributed and disbursed. So, a total of ₹5.00 dividend for the full year of FY26.

items.statement: Buyback under consideration again after regulatory changes; will update soon
items.quote: No, we had thought about it earlier, but the government regulations were not favo urable. We have started considering it again; it has been reintroduced. So, we will come to you very soon

items.statement: New labor law impact ₹40-50 crore on company; fuel & power costs increased; Lighting imported raw material ~30-35%
items.quote: In this too, we have already considered some things because new labo ur law that has come, because of which there is an impact of ₹40 crores - ₹50 crores on every company. So, considering that, we are giving the numbers, otherwise, we could have done ₹750 crores as well

items.statement: Middle East crisis caused export stoppage (~12,000 tons) and raw material shortage; US market opened as offset
items.quote: Look, mainly whatever targets we had set, but as you all know, the Middle East crisis that occurred in late February caused our exports to immediately become almost nil. So on the export account, our supply decreased by about 12,000 tons of material that was ready. This was a major setback. Secondly, overall, as soon as this Middle East crisis happened, there was a raw material crisis in India, wh

items.statement: ONGC Seamless-to-ERW opportunity major impact only in FY28 (9-10 month capex); not in FY27 guidance
items.quote: This is a good opportunity, and regarding what you said about ONGC, basically compared to seamless, the welded pipe and in this, we have already supplied 5,000 tons. And to upgrade this, R&D is already going on for upgradeable 5CT. But its major impact will come in FY28. It's taking a little more time.

items.statement: Capital allocation: 1/3 profit to dividends, 1/3 to business growth/working capital, 1/3 to capex; maintained for 2-3 years
items.quote: We have also maintained that there should be quality business, it should be export-oriented, value-added and high margin. So, if you compare the EBITDA percentage with peers – despite being in the steel pipe business, it is very good. I often say our relationship with the bank has ended; now our relationship is only with the shareholders. So even now, we ensure that apart from the corporate action

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance: high-single digit to low-double digit for combined business; double-digit volume CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: For FY27, we expect to achieve a high-single digit to low-double digit volume growth for the combined business, which will be followed by a double-digit volume growth over the next couple of years. We expect a double digit volume CAGR over the next 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 16%-18% for combined business over next 24-36 months
items.quote: In terms of margins, we expect the consolidated EBITDA margins to reach 16%-18% for the combined business over the next 24 to 36 months.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA target below 1.0x by FY29
items.quote: As guided in the past as well, we expect the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to go below 1.0x by FY29.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of approximately INR 25 crore each in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: So capex, I think, will be maintenance capex for both the years. I do not think capex will be large. Approximately, we can take INR 25 crore in each of the years.

items.statement: Net debt expected around INR 1,700 crore by end of March 2027 with upside bias
items.quote: By the end of March-27, you are looking at a net debt of approximately INR 1,700 crore or thereabouts. So you will see a reduction in the net debt with an upside bias to some extent.

items.statement: UK FTA custom duty reduction benefit estimated at 60-100 bps on combined business margins
items.quote: On the combined business basis, the margin benefit will be to the tune of 60-100 bps.

items.statement: Telangana price increase expected to have reasonable margin impact but timeline unknown
items.quote: Telangana is one of the potential states where we are expecting a price increase, but obviously, timelines are not known on that front. But given how large Telangana is for us as a state, it will have a reasonable impact on margins.

items.statement: Prag distillery capacity expanded from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum; government nod received; INR 59 crore invested; expected INR 10 crore annual bottling cost savings
items.quote: On the supply front, we have received the government nod for starting operations at our expanded capacity at Prag in Andhra Pradesh, one of the largest states for Tilaknagar Industries. The capacity has now increased from 6 lakh cases per annum to 36 lakh cases per annum. This expansion is a testament to Tilaknagar's push towards safeguarding supplies and demonstrating execution capabilities towar

items.statement: 75% of Imperial Blue business exited TSMA by Q4 FY26; remaining 3 states to transition by March 2027
items.quote: In the Q3 earnings call, we had mentioned that TI will exit the TSMA for significant operations by the end of Q4 FY26, and we have delivered on that. 75% of the IB business has exited TSMA till Q4 FY26. For the states where we have exited TSMA in Q4 FY26, we have already started full-fledged operations at TI units. Now only 3 states remain under TSMA, and we expect to transition them over the cour

items.statement: Karnataka policy change reduced MRP by INR 20 per nip for Imperial Blue and Mansion House; similar past reduction led to high-teens growth in state
items.quote: So as I had mentioned in my opening remarks, we expect an MRP reduction of approximately INR 20 on both the flagship brands, Imperial Blue and Mansion House, on the 180 ml pack size. So with the reduction in the MRP, we may expect a further uptake in the volumes going forward. items.statement: Working capital cycle expected at 53-55 days of gross revenue on ongoing basis
items.quote: Yes. So I think on an ongoing basis, Mehul, we can look at the working capital cycle in the range of 53 to 55 days of gross revenue. So that is the way I would look at it.

items.statement: Workforce increased from ~350 to 850 employees as of March 2026 for post-acquisition readiness
items.quote: During the last few months, we have onboarded several senior leaders as well as built a pan-India team to manage operations. We now have a fully built team to deliver continued success, having increased our workforce from around 350 employees to 850 employees as of March.

items.statement: Deferred consideration of EUR 28 million payable to Pernod Ricard after 4 years of acquisition; no other costs expected
items.quote: So Heer, there, as we mentioned in the earlier presentations as well, after 4 years of the acquisition, there will be a deferred consideration. There is a deferred consideration of EUR 28 million that we need to pay to Pernod Ricard. But apart from that, there are no other costs that are to be incurred.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 1 per share for FY25-26
items.quote: Lastly, the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR 1 per share for FY25-'26 to the members at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Input cost pressure expected from geopolitical scenario; cost optimizations identified to mitigate raw material price increases
items.quote: On the margin front, because of the current ongoing geopolitical scenario, we do expect some pressure on the input costs and margins. To combat this, we have identified and are working on several areas of cost optimizations, which will mitigate the impact of this increase in raw material prices.

items.statement: Focus on premiumization via dual engine: existing portfolio strength and robust NPD pipeline; Spaceman Spirits Lab partnership for luxury launches
items.quote: Our strategy to lead the premiumization trend is anchored by a dual engine, the strength of our existing portfolio and a robust NPD pipeline. This is further accelerated by our partnership with Spaceman Spirits Lab, which positions us to capture the market through targeted luxury launches.

items.statement: Brandy expansion into North and West markets planned for FY27 including mass, mid-prestige and luxury Monarch portfolio
items.quote: As it stands, we have not launched brandy in the northern markets. But having said so, we are in the process of doing that in FY27. This is true not only for the mass and the semi-prestige or mass and the mid-prestige portfolio, but even for our luxury portfolio in the form of Monarch.

items.statement: FY26 overall volumes up 68% to ~20 million cases (4 months IB); ex-IB volumes up 14% to 13.6 million cases; Mansion House Brandy crossed 10 million cases
items.quote: In FY26, our overall volumes increased by 68%. Ex-IB, our volumes increased by 14% to reach 13.6 million cases in sales. During Q4, our overall volumes increased by 135% on a year-on-year basis, crossing 8 million cases, of which IB was 4.6 million cases. Ex-Maharashtra, IB recorded a growth of around 9% versus Q4 FY25. With this impressive performance, TI continues to be largest P&A IMFL player i

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NSR INR 1,177 per case (+5.4% YoY); ex-IB NSR +2.6% YoY; FY26 NSR INR 1,165 per case
items.quote: The overall NSR increased by 5.4% to INR 1,177 per case for Q4 FY26 from INR 1,116 per case in Q4 FY25. On an ex-IB basis, the NSR increased by 2.6% in Q4 FY26. For the year ended 31st March, the NSR stood at INR 1,165 per case.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 net revenue INR 949 crore (+148% YoY); adjusted for subsidy INR 941 crore (+154%); EBITDA INR 155 crore (+97% YoY, 16.3% margin); adjusted EBITDA INR 146 crore (+124%, 15.5% margin)
items.quote: We witnessed a strong growth of 148% year-on-year basis to reach a net revenue of INR 949 crore during the quarter. Adjusted for subsidy, we recorded a growth of 154% to reach INR 941 crore. EBITDA stood at INR 155 crore for Q4 FY26, clocking a growth of 97% year-on-year and margin of 16.3%. Adjusted for subsidy, the EBITDA grew by 124% to reach INR 146 crore and a 15.5% margin on the combined bus

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR 2,346 crore (+70% YoY); adjusted INR 2,279 crore (+69%); EBITDA INR 419 crore (+64%); adjusted EBITDA INR 352 crore (+56%)
items.quote: For the year ending March-26, our revenues grew by 70% versus FY25 to reach INR 2,346 crore. Adjusted for subsidy, we clocked a growth of 69% to reach INR 2,279 crore. In the same period, EBITDA grew by 64% to reach INR 419 crore. Adjusted for subsidy, the EBITDA was INR 352 crore, a 56% increase versus FY25.

items.quote: We have seen some of that in Q4 because that was more the tariff overhang and some of the things that was had to share with customers and things of that nature.

items.statement: Dividend for FY26 at INR0.25 per equity share with face value INR5

items.statement: Expects similar EBITDA margins and company PSF in FY27

items.statement: Per store capex rising to Rs 2.7-2.8 cr including inventory; capex portion Rs 1.2-1.3 cr
items.quote: It's about Rs. 2.6 crores and it will increase because of the price increas e. So, it will become around Rs. 2.7 crores-Rs. 2.8 crores now. That includes CAPEX and inventory. So, the CAPEX would be about Rs. 1.2 crores-Rs. 1.3 crores and the rest would be paid inventory.

items.statement: Added 136 stores in FY26; total store count 325 with 3.5 mn sq ft
items.quote: We opened 33 new stores and closed 2 during the quarter and achieved a net addition of 136 st ores in the whole financial year, taking our total store count to 325 stores with approximately 3.5 million square feet of retail space.

items.statement: Plans 50-60% new area addition annually; targets 2,500 stores long-term
items.quote: I think we don't want to dilute our focus till we have at least 2 ,500 V2 stores.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS gross margin guided at 28-30% going forward
items.quote: So, going forward you can look for us to maintain this gross margin anywhere between 28 %-30%.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin guided to remain similar in near term due to high new store additions
items.quote: Because we are again guiding for opening more than 50% new area. So, it becomes a challenge to increase the company level PSF and expand EBITDA margin along with a 50% growth.

items.statement: Will pass on 3-4% yarn price increases to customers to maintain gross margins
items.quote: Yes, so we have seen some movement in yarn prices and that would have to be transferred to the customer. So, we will maintain our gross margins and prices might go up in the future by 3%-4%.

items.statement: Product mix shift drove ASP up 4-5%; men's 41-42%, women's 27%, kids 25%
items.quote: So, it's all because of product mix, the price ASP increase within the category is only inflationary. I think that would be around 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Targets inventory at 90-100 days and creditors at 45 days
items.quote: We are looking to maintain inventory at 90-100 days and creditors at 45 days.

items.statement: Old inventory >1 year <5%, >6 months <24%; 76% inventory <6 months old
items.quote: So, more than 1-year-old inventory is less than 5% and more than 6 months old inventory is less than 24%.

items.statement: FY27 expansion funded by internal accruals and cash; debt preferred over equity if needed
items.quote: Yes. For at least this financial year, we are covered with internal accruals and the cash on the balance sheet.

items.statement: 8 crore customer database; engages via WhatsApp, RCS, SMS with gift vouchers; no formal loyalty program
items.quote: We don't have a loyalty program per se, but we have a database of about 8 crore customers and we do reach them through WhatsApp, RCS, and SMS. We give them gift vouchers and other kinds of gifts, not loyalty points.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 SSSG 7.74%; FY26 SSSG ~8.6%; full price sales 89% in Q4, 90% in FY26
items.quote: The SSSG for Quarter 4 stood at 7.74%. There was a robust volume growth of 53% in the quarter. The full price sales contributed 89% in the 4th Quarter.

items.statement: Old stores PSF Rs 1,124; new stores PSF Rs 750; new stores start at 70% of mature PSF
items.quote: So, our old stores were at Rs. 1,124 per square feet for the whole year. And new stores were at Rs. 750 per square feet.

items.statement: New stores EBITDA positive from month 1 (breakeven ~Rs 500 PSF); mature in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, it is EBITDA positive from the first month itself, because the breakeven point is around Rs. 500 per square feet of sale. And they start at about 700 to 750. But to mature and reach old stores level, it takes about three to four years.

items.statement: New Labor Code impact not material; already recognized in results
items.quote: The impact of new Labor Code is not material and has already been recognized in our financial results.

items.statement: Geopolitical tension led to safety stock build-up in March; will normalize
items.quote: Lastly, due to geopolitical tension, we have increased our safety stock in the month of March for seamless availability of stock which has resulted into higher inventory levels in the month of March.

items.statement: Depreciation up Rs 6-7 cr one-time due to policy change expensing small items
items.quote: Yes, it is a one-time counting change. So, a lot of small items like nuts, hard tags, hangers, what we used to capitalize earlier, now we depreciated them because we want to expense it off.

items.statement: Seasonal inventory 15% carried forward; reprocessed and sold next season, not disposed
items.quote: So, about 15% of every season inventory is left with us, we sell it the next season, we don't dispose of any inventory.

items.statement: At least 6 senior leaders can represent company; most with 10+ years tenure; data-driven culture
items.quote: So, there would be at least six people who would be able to take the call if I am not available. And most of them have been with us for a journey of more than I think 10 years now.

items.statement: No international expansion planned; India market sufficient for 2,500 stores
items.quote: I think, sir, India is big enough for us to feed us for the next five years at least because we want to have 2,500 stores. So, we are not looking at any other geographies.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 15-18%; Q4 FY26 at 20.1%
items.quote: Margin will be around the same. There was a service mix. Because of that, margin has improved. And the EBITDA margin anywhere, it will be between the 15% to 18% always.

items.statement: Wind business EBITDA margin currently ~8%; expected to improve with localization over 1-2 years
items.quote: This current EBITDA margin is around 8%. And we'll be having a better margin, I mean, always in this wind business compared to the, our competitor. And there is various products under localization. So we see the same rate of EBITDA for the future also.

items.statement: Wind capacity targeting 2 GW by end of FY28; localization in progress
items.quote: Currently, we are still in the process of localization of many products. So it is still -- I would say, we will reach about 2 gigawatts by next year-end by capacity-wise.

items.statement: Diesel cost escalation 40-60% pass-through via contract clauses
items.quote: All our contract has the escalation clause, but not completely, it will be recoverable. There will be 40% to 60%, depending on the contract to contract, it is recoverable. It is a pass-through.

items.statement: Mobility demerger on track; NCLT hearing expected first week of June; completion in 60-75 days
items.quote: Currently, the courts are on holidays. It is a summer vacation in the court. And as of now, we should get the hearing on the first week of June. if we put a time line, another 60 to 75 days, this should get completed.

items.statement: Ash & Coal Handling adjusted revenue grew 28% in FY26 excluding trading businesses
items.quote: It is 28% to be precise.

items.statement: Thermal power capacity addition of 50 GW in 4-5 years supports structural ash handling demand growth
items.quote: Thermal power plant, as per the Government of India, there is new 50 gigawatt of the project is getting added in next 4 to 5 years' time. So thermal power requirement is going up. Power requirement per se is going up in India because of demand from every sector. And this, ash business will keep growing year-on-year.

items.statement: Building leadership depth; Anil Jain notes creating more leaders in the office
items.quote: It's not that being relaxed. It's just that we are trying to create more leaders in the office and try to give a chance to others to take up the questions.

items.statement: Management projects 43-44% AUM growth for FY27 as communicated to lenders
items.quote: So basically, for all the lenders, we have projected about 43% to 44% AUM jump for this year.

items.statement: Targets nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027 including guarantee-backed loans
items.quote: We remain firmly on track towards our medium-term objective of becoming a predominantly secured MSME lender, targeting nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027, including loans backed by guarantee program.

items.statement: Expects credit cost to go below 2% in FY27 from 3.32% in FY26
items.quote: I think, last 2 years have been on a high credit cost side. This year, we seriously expect that this number should go down below 2%.

items.statement: Plans to raise equity in second half of FY27
items.quote: So definitely, on our side, we will target to raise some equity in the second half of the year.

items.statement: AUM stood at INR893 crores as of March 2026 with 6% growth, decline due to ARC transaction
items.quote: AUM stood at INR893 crores as of March 2026. It's 6% growth, but the decline on AUM versus last year was due to ARC transaction.

items.statement: Secured loans now constitute around 68% of AUM including 5% unsecured loans backed by first loss guarantee
items.quote: Secured loans now constitute around 68% of our AUM, including 5% unsecured loans, backed by first loss fees guarantee compared to a significant lower share a few years ago.

items.statement: Secured disbursements increased to 67% in FY26 from 49% in FY25
items.quote: Secured disbursements increased to 67% compared to 49% last year, reflecting our continued focus on improving credit quality and long-term portfolio stability.

items.statement: Renewable energy loans expected to be around 10% of AUM by March 2027
items.quote: During the year, we also launched renewable energy loans, which would be a very significant part, I mean, maybe around 10% of the AUM by March '27.

items.statement: Renewable energy loan disbursement was INR50 lakhs in April, 10x in May, could reach INR5 crores in May
items.quote: Just to throw a light, in April, we started renewable energy loans and the expansion was around INR50 lakhs, which is 10x in May, and the number could reach about INR5 crores in May.

items.statement: Overall collection efficiency moved to around 93.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: As a result of these efforts, collection efficiency remained strong during the quarter with overall collection efficiency moving to around 93.5%.

items.statement: Current bucket efficiency improved to over 99.4% in March from around 99% in January
items.quote: Current bucket or X bucket efficiency improved to over 99.4% in March from around 99% in January.

items.statement: Resolution rates in bucket 1 (30-60) and bucket 2 (60-90) improved to over 70% and 75% respectively, highest since inception
items.quote: while resolution rates in bucket 1, which is 30 to 60 bucket, and bucket 2, which is Pre-NPA 60 to 90 bucket, improved to over 70% and 75%, respectively, the highest level achieved by the company since inception.

items.statement: Gross NPA and net NPA stood at 3.59% and 1.75% respectively in FY26 vs 6.61% and 3.42% in FY25
items.quote: Gross NPA and net NPA stood at 3.59% and 1.75%, respectively, compared to 6.61% and 3.42% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Credit cost for FY26 stood at 3.32% compared to 3.43% in FY25
items.quote: Credit cost for FY '26 stood at 3.32% compared to 3.43% in FY '25, with improving collection trends and stronger recoveries expected to support gradual normalization going forward.

items.statement: Net interest margin for FY26 stood at 13.9%, opex at 12.8%
items.quote: Net interest margin for FY '26 stood at 13.9%, while opex reported at 12.8%.

items.statement: Solar loan yield around 22.5%, overall yield 24% including fees
items.quote: Yield is around 22.5%. It will be around 24-ish if you include all fees and everything, yes.

items.statement: Solar loan ATS about INR4 lakhs, tenure 4 years, interest rate around 22%
items.quote: ATS is about 4 lakhs, 4 years is the tenure. And as we said that interest rate is around 22%, and overall yield becomes 23%, 24%.

items.statement: Opened 2 new branches in Bangalore peripheries and 1 in Jaipur, merging some rural branches
items.quote: Let's say, for example, we opened up 2 new branches in Bangalore -- peripheries of Bangalore because we feel there is a large business opportunity to capture there. We opened a branch in Jaipur, but kind of slowed down businesses in some of the branches which are more rural and kind of merged those with some of the existing branches in the vicinity.

items.statement: Many branches in early vintage (first 24 months), productivity improving as they mature
items.quote: Many of our branches are still in early vintage state, particularly within the first 24 months of operation. As these branches mature, productivity continues to improve steadily.

items.statement: Decentralized credit underwriting model deployed to reduce turnaround time and enhance efficiency
items.quote: the deployment of a decentralized credit underwriting model is helping reduce turnaround time and enhance operating efficiency.

items.statement: Launched renewable energy loans for MSME solarization (atta chakki, oil expellers, jaggery units, telecom towers)
items.quote: we have introduced one product, which is solar, where there is a lot of focus by the government, by foundations. So it's a replacement of diesel engines, so in solar atta chakki, oil expellers, jaggery units, telecom towers.

items.statement: Average ticket size in secured now INR6 lakhs, run rate INR8-9 lakhs
items.quote: you will notice that average ticket size in secured is now INR6 lakhs. And on a run rate basis, we are doing more of INR8 lakh, INR9 lakh kind of ticket size.

items.statement: Discontinued below INR5 lakh ticket size in secured for most branches in April
items.quote: And then in April, we discontinued below INR5 lakh ticket size in secured for most of the branches.

items.statement: Government working capital loan guarantee programs providing support
items.quote: you would have seen the news that government is trying to help with working capital loans and all through their guarantee program. So, I think government also will intend to protect things.

items.statement: Strong support from lending partners, relationships deepening with banks, NBFCs, capital market participants and development institutions
items.quote: On the liability side, we continue to see strong support from our lending partners. Our relationships with banks, NBFCs, capital market participants and development-focused institutions continue to deepen.

items.statement: Planning co-lending partnerships in secured space for FY27
items.quote: Right now, for the current plan, our net worth is adequate. We will look for some co-lending partners in the secured space. That's one.

items.statement: Employee cost high at 37-38% of AUM due to low AUM base, will decline as AUM grows
items.quote: Our cost is high. So one of the biggest reasons is that our AUM is low. So people who have joined us as a state head, I can tell you my state heads who are managing about INR100 crores here have been managing almost INR2,000 crores from where they have come in.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 29.48% providing sufficient headroom for growth
items.quote: Our capital position remains comfortable with a capital adequacy ratio of 29.48%, providing sufficient headroom to support future growth.

items.statement: Rural cash flows vulnerable to fertilizer supply issues and rainfall shortfall impacting agriculture productivity
items.quote: If fertilizers supply get impacted or rainfall is short, next year, you can have not so great agriculture productivity, which could then have some impact.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain EBITDA margin band of 12-14% despite input cost volatility
items.quote: We still hope to maintain our 12% to 14% band in terms of margin.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 2-3x industry growth (3-4%) maintained for FY27
items.quote: We continue to look at the market growing at about 3%, to 4%. And most of our segment strategies are focused on really doing that 2 -3x.

items.statement: Distribution growth target of 10-15% in urban and rural areas for FY27
items.quote: Distribution growth, we focus on 10-15% growth in both urban and rural areas.

items.statement: Chennai plant expansion on track for Q3 FY27, Silvassa for Q4 FY27
items.quote: We earlier guided that the Chennai additional capacity should come into stream by Q3 and Silvassa by Q4. As of today, we believe that we are in a position to meet these timelines.

items.statement: Tirex investing in new plant expected to be operational by Q3 FY27
items.quote: That plant will also be up and running in Q3 of this year. That is where Tirex company has started investing in the new plant.

items.statement: Record quarterly lubricant volume of 45,000 KL achieved in Q4 FY26
items.quote: For the quarter, we delivered for the first time 45,000 KL volume, which is the highest ever for any quarter ever in the history of the company

items.statement: Broad-based double-digit growth across all key segments including PCMO, CV, Agriculture, OEM workshops, B2B industrial
items.quote: Passenger Car Motor Oils and Commercial Vehicles delivered double -digit growth. Agricul ture segment also had a very strong robust double-digit growth

items.statement: EBITDA grew 8.5% to record INR 135 crores in Q4 FY26 despite rupee depreciation and Middle East crisis
items.quote: EBITDA also despite all the headwinds in terms of rupee depreciation and the Middle East crisis is starting March, we have been able to deliver EBITDA growth of 8.5% and INR 135 crores EBITDA for the quarter is again the highest ever EBITDA

items.statement: Multiple price increases taken and planned to pass on sharp base oil, additive, packaging cost increases linked to crude rally from $65-70 to $120
items.quote: There has been a fast escalation in the input cost of both all three base oil additives and packaging materials. That has necessitated frequent price increases, we would multiple price increases to pass on the cost to customers and consumers.

items.statement: Base oil supply currently adequate with 80-90% allocation from refiners; risk if crisis prolongs
items.quote: But as of now, we have been getting our mat erial with some allocation happening from some refiners at 80 -90%. But overall, we have been able to get our required material so far

items.statement: Base oil inventory increased to 45-60 days from normal 45 days for supply security
items.quote: We have tried to slightly increase that by 10-15 days, to create more supply security. But overall, we are still around, let's say, 45-60 days

items.statement: Tirex crossed INR 100 crores revenue in FY26 with 35-40% share of new DC bus chargers
items.quote: Tirex, has been gaining momentum and has crossed the landmark of INR 100 crores in the year.

items.statement: Tirex secured AC charger orders from MG Motors and VinFast
items.quote: We've also been able to get business with MG Motors and VinFast for AC chargers.

items.statement: Two data centre cooling products (PAO synthetic and mineral-based) developed, compatibility testing done, field testing next
items.quote: have informed you that we now have 2 products in our portfolio, which have been developed. items.statement: OEM partnerships expanded to 50+ OEMs across automotive, industrial, construction with double-digit growth
items.quote: We have mentioned more than 50+ OEMs. So I think for us, the strategy has been to focus our teams into each segment separately.

items.statement: Board recommended highest ever dividend of INR 51/share for FY26 (INR 21 interim + INR 30 final), 72% payout
items.quote: the Board has also recommended yesterday, highest ever dividend of INR 51 for the full year, which means a final dividend of INR 30, which follows the INR 21 interim dividend declared earlier in February and paid.

items.statement: Crude volatility ($65-70 to $120) compressing base oil lag from 2 months to 1-2 weeks, pressuring margins
items.quote: Earlier, we used to say the time lag was 2 months , now in these type of extraordinary situations, the time lag has, in fact, come down, sometimes to 1 week or 2 weeks.

items.statement: Supply chain risk if Middle East crisis prolongs; currently managing with inventory buffers and multiple sourcing
items.quote: But if the situation or the crisis continues significantly longer, then obviously, the entire supply chain for these refiners also may get slightly squeezed.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue crossed INR 4,000 crores for first time in FY26
items.quote: consolidated revenues crossed INR 4,000 crores, and EBITDA for the year also is the highest ever at INR 510 crores on a stand -alone basis and nearly INR 514 crores on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: GST implementation helped vehicle sales growth across 2-wheelers, cars, CVs, tractors
items.quote: The growth figures, as you all know, 2 -wheelers, cars, even EV penetration going up, commercial vehicles, tractors have been really good. Most of them see double-digit growth. And really, the GST also helped there

items.statement: Rupee depreciation and currency volatility keeping input costs elevated
items.quote: We remain watchful of the evolving macro environment, particularly the volatility now that we are seeing in the currency movements, which are obviously keeping the input cost pressures elevated

items.statement: Evaluating M&A opportunities while maintaining high dividend payout
items.quote: While we keep looking at the M&A opportunities, expanding our current business, we have increased the payout in the interim because we carry good cash on the balance sheet.
