items.quote: we are currently having an ongoing project with a combined GDV potential ofapproximately 290,000 square feet and estimated GDV of INR280 crores, with the next set of launches adding over INR600 crores GDV' by September this year.

items.quote: the project pipeline of what we are saying of INR2,100 crores GDV' that we are talking about this year, we are looking to at least double it over the next two years. And those kinds of projects are already in pipeline.

items.quote: Pre-sales, I can tell you in percentages. Every time we launch, we manage to get betweena 20% to 30% of the total inventory in pre-sales and that is what our model works on. items.statement: FY27 revenue contributors: Thane (Wagle Estate commercial), Pranam (Versova), Joshville (Santa Cruz), and Q1/Q2 launches; FY26 driven by Rivaan and Riviera
items.quote: In the coming year, we see Thane, we see Pranam which is the one in Versova, we see Joshville which is in Santa Cruz, and a couple of other launches which are going to happen in the first and the second quarter of this year to be the major contributors to the overall collections of Meghna.

items.statement: Total construction area of current and upcoming projects launching till December >1 million sq ft; similar increase expected over next two years; land holding metric not relevant for redevelopment model
items.quote: Having said that, a total construction area of the current projects and the upcoming projects which will get launched till December, will be more than a million square feet and a similar increase will happen over the next two years. So giving you a land holding as an answer for a redevelopment specialist doesn't make sense for us.

items.statement: Mumbai residential demand remains constant overall; absorption dips in micro-markets with larger supply; careful micro-market selection and pricing strategy to manage demand-supply dynamics
items.quote: So to be very honest, there is not a dip in demand. Demand actually is impacted of by supply more than anything else. The demand in Bombay remains constant overall. Micro-markets where there will be larger supplies coming in may see a dip in absorption more than a dip in demand. And that's why we are very careful in choosing the micro-markets we get into and the pricing also has an impact on it.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue expected to grow ~75% over FY26 with EBITDA margin 20-20%
items.quote: In terms of the guidance for FY26-27, we expect our consolidated revenue to grow by around 75% over FY26 with EBITDA margin to be 20% to 20%.

items.statement: Inox Green FY27 EBITDA guided upwards of INR600 crores
items.quote: With all our investments formally folding into Inox Green's ba lance sheet, along with organic growth, we maintain our FY27 EBITDA guidance to be upwards of INR600 crores

items.statement: Consolidated order book at 3.1 GW with 600 MW added in FY26; execution visibility >24 months
items.quote: Coming to the order book, we continue to have a large and very well-diversified order book of 3.1 GW, I repeat again, 3.1 GW, having added almost 600 MW in this financial year.

items.statement: Inox Clean Energy targets 14 GW capacity by FY29 adding ~3 GW+ annually, 20-30% wind
items.quote: Our Group Company, Inox Clean Energy, has large capacity addition plan with a targeted capacity addition of 14 GW by FY'29. It plans to add almost 3 GW plus capacity annually over the next few years. Out of this, about 20% to 30% is expected to be wind.

items.statement: Order book shifting from 100% turnkey to 75-80% equipment supply over 24 months; currently 50:50
items.quote: And over the past 24 months, we've completely turned this to now 75% to 80% being equipment supply. And mind you, these are very, very capable strong parties.

items.statement: Working capital cycle challenged by ECS supply delays and PSU payment delays; expect sharp improvement from equipment supply pivot and group orders
items.quote: In terms of the working capital cycle, there are various macro level issues which have happened, including our supply chain disruption, which has happened due to the ECS, which is one of the major components needs to come from -- needs to come, which has been got stuck, which has been -- the supplies has been delayed.

items.statement: Backward integrating into power electronics (transformers, inverters, ECS systems) in a major way; cranes and transformer manufacturing already in-house
items.quote: Over the course o f this year, we will elucidate further plans because we're looking at expanding into power electronics in a major way given the massive requirement of transformers, large transformers, small transformers, solar transformers, inverters, power electronics, E CS systems across the entire ecosystem

items.statement: Inox Green portfolio at 13+ GWp (10.5 GW wind, balance solar); acquiring 6.5 GW operational wind O&M assets of 2 companies
items.quote: Inox Green portfolio stands at 13 + GWp comprising of approximately 10.5 GW of wind assets and the balance being solar assets. This also includes the investment made to acquire 6.5 gigawatts of operational wind O&M assets of 2 companies.

items.statement: NCLT approved demerger of Inox Green evacuation infrastructure into Inox Renewable Solutions; ~INR1,000 crores gross block and INR50-55 crores annual depreciation removed from Inox Green
items.value: INR1,000 crores gross block; INR50-55 crores depreciation
items.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been eliminated from Inox Green's balance sheet. And subsequently, the annual depreciation of approximately INR50 crores to INR55 crores has been eliminated, thereby increasing the profitability.

items.statement: Inox Green machine availability averaged ~96.5% for entire portfolio
items.quote: Machine availability for the entire portfolio averaged approximately 96.5%.

items.statement: 2/3 of annual execution for next 4-5 years from Inox Clean and CESC; 1/3 from other marquee customers
items.quote: We are pivoting Inox Wind to a new avatar that would address the challenges as well as put us on a path for a major transformation that 2/3 of the annual execution for the next 4 to 5 years will be from Inox Clean and CESC, and the remaining 1/3 from other marquee customers.

items.statement: Equipment supply on LC terms provides upfront cash flow and passes steel price risk; turnkey margins erode with land/ROW cost escalations and payment delays
items.quote: equipment supply is a very f irm kind of those things. You have today a lot of control with the steel prices being passed on many of those things. And at the same time, these are very simple on LC terms mostly so that you get the cash flow up

items.statement: Inox Green has tax shield up to INR700 crores losses; no finance cost expected next year
items.quote: Out of INR600 crore fees, broadly everything will be converted into the operating cash flow. As such, there will be no depreciation, no finance cost, and we have a tax shield up to INR700 crore of losses.

items.statement: Inox Clean raised ~$750 million at couple of billion dollars valuation
items.quote: I think the value creation we are doing at Inox Clean, where we've raised close to $750 million at a couple o f billion dollars of valuation

items.statement: Vayuveer program generating ~600 highly skilled professionals annually; actively hiring Agniveer talent
items.quote: As part of the people strategy, our Vayuveer program at Inox Learning Academy, currently, we are generating almost highly skilled team of professionals of 600 annually to fuel our growth. We are also actively looking to hire Agniveer who are highly talented with strong passion to contribute to this.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions caused logistics issues, ECS supply delays, commodity cost increases, PSU payment delays impacting Q4 execution
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical issues have led to certain on-ground challenges and logistics issues in project execution. However, we continue to deliver strong margins supported by various initiatives which we have been undertaking in the past quarters.

items.statement: Government push for domestic manufacturing and reduced import dependencies benefits integrated players like INOXGFL
items.quote: As you are aware, there is a strong push from the government to increase domestic manufacturing and reduce import dependencies. Inox Wind and INOXGFL is extremely well placed to benefit from and contribute towards achieving these goals.

items.statement: Expect strong annual wind capacity addition of 8-10 GW over next few years driven by RTC, FDRE, hybrid additions
items.quote: Going forward, we expect to see strong annual wind capacity addition of 8 to 10 GW over the next few years driven by RTC, FDRE and hybrid capacity additions, as we see renewable power generation move structurally from being a source of infirm power to firm power.

items.statement: Inox Green FY26 EBITDA margin ~50% on INR426 crores turnover; acquisitions contribute ~50% EBITDA margin
items.quote: As far as the EBITDA margin is concerned, we are always 50%-odd which we have guided. It is about quarter-on-quarter, you are comparing quarter-on-quarter basis. Quarter-on-quarter basis, it can be low, a little bit high. But on an annualized basis, if you see out of INR426 crores of turnover which we have achieved, we have achieved INR210 crores of EBITDA margin, which is around 50%-odd.

items.statement: Inox Green dividend policy to be decided by Board after consolidation of two acquisitions
items.quote: Let the consolidation of the two companies happen. Once that happens, I'm sure the Board in all its wisdom will put in place a dividend policy.

items.statement: Inox Wind FY26 revenue INR4,500 crores (vs INR5,000 crores guidance); INR400 crores shortfall to recover in Q1-Q2 FY27
items.quote: as again st the guideline of INR5,000 crores, which we have given in the last call, we have achieved INR4,600 crores and this INR400 crores of makeover will happen in the qu arter 1, quarter 2 time scale

items.statement: New 4.4 MW turbine launch on track for commercial launch within calendar year 2026
items.quote: The launch of our new 4.4-MW turbine is on-track, and we expect to receive all approvals and subsequently commercial launch -- launching the product within this calendar year.

items.statement: Inox Clean fastest in India to achieve ~2 GW installed capacity and 6 GW solar module + 3 GW cell manufacturing capacity
items.value: 2 GW installed; 6 GW module; 3 GW cell
items.quote: Our latest venture, Inox Clean, which houses both our solar manufacturing and renewable IPP businesses is shaping up well and is the fastest in India to achieve about 2 GW of installed capacity and also the fastest to reach 6 GW of solar module along with 3 GW of cell manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Inox Green O&M revenue mix currently ~10% of consolidated; expected to move to 18-20% with acquisitions
items.quote: I think the revenue mix right now broadly is about 10% was O&M, 90% was Inox Wind. I think going forward, as the entire consolidated might of t he 2 acquisitions comes through, I think O&M will possibly be moving towards about 20%, 18% to 20

items.statement: Inox Green acquired 2 of top 4 wind OEMs that went bankrupt; sector largely consolidated with limited further acquisition opportunities
items.quote: Even in Inox Green, we went on to acquire 2 of the top 4 w ind OEMs, which went bankrupt in India. So, I think let's get to that scale, and then we'll see how to deploy that capital

items.statement: Receivables cycle to improve significantly with pivot to equipment supply orders and increased group company order proportion
items.quote: However, we expect the receivables cycle to see significant improvement going forward, given our s trategic pivot towards equipment supply orders going forward, as well as from an increase in the proportion of orders from group companies in the overall order book

items.statement: Inox Wind not providing MW-specific guidance; driven by revenue due to varied contract types
items.quote: As we have communicated on the last call, we are not giving any megawatt-specific guidances. We are driven by the revenue, keeping in view the contract which we are entering into, different kinds of contracts we are entering into.

items.statement: Pharmacies in hospitals and clinics are part of listed entity P&L; no plan for standalone retail pharmacy vertical like Apollo Pharmacy.
items.quote: All the pharmacies of all the hospitals and all the clinics are part of the P&L of the NHL listed entity.

items.statement: Samyat Healthcare is a 100% subsidiary of the listed entity; all related party companies are owned by the listed company.
items.quote: This is a subsidiary of the listed entity. All the related party companies that you see are owned by the listed company.

items.statement: Bangalore cluster ARPP north of INR 250,000 driven by high-complexity quaternary care: ~100 robotic cardiac surgeries/month, ~160 percutaneous aortic valve replacements, highest paediatric bone marrow transplants.
items.quote: We do almost 100 cases per month. Many competing hospitals do probably that in 1 to 2 months. I mean, 1 to 2 in a year, we do it in a month. That's the scale at which we operate.

items.statement: Kolkata campus limited to ~3.5 acres at RN Tagore Hospital; Rajarhat project will bring integrated quaternary care facility. Kolkata has ~30% of Bangalore's infrastructure scale (10 vs 45 bone marrow transplant beds).
items.quote: Kolkata, we have limited in scale because we can't expand within that small campus of around 3.5 acres in RN Tagore Hospital. So that's where when we come up with the Rajarhat project, we will have many integrated quaternary care facility all in one place.

items.statement: Clinics & insurance losses flat at ~INR 66 cr in FY26; similar run-rate cash burn expected in FY27 due to new clinic additions and corporate overheads for integrated care infrastructure.
items.quote: So you have to assume that a similar run rate of cash burn will continue on the clinics going into next year as well because we still have a significant ambition in terms of growth of clinics in our core geographies.

items.statement: India hospital margins have room for further expansion from transformation initiatives, but new center losses from mid-to-late FY27 will temper percentage margin growth.
items.quote: A lot of the things we put in place that have brought us to this journey still have room for growth and there's still a fair amount of work that we've put in place that we'll start to see. But of course you have to balance that out against the new center losses that will start coming in from the mid - to end of this financial year and going forward.

items.statement: No forward guidance given on ARPOB growth; expect to continue past performance driven by reduced length of stay and payer mix improvement; rack rate increases hover in low-to-mid single digits YoY.
items.quote: We expect to be able to continue the performance that we've had so far. But the one thing to note is that year-on-year, the rack rate and the price increases that we take hover in the low to mid-single digits.

items.statement: Practice Plus Group (UK) acquisition rationale: scale private-pay/insurance patient proportion and deploy NH technology platform to lower cost base, as done in Cayman.
items.quote: The first is to increase the proportion of patients coming from private sources that is self -pay or private insurance. Those patients inherently pay more for the same service. The second is an implementation of our entire technology platform that will allow us to meaningfully lower the cost base for all operational processes, similar to what we've done in the Cayman Islands.

items.statement: UK EBITDA margin improvement from ~7-8% at acquisition to ~10% in Q4 not yet steady-state; transition costs, IT separation, and cost reclassifications distort comparability; need 3-4 more quarters to baseline.
items.quote: We still have many moving parts. We have not fully separated from the seller. IT separation is still underway and costs are still getting grounded for us.

items.statement: GBP 150 million loan for UK acquisition serviced locally in GBP with no currency risk; cash PAT sufficient to service debt despite negative reported PAT due to non-cash amortization.
items.quote: The loan has been taken in GBP, and it is being serviced locally in the UK So there is no currency risk on this loan.

items.statement: India capex higher due to ~60% construction cost inflation vs 5 years ago; land cost higher in metros but amortized over 100+ years; efficiency gains from automation and paperless workflows to offset higher capex per bed.
items.quote: One is just naturally construction cost today is 60% higher than it was 5 years ago. These are post-pandemic-related cost increases that is beyond our control.

items.statement: Raipur expansion adds new tower to replace old O&M building; existing facility is full-service but dated; new tower to offer differentiated patient experience.
items.quote: The only thing that we felt we had to expand on the existing facility is the existing building is quite old, one of the oldest hospital structure that we run, O&M model we have with the trust.

items.statement: India hospital margin expansion from 21.5% to 25.1% driven by volume growth from transformation, high-end procedures (robotic cardiac, transplants), better payer/bed mix, and technology; gains seen as sustainable but watchful on crude/FX he
items.quote: The hard work which we have put in, in terms of the transformation and high-end procedures are actually kind of reflecting now on the bottom line.

items.statement: Cayman insurance loss ratio ~110-112% (claims/premium net of reinsurance) in Year 1; price increases of 30-35% kicking in June and purging unfavourable accounts expected to reduce losses significantly over next 3 quarters.
items.quote: I would say the loss ratio, I mean, we don't disclose it specifically, but if you look at the C IMA statistics, you can find out. So it's approximately about 110% to 112% is the loss ratio.

items.statement: Cayman hospital revenue growth to slow from double-digit to mid-single digits; insurance new client addition slowed to balance claims experience; international markets to drive growth once Cayman opportunity exhausted.
items.quote: You're not going to be seeing the same pace of growth in the revenue. Of course, the hospital margin has been preserved pre Camana Bay Hospital, post Camana Bay and even now through Integrated Care. So, that is stable.

items.statement: FY26 greenfield capex INR 109 cr vs INR 424 cr planned (75% miss) due to election-related labour shortages and permission delays; FY28 commissioning timeline for Rajarhat, HSR, Raipur, Bangalore still holds.
items.quote: Lot of the project has started. The miss was due to a lot of the election -related issues in that it was impossible to get construction workers to come for a large amount of time.

items.statement: Consolidated overheads ~28% without UK, ~23% with UK (UK overhead structure lower); acquisition one-time costs caused ~200 bps margin dilution, normalized margin ~22%; UK will not reach India/Cayman margin levels.
items.quote: Without U.K., we were operating overall, all overheads put together at about 28%. And with U.K., we'll see a 23% number.

items.statement: Occupancy not reported; typically 60-65%; management prefers ARPIP and throughput as performance measures over ARPOB/occupancy.
items.quote: We typically operate between 60% to 65% in terms of occupancy. We do not believe that either ARPOB or occupancy is a correct measure of performance.

items.statement: Standalone other income INR 127 cr includes INR 94 cr dividend from Cayman (eliminated in consol); remainder is group's real other income.
items.quote: That INR127 crores has INR 94 crores of dividend that has been received from Cayman to India. So , because of that, you are seeing that number not coming in consol -- consol that intercompany gets eliminated.

items.statement: India overheads grew ~8% vs 10% revenue growth; operating leverage absorbed by power/minimum wage inflation and one-time merger costs (legal, stamp duty); leverage to normalize next year.
items.quote: There are a lot of underlying cost inflation, which we are absorbing in our overheads with the leverage that is being created with the revenue growth.

items.statement: Clinics: 11 in Bangalore; plan to double count in FY27 with expansion to Calcutta; pace balanced against property acquisition, fit-outs, and cash burn; from FY27 clinics rolled into hospital business for reporting.
items.quote: We have a plan to double the number of clinics that we currently have, but the speed at which we do it would be balanced on the other side against the acquisition of those properties, negotiating the rent, doing the fit -outs and also maintaining a steady amount of cash losses in the business so that we don't go overboard.

items.statement: UK private-pay revenue was 7% at acquisition; absolute private revenue increased; progress with private insurers and visiting consultants; benefits expected over next 3-6 quarters; 2-year target too early to quantify.
items.quote: It's still early days, but we have seen an increase in absolute terms of private revenue. We are making a lot of progress with our relationship with the private insurers as well as visiting consultants.

items.statement: Kolkata growth 5-6% in FY26 due to lower international patients; domestic focus compensated revenue/EBITDA; digital marketing, clinics, insurance, clinical team strengthening to drive volume growth in 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We have set up a very strong base and consistent -- strong and consistent base as we speak. Now with the investment in the digital marketing with, as Viren had mentioned earlier also, with the integrated care and the clinics coming in with the insurance and also trying to strengthen the clinical team across the region in quaternary care and tertiary care, we will start seeing the volumes grow up i

items.statement: No expansion plans for North/West clusters; focus on South/East; SRCC Mumbai adult program launch in FY27 within existing infrastructure.
items.quote: No plans as of now. We have the existing cluster in the North and West. We will start expanding in SRCC Hospital in Mumbai and adding the adult programs in FY27.

items.statement: Radiology fully AI-powered; Medha team using AI for patient services, clinical anomaly detection, ICU risk scoring; AI integrated into transformation, not separate.
items.quote: Our radiology department is completely powered by AI. A lot of the radiologists use software that implements image guidance AI for helping them make the diagnosis.

items.statement: No long-term top-line growth guidance; aim to maintain current growth pace; step-up when new hospitals commission.
items.quote: Again, we're not giving guidance, but we're trying to maintain the pace of growth in our business. There will be a jump when new hospitals get added.

items.statement: North cluster (NCR) extremely competitive; late entrant with niche in cancer (Dharamshila) and community high-end (Gurgaon); will continue cost advantage and service focus, no strategic rethink.
items.quote: So yes, it is no surprise to us and to the investors that North has been extremely challenging region for us. We are one of the latest entrants to latest entrants to this market, and it is extremely competitive.

items.statement: Mumbai (SRCC) broke even in Q4 FY26; adult program approval with trust in advanced stages; expected to turn around profitability once adult program launches.
items.quote: Mumbai has broken even in Quarter 4. We are working towards the adult program starting in Mumbai. We are in stages of discussion with the trust for approval, and it's in advanced stages of conversation.

items.statement: UK acquisition debt on target's books (leveraged buyout); target's free cash flow to service debt over 7 years; group in expansion phase diluting ROCE/ROE, but investments are long-term ROCE-accretive.
items.quote: It is a leveraged buyout. So, the entire acquisition debt is on the books of the target. And therefore, the free cash flow that is being generated by the target, a significant portion of it will be used to pay the debt in the books over the next 7 years.

items.statement: Management will provide full-year FY27 guidance on the Q1 FY27 earnings call.
items.quote: We'll give guidance in the first quarter call for the full year.

items.statement: Consolidated margins expected to be similar or slightly higher in FY27; specific guidance to be given in Q1 call.
items.quote: But yes, we believe the margins should continue. I mean, in terms of consolidated basis, we should continue seeing similar numbers or maybe slightly higher, which will guide you at the end of first quarter.

items.statement: Management has capex guidelines and policies but declined to share specifics on Rediff or NBFC investments.
items.quote: But yes, in terms of the capex, we have certain guidelines and policies that we are not able to share a lot of information about, specifics on Rediff.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 103% YoY to INR 8,116 crores in FY26; net revenue grew 15% YoY to INR 603 crores.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations for financial year '26 increased to INR8,116 crores compared to INR3,923 crores in FY '25, representing strong year-on-year growth of 103%.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT grew 58% YoY to INR 332 crores in FY26; Q4 FY26 adjusted PAT grew 90% YoY to INR 95 crores.
items.quote: Our consolidated profit after tax for FY '26 increased 58% year-on-year to INR332 crores as against INR209 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Platform business (e-commerce) was flat to slightly higher in FY26; growth expected in FY27 from new products and international expansion.
items.quote: So I think that overall we have not seen big growth in that business. If you look at full year, and I'm not talking about the quarterly. Quarterly, you'll have some changes, of course, as you go through. But the full year numbers in the segment there, you'll see that they are somewhat flat to slightly higher.

items.statement: Strong merchant wins in Q4 FY26 across utilities, government, B2B payments; 5,000+ merchants onboarded on form builder in under a month; scaling to 3,000+ hotels with integrated CRS and payment gateway.
items.quote: So overall merchant traffic across thousands of our merchants were growing and also a lot of big wins that is there. So in India, specifically on the utility, government payments, B2B payments, everything was growing very well.

items.statement: Platform-plus-payments strategy driving growth: form builder for education/events, hospitality CRS integrated with Opera/Micros-Fidelio, automated OTA payment collection.
items.quote: for the hospitality industry, now we're sc aling up to more than 3,000 hotels, where we're building the entire central reservation system along with the payment gateway built in

items.statement: Growth driven by both new merchant acquisition and increasing wallet share from existing merchants moving volumes to CCAvenue.
items.quote: So growth is supported by additional merchants as well as increasing share of the existing merchants that process from us.

items.statement: AI embedded across practically all transaction processing: fraud checks, routing, onboarding, reconciliation, customer service, lending risk assessment.
items.quote: I can tell you for sure th at practically in all different areas of payments, we are using AI. So in one way, we can say that all of our transactions will have some component of AI-based checks and validations that are happening across the

items.statement: Internal AI metrics tracked: payment success rates via intelligent routing, transaction failure reduction, onboarding turnaround, cross-sell, fraud detection/response times, support resolution times, reconciliation settlement turnaround.
items.quote: But the things that internally we would want to track in some ways, are things like the payment success rates driven by intelligent routing using AI, some reduction in transaction failures and, in some ways, the way you would want to get productivity through onboarding turnaround times and increase the cross-sell across the ecosystem products.

items.statement: Strategic minority investments in NBFCs (Ratnaafin up to 2.5%, Online PSB Loans) to enable asset-light lending orchestration; no balance sheet lending planned.
items.quote: We are not going to put our balance sheet for lending. The strategy that we've applied is that we will work with NBFC companies to be able to open up our ecosystem, and that strategy will continue to percolate.

items.statement: XDuce (US-based) 20% stake held as associate; profitable company making few million USD annually; AvenuesAI does not control XDuce board or capital allocation.
items.quote: We have not acquired. We've taken 20% in XDuce. The participation of XDuce comes up in the share of associates of the company.

items.statement: International focus shifting from Middle East to United States in FY27 due to macroeconomic risk in Middle East and increasing US activity; US cross-border commerce and merchant acquiring seen as large underpenetrated opportunity.
items.quote: This year, we will pick up U.S. because of the macroeconomic risk in Middle East. And we are also seeing a lot more activities happening in the U.S.

items.statement: Rediff confidential DRHP filed; no further details can be shared due to regulatory compliance; updates will be provided as available.
items.quote: Given the regulatory compliances, we are not able to share anything additional at this time. But what we will do is we'll keep everyone updated in terms of where we stand.

items.statement: RediffPay (consumer UPI app) live in production; stabilizing and scaling; consumer-facing launches expected in coming weeks.
items.quote: And then we are also working on RediffPay, which is a consumer-facing UPI app. It's actually live and in production. And given the recent launches and also the number of transactions and being able to ensure that we are stabilizing and then scaling it up, the team has been working on it

items.statement: AI enterprise adoption slower than expected; management acknowledges timing misjudgment but believes bet stands test of time; frameworks evolving, token costs optimizing.
items.quote: So yes, I think that as a company would make bold bets in terms of -- and we don't control the adoption as much as we'd like to. But you'd want to make such beds in the years, it's worth it. It will stand the test of time. It's just not that there's some latency involved.

items.statement: Management emphasizes infrastructure-led, intelligence-led, ecosystem-led growth over subsidiary-led growth; focused on durable long-term operating leverage.
items.quote: Our strategy is not subsidiary-led growth. Our strategy is infrastru cture-led, intelligence-led and ecosystem-led growth. We are focused on building durable long-term operating leverage rather than short-term expansion at cost of sustainability

items.statement: AI revenue exists but not material in P&L; management embeds AI across all layers rather than separating as standalone line item; will disclose when material.
items.quote: We do have specific AI revenue as well, which from a size of the P&L is not material, but we think that there's a lot more potential in that. And as and when it becomes large enough that we'd want to talk about it, and you'll hear more and more of that in this year from us.

items.statement: Capex focus on algorithms and data (not compute/chip design); AI investment front-loaded in FY26 with operating leverage expected to kick in over time.
items.quote: But there are good, great complian ce standards in place even today, that much I can tell you. And I think that this exposure that comes in is about a small vulnerability in a piece of software, which was not patched, which was not even known, that risk is now becoming significantly more and something that we have to keep on reviewing and looking at.

items.statement: Operating leverage improving through automation, AI-led efficiencies, better payment routing, fraud optimization, deeper merchant monetization.
items.quote: As transaction scale increases, we are seeing improving operating leverage through automation, AI-lead efficiencies, better payment routing, fraud optimization and deeper merchant monetization opportunities.

items.statement: Differentiation via platform-plus-payments model (workflow customization, vertical solutions) vs vanilla payment gateways; sticky merchant relationships through integrated CRS, form builder, automated OTA payments.
items.quote: So it's a platform plus payments play that has come. Li ke for the hospitality industry, now we're sc aling up to more than 3,000 hotels, where we're building the entire central reservation system along with the payment gateway built

items.statement: Payment gateway business faces margin pressure; take-rate improvement requires work and optimization; management focused on improving take rates in FY27.
items.quote: We see pockets where we see expansion in margins that we will also incur capex. We are in the payment gateway business is somewhat -- there is margin pressure. So I think a combination of that is, of course, playing out.

items.statement: FY27 profitability not expected to show hockey-stick improvement; similar to past years; guidance to be given in Q1 FY27 call.
items.quote: I think, I mean, it's reasonable to assume that it will -- the profitability, we don't see a hockey stick in FY '27 in profitability. We'll work very hard in terms of ensuring that we are able to get our take rates better, and that will require quite a bit of work and optimization.

items.statement: AI agent framework design: customer intent always controlled by customer; merchant guardrails on agents; AvenuesAI provides infrastructure and kill-switch controls; two-factor authentication remains with customer.
items.quote: But the control mechanism of the merchant will always be -- or the agent will always be with the merchant. But it gets slightly more gray area because we are also the custodian and we brought the framework to build the agents.

items.statement: Transaction intelligence identified as primary input to profit pool; monetization via merchant data distribution, credit automation, workflows built on payments; MDR alone not the biggest value creation.
items.quote: I think transaction intelligence is an input into the profit pool. It's like the most important input in a profit pool. So if the output is profits, then the input is the transaction intelligence. And that's what we are after, which is -- and that becomes the monetization on merchant data distribution, credit automation, all the workfl ows built on top of payments.

items.statement: Targets 10-20% volume growth in FY27 with focus on Western India for AAC blocks and construction chemicals, and pan-India for AAC panels including bullet train stations and metros
items.quote: So, for FY27, we are targeting a volume growth in the range of almost 10% to 20% and our major concentration is on Western India for the AAC blocks and the construction chemical segment.

items.statement: Expects 10-14% increase in capacity utilization during FY27
items.quote: We expect a healthy 10 -14% increase in capacity utilization during FY27.

items.statement: Targets reaching 80-85% capacity utilization as first priority, then focusing on margin improvement
items.quote: And our first and foremost priority is to reach most optimum capacity utilization to the tune of almost 80 to 85% upwards. And once we are near there, we will be then focusing on improving our margin realization as well.

items.statement: Expects to return to profitability in FY27
items.quote: And hopefully in this year, we should be returning to profits again.

items.statement: Expects to pass on further cost increases to customers and improve realizations in next 2-3 quarters

items.quote: Second, the ongoing acquisition of Easy To Travel (ETT) is part of Company's strategic vision to accelerate international expansion and strengthen our position as a global travel and lifestyle experiences platform.
