So, from the current capacity of 600 metric ton, we will take it to 18,000 metric ton in phase manner of next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Current order book stands at Rs. 55 crores, comprising Rs. 42 crores from government (yearly contracts) and Rs. 13 crores from private customers (3-month or quantity contracts).
items.quote: Currently, order book is around about Rs. 55 crore and it depends upon the customer. Like if we are working with government customers, then they usually give one year contract. And if it is private customer, it is either quantitative-based contract or it is three-month contract.

items.statement: Manufacturing gross margin ~30%, trading gross margin ~21%; polymer additives expected at ~40% margin once commercialized.
items.quote: Currently, in terms of the manufacturing margins, we are standing at 30% approximately, whereas from polymer additives, we feel that the margins would be 40%. And in terms of the growth momentum, it will definitely increase in the EBITDA and PAT because manufacturing percentage in terms of margin is higher than our import trading margins.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 9% to 10% in FY26; management working to improve margins further via manufacturing scale, economies of scale, and sourcing strength.
items.quote: Our financial performance, which is last financial year we have closed is Rs. 318 crores we have closed and this is 50% growth from the Financial Year '25 and our EBITDA margins have increased from 9% to 10% and PAT has increased from 5% to 6%.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue growth driven by mix of volume increase and raw material price escalation (some products doubled in last 6 months).
items.quote: This is a mix of both. You can say that the volume has increased from 32,000 metric ton to 46,000 metric ton, which includes 4,400 metric ton of our manufacturing capacity. Of course, the prices have increased from the January to March quarter and even some of the products have doubled in last six months.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased sharply from January 2026; company uses strategic sourcing, long-term contracts, buyer's credit, and supplier credit to manage procurement.
items.quote: It is because of the increase in the prices of raw materials. And as I have said prices have increased specifically, from January onwards, the prices of raw material have increased.

items.statement: Manufacturing revenue share 23% in FY26; target to reach 50% in 2-3 years including food, feed, and new halogen-free flame retardants.
items.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

items.statement: Geopolitical scenario creating import substitution opportunity; domestic manufacturers queuing up to test and source food, feed, and polymer additives from the company.
items.quote: But on the other side, this is giving us an opportunity for our manufactured product because due to the geopolitical scenario throughout India, the material which is being sourced from the overseas countries is not available. So, we are the only alternative left or we are one of the alternatives left in India.

items.statement: Polymer additive trials ongoing with 5 customers; NDAs signed with 2 customers for halogen-free flame retardants targeting cable, wire, electrical, electronics, and later EV batteries.
items.quote: Yes, the trial is already going on with five customers and as I am not supposed to reveal the name of the customers, the trial is going with five customers, and we have already signed some agreements also in NDA with two of our customers also.

items.statement: Current working capital cycle 110 days; using invoice discounting for receivables and buyer's/supplier credit for payables to reduce cycle and improve cash flow.
items.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is of 110 days. We are trying to reduce this working capital cycle because it will improve in cash flow also in the organization.

items.statement: CAPEX funding to come from bank credit lines and IPO proceeds allocated for CAPEX.
items.quote: We have the credit lines available for CAPEX from the banks also. And we have some part of the IPO proceeds which we have raised for CAPEX. So, we will utilize both for taking our capacity to next level to 18,000 metric tons.

items.statement: R&D team of 11 people including 3 doctorates; added independent director from same industry to add value.
items.quote: Currently, we have 11 people who are working in that R&D team and three are doctorates in that team. And even we have introduced one independent director who is from the same line of business we are into so that he can add value into our line of businesses where we are growing.

items.statement: Sales volume grew from 33,000 MT in FY25 to 46,000 MT in FY26 (includes 4,400 MT from manufacturing).
items.quote: So, the volume was 33,000 metric ton in FY25 and this year it was 46,000 metric ton in 2026, which comprises of 4,400 metric ton of manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: No domestic competition in halogen-free flame retardants; barriers include technology, R&D, manpower expertise, and patents (3 to be filed in 6 months).
items.quote: In terms of halogen-free, we don't see any competition in terms of India. In terms of barrier, there are technical and technological barriers. There are R&D barriers. And what we feel ourselves is that we can give the strength of in-house capabilities.

items.statement: Three patents for halogen-free flame retardant technology to be filed in next six months to protect IP.
items.quote: There are three patents which we are going to file in next six months already because of this patent infringement and various related issues which we are trying to check it from our lives. But in next six months, we will try to file three patents.

items.statement: Key risks include geopolitical supply chain disruptions affecting imported raw material availability and polymer additive commercialization timeline (3-6 months for customer validation).
items.quote: It depends upon the geopolitical scenario. It depends upon the timeline of reaching in India because you never know what is happening throughout the world.

items.statement: Initial international buyer interest for halogen-free flame retardants; focus on domestic market first, then export.
items.quote: This product is good and we have received interest from foreign buyers also. But we are at a very initial stage. So, I do not want to project too many big things at this stage. But yes, this is a very good product and we have developed in-house capabilities for this and a lot of money we have spent on this product also.

items.statement: Trading portfolio consists of base oils and TG urea; not dealing in melamine or phenol.
items.quote: So, we are basically into base oils. We are into TG urea. So, these are the two products we work on in terms of import of trading products.

items.statement: Omega-3 and Vitamin D2 products in final stage of R&D pilot/industrial trial; commercialization timeline uncertain.
items.quote: Sir, these are in the R&D phase as of now. I cannot comment on the commercialization stage, but these are in the final stage of pilot, I would say, industrial trial. Commercial date is not possible to comment because this will take, might take some time to commercialize.

items.statement: Polymer additive plant (400 MT/month) at Rs. 250/kg average price implies Rs. 100 crores peak annual revenue at 100% utilization.
items.quote: This product ranges from Rs. 150 to Rs. 1000 flame retardant, if you are talking about. I take an average price of Rs. 250. So, 400 tons multiplied by 250 comes to be Rs. 10 crores. So, I think Rs. 100 crores, this will contribute in the turnover at 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Petrochemicals trading segment contributed most to FY26 revenue growth; food, feed, and petrochemicals all grew.
items.quote: As the turnover has increased by 50%, so all have contributed, but I would say petrochemicals have contributed the most.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 45-50% with operational EBITDA doubling
items.quote: At a consolidated level, we are expecting approximately 45% to 50% top -line revenue growth. More importantly, this growth is highly efficient. We project doubling our operational EBITDA, proving immense operating leverage embedded in our current business model.

items.statement: Aerospace segment FY27 revenue growth 25-30% with EBITDA margin maintained at 20%
items.quote: First, is to continue to grow aerospace revenues profitably. We have the order book, the capacity and the customer relationships to support this, which should deliver 25% to 30% revenue growth, with EBITDA margins maintained at 20% at the segment level.

items.statement: Consumer segment FY27 revenue growth 125-150% with EBITDA break-even by Q4 FY27
items.quote: On consumer, we see a revenue growth of about 125% to 150%. And Q4 FY27 will be the quarter wherein we will hit EBITDA break -even.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT break-even expected by H1 FY28
items.quote: However, as our consumer volumes ramp -up and our aerospace segment continues its strong performance, we fully expect to see consolidated PAT hit break-even by H1 FY28.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR160 crores for aerospace and INR500 crores for consumer segment
items.value: INR160 crores approx. And in our consumer segment, we have planned about INR500 crores approx
items.quote: On Capex: In our aerospace segment, we have planned about INR160 crores approx. And in our consumer segment, we have planned about INR500 crores approx for the full year FY27.

items.statement: Karnataka MoU for INR2,856 crores over 5 years across Belagavi and Hubballi clusters
items.quote: And in March 2026, we signed a second MoU with the government of Karnataka, committing investments of INR2,856 crores over five years across our existing clusters in Belagavi and Hubballi.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu MoU for INR1,900 crores over 10 years for vertically integrated aerospace ecosystem at Hosur
items.quote: In February 2026, we signed an MoU with the government of Tamil Nadu to invest INR1,900 crores for 10 years for a new vertically integrated aerospace manufacturing ecosystem within a new aerospace and defense park at Hosur, across 250 acres in the SIPCOT Shoolagiri Industrial Park.

items.statement: Aerospace order book stands at USD $889 million
items.quote: As a result, our order book in aerospace stood at robust USD $889 million.

items.statement: Consumer segment long-term EBITDA margin target 18-20% at 75-80% utilization
items.quote: It's pretty much driven by the utilization. You know, when you get to 50%, our expectation is to get 40% to 50% this year. When you get to somewhere around 75% utilization level, we start seeing the margin levels. So, journey continues

items.statement: Consumer segment utilization at 23% currently, targeting 40-50% by FY27 end
items.quote: Our primary focus this year will be driving capacity utilization from 23% today to a target of 40% to 50% by the year end.

items.statement: Installed annual capacity 4.70 million machining and molding hours with 434 CNC and 179 molding machines
items.quote: Our installed annual capacity has grown to 4.70 million, machining and molding hours on an annualized basis. We scaled our manufacturing operations steadily throughout the year to support the new and existing programs closing FY26 with a robust footprint of 434 CNC machines and 179 molding machines.

items.statement: Hasbro discontinued sourcing; signed long-term agreement with Mattel to absorb capacity impact
items.quote: Hasbro has informed us that it has revised manufacturing and sourcing strategy and told us they will stop raising POS with us. While this decision was unexpected, it will not impact the overall growth of the business. We continue serving other equally large and strategic customers.

items.statement: 93-94% of overall sales USD-linked including deemed exports

items.statement: Working capital normalization expected over next two quarters as logistics stabilize
items.quote: Yes. And we are taking precautions to do this most probably for another two quarters till we see the stabilization. Because generally the logistics has increased by five to six weeks what we have seen -- sea logistics.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.23x in FY26 from 0.99x in FY25
items.quote: Our net debt-to-equity ratio was 0.23 as of March 31, 2026, an improvement from 0.99x at the end of FY25, which shows that we are well capitalized for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: FY27 capex to be funded through borrowings and internal accruals
items.quote: Essentially, for FY27, we will leverage borrowings and also some bit of internal accruals to fund the planned capex.

items.statement: Ravi Kumar Assudani joined as head of engineering for consumer segment effective Q1 FY27 with 16 years Apple experience
items.quote: We are pleased to have Ravi Kumar Assudani join us as head of engineering for consumer segment effective Q1 FY 2027. Ravi brings over 16 years of experience at Apple Inc., where he led global tooling and manufacturing design operations across multiple product lines.

items.statement: Material cost increases in consumer plastics passed through to customers via back-to-back agreements
items.quote: On the consumer side, plastics especially, material prices have shot up. But because we have back-to-back agreement with the customers, that has been a pass ed-through to customers. Therefore, there has not been a significant impact on performance.

items.statement: Titanium lead time 52 weeks, special steels 65-75 weeks; proactively covering 125% of quarterly needs due to West Asia crisis
items.quote: Titanium and the superalloy, some of the steels, for example. In fact, right now, steels have one of the longest lead times in the industry. Some of the specific steels as high as - - we're talking 65 weeks to 75 weeks lead times. And titanium t ypically is 52 weeks lead time

items.statement: Aerospace segment ROCE 20% in FY26 up from 14% in FY25
items.quote: Aerospace segment ROCE for FY26 was 20%, up from 14% in FY25, which is in line with our expectation, and demonstrates our ability to scale efficiently.

items.statement: Consumer electronics asset turnover target 1.5x at peak utilization
items.quote: So, it should be closer to 1.5 level in the consumer electronics side.

items.statement: PLI income eligibility starts FY27; no PLI booked in FY26
items.quote: No. So, FY27 will be our first year where we will be eligible for the PLI.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing 5-6 week sea logistics delays and 6-8 day air freight increases; managing via inventory buildup
items.quote: Because generally the logistics has increased by five to six weeks what we have seen -- sea logistics. Air has gone up by six days to eight days, somewhere in that range.

items.statement: Aerospace portfolio expanded to 5,654 SKUs with 433 new parts added in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We added 433 new parts in Q4 alone, taking our total aerospace portfolio to 5,654 SKUs, with a 26% increase in the portfolio since last year.

items.statement: Management targets 30% revenue growth for FY27 but expects 14-15% as more likely
items.quote: We are shooting for 30% growth. Now will 30% happen? It's going to be a tough call. So historically, last couple of years, we've done 14%, 15%. I'll put my money more on that than on the 30%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins may dip slightly in FY27 due to AI investments and customer pricing pressure at renewals
items.quote: We're going to try and maintain it. There might be a little bit of a dip, Bharat, becau se of 2 reasons. One, we're investing in AI. And customers are expecting at renewal time contracts to be revised at a lower price because of the AI productivity that AI

items.statement: Sales pipeline reached USD 25 million, up from USD 5 million six months ago, driven by six big bets and new US sales leadership
items.quote: Vikas, the pipeline that we have today is in the region of USD 25 million. It's the highest we have ever had. So we've got some large deals which are happening, which we never got invited to before.

items.statement: 95-98% of growth comes from existing customers; focus on increasing wallet share in top 20 accounts which contribute 70% of revenue
items.quote: 95% to 98% of our growth will come from existing customers. So our top 20 customers, our focus is to keep all our growth from these 20 customers as much as possible, deepen relationships, increase wallet share with these 20 customers.

items.statement: Outcome-based billing currently ~10% of revenue; pushing to increase share by consolidating vendors and using human-agent delivery models
items.quote: Outcome-based today would be I would say, maybe about 10% only. And the rest is all time and material because historically, that is how this industry has grown and evolved, and that has been the traditional model.

items.statement: No significant capex required to reach $500M revenue target by 2030; investments in people and technology funded by internal cash generation
items.quote: When you say investment, Tech services is a people plus technology game. So as to build revenue, you need to invest in technology, and you need to invest in people. And because of the nature of the industry, we have enough cash generation, which will allow investment. So there is really no significant capex, which will be required to get us to the number of $500 million by 2030.

items.statement: Utilization capped at ~85% due to bench needs for project starts and agent building; headcount no longer linear to revenue growth due to AI
items.quote: I don't think utilization will go anything above 85%, unless you start including agents in utilization because agents will now be 100% utilized, okay? So that's the big question which I have for you.

items.statement: Actively looking for acquisitions up to INR 100 crore top line; funded by internal accruals with minimal borrowing; nothing imminent this quarter
items.quote: We can never afford a very big acquisition, Bharat, because of the -- we always do it with internal accruals, maybe a little bit of borrowing, but it's with our own money. So if we buy anything, it will be, I would say the maximum would be a top line of INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Hired Chief Growth Officer for US 9-10 months ago; UK/Europe Chief Growth Officer joining end of June; investing in AI training for developers and project managers
items.quote: We have a leader who is our Chief Growth Officer in the U.S. He joined us, I would say, now 10 months ago or 9 months ago. And we have a Chief Growth Officer for U.K. and Europe joining us end of June.

items.statement: Revenue crossed INR 1,000 crores in FY26 with 14% YoY growth; EBITDA margin expanded 201 bps to 18.57%; PAT margin expanded 91 bps to 13.23%
items.quote: For the full Financial year 2026, the operating revenue stood at around INR 1,007 crores, registering a strong growth of nearly 14% year-on-year. The EBITDA for the year stood at INR 187 crores, reflecting a healthy growth of around 28% year-on-year while EBITDA margins improved to 18.57% from 16.56%.

items.statement: Board approved final dividend of 55% (INR 0.55 per share), making total dividend 100% of face value INR 1
items.quote: The Board has also approved a final dividend at 55%, which is equal to INR 0.55 per equity share, making the total dividend to 100% of face value of INR1.

items.statement: Americas 50%, Europe 29%, APAC 21% of FY26 revenue; onsite 44%, offshore 56%; ~3% of 14% YoY growth from rupee depreciation
items.quote: The Americas contributed to nearly 50% of our total revenues, whilst Europe contributed 29% and the remaining 21% came from Asia Pacific and other regions. The on-site revenue mix was 44% and the offshore at 56%.

items.statement: Customer decision-making cycles elongated due to AI uncertainty; pipeline strong but conversions delayed; expecting pickup in Q1-Q2 FY27
items.quote: Growth is picking up, Bharat. But like I mentioned in my statement, decision-making by customers is getting deferred because of all the noise around AI. It has to settle down because at the end of it, enterprises have to spend money on their technology landscape.

items.statement: Customers expecting contract price reductions at renewal due to AI productivity; AI agent costs currently high but expected to decline
items.quote: And customers are expecting at renewal time contracts to be revised at a lower price because of the AI productivity that AI warrants. So there will be a little bit of compression.

items.statement: Risk of vendor consolidation if wallet share not increased; AI cost uncertainty; customer adoption delays; potential cannibalization of low-end work like testing
items.quote: If we don't increase our wallet share, there is always a risk of getting consolidated out when there is a vendor consolidation. So the focus is, and 95% of our growth will come from existing clients.

items.statement: Net cash and bank balance positive at INR 223 crores as of March 31, 2026; healthy cash generation supports strategic investments
items.quote: We are also pleased to hi ghlight that our net cash and bank balance is positive at around INR 223 crores as on 31st March 2026 indicating a healthy cash generation and liquidity to support our strategic investments and growth initiatives

items.statement: AI levels playing field; nimble mid-tier firms gain advantage over Tier 1s due to lower overheads, faster delivery, and ability to consolidate vendors with 25-30% cost savings
items.quote: Because if they make a mistake, correcting the mistake doesn't require as much time as in the past, where you only saw results after 3 or 4 years when it was too late. So because of agile, because of AI, because of accelerators, the game has changed.

items.statement: Zetechno and Ceptes acquisitions (Salesforce, ServiceNow capabilities) performing well; growth from these mixed into organic revenue
items.quote: These acquisitions, which we did in '24, '25, they have been doing pretty well. And some of the growth which you have seen in the current year is also on account of the revenue which has been generated from those acquisitions.

items.statement: Management declined to provide revenue or margin guidance for FY27 due to geopolitical volatility and supply chain uncertainty
items.quote: I actually do not give out any guidance, especially in a situation like today, where you do not know whether the war is ending tomorrow because you keep hearing that today is ending, no but it's not ending.

items.quote: depending on how quickly we are able to stabilize the operations, I think we should be better than market by anywhere between 5% and 10% because the preform seller is also making some money.

items.quote: On a revenue of about INR 450 crores, we generated a profit of about INR 21 crores and the outlook is decent.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA per ton expected to face INR100-160/t cost increase, confident of passing it on
items.quote: So look, we have -- we anticipate that in the near term, the next quarter, our costs would be impacted by anywhere between INR100 to INR 150 a ton, given our fuel mix and other things.

items.statement: Central India cement demand expected to grow 7-7.5% in FY27
items.quote: I'm sure that this fiscal in central, the industry will grow at least by 7%, 7.5%.

items.quote: We shall be in line with the industry growth in our region.

items.quote: We are investing around INR120 crores, INR130-odd crores -- you can take about INR130 crores in that product.

items.quote: So for the fiscal year '26, '27; it will be around total INR 100 crores. And next year, subsequently, it's really around 120.

items.quote: The EBITDA at INR584 per ton was up 10% year-on-year.

items.quote: On a year basis too, the impact on price was lesser as compared to the quarter -- quarterly basis. We did lose about INR 16 overall on price, and there was an impact of INR 11 on raw materials.

items.statement: Pet coke share reduced from 60-65% to ~55%, coal increased to 40% to optimize fuel cost
items.quote: Our pet coke to coal earlier, it used to be -- around 60%, 65% was the pet coke, and remaining coal and alternative fuel. Now during last maybe 2, 3 months, we had reduced the pet coke consumption by around 10%.

items.quote: Kcal, pet coke earlier used to be around -- maybe expensive 10%. Now currently it is really expensive, 30% over coal.

items.statement: Premium products 52% of trade volumes, up 9% YoY; trade mix 81% retail, 19% B2B
items.quote: Premium products portfolio, we are working on this and have been working on this consistently as a strategy for the last 3 years. And I'm very happy to state that we have achieved a number of 52%.

items.statement: Clinker consumption ratio ~60-61%, targeting 50-100 bps reduction via composite cement launch
items.quote: So our clinker consumption ratio is around 60%, 61% of the cement. And I think we will be able to reduce at least maybe 50 basis point to maybe 100 basis points in cement.

items.statement: UP elections in next year to boost Central India cement demand; monsoon seasonality to moderate near-term
items.quote: The upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh is going to provide a lot of impetus to cement demand in Central India.

items.statement: Repaid INR687 mn interest-free loan; company now debt-free with INR4,037 mn cash balance
items.quote: We did repay interest free loan of INR 687 million, and the company is now completely debt-free.

items.statement: Operating on negative net operating working capital consistently
items.quote: We continue to operate on negative net operating working capital.

items.statement: Recommended dividend INR7/share (70% payout on face value INR10) for FY26
items.quote: And we did recommend a dividend of INR7 per share in our Board meeting recently concluded.

items.statement: Board to evaluate share buyback suggestion from shareholder
items.quote: Maybe we will explore in the management committee and will discuss in the Board of Directors meeting, and we'll see.

items.statement: Plans to merge Zuari and Heidelberg entities; Karnataka 3 mt integrated plant underway; no fixed timeline
items.quote: Depending on the suitable time, yes, there are plans of eventually going in for a merger of all the entities.

items.statement: GST rate rationalization from 28% to 18% last year supports long-term demand
items.quote: Also because of domestic -- robust domestic consumption as well as the rationalization of the GST rate from 28% to 18%, which was down last year.

items.statement: El Nino heat wave risks agricultural output, rural demand, food inflation; monsoon expected to mitigate
items.quote: The El Nino effect that we are seeing, the heat wave sweeping through the northern part of India and the central part of India, would produce -- would pose a significant risk to agricultural output, rural demand and food inflation.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (West Asia) impacting pet coke/fuel prices; elevated inflation and currency depreciation concerns
items.quote: The geopolitical developments, particularly the West Asia conflict, is continuing to create uncertainty in global markets and commodity prices, where we already had some impact on pet coke and fuel prices.

items.quote: The company expects moderate growth across segments in the financial year 2026/'27. With stable domestic demand, we remain cautious and continue to closely monitor the potential impact of ongoing geopolitical developments on the broader economy.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust across segments; exports uncertain due to geopolitics
items.quote: From a domestic demand perspective, for now, we still see robust demand. We are watching what's happening largely to the economy and everybody else in the country.

items.statement: Order book building in railways and mining; construction moderate; compressor in down cycle
items.quote: Mining, for the last 2 years, we were not seeing good tenders coming in. The order velocity and the tender velocity was lower. But in the last 6 months, mining has picked up, and so our order book has started building up.

items.quote: The data center business contribution, so for the full year, the data center business would have contributed between 30% to 35% of our overall power generation domestic revenue, and for the quarter, approximately 35%.

items.quote: So, we had about INR250 crores of value.

items.quote: In Cummins India Limited, we have invested more than INR1,000 crores. What we have been using it for is continuously modernization of our plants and expanding our line capability, more output from the same line.

items.statement: India economic outlook steady supported by government manufacturing and capex focus; company focused on order execution, supply chain resilience, tech strengths
items.quote: India's economic outlook remains steady supported by government initiatives, focus on manufacturing and capital investment. The company remains focused on timely execution of orders, maintaining supply chain resilience and leveraging its technological strengths.

items.statement: Private and public CapEx continue to grow with pickup in cement, steel, pharma, data centres, and railways; no slowdown seen currently.
items.quote: We do not see a slowdown in private CapEx yet. We do not see a slowdown in public CapEx yet. items.statement: Sale of low-voltage motors business on track for completion in June 2026.
items.quote: The sale of the low-voltage motors business is on track for completion in June 2026.

items.statement: West Asia conflict may impact fertilizer demand; commercial buildings mixed; automotive picking up with two-wheelers stronger.
items.quote: We will have to wait and see what the impact of the West Asia crisis is on fertilizers. But chemicals are doing well. Pharma is growing well. Food and beverages is growing well also. Automotive is beginning to pick up. Two-wheelers are doing much better than four-wheelers, but the four-wheelers are also picking up as well.

items.statement: Price increases have a 3-4 month lag effect; two hikes done, will continue but cannot pass full 20% FX and 50-150% copper/silver increases
items.quote: The price increases always have a lag effect. And as I said, these are all short cycle businesses. So, the products that we are supplying today, once we announce a price increase, the impact of that is felt in 3 or 4 months later.

items.statement: One price hike taken prior to March, one post-March; 3-4 month lag before impact kicks in
items.quote: No. One was taken prior to March and one is being taken post-March. But again, as I mentioned, it is a 3 to 4 month time lag before they actually start kicking in.

items.statement: DI business grew 1.5% in quarter, 17% in 6 months; SI volumes up 17.5% in quarter, 23% in 6 months; railways pipeline strong
items.quote: If you see the overall presentation that Wolfgang gave and break that down by the individual segments that we have got over there, our DI business grew at 1.5% roughly, right, in terms of order income. And this is again, short cycle. I do not believe this is a reflection of the private sector CapEx right now. Overall, if you see for the year, for the 6 months, it's growing at 17%.

items.statement: Private sector CapEx in key segments growing at 8-10% on average
items.quote: So, I would say 8 to 10 on an average percentage growth. And I am talking CapEx in the segments that I spoke about.

items.statement: Data centre wallet share estimated at 10-20% of $100 CapEx; civil work is large part
items.quote: So, my estimation would be in the range of 10 to 20%.

items.statement: Railways pipeline deep and broad: 24,000 km signalling ordered, rest expected by end of next year; large opportunities in electrification and rolling stock
items.quote: 24,000 kms. of signalling has already been done… has already been ordered. We expect the rest to be ordered probably end of next year. But electrification and rolling stock, there are large opportunities that are already in the pipeline, and a good flow that is coming.

items.statement: Examining expansion of mobility factories in Nashik and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar due to order backlogs and pipeline; will update later
items.quote: So on factory expansions, we are examining the expansion requirements for our mobility factories, both in Nashik as well as in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in view of the order backlogs that we currently have, as well as the pipelines that we've seen coming up.

items.statement: Locomotive contract margins blended (delivery + O&M) at similar percentages; absolute margins grow with volume
items.quote: Oh, the margins are blended, the margins are blended. So what you see in the margins coming in for the first 40 locos, for the next 80 the margins in absolute values will be proportionately adjusted, but in percentage values they will be at similar percentages.

items.statement: Government fiscal challenges from oil crisis, rupee depreciation, inflation could impact ordering in 3-6 months; no slowdown seen yet
items.quote: Looking at the future, as I said, I think some of the drivers that the government is going to have to look at is how will the impact of the oil crisis play into the inflationary environment in the country? Will that have an impact on… and the depreciation of the rupee as well? That could give a challenge to the government in balancing the books.

items.statement: Smart Infra 70-75% localized; margin pressure from copper, silver, aluminium commodities not FX; price hikes on short-cycle, negotiation on project orders
items.quote: Yeah, it is largely localized, and I think we are 70 to 75% localized in the smart infra, and we continue to localize the remaining portfolio as well. items.statement: India-EU FTA to reduce import costs in some segments; indirect benefit from increased customer production
items.quote: So, yes, import costs for us will go down, particularly in some segments. We are still to evaluate the fine print of the FTA there, but we do believe that import costs in some segments of our business will go down.

items.statement: DI localization not viable without millions volume; only negligible elements like flow meters being localized
items.quote: Look, DI's products are primarily PLCs in terms of the hardware. It's primarily PLCs in terms of the hardware. And PLCs, you need a minimum volume, which runs into millions, to make a factory actually viable.

items.statement: Cash flow lower due to higher inventory (West Asia crisis buffer) and higher receivables/contract assets from revenue growth and mobility milestone billing
items.quote: One is, we increased our inventory levels also based on the West Asia crisis, to safeguard our customers and also be able to continue with manufacturing and supply to our customers. So, this is one reason why our cash is lower than we have seen in the past.

items.statement: Metals/steel slight slowdown in last 1-2 months; unsure if short-term or systemic; cement doing well
items.quote: Some slowdown in metals, in other words, in steel, a little bit. We are not sure whether this is short term or whether this is only for… whether this is more systemic, but there's some slight slowdown in the last 1 or 2 months.

items.statement: Early shoots of demand seen in April and May; expects demand to sustain

items.statement: Export duty of 30% makes iron ore exports uneconomical; pellet exports preferred
items.quote: With a 30% export duty, it doesn't make too much of a sense to do that. If you have to export, you should be exporting pellets.

items.statement: Non-executive pay revision under ministry consideration, already provided for from Jan 2026; executive revision from Jan 2027, marginal impact
items.quote: I think most of our employees are in non -executive cadre and their pay revision is being worked out right now, it is under the consideration of the ministry. But we always account for the higher wages, it is already been provided for. The increased amount of wages is already provided for in the books of accounts and so there's not going to be any large -scale effect on that.

items.statement: Legacy gold mine in Australia curtailed to break-even, shifting to exploration and refinery planning for profitability
items.quote: This year the operations just broke even, but now we have curtailed our production and we are now actually going full hog on exploration and proving of further assets because we have realized that given the gold prices unless you have your own refinery, making it very profitable becomes very difficult there.

items.statement: FY27 operating margin target above 13.8%, aiming for ~100 bps improvement
items.quote: Quantifying the last year, we maintained the operating margin of around 13.8%. That is the full year, Q4 was much better. So we don't expect Q4 will be repeated definitely. But we intend to do better than last year overall operating margin, which is 13.8%. So it should be better, maybe 1% plus.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 180-200 crores including EBO expansion
items.quote: Last year, we incurred around INR130 crores. Next year, we have planned around INR180 crores to INR200 crores. So that's for next year.

items.statement: Plan to open 100 new EBOs in FY27, 30-40% by December
items.quote: We are going to open 100 new outlets this year. And we are going to change our product mix, plus there will be some more addition in terms of distributors and retailers.

items.statement: 15-18% blended price hike taken across categories to offset cost inflation
items.quote: Sameer, we have taken 2 to 3 price increase in the market, and it was a gradual increase. Some were because of raw material, and one was because of the labor cost, which increased in Haryana. So roughly around 15% to 18% is the increase.

items.statement: Cost inflation estimated at 15-20% including 25-30% labor cost rise in Haryana and material cost spikes
items.quote: So we can say around 15% to 20% increase will be there overall on the cost side as on date.

items.statement: Q4 volume growth 5-6% normalized after GST destocking; April-May FY27 better but early
items.quote: Actually, the full impact w e started seeing after December onwards. So you can definitely say that 5% to 6%, we were able to grow in 2 quarters

items.statement: Premiumization push: Sparx range extending from INR 999-1,700 to INR 2,500-2,800; women/kids focus
items.quote: Now we are thinking about how we can offer more products at INR2,500 also. So the price and the premium we are increasing.

items.statement: EBO expansion into West and South India; quick commerce launch on Blinkit and Zepto
items.quote: Now we have identified some gaps in West. And going forward, definitely, we will enter Southern market also, seeing and understanding the consumer preferences.

items.statement: Volume growth target 4-5% annually for next 2 years
items.quote: Next 2 years, I think we have to be cautious. Intent is there, again, around, I think, 4% to 5% definitely, we want to grow our volume.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 16.5% vs 16.1% YoY; FY26 13.8%; improvement from backend efficiencies, volume leverage, lower discounts
items.quote: There are 2, 3 reasons for that. One was that a lot of back-end work is done in the plant to reduce the cost. Secondly, our volume has grown a lot. So the fixed cost remains same. The contribution has increased because of the volume and value and plus, we have reduced the discount given in the market also.

items.statement: Distributor count increased from 550 to 630; supplying to 70,000 retailers/MBOs; 420 EBOs
items.quote: So we have mentioned in our investor report also that we are cur rently supplying to 70,000 retailers/MBO outlets. And EBOs are 420 outlets. These are our own

items.statement: Exporting to 37 countries
items.quote: Plus we are exporting to 37 countries. Okay.

items.statement: Inventory at 75 days sales (~150 days COGS) noted by analyst; management did not comment on target
items.quote: Now when I look at our inventory, we have 75 days on sales, so that will translate to around 150 days on COGS.

items.statement: Cautious on near-term due to geopolitical uncertainty, inflationary pressure, consumer sentiment; price hike uptake being monitored
items.quote: While the momentum exiting FY 26 is encouraging, we must tread with caution due to the uncertain external environment amidst the ongoing geopolitical situation causing inflationary pressure, which could affect consumer sentiment.

items.statement: Ad spend maintained at 4-5% of sales; shifting focus from TV to digital/performance marketing
items.quote: So our expenditure is roughly around 4% to 5%, and it varies between brand to brand, whatever the requirement is. And secondly, a big expenditure is also on performance marketing on platforms like Amazon and Flipkart.

items.statement: Industry-wide price hikes taken; not only Relaxo; raw material inflation across footwear sector
items.quote: It is across industry, footwear industry. All the players have taken the increase of prices. It's not only Relaxo.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 14-15% despite geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: we still hope that we can be at the lower or 14%, 15% growth we still hope that we will get.

items.statement: Defense revenue expected at INR250-300 crores in FY27 with 75-80% capacity utilization
items.quote: We are expecting almost -- our capacity is 150,000, and we expect almost 75% to 80% execution this year.

items.statement: Defense EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 30-35% for coming years
items.quote: In the coming years, what the guidance we have given of 30%, 35%, it will prevail.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 includes INR400 crores for defense capacity augmentation, may spill to FY28
items.quote: we have a plan to augment our capacity, which has a capital outlay of INR400 crores, but it will be sprawled maybe in this financial year or it may be carried forward to the next financial year also.

items.statement: Steel capacity expansion from 5 lakh to 6 lakh tonnes via GI conduit pipes and front fork tubes in 9-12 months
items.quote: We are aiming it to increase to 6 lakh. But in this year, how much it will be added up that we will let you know.

items.statement: Hydraulic tubes capacity utilization at 50% in FY26, targeting 65-70% in FY27
items.quote: in the last year, we have come to 50% capacity utilization of the hydraulic tubes. And in this year, we hope th at we will be able to d o it to 65% to 70

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 94% in FY26, will decrease with new capacity additions
items.quote: for this year, capacity utilization has been 94%. And in the coming year, with the added capacity, it will come down definitely.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded above 10% in Q4 FY26 due to better product mix
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanding to above 10%, a double-digit figure, supported by a better product mix, operational efficiency, and improved realizations in specialized product category.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement to 33% is sustainable, not transitory
items.quote: There is no worry. Gross margin will be sustained. It is a sustainable margin, what we have given.

items.statement: Conduit pipe EBITDA margin 15-20% sustainable, front fork tube 15-16%
items.quote: Conduit pipe is basically for export to USA . It's a highly profitable item with an EBITDA o f around 15

items.statement: Order book described as healthy across all segments including defense
items.quote: Our order book is healthy; I can say that.

items.statement: Solar vertical sales grew 33% in FY26, strong demand outlook with India targeting 500GW+
items.quote: we have improved 33% sales to our solar vertical in this year. India is at 500 gigawatts plus. New capacities are adding every year.

items.statement: Defense demand very strong globally, supply constrained for next 4-5 years
items.quote: Demand, there is no doubt of demand. Supply will always be constrained. In next 4, 5 years, my perception is, supply will be constrained.

items.statement: Input cost increases from West Asia crisis being passed through with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: there is a price increase of all the consumables, and we are trying to pass it on to the customers, but it is always with a time lag. So it may take 3 months, to 1 quarter to 2 quarters to pass all these increases.

items.statement: Export impact 5-10% due to West Asia logistics, expected to resolve in 15-20 days
items.quote: exports because of time duration taken in reaching the consignment, it is taking more ti me. So it may impact some 5%, 10%, but we hope the matter will not be long for 12 months

items.statement: Inventory and debtor days increased due to export slowdown and domestic glut, not yet normalized
items.quote: our inventory has increased, our realization has slowed down, and it is beyond our control.

items.statement: Net debt at INR1,000 crores (INR800 crores working capital + INR200 crores term loan) with INR50 crores cash
items.quote: Net debt position, working capital loans is INR800 crores and term loan is INR200 crores. Total INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Debt repayment of INR54 crores in FY27 and INR51 crores in FY28
items.quote: FY26, during current financial year, it will be INR54 crores. And again, financial year '28, it would be INR51 crores.

items.statement: Increasing contribution from value-added engineering products: defense, solar, hydraulic tubes, GI conduit, front fork tubes
items.quote: our share of value-added products will keep on increasing. quarter-on-quarter and year after year.

items.statement: Defense production at 150,000 shells in FY26, augmenting capacity to 400,000 shells
items.quote: Already producing heavy caliber shells to the tune of 150,000 numbers and augmenting the capacity to 4 lakh shells.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing supply chain disruption, logistics delays, and commodity price volatility
items.quote: the West Asia crisis, it's a definitely a breaker for every industry, because supply chain is disturbed drastically.

items.statement: Private defense participation expected to scale from 30% to 50% in India
items.quote: Private participation is likely to scale to 50% in comparison to 30%, as it has been in the last year.

items.statement: Defense orders secured for up to 2 years of production capacity
items.quote: We have the orders that we can supply to for up to 2 years.

items.statement: Global shell demand 8-9 million vs 2-3 million supply capacity in next 1-2 years
items.quote: the demand today is 8 million to 9 million shells, whereas the quantity available or quantity to be started in the next 1 or 2 years, it may be 2 million to 3 million.

items.statement: Teams globetrotting to secure new technologies and markets for defense and solar
items.quote: our teams are globetrotting to grab all those new technologies.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR1 per share for Q4, taking total FY26 dividend to INR8.6 per share (172% of par value)
items.quote: I'm glad to announce that Board of Directors have approved the dividend of INR1 per share of par value INR5 for -- that is interim dividend for quarter 4. This made the total dividend of INR8.6 per share, which is 172% of the par value of share.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance: EXIM 8%, Domestic 15%, Overall 9.5%; conservative due to geopolitical factors, may revise at mid-year
items.quote: I would like to now give the guidance for this financial year '27. EXIM, I would like to give a guidance of 8%. Domestic, I would like to give guidance of 15%. Overall, will be 9.5%.

items.statement: Rail freight margin improved from 25.65% to 27.16%; overall operating margin rose from 29.99% to 30.89%; EBITDA margin target maintained at 24-25%
items.quote: Our rail freight margin increased from 25.65% to 27.16%, which is quite a healthy rail freight margin. It's a growth of 1.51%. Our overall operating margin increased from 29.99% to 30.89%. It's a growth of almost 1%.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR1,085.20 crore; FY27 capex budget approved at INR945 crore, may increase at mid-year review
items.quote: Capex achieved in last financial year was one of the highest, which is INR1,085.20 crores. And in this financial year, yesterday, Board of Directors have approved a capex budget of INR945 crores.

items.statement: Commissioned 43 high-speed rakes in FY26 (total 423); procured 4,729 containers (total fleet 57,746); added 500 tank containers, adding 200/month; Board approved 2,000 more tank containers
items.quote: We have commissioned 43 high-speed rakes in this financial year, taking total to 423. And we have procured 4,729 new containers, taking our total fleet size to 57,746 containers of our own.

items.statement: EXIM revenue crossed INR6,000 crore for first time; EXIM handling 4.21M TEUs (record); domestic bulk cement target 1M tons in FY27; gunny bales and tiles traffic reviving
items.quote: In EXIM, we crossed INR6,000 crores, that is INR60 billion for the first time, that is the revenue. For the first time in the company's history, which is all-time high. EXIM has performed exceedingly well.

items.statement: WDFC connectivity to JNPT commissioning by June 1, 2026; double stack trains to run NCR-JNPT; new terminals at Mandalgarh, Kadakola, Jajpur, Paradip; Nepal traffic via Raxaul and Biratnagar
items.quote: DFC connected to -- connectivity to JNPT will be commissioned by 1st June 2026, so we are quite ready. And last week, I had a meeting with top management of DFC Corporation, and they are quite optimistic that this -- from 1st June, they will be able to run double stack trains to JNPT.

items.statement: Will share haulage savings from double-stack upper deck (50% haulage) with customers via competitive tariffs to shift road cargo to rail
items.quote: And secondly, we will be tinkering with our tariff also because our company believes that without sacrificing margins, if we incur some savings, we will share those savings with our customers, part of the savings.

items.statement: Empty running reduced 10.5% overall in FY26 (EXIM -27%, Domestic -4%); Q4 domestic empty running cost rose 11.3% YoY to INR76.76 crore due to gunny bales disruption
items.quote: And due to the excellent operation planning, we reduced the empty running of rakes also and by -- in EXIM by 27% and in domestic around 4%, overall, 10.5% reduction in empty running of rakes.

items.statement: JNPT rail coefficient 15.12% (FY26), CONCOR share 60%; Mundra coefficient 24.6%, share 35.4%; Pipavav coefficient 57.5%, share 48.3%; overall EXIM market share 53.9% (down from 55.2%)
items.quote: JNPT rail coefficient was 15.12%, and our share was 60%. Mundra, rail coefficient 24.6%. Our share is 35.4%. Pipavav, rail coefficient is 57.5%. Our share is 48.3%.

items.statement: Liberalized DPD and cabotage policy drove 38% increase in DPD volumes; Indian Railways reforms on transit time and cost expected soon; PSA agreement enables domestic+cabotage containers on DFC-compliant yard
items.quote: We also unveiled a liberalized DPD and cabotage policy, which was very well received by trade, and we saw a 38% increase in our DPD volumes, which is now further going to grow in this financial year also.

items.statement: West Asia crisis hit March-April volumes; recovery from May; reefer exports grew 17%; containers to Middle East (700) stopped due to conflict; Far East routes started
items.quote: Our reefer exports also saw a very good growth of 17%. It's a healthy growth. And in this financial year also, there is a good demand in reefer volumes.

items.statement: Bulk cement in tank containers targeting 1M tons in FY27; food grain container trials successful; Aushadhi Express (pharma) launched with Maersk from Hyderabad; auto parts export +17%, buffalo meat +19%, aluminum ingots +22%
items.quote: I'm quite positive that in this financial year itself, we will be able to do at least 1 million tons of bulk cement in tank containers in domestic.

items.statement: MOU with PSA for dedicated JNPA-ICD services; Aushadhi Express with Maersk; talks with GAIL and Petronet for volumes; Bharat Container Shipping Line (30% stake) targeting top 10 global by 2047
items.quote: We have signed MOU with PSA that is Port of Singapore Authority for dedicated services between JNPA and CONCOR ICDs. This will be a big driver for growth for EXIM in the coming years.

items.statement: Rail coefficient at JNPT expected to rise from 15% to 18-19% in FY27, 30-35% in 3 years; road-to-rail shift driven by double-stack savings and assured transit
items.quote: So there are quite good indications that -- and we will be actually running time table assure transit train from NCR to JNPT. And secondly, we will be tinkering with our tariff also because our company believes that without sacrificing margins, if we incur some savings, we will share those savings with our customers, part of the savings.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties (US tariffs up to 50%, West Asia crisis, global slowdown) impacted textiles, marine products, gunny bales, tiles; PAT fell 4.5% in FY26
items.quote: There are trade restrictions and tariffs by United States up to 50% were imposed during the year. And this has severely affected the volumes, especially in textiles and marine products.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; key directors present: CMD Sanjay Swarup, Dir Projects Ajit Panda, Dir Intl Mktg Vijoy Singh, Dir Finance Vivek Gupta, PED Finance Harish Chandra
items.quote: I am accompanied by Mr. Ajit Kumar Panda, Director, Projects and Services; Mr. Vijoy Kumar Singh, Director, International Marketing and Operations; Mr. Vivek Gupta, Director, Finance and CFO; and Mr. Harish Chandra, Principal Executive Director, Finance, and Company Secretary of our company.

items.statement: Bharat Container Shipping Line JV (30% stake) with SCI and ports; capital allocation confidential, going to Cabinet
items.quote: CONCOR signed MOU for Bharat Container Shipping Line, in which we have a 30% stake. We are one of the majority partners of Bharat Container Shipping Line.

items.statement: ESG initiatives: 230 LNG trucks, 5 electric RSTs, 2 electric vehicles (trial); green logistics focus
items.quote: We have taken a lot of green logistics initiatives. We have 230 LNG trucks of our own. We have 5 electric RSTs and 2 electric vehicles, which we are using for trial basis

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 23% in Q4 FY26 and 100 bps for full year FY26
items.quote: EBITDA at INR 131 crore, which is up 5%. Margins expanded by 100 -basis points to 23%.

items.statement: Print segment EBITDA margin was 23% in Q4 FY26 and 14% for full year FY26
items.quote: operating EBITDA coming at INR 97 crore with a 23% margin. For the full year, advertising revenue at INR 1,148 crore, which is an 8% growth. Circulation revenue nearly flat, operating revenue at INR 1,500 crore, which is an 8% increase and operating EBITDA came at INR 208 crore with a margin of 14%.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 10% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 8% for full year FY26 driven by yield improvement
items.quote: advertising revenue growth of 10% at INR 313 crore, circulation revenue growth of 4% at INR 51 crore, operating revenue at INR 427 crore and operating EBITDA coming at INR 97 crore with a 23% margin. For the full year, advertising revenue at INR 1,148 crore, which is an 8% growth.

items.statement: Advertising revenue growth driven by pricing/yield increases, volumes flat
items.quote: the lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volume s have been by and large flat, which have tracked the industry. So , it's basically

items.statement: Rising newsprint costs amplified by weakening rupee and supply chain disruptions remain a concern
items.quote: rising newsprint costs, amplified by a weakeni ng rupee and the prevailing global environment of supply chain disruptions, trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical volatility, remains a concern that we are managing with cost discipline.

items.statement: Surrendered six loss-making Radio frequencies to sharpen network footprint
items.quote: On Radio, we did an entire portfolio review where all the five loss -making frequencies now and one loss -making frequency earlier totalling to six loss-making frequencies - those are the frequencies that we've surrendered back to the Government of India.

items.statement: Discontinued OTTplay business; no further material losses expected
items.quote: we've decided to call it quits on OTT play. And we've been leading the investors towards this direction for the last three or four quarters.

items.statement: No further exceptional losses expected from discontinued operations; statutory changes like new labour codes could impact financials
items.quote: Are we going to take any further closure losses on discontinued operations or exceptional losses? The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes, which are announced by the Government of India.

items.statement: Other income dropped ~INR 50 crore in FY26 due to mark-to-market losses on treasury portfolio from high yield curves
items.quote: The interest income has obviously, if you have tracked the yield curves, yield curves are at a record high . The 10Y, is close to about 7% and so on and so forth. So, there are quite a few mark -to-market losses that have impacted us as on 31 st March.

items.statement: AFE asset monetization policy: active sellers, not desperate, maximize value via portfolio strategy
items.quote: We are not holding these assets for the very long term. Of course, it doesn't mean that we will flip the assets within months. But at the earliest opportunity, when we think we can maximize the value for the organization, we will sell these assets.

items.statement: Investing in Print circulation copies for market share and prioritizing Digital businesses (Digicontent Ltd.)
items.quote: We have been investing in copies for getting a certain copy share, and we will keep on doing that, which have been financed by a very handsome yield improvement. So, we will keep on investing behind the core but a lot of investment will also go behind the businesses of tomorrow primarily Digital businesses.

items.statement: No current plans to return cash to shareholders; Board prioritizing investments in core and digital businesses
items.quote: Well, there is none so far.

items.statement: Company does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance
items.quote: As per usual practice, we do not provide specific guidance on revenue or earnings projections.

items.statement: Print advertising yield improvement is the key driver of EBITDA growth
items.quote: ad. rates or ad . yields is what we call them, have increased substantially. As you know of course, it's a full algorithm, you put in certain copies, you recruit new reader s, you give a certain value proposition to advertisers and you try to have certain level of AFE deals where the new guys can come on board who hitherto would not be advertisers and so on and so forth. And then you demand a cert

items.statement: Print copy share increased marginally in select markets as conscious strategy
items.quote: Yes, on a few markets, we have increased our copy share, which is part of our conscious strategy and we plan to keep it like that. But you have to understand that if you go after copy share, there are certain short-term trade -offs that you have to do for long -term gain, which we are doing on a market -to-market basis. But broadly, our copy share has gone up marginally.

items.statement: Advertising yield sustainability uncertain due to competitive reaction
items.quote: Well, to an extent, yes, but I won't do a carte blanche on that because there's an immediate reaction, which always comes from the competition. But our hope & prayer and even the plan that we have set out for ourselves – though we don't give forward guidance – is to keep our deals at a certain level and above not below.

items.statement: Radio segment: all remaining frequencies profitable after surrendering loss-making ones
items.quote: All existing frequencies are profitable frequencies and obviously our intent is to increase the profitability as we go forward.

items.statement: Other operating income surge in HMVL due to forfeiture of AFE contractual revenue
items.quote: As you know, in our AFE business, we've got these contracts with counterparties, and there is a certain contractual revenue, which has to come in a specified period of time. If that doesn't happen, that amount stands forfeited. So, that is on account of forfeiture.

items.statement: Assetvault (AasaanWill) investment is non-cash AFE deal for marketing partnership
items.quote: On Assetvault, you are right, the revenue is pretty small at this point in time. But as explained earlier, it's again an AFE investment. It's not a cash investment, it is our AFE investment, and there are certain marketing plans that, that company has for the market of India, where we would like to give our marketing properties and partner with them in the hope that the asset will become profitabl

items.statement: OTTplay wind-down: marginal P&L impact from servicing residual subscriptions until Sep FY27; cash outflows for contract exits
items.quote: subscriptions, which have been sold on or prior to 31st March, will have to be serviced for its life, which can typically be ranging from one month to six months at any point in time. If the unit economics of that is not working out, there might be marginal losses, etc., which will basically come into the P&L for FY 2027, but that will be a very small number

items.statement: Net cash position robust, north of INR 1,000 crore
items.quote: PAT came at INR 153 crore at a margin of 8%, and our net cash position remains robust, north of INR 1,000 crore.

items.statement: Management expects a better year in FY27 vs FY26, barring unforeseen geopolitical events
items.quote: So barring unforeseen new geopolitical events that can create supply challenges, demand challenges, we expect a better year going ahead.

items.statement: Strong momentum in US scaffolding business driven by AI and tech infrastructure investments, continuing into June quarter
items.quote: We are seeing a strong momentum even going forward into the June quarter across -- and this is mainly driven by investments in AI and tech ecosystem-driven infrastructure, which is leading to increased demand uptake of scaffolding.

items.statement: Drum closures demand stable with single-digit revenue growth; China growing strongly, rest of countries at 4-5% quantity and price growth
items.quote: It is quite st able. There has been, as you saw , some increase in the quantity of drum closures sales as well this financial year compared to the last. And the pricing has also been stable

items.statement: Scaffolding margin adjusted for one-time INR20 cr steel discount is 16-17% going forward
items.quote: So if you adjust for that, the margin comes to 16%. So is that right assessment? The margin going forward is 16%, 17%, right? Navneet Kumar Saraf: Yes. That is correct

items.statement: Engineering vertical investing in AI, bottom line may not grow proportionally with top line
items.quote: Demand is very strong, which is why we see growth in revenue, but we are also investing. And as a result of our investments, there can be some slower growth in the bottom line.

items.statement: Steel prices up 25% in last 3 months but fully passed on; aluminum cost managed via backward integration
items.quote: Steel prices have increased by almost 25% over the last 3 months, but we've been able to pass them on. So there is no real pressure on margins. Same applies with aluminum.

items.statement: Scaffolding capacity up 10-15% from debottlenecking; formwork extrusion at 100% utilization; scaffolding at ~90%; Mach One at 60-70%
items.quote: We are already doing some minor capacity increases in the scaffolding division this year. We are seeing about 10% increase in scaffolding capacity just due to some debottlenecking at our end.

items.statement: Mach One order book exceeds 4.5 lakh sq meters, over 6 months of production capacity
items.quote: Even today, we are sitting on order books in excess of 4.5 lakh square meters, which is more than 6 months actually of our current production capacity.

items.statement: Mach One top clients include Lodha, Birla Estates, Godrej Properties, Mahindra, Tata, Kalpataru, Sobha; top 10-15 clients constitute 70-80% of revenue
items.quote: We are dealing with numerous national pan-India developers like Lodha, like Birla Estates, Godrej Properties, Mahindra, Tata, Kalpataru, Sobha, all of these are our customers.

items.statement: Middle East contributes ~15% of scaffolding division revenue in FY26; EU scaffolding at 1.5% of revenue, market still dull
items.quote: About 15% of our scaffolding division revenue in FY26 would have come from the Middle East.

items.statement: US tariffs: scaffolding 50% under Section 232, drum closure 27.6%; tariffs now global, no absorption needed, China at disadvantage
items.quote: Scaffolding is 50% because we fall under Section 232 and drum closure has now also been added under Section 232, and it's 25% -- 27.6% to be precise.

items.statement: Mach One inventories increased due to delayed site mobilization and approvals; not concerned as projects on track
items.quote: As a result, our inventories have also increased, but we are not concerned about this because we are in close touch with the customers.

items.statement: Engineering vertical revenue currently INR80 cr/quarter, growing 8-10% per quarter; not jumping to INR120-130 cr immediately
items.quote: Currently, it is INR80 crores a quarter. So it cannot jump from there to INR120 crores in one quarter or so. But the way it is growing, it is growing at about 8% to 10% every quarter.

items.statement: Scaffolding and formwork revenue split roughly 50-50 in FY26 at INR1,342 cr total (INR680 cr scaffolding, INR660 cr formwork)
items.quote: This year, it was roughly 50-50. So INR1,342 crores. I think about INR680 crores or so was scaffolding and about INR660 crores or so was formwork.

items.statement: Yarn business at 10% EBITDA margin, EBIT breakeven due to INR46 cr depreciation; Q1 FY27 to improve on better spreads
items.quote: EBITDA, we are doing about 10% on EBITDA level. And I think it will in the quarter 1 of this financial year, it will improve by on account of the yarn spread being better.

items.statement: Mach One competitive intensity high with new entrants; Technocraft maintains premium pricing via backward integration and buyback model
items.quote: We are the only aluminum formwork company in the world that is backward integrated with our own aluminum extrusion plant. As a result of that, we are able to provide very high quality.

items.statement: Defense vertical still in sampling and approval stage with DRDO; no revenue visibility; earlier hopes of 5-10% of sales not confirmed
items.quote: We are making samples. We are being approved by DRDO and defense Department of the government. But there is nothing that we can share with the investors as of now.

items.statement: Plastic drum closures sold INR35 cr in FY26 at margins better than metal closures; no capacity addition needed, growth depends on product acceptance
items.quote: We have sold plastic drum closure about INR35 crores in the complete year. Yes. And the margin is, if not better. It is -- actually, it is more than the drum closure margin.

items.statement: Capex requirement going forward largely nominal or INR25-30 crores maintenance capex once projects complete in FY27
items.quote: Therefore, our capex requirement going forward remains largely nominal or in the range of INR25- INR30 crores, which we call as a maintenance capex once we complete our projects in the year FY27.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased sharply up to 10% and higher for crude-linked products due to geopolitical supply constraints
items.quote: As a result, raw material prices have increased sharply in certain cases to nearby 10% and even higher in case of crude-linked products.

items.statement: Crop activity expected to improve in June as monsoons hit Indian coastline; May sluggish due to heat
items.quote: The crop activity, though, is expected to improve in the month of June as the monsoons hit the Indian coastline.

items.statement: Rs 2,500 crore already spent on copper project as advances and machinery

items.quote: So, the main reasons for this which I would like to draw attention that as you could see in our balance sheet probably our inventory has increased about Rs. 100 crores because the works which are having some milestones couldn't be completed up to that extent and the inventory got generated.

items.statement: Government payment system change to SPARSH portal causing payment delays
items.quote: Third thing is the government has changed the payment system from the state and central government alliance. There is a new portal now in the capital of every state which ensures the share of the Central government and the state government.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated PAT margin ~15% distorted by unbilled work; expect PAT margin back to 15-17% within 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Once the whole inventory is clear and every unbilled bill is done, then margin will again come to 16%-17% or minimum 15% in coming quarters. It may take to restore everything further 2 or 3 quarters.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 21%; target to raise to ~25% in FY27
items.quote: So, 21% EBITDA we have already achieved in 25-26. We will try to rectify it and raise it to about 25%.

items.statement: No fresh fund raise planned; Rs 300 crore board resolution was enabling only
items.quote: Sir, that was just a permission from the Board that we took. We did not act on it. So, it is a resolution that is valid for one year. We just had it passed in the Board so that in case any eventuality arise, we do not have to go back to the Board.

items.statement: SPARSH portal implementation by RBI Treasury delaying central/state fund releases
items.quote: So, that is called SPARSH and that is taking its gestation period and payments are still not normal because Central government has to put the share and the state government has to put the prorata share.

items.statement: Concentrated in government urban water/sewer; 7 states; no plan to diversify to private or rural sectors
items.quote: We are not going to diverge from the government sector as of now. We are not planning. And from the water sector also, we are doing 70% to 75% business from the water sector, which is likely to continue.

items.statement: Government permission delays, payment cycles, election halts, bitumen supply, heavy rainfall cited as recurring external risks
items.quote: We cannot force government's hand. If government does not give permission to excavate roads, we cannot work there.

items.statement: Pledged shares reducing steadily; target zero pledge by end of FY28
items.quote: If you will check the latest filings by the company, the pledge numbers have been reducing relatively steadily, and by the end of next year, it will be zero.

items.statement: Order inflow pipeline Rs 2,500-3,000 crore; bid win target Rs 300-400 crore in near term
items.quote: And about Rs. 3,000 crores bids are in pipeline. And soon, depending upon the data and how we bid, how we select the bidding condition, we are looking for at least Rs. 300-400 crores potential of winning the bids in this month or in the coming month.

items.statement: Management reiterated 25-30% CAGR growth target for FY27
items.quote: So we have already announced that the CAGRs of 25 to 30% have has been maintained before right from our first earning call after getting listed and we have kept the promises and the promise keeps on continuing in the same manner.

items.statement: H2 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11% from 14% due to temporary low-margin tile products
items.quote: So, we introduced new design set of products, which we wanted to increase the volumes with. We were successful in increasing the volumes, but the sustainability for the margins was not supported enough.

items.statement: New technological advancement product delayed, expected to restore margins in FY27
items.quote: And the new technological advancement product that we had already scheduled up is delayed in the production side and it will be introduced this year by which the margins will be restored and probably improved as well.

items.statement: Debtor days improved from 163 to 114 days in FY26
items.quote: debtors improved substantially from 163 days to 114 days. Trade receivable declined to approximately 63 crore despite of higher business volume, reflecting stronger cash conversion and tighter working capital control.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings reduced from 28.98 crores to 13.89 crores in FY26
items.quote: Long-term borrowings reduced from 28.98 crores to 13.89 crores. This re flected our continued focus on the prudent capital allocation, financial discipline and creating a stronger foundation for future growth

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved meaningfully by 44% in FY26
items.quote: Another encouraging trend was been the improvement in the key operating metrics. Our working capital cycle improved meaningfully by 44%.

items.statement: Upper Thane cutting and polishing facility operationalized in FY26
items.quote: Another important achievement during the year was the operationalization of our Upper Thane cutting and polishing facility. This marks our first step towards backward integration and gives us greater control over customization, quality and execution timelines.

items.statement: Upper Thane facility reduced delivery time from 10-12 days to 24 hours for customized products
items.quote: Now after importing after implementing this step, we are able to deliver that product in the same manner within 24 hours as well, because of the hands-on expe riences of the skilled labors that we have, the own control over the fine tuning of the product segment

items.statement: Premium products Marmi Bella, Nextgen Quartz and customized surfaces driving margin improvement
items.quote: So, this Marmi Bella has been introduced as a premium segment of natural imported marbles. So that is a segment apart from the regular product the base that we have. And our concentration should be well enough for improving the Guneet's previous question of improving the EBITDAs and the net margins for this year as well.

items.statement: Export focus on West and South Africa with team deployed since October 2025
items.quote: So our focus that was initiated last year, mid last year, that is October onwards, we had focused on deploying the right team specifically focusi ng on the export departme nt. They are fruitful in giving results which should be operational in the first six months of this year

items.statement: Dubai Display Center launched as gateway for GCC and Middle East expansion
items.quote: One of our most important milestones was the launch of the Dubai Display Center, which strengthens our presence in the GCC re gion and serves as a gateway for future export expansion across the Middle East and Africa

items.statement: B2B contributes 80-82% of revenue, B2C balance
items.quote: B2B has always been highest into comparatively roughly about 80-82%. Roughly about 80 to 82% in the B2B segment and the balance would be from the B2C segment.

items.statement: All products sold under MCPL brand, no white labeling
items.quote: No, it has always been MCPL brand th at is the Legis logistic product logistic network company which is serve available for all the B2B network. So yes, the products are sold in the MCPL brand

items.statement: Gas supply disruption from Iran war caused 15-20 day price increase passed to customers in March
items.quote: But we our group manufacturers were sustain could sustain the manufacturing by the quantum of production that they could pre-plan and keep it in stock with them. And also we could sustai n the same by re-preordering it. So the pricing was increased at the last few last month of March, approximately 15 to 20 days by which the impact has been passed on to the customers

items.statement: Volumes grew 23-24% overall despite geopolitical issues
items.quote: No, we have given the volumes that we had planned for. We have increased the volumes by about 23-24% roughly overall.

items.statement: AI-powered MCPL Studio platform with 2D, 3D panoramic view and photo upload for faster customer decisions

items.statement: Further Capex and expansion plans underway for FY27, announcements pending
items.quote: So yes we do have and things are on time and on place, stay tuned for more further announcements that we'll be making it in public.

items.statement: All outstanding warrants converted, last promoter group warrant converted
