items.statement: Management expects working capital improvements sustainable despite externalities
items.quote: So far we have been successful even in extreme weather conditions that the global globe is currently facing. So yes, this looks like that it will be a sustainable approach that we are successful with for over a period of years.

items.statement: Family business with old and new generation working together delivering results
items.quote: And because of the combination of the family business wherein we have the old generation as well as the new generation working together, we are able to deliver results in the right manner at the right time.

items.statement: Asset-light model allows faster new product adoption vs manufacturers requiring 6-12 months for upgrades
items.quote: For manufacturer, if you want to upgrade the to a new size or latest technology, it will take a few months for them to upgrade, or probably a year too for import ing the right machinery, getting th e right tested product out in the market

items.statement: African export markets promising with contractual obligations being finalized
items.quote: There are a few markets that have opened up for MCPL and promised the tie ups that are required in various parts of Africa. So our first focus would be African region in the West and South of Africa.

items.statement: Italian marble division successful, driving B2C growth with better margins than tiles
items.quote: So that has been a very successful division. That is one of the factor why the B2C contribution towards sale in figure wise has improved last year and will grow to improve this year too. The investments have are planning up to be deploying more in that division so that we can have better margins compared to the the tiles division.

items.statement: Service contracts with lower margins but higher volumes will continue alongside premium focus
items.quote: It will be a mix of both. I'll not deny as to will not take up the service contracts which are coming in offer plate with us with the sustained relationship that we have with the group of team members that we are working with since years.

items.statement: Management refuses to quantify steady-state EBITDA margins for FY27-29
items.quote: Specifically talking about 27, 28 or future projections, I'm sorry I'll not be able to quantify.

items.statement: Trade secret policy adopted for working capital management, further tightening planned
items.quote: So our promise was to get better on the figures that were delivered in FY25 by which 26 has always been an impr ovement and the the trade secret policy which we have adopted by which the figures have improved and it has been successful we'll be tightening on the same and getting better result is always the aim

items.statement: Target to surpass 6,000 keys by FY30 with asset-light growth strategy

From EM Bypass sale, we expect additional cash flow improvement of close to 70 crores during the course of this year.

items.statement: Launched 7 properties adding 283 keys in FY26; 3 launches in Q4 (Darjeeling, Gangtok, Katra)

items.statement: F&B revenue crossed Rs. 300 crore in FY26, contributing ~43% of total revenue

items.statement: Flurys revenue grew 29% YoY in FY26; now 110 outlets, expanding to cafes format with flagship stores
items.quote: Flurys delivered robust revenue growth of 29% year-on-year during FY26, while continuing to deepen customer engagement across markets.

items.quote: We are pleased to welcome Mr. Rohit Kakra as the new Chief Operating Officer of Flurys effective April 2026, and we continue to strengthen leadership capabilities to support the next phase of growth for the brand. Mr. Rohit Kakra brings in 23 years of experience and was previously the Chief Operating Officer at Costa Coffee and Pizza Hut.

items.statement: Interest cost at 8.35% (bank MCLR), expected to remain under control; project financing interest capitalized as IDC
items.quote: The interest cost at present is 8.35%, which is the MCLR of the bank. So, it is expected to remain under that level only. One is that. So, interest costs are under control.

items.statement: Rs. 1,500 crore funding demand over 5 years, mostly from internal accruals; cash balance ~Rs. 80 crore
items.quote: So, there is a 1500 crores demand, which is being funded mostly through internal accruals, even if I take 250 crores as an EBITDA projection for five years. So, we do not have too high fund requirement.

items.statement: Board approved 75% dividend payout reflecting balance sheet strength and growth momentum
items.quote: The 75% dividend payout approved by the board reflects the strength of our balance sheet and growth momentum.

items.quote: There have been cancellations because of the geopolitical situation and the war in the Middle East. Large significant cancellations did take place in Delhi as well as in Hyderabad. But things have stabilized now and we expect the conditions to further improve starting now.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: high double-digit top line growth, EBITDA margins towards 5%, PAT approaching FY24 levels
items.quote: Our aim is to deliver growth in FY '27 with high double-digit top line growth. EBITDA margins moving towards 5% range and PAT approaching FY '24 levels as scale benefits, operating leverage and integration benefits begin to reflect in performance.

items.statement: Non-Keralam revenue contribution increased to ~47% in FY26 from ~28% in FY23, expected to exceed 50% in coming year
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that we have achieved meaningful progress on this front with non-Keralam revenue contribution, increasing to approximately 47% in FY '26 from around 28% in FY '23.

items.quote: As part of this strategy, we completed the divestment of Honda and Piaggio business and also entered into states like Andhra, Telangana, Punjab, Maharashtra.

items.quote: On the operating profitability front, reported EBITDA for FY '26 stood at INR203.4 crores, up 16% year-on-year.

items.statement: Pectin plant commercially started 7-8 days ago; targeting at least 50% capacity utilization in current year (~INR7-8 crores revenue).
items.quote: We are quite hopeful that this year, there will be a significant -- I mean, at least 50% of the capacity can be fully utilized for the current year.

items.statement: Tetra Recart capex ~INR30 crores total (INR24 crores machine, INR6 crores building); building can accommodate 3 more machines.
items.quote: So approximately INR30-odd crores of total capex, out of which INR24-odd crores was for the machine and INR6-odd crores for the building as such.

items.statement: Frozen segment target INR300-400 crores revenue in 3-4 years; capex plan under NHB cluster development program to be finalized in ~1 month.
items.quote: Our target is next 3 to 4 years' time, this segment to become INR300 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: Frozen food segment carries ~50% gross margins; supply chain costs ~10x ambient products.
items.quote: The frozen food segment actually has around 50% gross margins.

items.statement: Pectin gross margins ~70% at 50% utilization (INR7-8 crores revenue).
items.quote: So INR7 - 8 crores of revenue is what we can actually expect at 50% utilization and the gross margins are approximately around 70%-odd of that.

items.statement: Pricing is a direct pass-through of raw material costs; inflation factor considered annually in per-tonne margin.
items.quote: As always, our pricing remains a direct pass -through of raw material movements.

items.statement: Frozen foods volume grew ~28% in FY26 driven by value-added products and U.S. market interest.
items.quote: Frozen foods continued its strong momentum, delivering volume growth of approximately 28% during FY26, supported by increasing demand for value-added products and growing interest from the U.S. market.

items.statement: Middle East demand affected by geopolitical situation in March; expect normalization over time.
items.quote: In Q4, sales volumes were affected by the geopolitical situation in March, particularly in the Middle East, while realizations remained lower due to inventory produced from the lower cost 2025 crop season.

items.statement: Rural electrification and freezer penetration (300% increase post Campa launch) driving beverage industry growth of 8-9%.
items.quote: Since last 18 months, when the Reliance launched the Campa brand, the freezer supply to across the villages has increased by 300%. That's the data I got from the big brands. So now the growth story for the beverage industry is really looking very bullish.

items.statement: GCC exposure only USD2-3 million; Europe and US shipments delayed 15 days in March due to vessel availability, since shipped in April-May.
items.quote: Our exposure in the GCC country is not much. It is around USD2 million to USD3 million. So, overall revenue wise, there is no major impact. But yes, Europe and the US, whatever dispatch we are doing, that has got affected for the last 15 days of the year.

items.statement: Spices export diversification initiated for Europe, US, Southeast Asia; pesticide compliance and contract farming required, early stage.
items.quote: We are working for some European countries and some Southeast Asia. The negotiation and sample approval process, all things going on. So as of today, it's a very preliminary stage.

items.statement: ~45% of mango production inventory carries forward to next year; domestic dispatches peak Dec-Jun, exports uniform Aug-Aug.
items.quote: overall, if Foods and you want to understand that how much stocks carry forward, approximately 45% to -- 45% roughly stocks carry forward for the next year

items.statement: Inventory increase offset by reduction in vendor advances; net working capital stable.
items.quote: If you see this year, inventory plus advance to vendor has reduced to INR29 crores. So we have taken most of the material. So if you add up both these things, there is no change. It's on the similar pattern.

items.statement: Standalone borrowings reduced by INR16 crores to INR411 crores (consolidated ~INR421 crores including Kusum).
items.quote: Borrowings have been decreased. I mean if you see the balance sheet, overall borrowing has been decreased by INR15 crores -- INR16 crores. INR16 crores. It's not increased.

items.statement: Long-term debt ~INR71-72 crores; annual repayment ~INR20 crores from internal accruals; no asset sales planned.
items.quote: Our annual commitment is around INR20 crores. So, we'll be comfortable to pay from our internal accrual, not an issue.

items.statement: FY25 PLI incentive of INR33.86 crores received and recognized in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: A key milestone during the quarter was the receipt and recognition of the FY25 PLI incentive of INR33.86 crores, reflecting the successful execution of our growth investments.

items.statement: Total PLI scheme potential INR145 crores; INR83 crores received so far; INR60 crores remaining over 2 years.
items.quote: We've received around INR83-odd crores. The total that we can actually get under the scheme is around INR145 crores. So INR60-odd crores are remaining.

items.statement: PLI scheme requires minimum 10% CAGR growth up to 15% for incentives; already covered capex, balance 2 years net accruals.
items.quote: It was a onetime commitment and payback was in 6 years with a minimum 10% CAGR growth up to maximum 15% in that year for incentives.

items.statement: Internal strategy: reduce mango pulping share from 92% to 60% (other businesses 40%) in 4-5 years without degrowing mango.
items.quote: So, the internal strategy over a period of time is to actually make the other businesses contribute 40% of the total revenue without degrowing the mango business.

items.statement: HoReCa segment growing phenomenally; started B2B supply 2 years ago, now seeing good demand.
items.quote: One segment in India is growing since a few years is the hotel, restaurant and catering business, which is called the HoReCa segment. That segment is growing in a phenomenal pace. And we are now focusing also on that segment for a B2B supply.

items.statement: El Niño impact uncertain; raw material availability not a challenge but price volatility is; evaluating pre-production for FY28 hedge.
items.quote: It's very early to say. We are hearing, we are reading -- yes, definitely, if El Niño effect being agricultural commodity is definitely going to affect -- if it is so bad as we are reading the news.

items.statement: Promoter open offer at INR147 was voluntary to consolidate >25% holding; promoter adding shares, more disclosures expected.
items.quote: Yes. So basically, yes, you have rightly -- the open offer was voluntary because we wanted to consolidate the promoter holding over 25%.

items.statement: Buyback not a priority; focus on debt reduction and working capital for growth; conserving resources.
items.quote: I think the company will need to conserve more resources, not borrow more and increase the top line should the opportunities come our way.

items.statement: Targets annual export revenues up to Rs 1,000 crore by FY27-28 with deeper Russia/China penetration, EU re-entry, and domestic value-added build-out
items.quote: This is underpinned by a medium-term roadmap to FY27-28 where we are targeting annual export revenues of up to Rs 1,000 crore, supported by deeper penetration in Russia and China and re-entry into the European Union and a measured build-out of our domestic and value-added portfolio.

items.statement: Q4 revenue grew ~25% YoY to Rs 117.24 crore on healthy export demand and product diversification
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter still grew substantially by approximately 25% year-on-year to Rs. 117.24 crore, supported by healthy export demand and continued product diversification.

items.statement: FY26 revenue rose ~38% to Rs 524.7 crore; export revenue up ~23% with volumes up ~8%
items.quote: For the full FY25-26, the picture is considerably stronger: Revenue from operations rose by approximately 38% to Rs. 524.7 crore versus Rs. 380.5 crore in FY24-25. Export revenue grew by approximately 23%, with export volumes up by almost 8%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA up ~26% to Rs 36.03 crore; PAT up ~60% to Rs 15.90 crore (EPS Rs 4.06) reflecting operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA for the year increased roughly 26% to Rs. 36.03 crore and profit after tax grew by approximately 60% to Rs. 15.90 crore, translating to an earnings per share of Rs. 4.06 crore.

items.statement: PD Curl control product delivers incremental EBITDA margins of 5-10% over base; currently low volume but scaling
items.quote: So, in this specific scenario we have seen incremental EBITDA margins in excess of 5% up to almost 10% over and above our base EBITDA.

items.statement: ~20 containers planned for Middle East in Q4; half rerouted, 5 in transit stalled/rerouted, remainder held as inventory for reprocessing
items.quote: So, we had approximately 20 containers of shipments that were originally planned for exports in the Middle East in Q4. Of that, about half of those containers had to be rerouted to alternate destinations as it was advised by our customers to pause shipments considering the escalation of the war.

items.statement: 1 MW solar plant for captive use at processing division; part commissioned in Q4, balance shortly
items.quote: The company is in the midst of setting up a one-megawatt solar power plant for captive consumption in its processing division. Part of the project has already been commissioned in Q4 and the balance will be commissioned shortly.

items.statement: Slight improvement in overall capacity utilization contributed to FY26 profitability
items.quote: Besides this, there was a slight improvement in our overall capacity utilization. Which enabled us to improve our profitability.

items.statement: Abnormal fishmeal and soya price increases hit feed margins; pilot substituting fishmeal with insect protein shows encouraging farm-level results
items.quote: So, we had initiated a pilot project in terms of R&D where we have substituted a portion of the fish meal with insect protein and this initiative has been more than a year old with results mostly at the farm level being quite successful and encouraging.

items.statement: Some feed cost increases passed to contract farming partners; aim to pass better export realizations back to them
items.quote: So, some amount of the costs are being passed on to our channel farming partners but we intend to pass on better realizations to them by ensuring that at the exports level, we generate better contracts with improved margins.

items.statement: Value-added products ~7-10% of export volume in FY26; target to double share in FY27 if markets normal
items.quote: As far as our export portfolio is considered, value-added products made up roughly 7-10% of overall volume for the year gone by. And if all export factors remain fairly normal in terms of markets and geopolitics, we are hopeful of doubling that contribution in terms of percentage by volume.

items.statement: Entered China with black tiger shrimp (new product range) working with 5 customers; added 2 new clients in Russia; no new US clients in FY26
items.quote: We also penetrated a new market in the form of China for a new product range altogether, which is black tiger shrimp. In that context, we have worked with five customers so far in the year gone by and intend to penetrate the market deeper during the current fiscal.

items.statement: Commenced sales to Hyperpure in Q4 FY26 for domestic market (raw frozen shrimp); processing plant R&D for new products targeting Indian consumers
items.quote: In this context, we are happy to share that the company has commenced sales to Hyperpure in Q4 of FY2025-26 with the initial plan for the domestic market involving selling of base products such as raw frozen shrimp.

items.statement: Export mix balanced: US+China ~40%, Russia/SE Asia/Europe/Middle East ~60%; US tariffs cut from up to 50% to 10% from Feb 2026
items.quote: The US and China make up roughly 40% of our Exports portfolio. Russia, Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Middle East make up the remaining 60%.

items.statement: India-EU FTA signed; plant EU-certified; rebuilding Europe relationships a near-term priority; benefits gradual but direction encouraging
items.quote: The India-EU opportunity has firmed up. The FTA signed recently points to substantial tariff reductions for seafood exports from India. Our plant already carries an EU certification, and given our strong historical presence in Europe, rebuilding those relationships is a near-term priority.

items.statement: Industry represented to government for relief on fishmeal exports driving up domestic prices; hopeful for intervention
items.quote: We understand that a steep increase in fish meal price has been on the backdrop of global demand for fish meal rising and a lot of exports happening from India. So, we made representations to the government as an association and we are hopeful that the government can intervene to give us and the rest of the sector some relief.

items.statement: India shrimp exports ~Rs 50,000-55,000 crore; company market share 0.5-0.75% in exports, sub-2% in feed
items.quote: Indian exports for shrimp is typically in the region of around 50,000 to 55,000 crores. And we are ranging between 0.5% to 0.75% currently.

items.statement: Key risks: volatile raw material prices, erratic weather (intense weather reports), geopolitical/tariff instability
items.quote: Typically, the kind of business that we are in benefits from stability in terms of geopolitics, tariffs, and certain other potential trade barriers. So, in the short term, I think raw material pricing being volatile across the spectrum is a risk for the sector. And weather also being erratic, I think there are certain reports that there could be intense weather during the rest of the calendar year

items.statement: Employees credited for standing by company during difficult times
items.quote: And the key contributors are also the employees who stood by us during all these difficult times.

items.statement: Exports to U.S. and Germany expected to double in next 2 years
items.quote: Our export to the U.S. and Germany will grow to 2x in the next 2 years.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR3,000 crores
items.quote: But if you look at, I guess, on an overall basis, we are expecting to cross INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to exceed 10.25%
items.quote: So we expect that we should see an improvement in the overall margin levels as well going beyond 10.25% that we have achieved last year, if we exclude the onetime impact.

items.statement: Railway revenue target INR100 crores for FY27
items.quote: And we are hoping that this year, in the railways, we should be crossing INR100 crores as far as the railways are concerned.

items.statement: Defense revenue target INR50 crores for FY27
items.quote: and we are targeting -- we are trying to see how do we cross INR50 crores this year

items.statement: Export growth of 32% expected in FY27
items.quote: Sorry, the exports will grow by 32% this year, and primarily to Germany and to U.S.A.

items.statement: New orders worth INR2,500 crores secured over 5-year program life
items.quote: The company has also secured new orders worth approximately INR2,500 crores over a program life of 5 years, providing stro ng visibility for future growth

items.statement: 40 new product launches underway, revenue impact from Q3/Q4 FY27
items.quote: There are almost about 40 launches which are taking place at the moment and all new products, and you'll see the impact coming up in the coming quarters. Actually, end of the third quarter to fourth quarter.

items.statement: FY26 reported EBITDA margin 9%, adjusted 10.25% excluding one-time impacts
items.quote: Currently, the EBITDA is hovering at around 9%, wherein the impact of Labour Code is INR11 crores and the impact of lag settlement of raw material is around INR19 crores. So if you exclude this onetime impact, the margin increases from 9-odd percent to 10.25%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA margin 7.1%, adjusted 9.8% excluding one-time impacts
items.quote: So if you include these nonrecurring impact, wh ich is there in Q4, I guess the EBITDA, which is currently appearing at 7.6%, will rise to 9.8

items.statement: 75% of customers by value agreed to monthly raw material settlement cycle
items.quote: And I am glad to share that 75% of the customers by value have already accepted our request.

items.statement: Hosur facility expected operational from September 2026 for hybrid and EV programs
items.quote: The facility is expected to become operational from September 2026 onwards and will primarily cater to hybrid and EV-related programs for key OEM customers.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu government approved INR39 crores subsidy for 10 years starting FY27
items.quote: The company has also received an approval from Tamil Nadu government for a subsidy of around INR39 crores, which will start accruing from current financial year and will be available for the next 10 years.

items.statement: Aluminum and ferrous capacity utilization around 65-75%, smaller machines near 95%
items.quote: the iron side, our capacity utilization is in the region of about, I think, 65%, 70%. Kaushalendra Verma: Yes, 75%, around. Arvind Kapur: And in the aluminum side, it's also in about the same region. And of course, it could vary from the smaller capacity machines where the utiliza tion is close to 95

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 7 days from 33 days in FY26
items.quote: Working capital days improved to 7 days from 33 days last year, while the cash flow from operations stood at INR331 crores during FY '26.

items.statement: Renegotiating raw material settlement cycle to monthly and reviewing low-margin products for price improvement
items.quote: We are under discussion with our customers to renegotiate our RM settlement cycle and also discussing renegotiating on the components, which is impacting our margin. We are also reviewing our entire portfolio of our business, specifically identificati on of the low-margin products and we will be negotiating with our customers to improve product profitability

items.statement: New programs across transmission, braking, engine and EV applications with Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Hero, Bosch, Cummins, Knorr-Bremse
items.quote: We also continue to strengthen our business pipeline with new orders across customers, including Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Hero, Bosch, Cummins and Knorr-Bremse. These programs across transmission, braking systems, engine and EV-related applications provide good visibility and are expected to support future growth over the coming years.

items.statement: Railway modernization investment of INR200,000 crores creates major opportunity
items.quote: And as railways are modernizing and INR200,000 crores are being invested on modernization of the total railways, that includes the lines and building of lines, et cetera, et cetera, we are going to be major participants there.

items.statement: Machine tools business started external sales, first sale completed recently
items.quote: So earlier, we would make them only for ourselves, but now since we had created capacity, we've also started selli ng them in the market. And we've just done our first sale very

items.statement: Geopolitical risks could impact export growth targets
items.quote: Unless, of course, the global -- the geopolitics which is happening and that brings about some disaster, I think we are ready to reach the levels that we are talking of now.

items.statement: Land monetization discussions ongoing, rejected INR700 crores offer seeking better value
items.quote: Like I mentioned last time that we were offered INR700 crores, and we had said no to that, because we were looking for a much better value, so that we could actually reward our shareholders.

items.statement: Private Markets recovery target INR250-300 crores for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: We had guided INR250 crores to INR300 crores of recovery in each of the years FY26, '27 and '28, we've achieved over INR270 crores in FY26, and we seem to be pretty much on target to be between the INR250 crores and INR300 crores number for

items.statement: Affordable Home Loans AUM growth target 25% YoY, targeting IPO by 2028-29
items.quote: Affordable Home Loans, our target, as I said, is to IPO the business by 2028, '29. The business has done very well. It's at INR3,500 crores of AUM, and we expect to grow AUM at 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: Group targets 15% revenue growth and 15% ROE at end of investment cycle
items.quote: Two most important things for us will be 15% revenue growth and 15% return on equity at the end of the investment cycle for these businesses.

items.statement: Committed to declaring 50% of PAT as dividend annually
items.quote: we are comm itted to declaring 50% of that PAT as dividend every year for our shareholders

items.statement: IPO pipeline strong at INR140,000 crores but execution slow due to FPI selling and market volatility; H2 expected better
items.quote: On the IPO front, our pipeline is at INR140,000 crores. There is a little bit of volatility in the markets that we continue to see, which was there in Q4 and Q1 of this financial year as well and until the FPI selling continues, it's becoming increasingly difficult to get IPOs done.

items.statement: Corporate credit and private equity placements expected to pick up in H2 FY27 if equity markets remain slow
items.quote: With a lag effect, usually, which is around 6 months, you see a lot of pick-up in credit and pick-up in private equity placements. So both those businesses, if equity continues to slow, will pick up even more after a 3- to 6-month lag.

items.statement: CACM closed 41 transactions worth INR95,000 crores in FY26; filed 55 IPOs worth INR140,000 crores
items.quote: We closed 41 capital markets transactions aggregating to approximately INR95,000 crores in FY26. In addition, we have filed documents for 55 IPOs aggregating to an issue size of approximately INR1,40,000 crores, and the pipeline of transactions is increasing.

items.statement: Private Markets corporate loan book INR2,685 crores, real estate INR1,100 crores, non-core INR228 crores; distressed credit investments INR3,665 crores
items.quote: We have INR2,685 crores in corporate loans. We have INR1,100 crores in real estate loans. We have a small non-core book on MSME and financial institutions, which will become zero by the end of the year, which is INR228 crores. So that's the INR4,000 crores sort of breakup.

items.statement: Wealth Management recurring AUM grew 10% YoY to INR31,000 crores; recurring proportion increased to 29%
items.quote: The recurring AUM of all our wealth businesses grew by 10% year-on-year to approximately INR31,000 crores. The proportion of recurring to total AUM has also increased to 29%.

items.statement: BlinkX digital broking investments INR40-50 crores annually being trimmed significantly; savings visible in next quarter
items.quote: We are trimming those down. We are cutting those down significantly. You'll hear more about the plans around BlinkX but you will see that number go down significantly over the next 3 to 6 months itself.

items.statement: Wealth Management RM strength up 30% YoY to 1,046; branches up 10 to 72; franchisees up to 874
items.quote: Our sales and RM strength has increased by 30% year-on-year to 1,046 employees. On physical expansion on a year-on-year basis, branches have increased by 10 to 72 branches and franchisees have increased to 874.

items.statement: Domestic mutual funds conservative on IPO pricing; issuers taking wait-and-watch approach
items.quote: We are seeing domestic mutual funds being very conservative when it comes to pricing of IPOs and transactions. And at the same time, I think there is a wait-and-watch approach all the issuers are taking.

items.statement: Wealth Management flywheel: investment banking transactions drive account opening and transactional revenue, converting to recurring revenue; reverse origination from wealth to investment banking improving
items.quote: The number of referrals we are getting now from our Wealth Management for our investment banking business also has improved, which is a very, very good sign, because there is reverse origination happening in the flywheel as well.

items.statement: CACM has highest research coverage on Street (~400 active, ~150 soft); #1-3 across products; derivative business added last year
items.quote: We have the highest research coverage on the Street. This was a tactical decision taken 2 years ago and fully executed. We're almost at 400 stocks in terms of active coverage and almost 150 stocks in terms of soft coverage. There is no Tier 1 bank on the Street, which has this kind of coverage.

items.statement: Government tax leeway for non-promoter shareholders via buybacks; actively advising clients on buyback proposals
items.quote: Also, the government has given a very good tax leeway for non-promoter shareholders to be rewarded through buybacks. So we are engaged with a lot of them, and you will see some announcements just as we have seen with some IT companies.

items.statement: Affordable Home Loans collection efficiency 99.4%, gross NPA 0.5% as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: The gross NPA stood at 0.5% and collection efficiency stood at 99.4% for March 31, 2026.

items.statement: Bajaj Allianz invested INR65 crores for 2.1% in JM Financial Home Loans at INR48/share (INR3,100 crores valuation) in June 2025
items.quote: Bajaj Allianz picked up 2.1% shares of JM Financial Home Loans Limited at INR48 per share valuation, which b enchmarked our valuation to INR3,100 crores. They invested INR65 crores

items.statement: Dividend increased per guidance; INR5.95 per share aggregate over last 4 quarters (~INR570 crores total)
items.quote: In line with our earlier guidance, we have increased the dividend to shareholders. Over the last 4 quarters, an aggregate of approximately INR5.95 per share of dividend has been paid or proposed, resulting in a distribution of approximately INR570 crores as dividend.

items.statement: Wealth Management added 80 RMs during FY26; productivity gains expected in next 3-6 months
items.quote: These people that have joined and the team that we have built up, the 80-odd RMs that we've added during the year have come in, in different times of the year or different months of the year as well. So we are expecting that a lot of the productivity gains will now start kicking in over the next 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Private Markets distressed credit recoveries on track; real estate repayments significant; non-core book to be zero by year-end
items.quote: There has been a significant amount of derisking on the balance sheet with a lot of repayments and prepayments on the real estate side. And incrementally, this year, we'll see a lot of repayments on the distressed credit side.

items.statement: CACM revenue grew 26% over 2 years (INR592 to INR946 crores); operating profit before tax grew to INR452 crores at 48% margin
items.quote: We've seen a revenue growth of 26% for the 2 years in that business. And our revenues have moved from INR592 crores to almost INR946 crores. And we've seen our operating profit before tax grow from INR328 crores to INR452 crores and a healthy margin of 48%.

items.statement: FY27 pre-sales target of Rs. 2,200 crores; Senior Living sales target to cross Rs. 700 crores
items.quote: The pre-sales target for this year is Rs. 2,200 crores that we are targeting. But I would say more importantly, I think we are really looking to grow Senior Living. Senior living is targeted to cross even Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be better than FY26; FY28 margin materially better than FY27
items.quote: But the margin profile for a full year basis in 2027 will be better than 2026. And the margin profile in FY28 will be better than 2027 overall. That's the general expectations right now.

items.statement: Targeting 20%+ reported ROE in FY27
items.quote: I think we are on track to get to more than 20% reported ROEs for the year.

items.statement: FY30 cumulative PAT target of Rs. 2,000 crores; on track to achieve
items.quote: As of now, we are on track to achieve that number. Overall, we seem to be on track.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 booking value Rs. 1,290 crores, up 225% QoQ and 124% YoY; driven by Ashiana Aaroham Gurugram launch (Rs. 833 crores)
items.quote: The value of area books stood at Rs. 1290 crores, reflecting strong growth of over 225% sequentially and 124% year-on-year growth. The performance was primarily driven by successful launch of Ashiana Aaroham Phase-I and Phase-II in Gurugram which contributed booking value of around Rs. 833 crores at launch.

items.statement: FY26 highest ever booking value Rs. 2,421 crores, up 25% YoY; Senior Living record bookings Rs. 570 crores, up 55% YoY
items.quote: FY26 was one of the strongest years in the Company's history. The Company achieved its highest ever booking value of Rs. 2,421 crores, reflecting growth of 25% year-on-year. The Senior Living segment also delivered record bookings of Rs. 570 crores during the year, registering growth of around 55% year-on-year.

items.statement: Senior Living portfolio: 5 projects to launch in next 12-24 months with GDV > Rs. 6,500 crores across Chennai, Bangalore, Bombay-Pune region
items.quote: We have picked up five projects that we need to launch in the next 12 to 24 months having a GD V (Gross Developmental Value) of more than Rs. 6,500 crores in those five projects across Chennai, Bangalore and the Bombay, Pune region

items.statement: Land bank expanded: ~96 lakh sq ft total (including recent Vadgaon 20 lakh sq ft and Bangalore 11 lakh sq ft), ~4x annual throughput
items.quote: With that, I think we get to about 96 lakh square foot in total, which is about 4x of our annual throughput right now.

items.statement: Capital allocation focused on growing business, bulk towards Senior Living; no large buybacks or dividends planned; dividends on absolute terms will grow
items.quote: So, right now the thought is deploy as much as we can in growing the business rather than returning back capital to shareholders either by form of buyback or dividends. That is the intent as of now. As I said, Senior Living is a place where I think we will deploy bulk of this capital.

items.statement: Project-level gross profit margins 35-40%; project-level margins 30-35% after 5-6% selling costs; land cost 10-20%, construction cost 40-50%, soft costs ~5% of revenue
items.quote: I would say these projects at the project level before, let's say, general administrative expenses of the corporate, should operate at about 30%-35% of margins. Now, how the corporate fixed costs will behave as a percentage will depend on total top line. But that's what we would expect to do that. I think we can look at about gross profit margins of between 35%-40% and you are looking at about 5-6

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA Rs. 35 crores, margin 10.43%; PAT Rs. 21 crores, margin 6.26%
items.quote: EBITDA for quarter stood at Rs. 35 crores registering growth of around 19% year-on-year while EBITDA margin was at 10.43%. PAT stood at Rs. 21 crores remaining broadly stable on a year-on-year basis with margin around 6.26%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA Rs. 176 crores, margin 14.85% (up 281% YoY); PAT Rs. 118 crores, margin 9.93%
items.quote: For the full year FY26, total income increased to Rs. 1,187 crores more than doubling compared to FY25 in the wake of higher deliveries. EBITDA stood at Rs. 176 crores registering growth of 281% year-on-year while EBITDA margin at 14.85%. PAT for FY26 stood at Rs. 118 crores compared to Rs. 18 crores in FY25 while PAT margin improved to 9.93%.

items.statement: Blended realization expected to move to ~Rs. 10,000/sq ft as Senior Living share increases and premiumization continues
items.quote: I would say our realizations should be in this 9,000 to 11,000 kind of a range. I would say maybe, hopefully should move to about 10,000 on a blended basis as Senior Living starts becoming a larger profile.

items.statement: Construction cost inflation expected 8-10% YoY in FY27; no inflation underwritten in project economics pre-launch; post-launch assume CPI for both cost and price
items.quote: I think we are expecting about 8-10% increase in construction costs in this financial year, on a year-on-year basis, as of now, given the information we have.

items.statement: Price points achieved leave sufficient room for margins to improve even if costs rise; faster execution hedges inflation
items.quote: I think the price points that we have been able to achieve in our projects leave sufficient room that even if costs increase, our margins will actually continue to improve on the reported basis because we have been able to lock in good prices on those projects with relatively low land costs.

items.statement: Strong residential demand, premiumization trends, preference for branded developers; Senior Living gaining traction from demographics, urbanization, community-based living preference
items.quote: The Indian real estate sector witnessed strong momentum during FY26, supported by resilient residential demand, premiumization trends and increasing preference for branded and organized developers.

items.statement: Senior Living structural demand: aging population, financially independent seniors, lower fertility, higher savings; Western/Southern/Northern India changing structurally
items.quote: Aging in India and increasing financially independent seniors in India is a fact and given. That's just how demographic profile is. People are living longer, health is better, fertility rates are lower, financial savings have increased, so seniors who retire now will have wealth rather than financial dependence on the next generation.

items.statement: EAC FY26: 226.19 lakh sq ft, up 30% YoY; Q4 FY26 EAC: 6.65 lakh sq ft, up 60% YoY; in line with committed timelines
items.quote: Execution remained robust throughout FY26 with EAC increasing 30% year-on-year to 226.19 lakhs square foot in line with project commitments and execution schedules.

items.statement: Launch pipeline FY27: Ashiana Oma (next couple months), Aaranya & Tattvam (Q4 FY27); Aaroham Phase-III; at least one phase in each Senior Living project (Advik, Amodh, Vatsalya, Swarang)
items.quote: New projects, we are looking to launch Ashiana Oma, Ashiana Tattvam, and Ashiana Aaranya. Ashiana Oma is a premium housing project in Jaipur where all approvals have been received. We should launch in the next couple of months. Ashiana Aaranya and Ashiana Tattvam are slated for launch in the Q4 of this year.

items.statement: New project launches targeted FY28: Wavarle, Vadgaon, Bangalore; deliveries build-up FY30-FY31; most phases wrapped by FY31
items.quote: The other three projects, which is Wavarle, Vadgaon and Bangalore, we are targeting to launch in FY28. There will be build-up in FY30 and FY31 deliveries and values there. Most of it will be built not through new launches of projects, but launches of existing phases.

items.statement: Pre-tax operating cash flow Q4 FY26: Rs. 167 crores (+7% YoY); FY26: Rs. 577 crores (highest ever, +34% YoY); working capital met through customer advances; construction funding only if need-based
items.quote: Further, pre-tax operating cash flow for FY26 stood at Rs. 577 crores which also was highest ever registering growth of 34% year-on-year reflecting strong sales momentum and healthy collections.

items.statement: Customer collections FY26 all-time high Rs. 1,762 crores; strong collection efficiency
items.quote: Customer collections reached an all-time high of Rs. 1762 crores during the year, supported by timely execution, successful launches and strong collection efficiency.

items.statement: Low debt, high cash position; construction mostly financed from customer advances; IFC invested Rs. 100 crores NCDs in Aaroham Gurugram
items.quote: In addition, Ashiana Aaroham Gurugram received funding support from IFC through allotment of Rs. 100 crores of listed unsecured redeemable NCDs.

items.statement: Capital allocation framework: ROE single most critical metric; GP margin ~30% key project evaluation metric; not land-banking, launching quickly
items.quote: I think we always chase profitable growth. So, the ROE remains the single most and the strongest metric. And of course, the GP margin, roughly 30% that we have talked about in the past, remains the single most critical metric basis which we evaluate the project economics.

items.statement: Maharashtra Senior Living policy 2025 encouraging but not yet operational (rules not framed, not incorporated in DCR); MAHARERA defined Senior Living marketing requirements; other states not following Maharashtra yet, some over-regulating
items.quote: The policy of Maharashtra is also not yet notified in the sense the rules are not framed, the policy framework that needs to be incorporated in the development control regulations have not yet been incorporated. So, the policy is right now, I would say, more of an intent and less of an operational policy that you can actually utilize.

items.statement: Senior Living sold mostly directly (specialized sale); channel partners limited; 50% Amodh customers from Bombay; Utsav Lavasa significant Bombay customers historically
items.quote: We will be doing it at the highest end of any Senior Living that we have done that we can tell you. And will we have channel partners I think Senior Living we have started using channel partners but the reliance on channel partners is very limited. The Senior Living market is sold mostly directly because it's more of a specialized sale to a specialized customer.

items.statement: Senior Living: more serious players growing industry size; Ashiana differentiates via brand equity, delivery track record, operational capability, large-scale projects (12-15 acres) with superior amenities vs typical 2-4 acre projects
items.quote: I think overall the size of the industry grows. Rather than thinking it through a lens that more and more competition will arise, I think more and more serious players join in. I think the industry overall, the size will increase, it will gain, and players like us or for that matter any other serious player will also stand to gain.

items.statement: Key risks: execution/delivery timeline slippage (materials supply, labor shortages), Senior Living growth slower than expected, managerial bandwidth constraints, market selection errors, approval delays, construction cost escalation
items.quote: Achieving delivery timelines right now. I think the supply of materials, our scaling up of execution, some labor shortages that people are talking about. Meeting the delivery timelines will be our biggest sort of thing.

items.statement: Signs of oversupply visible in Gurugram (heavy launches, unsold inventory up 2 quarters) and Pune; if continues 4 more quarters will be oversupplied; Bhiwadi, Jamshedpur, Jaipur no oversupply yet
items.quote: There is no oversupply yet. Signs of some oversupply in Gurugram and Pune are visible. Whereby in last two quarters in Gurugram we saw very heavy launches so absolute unsold inventories increased substantially for two quarters in a row.

items.statement: Senior Living sales CAGR >50% over last 5 years (Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 570 crores)
items.quote: We have gone from Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 570 crores in a 5-year period in Senior Living. I think the key metric that we are looking for pre-sales is to really, really revive Senior Living.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guided at 12-13% for FY27 in INR terms
items.quote: Overall company as a whole, we should be able to, including Unichem and put together around 12% to 13% kind of growth on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 22-22.3% for FY27
items.quote: And on EBITDA side from 20.7% currently on a consolidated basis, I think it shoul d be almost around 22% or 22.3% something more or less on that line

items.statement: Unichem EBITDA margin guided at 12-13% for FY27
items.quote: We foresee that I think Unichem margin may become around 12% to 13% in the current financial year from that level.

items.statement: Unichem US business growth guided at 10% for FY27
items.quote: And I think in current financial year, their U.S. business should grow by around 10%.

items.statement: Ipca standalone EBITDA margin improvement guided at 1-1.25% for FY27
items.quote: I have given the projections also of guidelines for the EBITDA margin for whole of the year that it should -- it will move by around 1% to 1.25% in the current financial year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 25.18% in FY26 from 22.66% in FY25
items.quote: And for the financial year March '26, overall EBITDA margin stand-alone for co mpany has gone up to around 25.18% as against 22.66% in March '26, an overall improvement of around 2.52

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 20.72% in FY26 from 19.94% in FY25
items.quote: And for all of the financial year, March '26, EBITDA margins has improved to around 20.72% a s against 19.94% in March '25, an improvement of around 1.78

items.statement: Unichem EBITDA margin declined from 12% to 8% in FY26
items.quote: But as far as Unichem is concerned, their overall EBITDA margins has decl ined from 12% to around 8% and their turnover has not moved up

items.statement: Overall material costs expected to rise 10-12% in FY27 due to supply chain disruptions
items.quote: overall, I se e if current end of petroleum prices remain, overall material costs should rise by almost around 10% to 12

items.statement: Domestic price hike of 6-7% planned for FY27 to offset input cost inflation
items.quote: Looking at the overall input cost increase, we -- this year price rise a little higher, may be around 6% to 7% to offset the kind of price increase which has happened at the marketplace.

items.statement: Freight costs increased ~25% in Q4 FY26 due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: Overall, I think our freight cost has moved up by almost, I think, in the fourth quarter by almost around 25%.

items.statement: Domestic formulation grew 12% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in FY26
items.quote: Our domestic formulation business in Q4 FY26 has delivered a growth of around 12%. Business was at around INR853 crores as against INR764 crores in Q4 2025.

items.statement: Export formulation grew 9% in FY26
items.quote: Our export formulation business has delivered a growth of around 9% for the financial year '26 to around INR2,083 crores from INR1,919 crores.

items.statement: US business grew 14% in FY26 to INR1,567 crores
items.quote: Overall, for the whole of the financial year, U.S. business is around INR1,567 crores as against INR1,379 crores last year. So U.S. has given a growth of around 14% on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Generic formulation grew 17% in FY26 excluding tenders
items.quote: Generic business, excluding tenders, has delivered growth of around 17% for the financial year to around INR1,149 crores from INR982 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Institutional business declined 24% in FY26 to INR270 crores
items.quote: Our Institutional business has declined during the year to around INR270 crores from around INR355 crores in last financial year.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by product mix shift toward domestic, ROW, cardiac and generic businesses
items.quote: The improvement in overall margins is by and large because of product mix changes. Domestic business is doing good. ROW market busine ss is doing good. Cardiac business proportions has moved

items.statement: Pisgah Labs formulation facility in US expected to commission in Q4 FY27
items.quote: I think probably I think in the fourth quarter of the current financia l year, they should be able to ready to commission the plant

items.statement: Ipca inventory and receivables barely consumed cash in last 2 years
items.quote: If you look at overall last 2 years, if you look at '25 and '26 by large, put together, our inventory is at the inventory and receivables entire -- there's hardly any money has been put in overall in working capital.

items.statement: Unichem shifted from 40% air shipments to 4-5% to reduce logistics cost
items.quote: Significant amount of air shipment was there in Unichem maybe a year back to almost around 40% kind of shipment was moving by air. Now it's hardly around 4%, 5% kind of shipments ar e moving it

items.statement: Six Ipca brands among top 300 in industry; market share improved to 2.09% in MAT March 2026
items.quote: Six of our brands are featuring among the top 300 brands in the industry. In both chronic and acute segment, we are continuously beating the market.

items.statement: Krebs Bio Nellore plant turned EBITDA positive; other plant has polishing department issues
items.quote: One of their plant, which is at Nellore has started EBITDA positive. Other plant, there are certain concerns going on right now as far as polishing departments are concerned.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Iran-US, Strait of Hormuz) driving freight cost inflation and cargo availability issues
items.quote: So that will have some impact on the overall number on the profitability till the time this issue of -- issue remains of Iran-U.S. kind of conflict, which is currently happening, the Strait of Hormuz and all that kind of thing.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR3,400-3,500 crores; PAT guidance INR700-750 crores including Adcock share
items.value: INR3,400-3,500 crores revenue; INR700-750 crores PAT
items.quote: Our expectation is, Rahul, that we should do about INR3,400 crores to INR3,500 crores of revenue. Our PAT expectation is between INR700 crores to INR750 crores.

items.statement: Adcock Ingram FY27 revenue $580-600 million; PAT $47-48 million subject to FX
items.quote: And in addition to that, our South African associate firm should do, depending on the exchange rate, about $580 million to $600 million of revenue. And the PAT expectation of that is about $47 million to $48 million

items.statement: Earnings to compound 15-25% annually from FY28 onwards after FY27 base year
items.quote: I think we see that our earnings should compound around 15% to 25% every year starting from '28. So '27 will be a base year where we'll settle around INR700 crores, INR750 crores.

items.statement: FY27 margins to contract significantly; PAT to drop by half from FY26 INR1,400 crores to INR700-750 crores
items.quote: I think we've given guidance. I think this year it's going to decline. So as I said, there will be a dip in our earnings this year. This year, I mean, March, obviously, we did about INR1,400 crores PAT, as you're aware. So it's going to drop by half.

items.statement: Revlimid decline drove Q4 FY26 revenue drop; Middle East war caused freight cost increase but supply managed
items.quote: This quarter, First question was what is the impact? I think as you rightly pointed out, there's an impact of Revlimid that there's a decline. Second question was, did we have an impact of Middle East? We were able to supply the product. We had some challenges, but we were able to supply. But there's been an increase in the freight expenses because we had to reroute from our traditional carriers,

items.statement: Q4 other expenses up due to R&D spend and INR20-30 crores engineering write-down
items.quote: Yes. So R&D and engineering write-down would be around INR20 crores to INR30 crores. And R&D would be the remaining -- large part of the remaining would be the R&D.

items.statement: FY27 R&D spend expected at 7-9% of revenue; baked into PAT guidance
items.quote: In terms of like R&D expenditure next year, I think we expect to spend about 7% to 9%. And in terms of earnings, we have already budgeted that. And I think our PAT assumes this expenditure.

items.statement: Agrochem input raw material costs up 25-30% due to West Asia war; domestic business more impacted than exports
items.quote: First, one of the things like which Mr. Rajeev also mentioned earlier, the material costs are going up, right? So we have already seen 25% to 30% increase in the input raw materials.

items.statement: Semaglutide vial launched day-1 in India; pen launched month later; vial doing INR2 crores/month; annualized target INR75-100 crores
items.quote: We are thinking that we should be able to do about INR75 crores to INR100 crores annualized over the year. We'll be able to achieve it. This is our expectations.

items.statement: Pomalidomide launch competitive with 4-5 generics; no meaningful revenue bump in Q4
items.quote: I didn't see a bump honestly, Rahul. It's fairly competitive. we had a little bit of a sale, but nothing substantial that can make a meaningful impact on the earnings. It was a reasonable launch, I think we launched with multiple generics, even though namesake it's an exclusivity, but I think we had multiple generics in the first wave. I think 4 or 5 guys had exclusivity.

items.statement: Semaglutide India sales via partners Eris and Glenmark; combined run rate INR4-5 crores/month including partners
items.quote: And our partners, I think our sale, if you see, you will be having about INR4 crores to INR5 crores bump in our earnings, including our partners.

items.statement: Three US FDA facilities inspected and cleared in 2025 (Kothur, Chennai, Mekaguda); Vizag pending inspection
items.quote: We have 4 U.S. FDA facilities in our system. We have 2 API plants and 2 finished dosage factories. In the year 2025, we had inspections in 3 of them. Kothur, which is our formulation facility; Chennai, which is our API facility; and Mekaguda, which is our API facility. So all 3 got inspected, all 3 got cleared and we got EIRs. Vizag is a facility that has not had an inspection, I think nearly, I t

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary FY26 revenue ~INR280 crores; targeting $55-60 million in FY27
items.quote: I think our Brazil turnover of our sub this year was about INR257 crores, plus we have some billing directly from India. So maybe that was about INR30 crores. I don't recollect the number, about INR280 crores. So we are expecting that business should go to INR55 million to INR60 million this year.

items.statement: Canada subsidiary FY26 revenue INR229 crores; expecting 10-15% growth in FY27
items.quote: Canada, we are expecting will grow around 10% to 15%. It's already a fairly comfortable business. We have a couple of big launches, but that's in '27, '28, not in '26, '27. So that's one. Then obviously, South Africa is going to get added. So I think that' s fair. I think these are the major ones that are driving.

items.statement: Actively pursuing 1-2 large acquisitions with INR2,400 crores net cash; targeting FY27 close but nothing finalized
items.quote: We are looking at a couple of transactions. Yes, sure. I think as Amit said, we have about INR2,400 crores net cash. So very comfortable we can look at 1 or 2 large acquisitions. So we're looking at different things. As of now, I don't have an update, but hopefully, we'll be able to achieve something in this financial year as well.

items.statement: 8 million USD investment in eGenesis (xenotransplantation); 2 human transplants done with 6-month survival; more transplants expected in 12-18 months
items.quote: The other ones, primarily, I think the biggest one that we have done is we've done an 8 million investment in eGenesis. That is probably the most exciting of our innovative pipeline. So that you've probably seen the news. They are the first company in the world, which has done a genetically modified pig kidney, which was transplanted into human being. They have done 2 patients so far. And the pati

items.statement: US filings: 7-8 in FY26 with no major first-to-files; targeting 8-9 filings in FY27 with 1-2 complex/first-to-file
items.quote: I think we've done about 7 to 8 filings in the U.S. And good ones, we didn't hit any major first to files. Hopefully, this year, we are trying another 8, 9. So trying to target a couple of complex and first to files. Hopefully, we'll have 1 or 2 this year.

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences FY26 revenue INR140 crores vs INR60 crores FY25; demerger underway for focused approach
items.quote: So in terms of sale, let's say, this year, we ended up close to INR140 crores, right? And as opposed to a declared number for last year was about INR60 crores.

items.statement: No buyback planned; cash reserved for acquisitions to diversify earnings and reduce volatility
items.quote: No. I'll tell you the reason for that is because my personal belief is this cash should be used for an acquisition, which will give us more long -term return. I think there are opportunities where we can diversify our portfolio and build a stronger global footprint company.

items.statement: FY27 effective tax rate ~25% including surcharge under new tax regime
items.quote: So, including the surcharge, it would be around 25%.

items.statement: Group net cash INR2,400 crores at end of FY26
items.quote: Yes. So net cash would be around INR2,400 crores at a group level.

items.statement: Business inherently cyclical with roller-coaster earnings; acceptance of volatility needed; diversification strategy to reduce but not eliminate
items.quote: See, Manohar. let me answer this in a way that you're comfortable. See, the nature is you need to accept that certain businesses are roller coaster. I think our communication has been very clear that you're going to have a couple of good years, then you'll only have 1 or 2 years where it's going to dip. That's the nature of this business.

items.statement: Adcock Ingram stake at 35%; option to increase when major shareholder offers; strategic for South Africa market access
items.quote: And right now, our position in Adcock is about 35%. Hopefully, over a period of time, we'll be able to increase our shareholding as a nd when major shareholder gives us an opportunity. I think that's the arrangement that we have.

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences adding people, products, and channel partners to drive growth
items.quote: So all these activities are going on. So I think we're fairly confident going forward. And that's also one of the main reasons for demerging and having more focus on the business.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR816.9 crores vs INR1,287.3 crores YoY; PAT INR269 crores vs INR406 crores YoY
items.quote: For the fourth quarter, which ended March 31, 2026, the company recorded a net revenue of INR816.9 crores on a consolidated basis as against INR1,287.3 crores during fourth quarter of last year. The profit for the fourth quarter on a consolidated basis was INR269 crores, including the share of profit of associates, as against INR406 crores same period last year.

items.statement: Management targets 18-20% consolidated EBITDA margin for FY2026-2029
items.quote: We are targeting to maintain around 18% to 20% overall, the profitability of EBITDA in the coming years 2026, 2027, and 2028, 2029.

items.statement: Management estimates around Rs 50 crore capex for future expansions, still evaluating alternatives
items.quote: As we look ahead, management estimates around 50 crore capital could be required to support future expansions, however the management is still evaluating its alternatives as of now.

items.statement: Healthcare demand growing due to rising life expectancy, diabetes prevalence, and preventive care awareness
items.quote: Rising life expectancy, increasing prevalence of diabetes and age-related vision disorders, greater awareness of preventive health care, and improving affordability of specialized treatment continue to support demand across the sector.

items.statement: Hospital segment has ~70% gross profit and 15% operating profit; listed peers at ~20% EBITDA
items.quote: In the hospital segment, we have around 70% of our GP and 15% of our overall operating profit, but as we compare the other hospitals, listed hospitals, we can find around 20% of the EBITDA we can find with other hospitals.

items.statement: Healthcare revenue grew with higher patient volume, procedures, utilization, and clinical activity
items.quote: Across our healthcare operations, we witnessed growth in patient volume, procedures, utilization levels, and overall clinical activity.

items.statement: Existing facilities in Kerala and Chennai strengthened performance via improved utilization, doctor relationships, and procedure intensity
items.quote: Existing facilities across Kerala and Abate AS Industries June 3, 2026 Chennai strengthened our operating performance during the year, benefiting from improved utilization levels, expanding doctors’ relationship, and increasing procedure intensity

items.statement: Trade receivables increased with healthcare scaling; TPA and institutional settlement cycles affect collections
items.quote: Trade receivable increased during the year as healthcare platform continued to scale, while healthcare receivables are naturally influenced by TPA and institutional settlement cycles.

items.statement: Debt levels remain manageable, providing flexibility for future expansion opportunities
items.quote: Debt level remains manageable and provides flexibility for future expansion opportunities.

items.statement: Capex to be funded prudently while maintaining strong balance sheet, positive cash flow, and low leverage
items.quote: We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet, positive cash flow, and low leverage provide us with flexibility, but we intend to deploy capital very prudently.

items.statement: Healthcare contributes ~22% of revenue; long-term target 70-80% as dominant profitability driver
items.quote: Healthcare currently contributes approximately 22% of consolidated revenue, but its strategic significance extends far beyond its current revenue share.

items.statement: Positive operating cash flow of Rs 6.1 crore in FY2026 vs negative in FY2025; intends to improve cash conversion and collections
items.quote: The company moved from negative operating cash flow in FY2025 to positive operating cash flow of approximately Rs.6.1 Crores in FY2026.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 161.68 crore, up 67% YoY; PAT Rs 12.3 crore, up 10x YoY
items.quote: Consolidated revenue increased to approximately Rs.161.8 Crores compared to Rs.96.6 Crores in FY2025, representing growth of nearly 67% year-on-year.

items.statement: Net worth increased to approximately Rs 199 crore despite continued growth investments
items.quote: Net worth increased to approximately Rs.199 Crores despite continued investment in growth initiatives.

items.statement: Focus on organic expansion, capacity optimization, strategic partnerships, and selective acquisitions to build healthcare-led platform
items.quote: The company will continue to pursue growth through a combination of organic expansion, capacity optimization, strategic partnerships, and selective acquisitions, where they strengthen the overall healthcare ecosystem.

items.statement: Bahrain operations provide GCC relationships, talent pool, and long-term healthcare partnership opportunities
items.quote: The GCC presence offers access to regional relationships, healthcare talent pool, and potential long-term opportunities in healthcare service and partnerships.

items.statement: Education segment with nearly two decades of optometry and healthcare training creates talent ecosystem supporting healthcare network
items.quote: Through nearly two decades of optometry and healthcare training initiative, Abate has developed a talent ecosystem that supports the healthcare network.

items.statement: Medium to long-term conductor EBITDA margin guidance of INR35,000-36,000 per metric ton plus tailwinds
items.quote: based on the historical EBITDA margin that we have made, we expect that from a medium to long-term perspective, our conductor margins could be in the range of INR35,000 to INR36,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR1,500 crores, up from INR740 crores in FY26
items.quote: We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex breakup: Conductor INR400 crores, Oil INR200 crores, Cable INR850 crores
items.quote: Around INR400 crores would be coming from conductor division, around INR200-odd crores on oil division, and cable would be in the range of INR850 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization: Conductor 90-95%, Cable 85-90%, Oil 65-70%, Lubricants 85-90%
items.quote: on the conductor division, our capacity utilization currently will be about 90% to 95%. And similarly, for cables, it could be close to about 85% to 90%. Oil division, as the operation are not so capital intensive, we would have enough capacity because it would be in the range of 65% to 70% capacity.

items.statement: Conductor order book at INR7,671 crores as of March 31, FY26 order inflow INR11,450 crores
items.quote: Order inflow during the year came in at INR11,450 crores. The order book as on March 31 stands at a healthy INR7,671 crores.

items.statement: Cable division pending order book at approximately INR1,800 crores
items.quote: The pending order remains at approximately INR1,800 crores.

items.statement: Short-term slowdown expected due to higher metal prices, freight costs, war premiums, manpower issues, and domestic capacity additions creating pricing pressure
items.quote: the short-term period, as mentioned, will see slowing demand. And there are several factors for this. You have significantly higher metal prices. Added to that are higher premiums both for aluminum and copper. There is higher freight costs involved, including the war premiums that have been applied on all export shipments

items.statement: U.S. market showing strong traction led by data center opportunity; supplied 3 major U.S. data center projects worth ~$15 million in cables
items.quote: We've supplied to 3 major data center projects so far in the U.S. The total of cables that have gone in there is in the range of about $15 million. And with this, we are now slowly getting more and more access and RFQs which we are being asked to bid upon.

items.statement: Medium-sized U.S. data center requires $25-30 million worth of cables; India 50MW facility needs INR2 crores cables
items.quote: a medium-sized data center that you would supply in the U.S. would be taking about $10 million to $12 million worth of cables -- of just the medium voltage cable. And you would probably have something equivalent in terms of the other low voltage cables in this. About $25 million, $30 million for a medium-sized data center in the U.S.

items.statement: Cable division EBITDA margin 10.2% for FY26 vs 10.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA post forex grew by 27.1% to INR633 crores at a margin of 10.2%.

items.statement: Aluminum premium (MJP) increased, freight costs up, LME-SHFE spread $330-360/ton for aluminum creating Chinese competition
items.quote: There is a fairly large difference between LME and the Shanghai Metal Exchange, what we call the SHFE prices which, for aluminum, has increased to about $330 to $360 a ton.

items.statement: Specialty polymer supply disrupted from Middle East (Abu Dhabi) plants due to war; prices increased for aluminum, copper, polymers
items.quote: There's clearly been an impact from the war on both the price and availability of specialty polymers, many of this were being sourced from multinational plants that are located in the Middle East area, notably in Abu Dhabi.

items.statement: B2B channel business crossed INR500 crores in second year; added 120 B2C and 25 B2B distributors
items.quote: Our B2B channel business which we have started, this is only the second year of its operation, has now crossed INR500 crores. We also expanded our distribution network by adding 120 new B2C distributors and 25 new B2B distributors.

items.statement: APAR sole HVDC transformer oil supplier to Hitachi Energy, GE, Siemens; orders to come in FY27-FY28
items.quote: Fortunately, the 2 main players in this -- or rather, the 3 main players in this are Hitachi Energy, your GE and Siemens. And APAR is the principal and only supplier to all of these 3 companies so far in terms of the HVDC transformer oil.

items.statement: UltraTech/Aditya Birla Group entering building wires segment; Adani Group focused on light-duty cables; APAR focused on specialty cables
items.quote: After Ultra Tech disrupted the paints market, now they are investing and wanting to launch basically wires. We see our strength really in cables and especially in the specialty cables for all the segments that I mentioned to you.

items.statement: India non-fossil capacity 250-270 GW (3rd largest globally); FY26 solar addition 54 GW, wind 6 GW; transmission addition 113,000 MVA (30% YoY)
items.quote: There has been a substantial increase in the clean energy additions which have happened, the non-fossil fuel-based capacity additions, which for the last quarter has been 50 gigawatts plus, which is the highest ever in a financial year. This brings the country's total non-fossil capacity to anywhere between 250 crores and 270 crores

items.statement: India data center capacity 1.5-1.7 GW currently, expected 5 GW by 2030 (base) or 7-8 GW (optimistic); $30B+ investment
items.quote: The current data center capacity in India is anywhere between 1.5 and 1.7 gigawatts, which is expected to scale in a base case to 5 gigawatts by 2030 with a more optimistic estimate going up to 7 to 8 gigawatts. This will attract more than 30 billion in investments

items.statement: Middle East war disrupting supply chains, freight, refinery operations; Iraq conductor deliveries pushed out; transformer oil shipments to Saudi/Kuwait halted in March-April
items.quote: I see that the Middle East business will continue to remain a little bit subdued until this war gets completed. There's also an impact in the Conductor division where we have certain contracts with Iraq and some of these places, where the deliveries wil l get pushed out until there's a resolution over here

items.statement: Manpower issues at project sites due to elections in East/Northeast India impacting goods transit and port operations
items.quote: There have been several manpower issues in the recent months at various project sites with the elections coming up in the East, and this has impacted the transit of goods to some extent within the country, but much larger in the form of the operation of the ports.

items.statement: Targeting 10% YoY volume growth in Conductor, 25% YoY growth in Cable business
items.quote: Overall figures, we are continuing to look at a 10% growth year-on-year on our Conductor side by volume. We are looking -- continuing to look at growing by 25% a year in our cable side of the business as well.

items.statement: CTC conductor exports starting with Middle East approvals; working on Europe and U.S. approvals for FY27-FY28
items.quote: Initially, we have got approvals from Middle East manufacturers and has started exporting to them. We are now working towards getting approvals in Europe and the United States as well. So as you see, as we look at FY27 and FY28, we will want to broad base ourselves and look at exports.

items.statement: Management plans to increase royalty rate by 10-15% annually alongside ~10% volume growth
items.quote: Going forward, we are also planning to increase 10% to 15% every year along with a volume growth of around 10%, which we are achieving from last 2, 3 years.

items.statement: FY26 profit before tax margin was 13.8%
items.quote: Profit before tax margin stood at 13.8% for FY26.

items.statement: FY26 franchisee volume grew 10% to 37.9 lakh metric tons
items.quote: Our steel volume from franchisee route have stood at 37.9 lakh metric tons in FY26 as compared to 34.4 lakh metric tons in FY25 year-on-year growth of 10%.

items.statement: No new franchisee units planned; focus on expanding capacity of existing units
items.quote: We are focusing on the volume growth of the existing units. We are not inclined to add new units, but inclined to increase the capacity of existing units.

items.statement: Own plant capacity 1.25 lakh metric tons at 100% utilization; franchisee network capacity ~5 million metric tons
items.value: 1.25 lakh metric tons own; ~5 million metric tons franchisee
items.quote: We have only one plant from where we are catering to Delhi and NCR market. The capacity is around 1.25 lakh metric tons of our plant, which we are utilizing 100%.

items.statement: Royalty rate increased to INR435/ton in FY26 from INR398/ton in FY25
items.quote: This year, the average rate is INR435 per metric ton which was INR398 last year.

items.statement: India steel consumption grew high single-digit in FY26; structural demand from infra, housing, urban development
items.quote: India witnessed high single-digit growth in steel consumption during FY26, reflecting healthy underlying demand across key end user segments, including real estate, infrastructure and industrials.

items.statement: Dealer network expanded to over 12,500 dealers across India
items.quote: We now have over 12,500 dealers spread across India.

items.statement: Competes nationally with Tata Steel, Jindal; claims 20% retail branded TMT market share
items.quote: On the estimated basis, we are calculating retail branded market share is 20% of Kamdhenu brand product, retail branded.

items.statement: Government capital outlay of INR12.2 lakh crores in union budget supports construction activity
items.quote: The government has signalled its commitment to capital formation through a capital investment outlay of INR12.2 lakh crores announced in the union budget which is expected to act as a strong multiplier for construction activity and allied industries.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free as on June 31 March 2026.

items.statement: Board announced dividend of INR0.40 per share (40% of face value)
items.quote: The Board has decided to announce a dividend of INR0.40 per share i.e., 40% of the face value of INR1 each.

items.statement: Treasury policy being framed for INR300+ crores cash; no further paint business investment planned
items.quote: We are working on that. We are framing a policy for treasury and we are planning on that how we can reward to our shareholders.

items.statement: Invested INR20 crores in paint business in March 2026 for 4% equity; no further infusion planned
items.quote: In fact, this is only the investment, which we are planned, because the rate of the share was so low. And with the investment of INR20 crores, we have increased the equity of 4% in this business.

items.statement: Royalty income grew 25% to INR175 crores in FY26 driven by rate increase and volume growth
items.quote: Royalty income through franchisee stood at INR175 crores in FY26 as compared to INR139 crores in FY25, a growth of 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: Brand premium averages INR2,600/ton nationally; up to INR6,000/ton in some states
items.quote: Today, in all over India, our premium is around INR2,600 per ton. In some states, our goods are sold for INR6,000 per ton extra, which is the best local brand there.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions creating volatility in crude oil and natural gas costs, pressuring margins near-term
items.quote: Geopolitical disruptions continued to create volatility in other key input costs, particularly crude oil and natural gas, which have a meaningful bearing on overall cost structure across the steel industry.

items.statement: Domestic iron ore prices trended up in FY26; global iron ore stable; crude oil and gas volatile
items.quote: Domestic iron ore prices have trended upwards supported by an up cycle driven by strong domestic demand. While global iron ore prices have remained relatively stable.

items.statement: Investing in dealer training, support and technology-enabled tools to strengthen relationships
items.quote: We are also investing in strengthening the quality of our dealer relationship through training, support and technology-enabled tools that help dealer manage their business more effectively.

items.statement: South region identified as underpenetrated at 15% of volume; North 31%, East 35%, West 19%
items.quote: In North, we have 31%, East, we have 35%, West we have 19%, and South, we have 15% on the overall volume. So obviously, we are planning to increase our market share in the South.

items.statement: Gokul Jaykrishna stepped down as CEO after 8 years, remains Managing Director; Arjun Jaykrishna appointed CEO
items.quote: As of the last Board meeting, I stepped down as the CEO of Asahi Songwon Colors Limited, and it's been an amazing journey of eight years as a CEO and 17 years as Managing Director.

items.statement: Management targets AZO EBITDA margin ~13% and API EBITDA margin 15-16% at steady state
items.quote: For both answering on EBITDAs for both the ATC as well as Atlas business, we would guide that Management would like to target EBITDA margin of about 13% of the AZO business. And eventually, if we get the API business right, 15% to 16% in the API business going forward.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6% from 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25
