items.quote: The EBITDA margin as well expanded to 15.6% in Q4 FY26 compared to 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25, once again representing an expansion of 407 basis points year-on-year and 702 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA margin slightly compressed to 10.43% from 10.63% in FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the year was Rs. 10.43% compared to Rs. 10.63% in FY25, a small compression of 21 basis points.

items.statement: Blue Pigment margin improvement driven by stronger realization supported by elevated raw material prices from geopolitical volatility
items.quote: The volume growth was modest, and a meaningful portion of the improvement was driven by stronger realization, supported by elevated raw material prices aimed at ongoing geopolitical volatility.

items.statement: US tariff reduction led to revival in US and global export demand for Blue and AZO pigments
items.quote: We have seen a revival in that. So, our US business, once the tariff has been reduced again, it has again started to improve.

items.statement: AZO expansion CAPEX Rs. 10-15 crores to increase capacity 1.5x, financed via internal accruals; civil infrastructure already in place
items.quote: we would be expecting an expansion of much better ROC, ROE for the investment because we will be investing somewhere around, I think, Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 15 crores. And this would help us boost the capacity by almost, it wo uld go to 1.5x

items.statement: CEP Certification for API business expected by end of current financial year (FY27) to support export growth
items.quote: progress is being made towards achieving our CEP Certification and we are confident that by the end of the current financial year we would be able to get this certification which will be a milestone that will support volume growth and access to more profitable export segments.

items.statement: AZO segment achieved full-year EBITDA positivity and cash break-even in FY26
items.quote: Encouragingly, the AZO segment achieved EBITDA positivity for the full financial year as 2020. The business has also reached cash break even during the year.

items.statement: API segment achieved full-year EBITDA positivity in FY26
items.quote: The API segment also achieved EBITDA positivity for the full year FY26.

items.statement: New API product Etoricoxib commercialized; R&D exploring additional products beyond Pregabalin (60-70% of API revenue)
items.quote: we have been able to execute a few products that we have successfully developed in the R&D, taken in the plant and now commercialized as well, like Etoricoxib, for example.

items.statement: Re-engaging US AZO customers after tariff reduction; positive discussions with prospective US customers during recent visit
items.quote: I made a visit to the US as well, where I got the opportunity to meet several of our prospective customers. And this was just two weeks back. And we have had positive discussions. And becau se of the tariff going down once again, I have been able to open up some discussions

items.statement: Chinese competition in AZO intensified after US-China tariff war; structural opportunity if China-US relations disrupt again in 3-5 years
items.quote: directionally we continue to believe over the next 3-5 years there could be any time a big opportunity where China and US have a major disruption in relations and this could present an opportunity for India in the AZO business to suddenly leapfrog and grow.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility, elevated raw material costs, and competitive pressures remain key risks; demand environment still below pre-tariff levels
items.quote: The path ahead requires navigating a still uncertain global environment with geopolitical volat ility, elevated raw material costs, and competitive pressures remaining

items.statement: Confident of sustained strong EBITDA-centered performance in Blue business in coming year; target Rs. 1000 crore revenue in next few years
items.quote: We will certainly be looking to grow, and we certainly have the goal of reaching Rs. 1000 crore as a company within the next few years.

items.statement: Cash flows strong across all four units supporting faster debt reduction
items.quote: Cash flows have been strong through all the verticals, all the four units. So, I think it positions the company in a very good way over the next three years to strategize growth.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR40-50 crores and for FY28 is INR35-40 crores.
items.quote: Yes, so Yes, the capex for FY27 most likely would be in the range from INR40 crores to INR50 crores and for FY28 another would be in between INR35 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Extrusion capacity increased from 10,000 to 24,000 tons per annum with the new Italian press at Pithampur; Dewas facility acquired for tubing business.
items.quote: During the year, we successfully commissioned the new Italian extrusion press at Pithampur, increasing our extrusion capacity from 10,000 tons per annum to 24,000 tons per annum. We also completed the acquisition and refurbishment of the Dewas facility, which will become the foundation for our future tubing and downstream value-added business.

items.statement: Focus shifting to value-added products (anodizing, powder coating, machining, tubing) targeting 25% margin premium over extrusion; aim to sell 100% of extrusion as value-added eventually.
items.quote: Our focus has always been now that we've added extrusion capacity, we are adding capacities for our value-added products. That means anodizing, powder coating, machining, and tubing, which is the new business, which command very significant margins of close to 25% over and above the extrusion margins.

items.statement: Advance of INR16.4 crores in other non-current assets includes office purchase for Delhi registered office and normal operating advances; not related to Dewas equipment.
items.quote: Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes. It is just advance. Basically, you must have been updated because we have purchased one office for our Delhi registered office. So, we have now purchased one office, so that was the advance that we have given to and there was some other portion to other related to some normal operating business.

items.statement: Net worth increased 54% to INR274 crores driven by INR83 crores preferential capital raise and profit retention, strengthening balance sheet.
items.quote: Net worth of the company increased significantly by 54% from INR178 crores to INR274 crores. The improvement was primarily driven by the preferential capital raised by the company amounting to INR83 crores along with the retention of profits, which further strengthened the company's balance sheet and long-term financial position.

items.statement: Aluminium price pass-through exists for raw material but operating cost increases (energy, finance, depreciation) cannot be passed on immediately; gross margins compressed to ~8%.
items.quote: Yes, of course, we are a converter only. So basically, we pass on the higher increased whatever the in terms of aluminium prices are increased. But yes, the operating cost we are not able to pass on an immediate basis though we have started discussing with the customers and trying to pass on that cost as well.

items.statement: US tariffs of 50% on aluminium products since 2024 unchanged; Make in India and import substitution initiatives driving domestic defense/aerospace demand.
items.quote: The duty story of, you know, on aluminium products of 50% have been there now since I think 2024 once when the American administration came into the government. So, it has not changed. It's been stagnant.

items.statement: FY26 extrusion volume ~7,300 metric tons; blended realization ~INR340/kg; export share 50% of manufacturing revenue.
items.quote: For FY26, the total extrusion capacity as well as value-added segments combined was almost 7,300 metric tons. And the average sale realization per kg was around from extrusion, it was INR340 per kg, and again from the value-added segment, it was comparatively higher.

items.statement: Additional employee costs expected in FY27 as part of INR7-10 crores ramp-up costs for new capacities.
items.quote: So, Yes, since again the FY27 would be a investment and commissioning year where our ramp-up cost will, I think will add up to again by INR7 crores INR10 crores in FY27 this year as well unless and until we obtain that operating kind of leverage. This additional cost in form of depreciation, finance cost, and another employee cost, trial runs and all will add up to another INR10 crores.

items.statement: Expect profit growth of 20% to 30% in FY27
items.quote: We expect profit growth in the range of 20% to 30% this year.

items.statement: Expect U.S. D2C revenues to organically grow 35% to 40% to INR375 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: Based on current momentum and market tailwinds, we expect our U.S. direct - to-consumer revenues to organically grow between 35% to 40% this year to INR375 crores by end of

items.statement: Target INR1,000 crores D2C brand revenue by FY29
items.quote: Our ambition is to build a INR1,000 crores direct-to-consumer brand by FY29, supported by continued expansion of Jean Dousset and growth across our various other brands.

items.statement: Expect zero net debt position in next 2 years
items.quote: Our expectation would be that over the next 2 years or so, we should be at a zero net debt position.

items.statement: Plan to open 4 additional Jean Dousset stores in U.S. metropolitan luxury markets in FY27
items.quote: We are now preparing for the next phase of retail expansion with plans to open 4 additional stores across key metropolitan luxury markets in the U.S.

items.statement: Each existing Jean Dousset store generates INR30-35 crores annual sales and INR8-10 crores bottom line contribution
items.quote: Each existing Jean Dousset store generates between INR30 crores and INR35 crores in annual sales depending on the location, demonstrating the strong scalability and revenue potential of the brand's retail model.

items.statement: U.S. D2C revenues grew 44% to INR275 crores in FY26
items.quote: Our U.S. D2C revenues grew by a strong 44% to reach INR275 crores for the full year, with both Jean Dousset and other brands growing aggressively.

items.statement: U.S. D2C EBITDA margin improved to 12.6% in FY26 from 11.3% in FY25
items.quote: U.S. D2C EBITDA numbers improved in line with increasing revenues, reaching a very impressive 12.6% for FY26 versus 11.3% for FY25.

items.statement: Expect D2C EBITDA margins of 15% to 20% as business scales
items.quote: And as I've mentioned that the EBITDA margins on that are 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Net debt around INR200-250 crores; repaid INR120 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Currently, our investment is about INR100 crore s and cash is INR100 crore. We have INR200 crores in investments and cash, and total debt is INR450 crore s. So net debt is around INR200 crores

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic D2C opportunities; look for undervalued branded assets with 3-5x growth potential
items.quote: We've successfully grown each of the 3 acquisitions that we've done between 3x and 5x over the preceding 4 to 5 years after acquiring the brands.

items.statement: Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry D2C channel growing 30% to 40% organically
items.quote: Because of this focus, we've been seeing a 30% to 40% organic growth in this channel.

items.statement: Natural hedge from USD-denominated inputs (gold, diamonds) plus forward contracts for INR exposure
items.quote: A lot of our sort of inputs such as gold as well as diamonds are also sort of purchased in US dollars itself. So that is sort of a compensating hedge that we have against our revenues. And for the INR part, we take forward contracts with banks to the extent of our INR exposure.

items.statement: No dividend for current year; priority is growth capex and debt repayment; may consider buyback after zero net debt
items.quote: for the current year, we've decided not to distribute a dividend because I think the current priority is investing in the growth of the business. We're seeing significant opportunities for the ramp-up of the Jean Dousset brand and it requires capita l expenditure to fund the retail store expansion

items.statement: Jean Dousset (great-grandson of Louis Cartier) runs premium lab diamond brand selling engagement rings at avg INR8-9 lakhs
items.quote: Jean Dousset, as a reminder, he's a great grandson of Louis Cartier, and he runs, we run the most premium luxury lab diamond brand in the world, selling lab diamond engagement rings fo r an average price of about INR8 lakhs to INR 9 lakh

items.statement: FY26 revenue grew 29% YoY to INR2,572 crores; EBITDA grew 22% to INR204 crores; PAT before exceptional items grew 36% to INR100 crores
items.value: Revenue INR2,572 crores, EBITDA INR204 crores, PAT INR100 crores
items.quote: During the year, our revenue grew by 29% year-over-year to INR2,572 crores, while EBITDA increased by 22% to INR204 crores. Profit after tax before exceptional items grew by 36% to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue before bullion sales grew 33% YoY to INR686 crores; EBITDA grew 40% to INR57 crores; PBT before exceptional items grew 83% to INR36.5 crores
items.value: Revenue INR686 crores, EBITDA INR57 crores, PBT INR36.5 crores
items.quote: During Q4 FY26, our revenue before bullion sales grew by 33% year-on-year to INR686 crores with EBITDA growing by 40% to INR57 crores. PBT before exceptional items grew sharply by 83% in Q4 to reach INR36.5 crores.

items.statement: U.S. luxury jewelry market remains a significant opportunity with promising pipeline of store rollouts and organic growth momentum
items.quote: The U.S. D2C market continues to be a significant opportunity for us with a promising pipeline of store rollouts and organic growth momentum across brands.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR4,675 crore entering FY27
items.quote: We enter FY27 with an order book of INR4,675 crore, providing healthy revenue visibility and reaffirming customer confidence in our capabilities and execution.

items.statement: Targets INR10,000 crore revenue with minimum 15% EBITDA margins by 2030
items.quote: And as I mentioned, long term, by 2030, we expect the company to be at about INR10,000 crore of revenue with at least minimum 15% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Expects to double container revenues in FY27
items.quote: However, the business continues to grow in FY27, our expectation is that we'll be doubling our container revenues from last year.

items.statement: Aspires to build INR1,000 crore revenue business in batteries and energy storage over next 3-4 years
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aspire to build a INR1,000 crore revenue business in batteries and energy storage over the next 3 to 4 years, supported by a growing order pipeline and favourable industry dynamics.

items.statement: Odisha Greenfield wheelset project partial production by end FY27, full commissioning by end FY28
items.quote: Partial production is expected by end of the current financial year, with full commissioning targeted by end of FY28.

items.statement: Odisha wheelset plant interim operations by March 2027, final commissioning by March 2028
items.quote: March 2027 is what we are saying for the interim and March 2028 is for the final commissioning.

items.statement: Wheelset business achieved 17% EBITDA margin in FY26 vs 12% in FY25
items.quote: There, as we have reported, we have achieved a significant higher EBITDA margins. We achieved 17% EBITDA margins as compared to 12% last financial year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.4% for FY26
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR363 crore, translating into a margin of 12.4%.

items.statement: Entering passenger mobility segment in FY27 via strategic partnership with global rolling stock manufacturer
items.quote: Passenger mobility is a strategic portfolio and priority for Jupiter Wagons, and we are preparing to enter the passenger mobility segment in FY27, backed by our deep manufacturing capabilities and technology partnerships, thus creating an important new avenue for growth and diversification.

items.statement: Stone India received RDSO approval for freight brake system, commercial production from July 2026
items.quote: Commercial production is expected to commence in July 2026.

items.statement: Jupiter Electric Mobility commissioned cell-to-battery manufacturing line in Indore
items.quote: To strengthen vertical integration and manufacturing efficiency, we commissioned a cell to battery manufacturing line in Indore, enhancing our ability to scale as demand grows.

items.statement: Signed MoAs with Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy adding 110 MW BESS to FY27 order book
items.quote: We are also pleased to sign MoAs with Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy, resulting in 110 megawatts of BESS business being added to our FY27 order book.

items.statement: Signed long-term supply arrangement with Tatravagonka for wheelsets from Odisha facility
items.quote: Moreover, we also signed a long-term supply arrangement with Tatravagonka, one of Europe's leading wagon manufacturers under which we will supply wheelsets for their requirements from our upcoming Odisha facility.

items.statement: Expects sizable market share in upcoming Indian Railways wagon tender for next 3 years
items.quote: And given Jupiter's strength and market share, definitely, we expect sizable order book a nd our expectation is that the orders which would come out would be at least for Railways' requirements for the next 3 years

items.statement: Faced supply chain disruptions in Q4 FY26 due to consumables availability, not wheelsets
items.quote: The last quarter, it wasn't on account of wheelsets so much, but on account of availability of other raw materials, mainly consumables, which caused the disruption.

items.statement: Inventory increased from INR769 crore to INR1,079 crore; expects normalization from Q2 FY27
items.quote: So there will be a rationalization in the inventory days. It was a short-term challenge, as I've told you because of certain disruptions, which we did not anticipate.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed credit rating at AA(-)/Stable for long-term and A1(+) for short-term debt
items.quote: Our financial position remains robust, supported by the reaffirmation of our credit rating by CRISIL at AA( -)/Stable for the long-term debt and A1(+) for short-term debt.

items.statement: Government announced PLI scheme for container manufacturing with INR10,000 crore budgetary allocation
items.quote: The Government of India's recently announced Production-Linked Incentive scheme for container manufacturing supported by a INR10,000 crore budgetary allocation, provides a strong policy tailwind for the sector.

items.statement: Expects PLI subsidy in 8-10% range to bridge cost gap with Chinese container prices
items.quote: But what we can understand that it's quite substantial, and it could be in the range of 8% to 10% is what we are believe to understand.

items.statement: Building export business via Tatravagonka partnership and engaging additional global partners
items.quote: This partnership represents a significant step in building our export business and validates our manufacturing capabilities. We are actively engaging with additional global partners to expand our international footprint and create long-t erm value for our shareholders

items.statement: Wheelset business revenue crossed INR500 crore in FY26
items.quote: The business crossed INR500 crore in revenue during the year while maintaining a healthy EBITDA margin of around 17%.

items.statement: Railwheel factory revenue grew from INR343 crore to INR528 crore in FY26
items.quote: Even in terms of revenue, the revenues have substantially increased from INR343 crore to INR528 crore.

items.statement: Pending wagon order book: ~2,000 wagons for Indian Railways and ~5,400 wagons for non-Railways totaling ~INR3,100 crore
items.quote: The pending number of wagon is right now around 2,000 wagons is Indian Railways and about 5,400 wagons, roughly, is the non-Indian Railway order book, which is totalling close to about INR3,100 crore.

items.statement: Executed 1,347 wagons in Q4 FY26
items.quote: 1,347 is the total executed in the last quarter.

items.statement: Wagon tender delay is a small hiccup; expects course correction this year with tender release anytime in 2026
items.quote: I think it is just a small hiccup, which is there. But again, I think we expect the course correction to happen this year.

items.statement: Not considering wagon leasing; will focus on core manufacturing competence with GATX partnership
items.quote: Our aim is to focus on our core competence, which is wagon manufacturing and the leasing part for the time being, it should be taken care by the experts.

items.statement: Targets 50% revenue growth rate for next 2-3 years and aims to maintain profitability rate
items.quote: If we are able to maintain that over the next two, three years, that would put us at a very, very good po sition in the next three years. So, our target is to maintain the same growth percentage and ensure that we are able to maintain the same rate of profitability as well

items.statement: Expects to execute 60% of INR1600 crore order book in FY27, 40% spillover to FY28
items.quote: So, approximately we have a balance order book of INR1600 crores, out of which we expect in the coming year, 60% approximately of this balance order book should be executed in the coming year. 40% of it will be spilled over into the next year.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1600 crore (4.46x FY26 revenue) diversified across buildings, roads, railways, river protection
items.quote: The company ended financial year 2026 with an order book of INR1600 crores, equivalent to 4.46x of our financial year 2026 revenue, providing strong visibility for sustained growth in the near to medium term.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline of INR3000 crore with results expected in 30-45 days; full year pipeline of INR7000-8000 crore
items.quote: Currently, we have a bidding pipeline of about INR3000 crores, for which we're expecting the results to come in the next about 30 to 45 days. And in the coming year as a whole, I can say, we will have about INR7000 crores to INR8000 crores in the bidding pipeline, in the entire year.

items.statement: EPC segment margins vary 13-20%, average ~15%; real estate segment margins ~85%
items.quote: So, they all vary between 13% to 20%. So, certain niche works, we get 18%, 19%. The general infrastructure works, 11%, 12%, 13%. So, the average we get about 15% in the EPC sector.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 280 bps to 22.83% in FY26 due to operating leverage and monsoon quarter execution
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 280 basis points to 22.83%, reflecting the operating leverage achieved through higher revenue volumes and significantly improved resources utilization during the monsoon quarters.

items.statement: Sees multi-year growth from Northeast infrastructure spending: highways, hydropower, border infra, railways, institutional buildings
items.quote: So, companies -- there are very few companies that are, you know, have a very strong embedded experience in the Northeast. So, we stand to benefit from all the infrastructure spending that is expected to happen in the next 10 years.

items.statement: Planning new retail/commercial/residential project in Guwahati worth ~INR500 crore over 4-5 years with 4 lakh sq ft leasable area
items.quote: And this project will be built phase-wise with the approx. total value accumulated to about INR500 crores in the next four to five years, phase-wise. So, the area would be approx. -- it's still under planning phase, but the commercial leasable area is expected to be about 4 lakh square feet.

items.statement: New real estate project launch expected in 4-5 months; revenue jump expected by end of year
items.quote: So, maybe in the next four to five months, we will launch the project. So, this year you should see by the end of the year, we're expecting to see a jump in the real estate revenues, but after the new project is launched.

items.statement: Promoter shares pledged since 2014; working with lenders for release over next 1-2 years as debt reduces
items.quote: Well, the shares have been pledged in 2014, and in the regular consortium meetings, we have a word with our lenders to release the same. And we are working on that, and we hope so in next year or two, we get released all the pledge

items.statement: Will use surety bonds, bank guarantees, and JV partnerships to fund growth capital needs
items.quote: So, we are -- we have applied and also received -- surety bonds are now accepted across all departments. So, with surety bonds -- with the mix of surety bonds and bank guarantees, we expect to support the required cash flows for these new projects. Also, we have a strategic model wherein we have joint ventures with other companies.

items.statement: ~70% of order book revenue retained by BIL, ~30% to JV partners; varies by project
items.quote: So, approximately you could say 70% of the order book revenues will come into BIL and the 30% will go into our joint venture partners.

items.statement: Execution period for projects typically 2-3 years maximum
items.quote: About two to three years. Maximum three years and two years minimum.

items.statement: Weather/El Nino risk monitored; vineyards have drip irrigation and canals full from last year's rain; no major concern currently

items.statement: Consolidated revenue crossed ₹100 crore milestone for first time in FY26

items.statement: Supply chain challenges and inflation impact from war situation; customers being supportive

items.statement: Defence sector entry slower due to direct PSU targeting and tendering process timelines

items.statement: Prioritizing working capital efficiency and healthy cash flows in FY27

items.quote: Steel ware as it ramps up and glassware as it starts becoming more profitable, we should sce improvement about 2.5%, 3% EBITDA margins in the consumerware category.

items.statement: Writing instruments margin to recover to Unomax levels over couple of quarters as product mix improves
items.quote: And now that we have taken it over, it sillis not a very profitable business at this point of time because of the product mix. And as we arc changing the product mix, the profits will be in line with what we were - we used to do Unomax. So that will take a couple of quarters to come back.

items.statement: MRP hikes of 12-20% taken across all product lines due to rising costs
items.quote: There has been a lot of escalation in prices, about 12% to 20% MRP rises that we have taken across all our product lincs, which we had to because of these rising costs.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed on to consumers; selling prices adjusted up and down with raw material costs
items.quote: with regards to raw material prices actually it always, as we have said in the past, we increase our selling price in accordance -- I mean whatever raw material prices, we pass on the burden to the end consumer

items.statement: Q1 FY27 demand subdued due to Middle East crisis, rising costs, and price hikes; volume growth may be lower
items.quote: I think, yes, Q1 looks a little challenging. So we are trading very cautiously because we have been impacted. I think most companics have been impacted by all sides, whether its rising raw material prices, labor issues, basically rising production costs, overall demand being also a littlc subducd

items.statement: E-commerce and quick commerce channels now contribute ~17% of overall revenue with profitability in line with other segments
items.quote: During the quarter, we also witnessed a continued increase in revenue contribution from c- commerce and quick commerce channcls. These channcls now account for neatly 17% of our overall revenue with profitability broadly in line with other business segments.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.01% as of FY26 end
items.quote: Debt-to- equity ratio stands at 0.01%.

items.statement: Actively engaging authorities for protection against Chinese glassware dumping
items.quote: We are actively engaging with relevant authorities to seek some protection against these dumping -- against this dumping happening from -- mainly from China.

items.statement: New competition in Opalware emerged ~6 months ago; company trading cautiously to maintain market share while exhausting current capacity
items.quote: There has been new competition which has come in about 6-0dd months back. So we arc secing how that shapes up as well and in the future, of course, we will look at expansion post everything settles, and there is no crazy price wars.

items.statement: Writing instruments seasonality: Q1 and Q4 (Jan-Jun) are strongest, contributing ~1.5x other quarters
items.quote: Scasonal, your back-to-school is your biggest quarter, basically, which is the first quarter and the last quarter does better. So your Jan, Feb, March till June end s very, very good, and then it takes a slight dip. So the next 2 quarters arc a little less - it's almost like a 1.5% happens in the lnst quarter and the first quarter

items.statement: Q1 FY27 headwinds from Middle East crisis, rising raw material and energy costs, labor issues, subdued demand; hopes for cost peak and improvement post-Q2
items.quote: No, no, it's not seasonality. It's mostly the current crisis that we're going through. Okay. And what makes you to fecl that the things will look after Q2 onwards? I don't really know if things will look up. I hope things will be better. I don't know what the political leaders of the world will do. But Im hoping that because I believe that we have hit the peak in terms

items.statement: Government/institutional orders stretching receivable days; anticipated and typical for such orders
items.quote: Some of our receivable days have - is looking a litle bad because of a couple of institutional government orders, government tenders that we have taken, though - and this is a typical city with the government order, it was anticipated already.

items.statement: Writing instruments exports growing and providing better margins; helps offset steep price increases
items.quote: And also export-wise, exports, of course, have been helpful in the sense that they've given better margins, and that will continue to happen for the - over the next - course of the next year as well. And that should also help offsct some of the stecp price increascs.

items.statement: Plastic raw material costs increased but Q4 impact mitigated by adequate inventory; rising energy costs impacted glassware but manageable
items.quote: There was an increase in plastic raw material costs, but we had adequate inventory to mitigate the impact in Q4. Additionally, rising energy costs had some impact on glassware production, which remained manageable during the quarter.

items.statement: Capacity expansion to 16,000 machines on track for commercial operation in Q2 FY27 (September)
items.quote: To support this growth, our plan to expand our annual capacity to 16,000 machines remain on track for a commencement of commercial operation in quarter 2 of this financial year.

items.statement: Current installed annual capacity is 6,000 machines across India and Huron
items.quote: We currently have an installed annual capacity of 6,000 machines in India and Huron together during the year.

items.statement: Facilities operated at over 100% utilization during peak demand months in FY26
items.quote: One of the key challenges we encountered was capacity constraint with our facilities operating at utilization level exceeding 100% during peak demand months.

items.statement: Order intake for Q4 FY26 was INR700+ crores; FY26 order intake was INR2,364 crores
items.quote: Speaking of our order intake, our order intake for Q4 FY26 stood at INR700 crores plus, driven by all sectors and particularly by auto and general engineering segment. For FY26, the order intake stood at INR2364 crores.

items.statement: Outstanding order book as of 31 March 2026 stands at INR4,732 crores
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our outstanding order book stand at INR4,732 crores, which is very healthy and growing.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 31.9%; FY26 EBITDA margin 28.9%
items.quote: On the profitability front as well, quarter 4 EBITDA stood at INR191 crores with margin of 31.9%, while FY26 EBITDA stood at INR564 crores with margin of 28.9%.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 24.6%; FY26 EBITDA margin 25.2% after revenue reversal impact
items.quote: As a result, consolidated EBITDA for Q4 FY26 stood at INR147 crores with a margin of 24.6%. FY26 EBITDA stood at INR527 crores with a margin of 25.2%.

items.statement: Management expects steady-state EBITDA margin of 25%+ despite product mix changes
items.quote: But our margin profile, let's say, it's going to be at 25% -- 25% plus, it will be remained there.

items.statement: Demand environment positive across domestic and global markets with pickup in auto and general engineering sectors
items.quote: The outlook across both domestic and global markets remain positive across all manufacturing sectors and especially we have seen a good pickup in auto and general engineering sectors.

items.statement: Raw material costs increased 2-3% in last 2 months; prices increased for new orders from 1 May to compensate
items.quote: Let's say, today, in the last 2 months, we have seen the cost has been increased, close to 2 to 3 percentage over there on raw material prices. On our -- from 1st of this May, we have increased our prices for the new -- to our new customers and new orders over there basically.

items.statement: Working capital requirement expected to reduce with new capacity; cash flow conversion improving quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: We are able to see the more working capital requirement is going to be reduced there. And we see the conversion of a cash flow over there basically. Even this year also from the last year to this year, the last year, we were into negative cash flow to we entered into positive, and we are looking to be a very robust cash flows in quarter-on-quarter in coming days over here and there.

items.statement: Debt increased by ~INR300 crores for capacity expansion; working capital debt up only INR45 crores; no further debt increase expected
items.quote: So I'll tell you the debt, what we have increased in this year is close to -- close to INR300 crores is the debt has been incurred on our capacity expansion basically, okay, on our new capacity there. Only working capital has increased only INR45 crores to be there.

items.statement: Export control investigation ongoing at Huron; no material adverse impact on operations; revenue reversal of INR67 crores is deferment not write-off
items.quote: However, as previously disclosed to the stock exchange, an ongoing investigation is being conducted by the export control authorities concerning certain export order at Huron. The investigation has had no material adverse impact on the company's operations, including order execution, exports, customer servicing or ongoing manufacturing activities.

items.statement: Revenue reversal of INR67 crores at Huron due to export license clearance pending; will be recognized once licenses received
items.quote: Once we get this, let's say, the situation that in investigation, there are a few machines was under POCM and that was not available the export license clearance. So they stated that once this export license you will receive, you can immediately can convert it into your revenue in the coming quarters over there.

items.statement: Average realization per machine INR35.62 lakh for FY26
items.quote: This year, the total realization is INR35.62 lakh.

items.statement: Order book mix: 38% aerospace & defense, 20% auto & auto components, 19% general engineering, 4% EMS
items.quote: The industry-wise breakup is as follows: 38% from aerospace and defense, 19% from general engineering, 20% from auto and auto components and 4% from EMS and balance from the other sectors.

items.statement: Aerospace & defense largely high-end (>INR2 cr); auto & general engineering mostly entry/mid-level (up to INR2 cr)
items.quote: Basically in aerospace and defense, is largely on a high end. You can consider --yes, largely all are in high end basically. Almost our 40% is in high-end and 60% in entry-level and mid-level there.

items.statement: Customer base expanded to 15,000+ across manufacturing sectors in India
items.quote: You know that we have more than 15,000-plus customer base now in India across manufacturing sector there.

items.statement: New capacity expansion of 10,000 machines (6,000 to 16,000) progressing on schedule for September commencement
items.quote: With our ongoing expansion of 10,000 machines progressing on schedule and expected to commence operation by September.

items.statement: Investigation conclusion timeline uncertain (could take 2-5 years); INR67 cr revenue recognition deferred until export licenses received
items.quote: It will take very long time, 2 years, 3 years, 5 years, we don't know. We can't comment on that also today.

items.statement: Huron standalone revenue expected to normalize to INR300-350 crores in FY27
items.quote: So FY27, we are seeing to come to a normal level first, and that normal level is close to INR300 crores to INR350 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 8,000-9,000+ machines in FY27 with new capacity available for last 6 months
items.quote: So close to, you can say, additional, let's say, right now, we are almost 100% but the 50% of that area, we will reach maybe around 8,000 something machines to be there, 8,000 or 9,000 plus.

items.statement: No plans to sell Huron business; well recognized with customers and near to them
items.quote: Not at all. We are not looking at all because we have been very well recognized over there to all our customers, and we are very much near to our customers.

items.statement: Added ~25 people in manufacturing at Huron; new facilities operational from November
items.quote: We have added around 25 people in manufacturing there, okay? And we entered all the additional new facilities from November onwards.

items.statement: EMS orders delayed as clients optimizing capacity; no major investment in last 1.5 years; expecting results soon with PLI schemes
items.quote: So basically, right now, they all are optimizing their manufacturing capabilities and capacity there. So we are just -- the delay side we are seeing from all the EMS player there. Nothing has been invested much on the last component manufacturing in the last 1.5 years there.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline 18-20 months; FY27 execution quantum not quantified yet
items.quote: So basically, right now, with this total order book, we have INR4,700 crores. And based on the commitment, we have to execute in 18 to 20 months over this.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be better than Q4 FY26 and better than Q1 FY26 on both GTV and GP
items.quote: As a whole, we would still expect Q1 to be better than Q4, and we would also expect Q1 to be better than same period last year.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow business north of 20% (early-to-mid 20s) unless serious downward movement in base normalcy
items.quote: The whole business plan was anchored around this growing north of 20%. We do believe that unless some serious downward movement happens in the base of where normalcy sets in, we should continue to grow in that range.

items.statement: SG&A growth will slightly taper down from current 16%; top line should grow faster than SG&A leading to operating leverage
items.quote: The SG&A growth will not accelerate from where it is, it will slightly taper down as well. Hopefully, the gap between SG&A growth and GTV growth will increase, which will lead to operating leverage and expanding margins.

items.statement: EBITDA-to-GTV ratio expected to move up starting FY27 as SG&A growth tapers and hotels mix grows faster than air GTV
items.quote: I think that's a reasonable assumption and it's a function of two things. One yes, absolutely as SG&A growth tapers down margins should expand and secondly the saliency mix will also help as our hotels business, which is higher margin business grows faster than the air GTV.

items.statement: CFO-to-EBITDA and FCF-to-EBITDA ratios targeted to return to >100% by end of FY27
items.quote: Historically, as well, we have been delivering more than 100% per se and that's what we would strive to do by end of this financial year as well.

items.statement: ETR for FY27 expected around 18% to 18.5% similar to Q4 FY26
items.quote: The expected tax rate for ETR would be similar in the range of in the Q4, which would be around 18% to 18.5%.

items.statement: Classic Vacations integration to be completed by end of Q3 FY27 (end of calendar year)
items.quote: We are probably about halfway through the integration process, but we intend to complete the integration by the end of Q3, by the end of this Calendar Year.

items.statement: Middle East and Israel severely impacted by war; recovery sharp when positive news (e.g., April ceasefire) but volumes not yet exceeding pre-war levels
items.quote: In the markets like the Middle East and Israel, where we have a more direct impact of the war, we are starting to see increasing recoveries to the extent that in pockets we are seeing volumes which are similar to the pre -war volumes, not exceeding those

items.statement: LATAM to see moderate growth in FY27 due to currency volatility and structural headwinds beyond company control
items.quote: LATAM will see moderate growth compared to the overall enterprise because of the fact that there are significant headwinds which go beyond just our own business over there and you articulated them already.

items.statement: Jan-Feb FY26 showed strong operating leverage, margin expansion, and EBITDA growth YoY; March war impact washed out full quarter leverage
items.quote: you will see that in Jan and Feb, we were seeing very strong operating leverage, margin expansion, as well as EBITDA growth on a year-on-year basis for these two months, compared to the same period last year. Of course, March was a complete washout for us because of the war. Hence, on a full q uarter basis, the operating leverage did not flow

items.statement: Hotels business higher margin than air; growing hotels saliency helps EBITDA-to-GTV ratio expansion
items.quote: secondly the saliency mix will also help as our hotels business, which is higher margin business grows faster than the air GTV.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers grew dramatically YoY due to market development investments in new travel agencies
items.quote: If you see, the number of monthly transacting buyers on a year-on-year basis has grown very dramatically in the last one year. So, that is where all the investment that we made has gone in and we will start to see the results from it in the coming year.

items.statement: No immediate short-to-midterm downward pressure on take rates; intend to maintain current levels, not improve them; growth driven by higher take-rate markets (NA, Europe)
items.quote: We are not anticipating any immediate, right? When I say immediate, I mean short to midterm downward pressure on take rates. We absolutely intend to maintain them at the current levels. We are also not trying to improve our take rate from where they are.

items.statement: Expedia not a direct competitor in most retail markets; B2B market growing faster than B2C globally
items.quote: We don't directly compete with them in many of the markets that we are growing in. So, I think I guess without knowing the color of their growth, it's hard to comment on where it is coming from. But from our perspective, we don't see Expedia as an immediate direct competitor for the most part, especially on the retail side of things.

items.statement: Airline capacity cuts temporary; fares up but passengers still traveling; corridors shifted shorter (intra-Europe, Asia Pacific); booking windows shrunk
items.quote: The other thing that has happened is that the booking windows have also shrunk a little bit, which is why overall, the industry remains hopeful that if some resolution happens to the war in the next few days, we can still capture the June, July, August, September summer traffic.

items.statement: FX impact on consolidated GTV ~4-5% YoY for FY26; primarily affects hotel GTV
items.quote: the overall impact would be in the range of on a YoY basis for the full year would be around 4 to 5%.

items.statement: Debt tenure 5 years with 1-year moratorium; repayment starts Q3 FY27 over remaining 4 years
items.quote: We have a debt for a period of five years. So, we have a moratorium on repayment for one year. A repayment would start from Q3 of this year and would be, would remain there for another four years.

items.statement: Tech cost capitalization for new features/products with future economic benefits; amortization 3-5 years per project; maintenance expensed
items.quote: Only the developments which are happening for which would be able to generate any future be nefits, that cost gets capitalized and the amortization period for the same varies from 3 to 5 years, depending upon project-to-project

items.statement: Classic Vacations intangibles recognized: supplier relationship asset ~$50M amortized over 15 years
items.quote: Primarily, the amortizable asset, there is the supplier relationship asset, which is around 50 million in cost, and that would get amortized over a period of 15 years.

items.statement: Hotel GTV growth driven by new agents (15% of 22% total growth in FY26); old agent growth depressed by Middle East war impact in March
items.quote: This specific year, this number got depressed a little bit because our Middle East is our oldest market. The old cohorts are heavily dominated by the Middle East travel agencies and they saw a very massive hit in their business in March.

items.statement: Retail vs API mix ~50:50 on hotel GTV; retail higher on GP
items.quote: At an enterprise level for the hotel business, would roughly sit around, 50:50. Gaurav Bhatnagar: So, about 50:50 on GTV and probably higher for retail on GP

items.statement: War escalation risk: if geopolitics worsens, Q1 recovery assumptions invalid; Middle East outbound migration and inbound travel uncertainty
items.quote: If things were to change for the worse, in terms of the just geopolitics, then who knows what happens but let's assume that there is no good news and no bad news beyond what is today.

items.statement: Key account manager maturity curve 6-9 months to meaningful productivity (break-even then profitability)
items.quote: remains about a six to nine month window where they start to become meaningfully productive and meaningful productive in the sense that it is starting to almost break even on cost and then there is profitability after that

items.statement: Management expects to maintain FY26 performance levels in FY27, with review after Q2
items.quote: We expect we'll at least we will maintain FY25-'26 levels of performance as of now. But we will be reviewing this opportunity in say by next quarter or after second quarter, once the situation is improved.

items.statement: No significant capex planned for FY27 due to market uncertainty
items.quote: There is no much capex planned this year. But again, it is not predictable. This market is not predictable.

items.statement: UAE Ras Al Khaimah plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons with less than 50% utilization
items.quote: Our capacity is 1,200 metric tons in the Ras Al Khaimah plant. And currently, less than 50% is being utilized in this Ras Al Khaimah plant.

items.statement: Indian operations utilization at 45-55% across tyre and retread segments
items.quote: Indian operations, it's around 45% to 55% for this different for tyre and the retread segment. Retread segment it is around 55% and tyre segment it is around 45%.

items.statement: Tyre production volumes grew 36% YoY in FY26 to 535,870 units
items.quote: If you look at the '25 volume of tyres what we have manufactured is 3,93,253 tyres, but '26 we could do 5,35,870 tyres. That is a 36% growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 14.6% in FY26 from 19.8% in FY25 due to GST changes and raw material volatility
items.quote: excluding other income for FY26, stood at INR47.8 crores as compared to INR57.91 crores in FY25. EBITDA margin for the year stood at 14.6

items.statement: Management targets 10-13% EBITDA margin going forward through operational efficiencies
items.quote: We always try to keep minimum 10% margin, that is a fact, but then due to our efficiency, otherwise our pricing will not be feasible in the market. So, and again we try hard in our in-house to reduce the waste and scrap and all those additional elements and the operational efficiency to get another 2%, 3% margin. So, -- 10% to 13% will be an acceptable margin level what we are foreseeing.

items.statement: GST rate changes reduced retreading competitiveness: new tyres at 18% vs retread at 18%, agricultural tyres at 5% vs retread at 18%
items.quote: Due to this GST revision in last September where the GST rate of tyre reduced to 18% and retread materials again tax rate same 18%. So due to this there is a pressure on the retread business margin, margin of the retread business. And even agricultural tyre GST reduced to 5% while the retreading material still taxed at 18%.

items.statement: Retread manufacturers association petitioned government to reduce GST on retread materials from 18% to 5%
items.quote: We now this association of retread manufacturers have approached the ministry or Government of India to reduce GST on retread segment to 5%. That is under consideration by Government of India.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to 4-5 months inventory holding for seasonal rubber and 3-4 months dealer credit periods
items.quote: we are holding good amount of inventory also. That's also we have to keep because 4 to 5 months inventory we are holding because rubber is a seasonal product. So there is a lot of price variations happening in between the seasons and there is rubber ta pping off-season is there in June, July the rainy season and all

items.statement: Credit period extended by one month due to GST reforms and geopolitical uncertainty, plan to reduce gradually
items.quote: Now, currently, in last, for last few quarters, especially from this GST reforms and all, and this war and all, this credit period slightly increased by at least by another 1 month. But this is not a long-term thing. We also want to reduce it to a comfortable level.

items.statement: Consolidated debt-to-equity ratio at 0.03x as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: our balance sheet remains strong with a consolidated debt -to-equity ratio of only 0.03 x as on 31st March 2026, providing us adequate financial flexibility to pur sue future growth

items.statement: New heavy-duty tractor rear tyre category receiving encouraging market response through dealer network
items.quote: The newly introduced heavy-duty tractor rear tyre category has started receiving encouraging response from the market through our dealer network and further strengthens our position in the agriculture segment.

items.statement: UAE operations expanding market reach in tread rubber exports with supportive business environment
items.quote: We were able to expand our market reach in select segments where competitive intensity moderated, especially in tread rubber exports. Our strategic focus on customer acquisition, distribution expansion, and deeper market penetration supported revenue growth during the year.

items.statement: US business started in FY26 with repeat orders coming in, Europe market being explored
items.quote: Next is the precured, we are now exploring the Europe market as well. So that also, in America, we have started in the last financial year, we started the US business. And people are now slowly placing the repeat orders.

items.statement: New Gujarat depot launched December 1, 2025 to strengthen Western India distribution network
items.quote: In line with our strategy to strengthen domestic distribution and improve customer reach, we also expanded our presence in Western India through the launch of a new depot in Gujarat, which commenced operations on December 1st, 2025.

items.statement: Terra Rubber recycling initiative processing internal scrap for cost savings, road trials showing positive results
items.quote: What we are trying to do, whatever scrap or waste generated out of Tolins Tyres operation, we know the quality of the scrap. So that material we are processing, started processing in Terra Rubber and started integrating into our products.

items.statement: Replacement demand healthy driven by fleet operators focusing on cost optimization and tyre life extension
items.quote: Driven by healthy replacement demand, improving rural and agricultural activity, steady movement of commercial vehicle segment, and increasing focus on cost -efficient mobi lity solutions, the retreading industry continues to benefit from fleet operators focusing on cost optimization and tyre life extension

items.statement: Middle East war creating logistics issues and uncertainty for UAE operations and export markets
items.quote: You know the war happening in the Middle East. So that is going to, we have to wait and watch how the things are going in that area.

items.statement: China dumping materials in GCC countries with up to 1-year credit periods affecting UAE competitiveness
items.quote: otherwise China is dumping materials in the GCC countries and all with a lot of extra credit period extending up to 1 year and all. That is not in our control

items.statement: Scouting for acquisitions in recycling space for Terra Rubber, nothing finalized yet
items.quote: Going forward, we are looking at some acquisitions in of some facility in this area. That is what we have in mind in Terra Rubber.

items.statement: Automation and AI tools being implemented on factory floor to reduce unwanted inventories and improve planning
items.quote: Also, we are implementing a lot of AI tools in the floor so that those kind of planning and inventory, where we have unwanted inventories, we are trying to reduce. All those things are being handled.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 volumes declined QoQ due to March uncertainty from war, but grew YoY
items.quote: Quarter to quarter basis there is decline because Q4, there was a lot of uncertainties in the market and all, especially in March and all. The volumes reduced considerably. On a year-on-year basis, there is a growth.

items.statement: Competing successfully with tyre majors in retreading materials for 40+ years with expertise in road conditions and casing qualities
items.quote: We are competing with these tyre majors and we have been very successful over the last 40 years in this business. So we know the terrain, the road conditions, those kind of things, and we have the products which is applicable for even for carts, planes, all those areas.

items.statement: Marketing spend minimal, focused on point-of-sale branding at dealer shops rather than heavy advertising
items.quote: What we are doing in the marketing side, we are having a very strong team of marketing managers across the country. They are doing a wonderful job, and the branding what we are doing for the tyre is the last point, where the sale is happening.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crores with PAT of INR270-280 crores (13.5-14% PAT margin)
items.value: INR2,000 crores revenue; INR270-280 crores PAT
items.quote: So the combined -- for this combined, I do understand that the profitability can be at a level of somewhere around 14%, so INR270 crores to INR280 crores can be the PAT number, which we will look forward to on a topline of INR2,000-odd crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance lowered to 21-22% for FY27 from previous 22-24% due to global crisis impact
items.quote: However, for the global crisis, I am reducing my EBITDA guidance to somewhere around 21% to 22%, which was earlier 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Total order book at INR6,814 crores including water/wastewater execution INR2,733 crores, water/wastewater O&M INR951 crores, renewable execution INR2,051 crores, renewable O&M/IPP INR1,079 crores
items.quote: our total order book has surged to over INR6,814 crores, providing robust revenue visibility over the next 24 months. This comprises of water and wastewater execution order book of over INR2,733 crores, operation and maintenance order book of over INR951 crores from these water and wastewater projects. In the Renewable segment, the execution order book is over INR2,051 crores, and the O&M and IPP

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance of at least INR2,500 crores
items.quote: For FY27, we would look forward to at least INR2,500 crores further order book.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR1,200 crores submitted bids and INR5,000 crores upcoming bids of interest
items.value: INR1,200 crores submitted; INR5,000 crores upcoming
items.quote: Current bid pipeline as of now is somewhere around -- the bid pipeline where we have submitted our bid is somewhere around INR1,200 crores, and the projects for which bidding is to happen where we are interested, it is somewhere around INR5,000 crores further.

items.statement: BESS EPC PAT margin expected around 10% currently, with blended renewable PAT margin of 10-12%
items.quote: In the BESS business, which is EPC, we will expect PAT margin somewhere in the range of 10%.

items.statement: Water/wastewater O&M margins higher than execution; O&M forms 3-5% of total revenues currently
items.quote: The operation and maintenance order book for wastewater treatment projects is INR950-odd crores, and then for that IPP income or renewable projects O&M, that is INR1,000 crores. Right now, as the executions are continuing in the wastewater treatment segment as well, on a year-on-year basis, the O&M values, these are increasing and the margins are comparatively higher in comparison to execution.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 estimated at INR20-30 crores for equipment requirements on new projects
items.quote: So we don't see any major capex going on. Apart from the capex which we have done in the last financial year, but I think it can be to the tune of INR20 crores, INR30-odd crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Working capital cycle stretched to 166 days (inventory 11, receivables 53, UBR 195, creditors 92); targeting reduction to ~90 days in FY27
items.quote: Currently, the unbilled UBR days are 195 days. Let me give you the split; inventory days are 11, receivable days are 53, UBR days are 195, creditor days are 92, so the net working capital cycle is 166.

items.statement: Total debt INR422 crores (long-term INR250 crores, short-term INR175 crores); debt/equity 0.34x; max comfort level 1:1 debt/equity
items.quote: Right now, I am pleased to confirm that the finance cost has not gone high, rather it has dipped from the last financial year. The total debt in the books right now is to the tune of INR422 crores, out of which the long-term debt which is paired to the assets or term loans HAM project, it is INR250 crores and short-term loan is somewhere around INR175 crores.

items.statement: Price variation clauses cover part of cost increases but not entire market price increases; deferring lithium-ion battery procurement for BESS projects until prices stabilize

items.statement: FY26 was a challenging year due to geopolitical tensions, Middle East crisis, heavy rains, and airline disruptions, but industry fundamentals remain strong.
items.quote: Actually, t his yea r, and if you see our results , that may not be entirely reflected , b ut it was a very challenging year. items.quote: The only conclusion we could come to, albeit not validated, is that at that time, India got, unfortunately, a lot of very negative publicity in the international press on the very poor quality of air we have in North India.

items.statement: February saw strong demand across geographies driven by better air quality, weather, and the AI Summit, not solely the summit.
items.quote: February is a buoyant month. And perhaps people … one reason for the increase could be, i s that people who were planning to travel to India in the winter months, actually chose February rather than January . A ir quality is significantly better

items.statement: Domestic share increased substantially in Q4, compensating for foreign tourist decline due to West Asia conflict; foreign travel seasonally low in summer months.

items.statement: Trident brand full year RevPAR grew 10.2% vs Upper Upscale segment 5% growth.
items.quote: For full year this segment saw a growth of 5% while Trident Hotels had a growth of 10.2% on account of both, occupancy and ARR being higher than the competition and versus last year.

items.statement: EIH owned hotels full year occupancy 76.8-77%, RevPAR ~Rs 17,400, up 8.5% YoY.
items.quote: So, the full year occupancy for our own hotels was 76.8 or 77% for the year.

items.statement: Excluding one-time items (Mashobra, wage code), FY26 profit grew 2% YoY.
items.quote: So, if we exclude those one-timers, our profit has grown by 2% versus last year.

items.quote: what is our normalized working capital cycle 50 days, 55 days? 65 days. Yeah, let's say about 55-60 days off much shorter for the metals vertical.

items.statement: Gross debt increased only INR43 crores to INR211 crores in FY26 despite capex, debt-to-equity 0.30x
items.quote: While the company continued to invest aggressively in capacity creation, consolidated gross debt increased by only INR43 crores during FY '26 from INR168 crores to INR211 crores. Consequently, the gross debt-to-equity ratio remains comfortable at 0.30x as against 0.25x in the previous year.

items.statement: INR400 crores credit lines sanctioned but not drawn pending Bhopal plant restart
items.quote: We have got about INR400 crores of lines already sanctioned. But due to our conservative nature, we did not take the lines until the Bhopal plant is operational.

items.statement: Promoter shareholding increase planned for Phase 2 of UP project when capital needed
items.quote: The promoter holding -- I mean if the promoters want to put in money. There has to be end use for that money in the company. So we see it when we do the Phase 2 of the UP project.

items.statement: Company Secretary resigned for personal reasons, internal auditor rotated for governance
items.quote: The Company Secretary belonged to Delhi and he had some personal issues to take care of, that's why he moved back to Delhi.

items.statement: Appointing dedicated compliance officer to prevent future license disruptions
items.quote: Also, we are working on better compliances. We are in the process of appointing a dedicated compliance officer who is going to take care of all the compliances.

items.statement: Bhopal plant supplied 50% of volumes; license suspension since February 2025 impacting Delhi, Jharkhand, UP, CSD supplies
items.quote: So roughly 50% of our volume was coming from there.

items.statement: Bhopal market share recovery expected in 6-7 months after restart; Karnataka share improving quarter by quarter
items.quote: In the next six to seven months, I think as soon as it starts, we should be able to recover past numbers in Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Karnataka excise duty rationalization implemented May 2025, reducing consumer prices in mainstream/economy segments, no impact on company revenues or margins
items.quote: It is a very good question. So, there is no impact. It's only consumer price, which has come down, consumers will benefit from this. It has no impact on our revenues.

items.statement: FY26 beer volumes down 20% to 187.19 lakh cases, total volumes down 17.7% to 202.22 lakh cases
items.quote: Consequently, beer volumes declined by 20% to 187.19 lakh cases during Full Year FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR1,233 crores (-14.8%), EBITDA INR89.7 crores, PAT INR10.2 crores
items.quote: Consolidated revenue declined by 14.8% to INR1,233 crores, while EBITDA declined to INR89.7 crores and PAT stood at INR10.2 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected better than Q4 FY26 due to improved utilization at Hassan and Odisha, Bhopal inventory sale, and annual costs absorbed in Q4
items.quote: I think quarter 1 would be, I think, in terms of numbers should be better than quarter 4.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15% year-over-year
items.quote: we expect a 15% revenue jump year-over-year. That's how of course, the effort is for much more, but of course, those are internal targets, but we feel our 15% year-over-year is something which we feel is achievable.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement guidance of 0.5% to 1% year-over-year
items.quote: we expect that 0.5% to 1% gross margins improvement will always be there. That is what we factor in for, we factor in for more because of the product mix, the geography mix and the pricing.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of around 18% for FY27 and above 20% by 2030
items.quote: After the scale-up of the Indore, I feel the EBITDA margin for '26, '27 should be in the range of around 18%. And over a year -- year-by-year, there will be improvement of about between 0.5% to 1% over the year-to-year to come. And it can go up to by 2030, it can go above 20%.

items.statement: Gross debt expected to remain around INR400 crores for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Today, our debt is around INR400 crores, total debt, gross debt is around INR400 crores. And looking to the present situation because the top line is going to increase, there will be additional requirement of working capital. So we feel this INR400 crores will be the top test loan, and it is going to remain at this level only.

items.statement: No new greenfield capex foreseen for next 2 years; only replacement capex of ~INR20 crores per year
items.quote: for the next 2 years, we don't see any, for say capex. But of course, as you know, Navsari is almost now some machines are 20 years old, some are 15 years old, some are recent. So always, there will be a replacement capex of around INR20 crores year-over-year, which will keep on happening to ensure the continuation of business. But any new greenfield capex will not at least as of now, I don't fore

items.statement: Indore facility reached 30% capacity utilization and EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We told you at the start of the year that we would reach 30% capacity utilization by year-end. We got there on target. Indore in Q4 reached its EBITDA breakeven with the capacity scaling up.

items.statement: EU GMP audit completed in December 2025; certificate pending
items.quote: The EU GMP audit, which was also committed was completed in the first week of December 2025 by the Portuguese Competent Authority. The certificate is pending. We expect that to come through soon, and that will open up multiple EU markets for us.

items.statement: 40 product tech transfers complete at Indore; 27 under development; 200+ state FDA approvals; 20+ Indian pharma companies audited/using Indore as CMO base
items.quote: We have 40 product tech transfers complete with another 27 under development and stability testing. We have almost 200-plus state FDA approvals in hand. We have more than 20 Indian pharma companies that have audited or actively using Indore as the CMO base.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.73% vs 13.17% in Q4 FY25; FY26 EBITDA margin 16.26% vs 16.91% in FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in the Q4 of last financial year was 13.17%. The EBITDA margin for Q4 of the current financial year is 17.73%.

items.statement: Navsari margin expected to settle at 18-18.5%; Indore margin expected at 31-32% at full utilization
items.quote: Navsari margin was 20%, and because of increasing the cost every year, we feel that Navsari margin is going to remain at around 18% to 18.5%. Whereas in case of Indore, because of the new plant, energy efficient plant and large size of life-leisure product. Therefore, the Indore margin, we expect around 31% to 32%.

items.statement: New launches expected to contribute INR20-30 crores annually; potential blockbusters in FY28-29 could add INR40-50 crores
items.quote: we foresee that every year, there will be around INR20 crores, INR30 crores of new launches, depending on the molecules. items.quote: a major global health organization has now finally partnered with us on our most complex injectable asset, giving us access to public health procurement across 109 countries.

items.statement: New product approvals received in Myanmar, Philippines, South Africa, Colombia, Germany, Ecuador; dossiers filed in 18 new countries
items.quote: we've received new product approvals in Myanmar, the Philippines, South Africa, Colombia, Germany and Ecuador. We filed dossiers in 18 new countries for multiple of our complex injectable molecules.

items.statement: International business model shifted from distributor-held MA to Gufic-held MA via Gufic Ireland for EU and own filings in key markets
items.quote: We've spent FY26 switching to a model where Gufic now holds the marketing authorization through Gufic Ireland for the EU market, for example, and to our own filings in key markets. We control the IP in this setup. And when you hold the MA, you monetize the asset in 3 distinct ways: the direct supply, the out-licensing and the tech transfer fees.

items.statement: Critical Care receivables reduced from 140-150+ days to CFA-led stockist model; INR22 crore revenue impact across Q2-Q4 FY26; collection now complete
items.quote: We went into FY26 with outstanding receivables from direct hospital billing that was sitting at almost 140, 150 days plus, and that was simply not sustainable. items.quote: Earlier, maybe we were 80%, 85% outsourced. Now we have come to around 65%. Down the line, we hope that 50% of our API can be done in-house eventually.

items.quote: We have taken some batches. There are some batches that are going to be taken in July and August, which would trigger our U.S. FDA inspection by the end of the year once we file them. We hope for, I would say, inspection maybe as per them. Of course, that our clients and the U.S. FDA, depending on their calendars, they will trigger the inspection maybe next year or something. items.statement: GLP-1 CMO opportunity seen as 1-2 year phenomenon; saturation expected down the line
items.quote: CMO business is something which again, I'm repeating, the GLP-1 is a, I would say, this year, maybe next year phenomena also because you see that saturation coming in down the line as a CMO partner. So we foresee there will be a static margins happening there.

items.statement: Significant leadership hiring in international infertility, aesthetics, hospital care platforms in FY26; contributions to reflect more in FY27
items.quote: we were investing significantly in the leadership bandwidth, bringing in new heads across international infertility, aesthetics and the hospital care platform, people whose contribution will reflect more in FY27 than in FY26.

items.statement: Invested INR6.5 crores in Saraswat Bank shares (face value INR10) for relationship maintenance and 15% dividend yield vs 8% borrowing cost
items.quote: The bank has come with the proposal to allot only around 24 top customers for this year allotment as a face value of INR10 each. The past history of the bank is that they are giving a dividend of around 15% every year. And if we get a 15% return on the investment, whereas we borrow the same amount at 8%, one advantage is that we will going to earn because of this extra income of 7% to 8%.

items.statement: R&D spend 8-12% of revenue annually; focus on peptides, NDDS, complex injectables, liposomal, depot suspensions
items.quote: Because every year, we do almost R&D, which is worth almost 10% at least 8% to 12% depending on the year and how the CFO gives us any budget. But we spend 8% to 10% of our top line revenue in our R&D budget every year.

items.statement: FY29 AUM target of 500 crores
items.quote: Looking forward, our FY29 target is an AUM of 500 crores and our path is anchored by three pillars of the Shalibhadra 2.0 strategy that I want to speak in specific.

items.statement: Target 100 branches by FY27
items.quote: We are targeting 100 branches by FY27, with selective entry in high-potential new states, including Karnataka and Goa, adding to our existing presence across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.

items.statement: Expect ROA to decline to around 7% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: Currently, ROA is in the range of 8.65%. So, within next two to three years, we expect it to be around 7%.

items.statement: Nationalized bank borrowing share to reach 50-60% by FY29
items.quote: Currently 40% is the nationalized bank borrowing and we expect this to be in the range of 50 to 60%. Going forward, maybe next year, around FY29, 60% would be a better ratio.

items.statement: NNPA expected to remain around 1% for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Currently, our NNPA is in the range of 1%. Going forward, I think it will be in the same range. For next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Target 500 crores AUM in 3 years and 1000 crores in 5 years if all goes well
items.quote: We have targeted 500 crores within three years. Maybe another two years, within five years, we'll be able to reach 1000 crores AUM if everything goes right.

items.statement: Capex of 20 lakhs per branch with break-even in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: And with respect to capex, normally there's a capex of 20 lakhs per branch. That is the initial investment which is required. And normally within say one, one and a half year, the branches recover that.

items.statement: Branch rollout target of one branch per month to reach 70 branches by end of current calendar year
items.quote: So, branch rollout schedule would be to reach 70 branches by current calendar year. That is our main target. And going forward, maybe it will end the year by 75 branches and next year maybe we'll reach 85 branches.

items.statement: AUM grew 25% YoY to 220 crores in FY26
items.quote: We closed the year with an AUM of 220 crores, a 25% growth from 176 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Expect 300 crores AUM from existing products and 200 crores from new products at 500 crores total AUM
items.quote: So, if we reach a scenario where we reach 500 crores of AUM, I expect that around 300 crores would be from existing products, that is two-wheelers and three-wheelers, four-wheelers. And around 200 crores of AUM would be from newer products.

items.statement: Yield on advances declined from 25.4% to 20.8% due to market rate reduction and competition
items.quote: Overall yields in the market have also reduced at the rate with what we are lending. Not for our institution, but for larger banks also. There has been a reduction in margin, overall reduction in lending rates.

items.statement: Credit cost expected at 1% for mortgage loans vs 2% for two-wheeler loans
items.quote: We expect that the credit cost will be in the range of 1% in the case of mortgage loan.

items.statement: Target product mix of 60% two-wheelers and 40% newer products in next three years
items.quote: So what, what I said earlier, also what we're targeting is that next three years two wheelers would remain at 60% and what other newer products would be 40%.

items.statement: 40% of new loans to existing customers; 5 lakh credit-worthy customer franchise
items.quote: So, currently, 40% of the whatever new loans we are offering are to the same existing customer. Over the last two to three decades, we have accumulated around 5 lakh credit-worthy customers.

items.statement: Competition may pressure margins; ROA expected to decline to 7% in 2-3 years
items.quote: There may be some pressure on our margins and maybe in the next two to three years, the ROA will be in the range of 7%. There may be some reduction in spread because of competition.

items.statement: Fixed lending rates insulate from RBI rate changes; borrowing cost impact only on spread
items.quote: See, all our loans are at a fixed rate of interest at what we lend. So, our lending rate remains same irrespective of whatever may be the action by RBI.

items.statement: Total borrowing 50 crores as of March 31; 40% from nationalized banks at 10-10.5%
items.quote: So, as on 31st March, o ur total borrowing was around 50 crores out of which I think 20 crores would be from nationalized banks. So, currently 40% is the nationalized bank borrowing

items.statement: NCD cost to gradually reduce from 12% as experience grows
items.quote: Firstly, that was the first time that we have raised NCD. That's why we raised it 12%. Going forward, now we have an experience of how to raise NCD, what is the process involved, who are the investors. So, there will be a gradual reduction in the interest rate that we offer on NCDs.

items.statement: GNPA at 2.94%; CRAR at 78.28% providing headroom to scale to 1000 crores AUM without equity dilution
items.quote: We maintained our nearly 100% secured book, kept our GNPA 2.94% and brought our CRAR to a very strong 78.28% which gives us a substantial headroom to scale without needing equity dilution for the foreseeable future.

items.quote: In the areas where we are operating currently, we could say around 60% of the vehicles which are being sold are financed by us in the geographies where we are operating.

items.quote: Typically, if a branch reaches 50 lakhs of AUM, that is a good thing if it is able to reach that AUM, maybe say within 1-1.5 years. And that would be a break-even point also.

items.quote: Majority of our customer depend on agriculture as their source of income. So, if there is some drought, or maybe because of there is some irregular rainfall, that would be a dampener because of which there will be a spike in NPAs and we might have to slow down our growth.

items.quote: Almost 100% of the process is automated. So, the entire process, right from onboarding the customer up to disbursement, up to collections, everything goes into automation.

items.quote: Till 1,000 crores of AUM, we do not need any further equity dilution. With the use of NCDs and term loans, that is why we have debt, we wil l be able to reach an AUM of 1,000 crores in near future without diluting
