items.statement: Acemoney: 1.5 lakh merchants with POS, 60k sound boxes, INR1,140 crore digital transactions in FY26.
items.value: 1.5L POS, 60k sound boxes, INR1,140 cr txns
items.quote: Currently, we have approximately 1.5 lakh merchants on boarded for POS machines and added approximately 60,000 sound boxes. Over the year, we also facilitated digital transactions of approximately INR1,140 crores.

items.statement: Acemoney breakeven revenue run rate ~INR4.5 crore per quarter.
items.quote: to achieve breakeven, it will be slightly less. Then we will be probably at about INR4.5 crores per quarter is what the breakeven revenues will be.

items.statement: Applied for payment aggregator license from RBI for holding company.
items.quote: we are also applying and trying to secure in the main company, the holding company, a payment aggregator license from the RBI.

items.statement: Management guides 25-30% revenue growth for FY27 and expresses confidence in achieving 35% PAT growth
items.quote: we are very confident that we will be growing at that pace. And since we have come up with our new retail store where our -- which is going to add an additional boost to our bottom line, so our margins are going to be higher. So our PAT would be improved. So in that case, we are confident of achieving 35%.

items.statement: Management targets retail contribution to reach 25% of total sales within 2 financial years
items.quote: we have already defined that in upcoming 2 financial years, we would be reaching at least 25% of the total sale as a retail contribution.

items.statement: Retail segment margins expected at 10-12%, higher than current blended margins
items.quote: In that, we have surely a higher margin bracket that is somewhere around 10% to 12%. So it is going to add up an additional bottom line improvement.

items.statement: Management expects margins to sustain and improve on a consistent and sustainable basis due to shift to higher-margin segments
items.quote: So our margins have improved, and we are improving on that on a constrained and sustainable basis. So in near future also, the margins will surely improve. The bottom line, it will surely improve.

items.statement: New flagship showroom of 10,000 sq ft (6,800 sq ft sales area) opened in Chennai 2 months ago
items.quote: Since the flagship showroom of 10,000 square feet, we have a sales area of around 6,800 square feet there. In that case, we cannot define perfectly immediately because only 2 months have gone with the new store.

items.statement: Plans to expand retail footprint with smaller format stores initially in Tamil Nadu, then pan-India
items.quote: Since we have started up with our flagship showroom in the upcoming years, we do have plans of expanding into a retail store, not of the same size of what we have done. We also are a smaller size. And since we have a strong presence, our presence in South India in Tamil Nadu. So initially, we are going to expand in surrounding Tamil Nadu and later on, we will be planning to expand pan-India.

items.statement: New Chennai showroom targets INR 450-500 crores revenue in near future
items.quote: That's what, with the new store, we are -- we have defined targets of around INR450 crores to INR500 crores in the near future.

items.statement: Current inventory cycle 70-75 days, overall working capital cycle 52 days; inventory days increased due to new retail store stock
items.quote: Sorry, inventory cycle is around 70 to 75 days. And overall, the working capital cycle is 52 days. Since we have entered an additional stock for our retail store now, the inventory turnover cycle has been a little increased, number of days have increased.

items.statement: Receivables collected within a week maximum
items.quote: overall working capital days are 52, but data and all we receive in a week maximum.

items.statement: Inventory turnover target of 3-4 turns for retail segment; B2B turnover cycle very fast
items.quote: And basically, for the B2B segment, the turnover days are very high. What they say turnover cycle is very fast. And for the retail segment, yes, it would be at least whatever stock we are holding, we are expecting to have 3 to 4 turns.

items.statement: No fundraising planned for expansion; growth to be funded internally
items.quote: Yes, initially, the management has not planned for any fundraising or anything of that sort. It would be done -- any expansion plan, currently, it is planned on internal funding only.

items.statement: Demand resilient despite elevated gold prices; any impact from price spikes or policy changes is short-lived (1-2 fortnights or 1 month)
items.quote: But that is diluted into the market and diluted in the minds of the consumer in a very short period of time, maybe, say, 1 or 2 fortnights or even 1 month. Then once again, it's normal. So we do not see any, what they say, reduction in demand or pain.

items.statement: PM Modi's appeal to stop gold buying seen as short-term impact (1-2 months); long-term demand strong due to cultural significance and household gold recycling
items.quote: Maybe yes, for a shorter period of time, say, 1 or 2 months, there are clear idea about how things are operating on the recyclable household gold.

items.statement: No margin decline from PM's appeal; top line may temporarily reduce but gold exchange/recycling adds business
items.quote: No, there is no decline in margins at all. Yes, there is a possibility that for a certain period of time, smaller period of time, yes, the top line may be sales may reduce, but even then the consumers are ready to exchange their gold. And that exchange recycling of household gold will add up business only, and there are no impacts on margin.

items.statement: Inventory management and pricing policies mitigate impact of 15-20% gold price fall on inventory value and profitability
items.quote: As we have an already, what they say, inventory management and pricing policies and all, and we have a very vast experience of managing all those. So it may not have much impact because everywhere when it is -- whatever we sell, we buy it back and we have an inventory management system. So whatever the price corrections happen, it is not going to impact our margins or our business.

items.statement: Retail average invoice size INR 1.5-1.7 lakhs; wholesale ticket size not defined due to diverse client base
items.quote: But yes, for the retail segment, say, average invoice size is somewhere around INR1.5 lakhs to INR1.7 lakhs.

items.statement: Differentiation through 5-decade legacy, in-house design capabilities, first-to-market with high-demand designs, and handmade jewelry
items.quote: And we have been producing our own design. It has been widely accepted and it has been on the longer run, we have been creators of the, what you say, latest design with the market requirement. And we have been expertise in that for a very long time. That makes us different from the -- all other competitive players.

items.statement: Strategic focus on premiumization via Vajraa Diamonds brand gaining traction; lightweight and low-carat jewelry introduced to address high gold prices
items.quote: Furthermore, our strategic focus on premiumization, particularly through our diamond jewelry segment under the brand Vajraa Diamonds is gaining traction. The positive response from customers and trade channels reinforces our confidence in driving value-led growth through design innovation and category expansion.

items.statement: Asset-light manufacturing model with outsourced production across India; designs sourced in-house and from artisans
items.quote: So we have been operating into an asset-light manufacturing. As you know, our primary, what they say, base is designing in diamond and jewelry industry, the primary is designing. And we have spread over all over India, various factories which have been working for us.

items.statement: FY26 total income INR 2,051.02 crores (+15.71% YoY), EBITDA INR 126.99 crores (+95.69% YoY), EBITDA margin 6.19% (+253 bps), PAT INR 89.42 crores (+98.87% YoY), PAT margin 4.36% (+182 bps)
items.quote: During FY26, we reported healthy improvement in overall financial performance with total income increasing by 15.71% year-on-year to INR2,051.02 crores, EBITDA stood at INR126.99 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 95.69%, while EBITDA margin improves by 253 basis points year-on-year to 6.19%.

items.statement: H2 FY26 total income INR 1,098.26 crores (+8.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 73.21 crores (+102.79% YoY), EBITDA margin 6.67% (+312 bps), PAT INR 50.72 crores (+103.6% YoY), PAT margin 4.62% (+217 bps)
items.quote: For H2 FY26, total income stood at INR1,098.26 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 8.1%. EBITDA stood at INR73.21 crores, registering a growth of 102.79% year-on-year, while EBITDA margins improved by 312 basis points year-on-year to 6.67%.

items.statement: Execution risk in retail transition seen as low due to legacy presence in both B2B and B2C segments
items.quote: Now we are planning to expand B2C also so that we can improve our bottom line and match with the competition of B2B also. So in that case, this what they say, having into B2C market is not new for the company, it is a long legacy, and it is carry forward.

items.statement: Government initiatives on gold monetization and recycling could reduce import dependence and create sustainable domestic supply chain
items.quote: Initiatives such as expanding the gold monetization ecosystem and granting license to eligible entities for gold collection, recycling and monetization are aimed at mobilizing idle gold holdings. This could help reduce India's dependence on gold import, improve the current account deficit and create a more sustainable domestic gold supply chain.

items.statement: Management cites long legacy and experienced team as key to managing design, production, and market cycles
items.quote: And the management has a very vast experience of managing all this. So in that case, yes, we are very confident of growing at a pace of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: FY26 presales guidance of INR600 crores surpassed with actual presales of INR615 crores
items.quote: FY26 was a strong operational year for the company, with presales increasing by 23% year-on-year to INR615 crores, surpassing our guidance of INR600 crores.

items.statement: FY26 presales grew 23% YoY to INR615 crores; sales area up 42% to 1.31 lakh sq ft; collections up 9% to INR421 crores
items.quote: For FY26, the company delivered a strong operational performance with sales value increasing by 23% year-on-year to INR615 crores, surpassing the company's guidance of INR600 crores. Sales area during the year increased by 42% year-on-year to 1,31,167 square feet, while collection grew by 9% year-on-year to INR421 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 39.7% from 37.4% in FY25; PAT declined to INR90 crores due to higher finance costs from acquisitions
items.quote: EBITDA for the year increased to INR223 crores from INR207 crores in FY25, while EBITDA margins improved to 39.7% from 37.4% in FY25. PAT for FY26 stood at INR90 crores. The decline in PAT during the year was primarily attributed to the higher finance costs arising from strategic acquisitions.

items.statement: Acquired 100% of Hally Pacific Private Limited for INR30.40 crores (land at Sayani Road, Prabhadevi, GDV INR200 crores); signed binding MOU for land contiguous to Suraj One Business Bay (additional 1.5 lakh sq ft, GDV INR800 crores)
items.quote: Additionally, during the quarter, we have successfully completed the acquisition of 100% shareholding in Hally Pacific Private Limited, which owns a strategically located land at Sayani Road, Prabhadevi Mumbai. The acquisition completed for a consideration of approximately INR30.40 crores, strengthens our development pipeline in South Central Mumbai with an estimated GDV potential of INR200 crores

items.statement: Ongoing projects unsold inventory GDV ~INR1,100 crores; upcoming pipeline 12.12 lakh sq ft at avg INR60,000/sq ft = INR7,500-7,600 crores GDV
items.quote: So, on the ongoing portfolio unsold inventory, we are estimated to -- considering the current market value is close to INR1,100 crores. For the upcoming portfolio of projects, 12 lakh 12 thousand square feet is the total carpet area, which, on an average at INR60,000 per square feet translates to close to INR7,500 crores, INR7,600 crores.

items.statement: FY27 presales guidance to be given in next quarterly call; management expects better performance due to commercial project launches and institutional demand
items.quote: We can give the guidance. We are planning to do the guidance in the next call. Of course, we estimate it will do much better than this year because most of the projects, especially our commercial projects in the launch stage, and we see good interest from institutional demand. So, we will give a guidance of presales in the next call.

items.statement: FY26 average realization fell to INR45,775/sq ft from INR54,586/sq ft in FY25 due to higher contribution from value luxury and commercial vs luxury projects (Palette INR65-70k, Ocean Star INR85-90k)
items.quote: So in FY26, we have launched value luxury projects and the major sales have come from value luxury and commercial, wherein FY25 had contribution from luxury projects like Palette and Ocean Star, where the market prices for Palette is in range of INR65,000 per square feet to INR70,000 per square feet and Ocean Star is INR85,000 per square feet to INR90,000 per square feet. So that is the product mi

items.statement: EBITDA margins guided at 35-40% for upcoming portfolio; commercial projects at 25-30% EBITDA margin (vacant land acquisitions), residential at higher margins
items.quote: So, EBITDA margins would be in the range of 35% to 40%, close to 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Net debt INR579.91 crores as of Mar 2026; targeted FY27 net debt INR600-650 crores (temporary increase from new launches, then reduction from project completions)
items.quote: So, debt would be -- we are targeting for new projects, there will be increase in debt, but the old projects which we are going to complete in this particular financial year, the debt will come down. So overall, we estimate net debt of close to INR650-odd crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Weighted average interest cost ~13% (up from 12-12.5% due to land acquisition funding at higher rates)
items.quote: So overall weighted average interest rate is close to 13%.

items.statement: FY27 launch pipeline: INR500-600 crores residential GDV (over 3-9 months) + commercial launches (full year effect) = total ~INR1,400 crores GDV launches
items.quote: No. So, the residential side still remains at INR600 crores like we committed earlier. The shortfall, which was done earlier of INR800 crores was the commercial, which we have now acquired, and we see that launch also happening. So, if you add both, it's between INR1,400 crores is what we see a launch pipeline right now, including the commercial.

items.statement: Strong commercial demand seen; residential sales decline attributed to limited inventory (INR150 crores remaining), not buyer slowdown; new society redevelopment tie-ups signed, announcements soon
items.quote: It's majorly attributed to the limited inventory.

items.statement: Bandra (Mount Mary) project: 2 of 3 land parcels conveyed; balance acquisitions targeted in next 2 quarters; launch readiness minimum 1 year away (likely FY28 Q1)
items.quote: The 2 land parcels, our internal timeline is to complete all the acquisitions in the next 3 to 6 -- the next 2 quarters would be going for acquisitions of the balance lands. And we've already started preparatory work in terms of initial feasibilities and everything else. So, we look at least a year from now, minimum a year from now for launch.

items.statement: FY26 average realization INR45,775/sq ft (corrected from INR46,895); Q4 FY26 realization INR45,618/sq ft (corrected from INR45,648)
items.quote: Average realization for FY26 stood at INR46,895 (Wrongly said kindly read it as 45,775) per square feet. Realization remained relatively moderate during the year due to a higher contribution from the value luxury segment as compared to the contribution of luxury segment in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 presales INR128 crores: commercial INR54.6 crores, residential INR74 crores; commercial sales skewed due to full-year launch effect vs residential launches phased over 3-9 months
items.quote: So just to correct, we have achieved in quarter 4 INR128 crores of presales, out of which the commercial project has contributed close to INR54.6 crores in the GDV. So, what remains is INR74 crores coming from residential segment.

items.statement: No external credit rating currently (only bank internal ratings); plans to get rated under discussion; stock price down ~50% in 1 year despite operational delivery
items.quote: I think right now, there's no rating done by an agency as of now. It's more internal -- it's more of the bank's internal rating.

items.statement: Market share growth strategy: focus on society redevelopments adjacent to existing projects for FSI/cluster value addition, not isolated societies
items.quote: So, I think the way forward would be society redevelopments, which are joining our ongoing projects so that we could add maximum value to -- in terms of FSI or in terms of cluster redevelopment. So, this is what our main focus would be on. We would not just do isolated society, but something which is ongoing to our existing so that it adds value in terms of FSI and FSI potential.

items.statement: Targets PAT to grow 4x-5x in 3-5 years; minimum INR300 crore PAT for FY27
items.quote: Our target for 3 to 5 years is 7,000 to 10,000 beds. The target for the next 4 years is to increase PAT by about 4 x to 5x from here.

items.statement: Targets INR3000 crore revenue in 3-5 years with 50-50 services-products mix
items.quote: We see INR3000 crores in sales in the next 3 to 5 years, so why would we focus on INR2 crores to INR4 crores?

items.statement: Operational beds to increase from 2,300 to 2,800-3,000 in 3-4 months; target 3,000-3,500 by March 2026
items.quote: Currently, we have about 2,300 operational beds, which we will increase to 3,000 operational beds in the next 3 to 4 months, with 445 more in active deployment.

items.statement: Can add 2,000 beds within a year when Ayushman scheme payment portal is ready
items.quote: As soon as any news comes from the Government of India and their payment portal is fixed, I have the power to immediately increase 2,000 beds within a year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 44% (up 1,360 bps YoY); Q4 margin 36% impacted by INR21 crore one-time items
items.quote: EBITDA margin in FY26 reached 44%, up from 30% in FY25, an improvement of 1,360 basis points in a single year.

items.statement: Excluding one-time items, Q4 EBITDA margin would be ~46%
items.quote: You are absolutely right. Actually, what happened is that our labour laws changed, so the impact of that came in.

items.statement: FY26 IPD volume up 65% to 40,450; OPD volume up 69% to 600,000+; Q4 OPD/video/daycare up 247%/214%/139% YoY
items.quote: For the full year FY26, IPD patient volume increased by 65% to 40,450. OPD patient volume increased by 69% from FY25 to reach over 6,00,000.

items.statement: Health insurance contribution rose from 4% to 26% of total sales in one year
items.quote: For the last 1 year continuously 1 year ago, our health insurance contribution was 4%. Today, my health insurance contribution has reached 26% in total sales.

items.statement: Product vertical contributed INR416 crore (52% of revenue) in FY26; gross margins >85% on 330+ SKUs
items.quote: Under the product business, we have more than 330 SKUs, gr oss margins exceeding 85%, and we follow AYUSH standards and Government of India

items.statement: OTC pharmacy retail expansion launched; 9 new products in last 3 months; pregnancy wellness products launching in June
items.quote: We are expanding the product portfolio into OTC pharmacy retail. New launches have already begun, and international expansion has also started from the UAE.

items.statement: Empaneled with CGHS, CAPF, ECHS, Air India, Air Asia, major insurers, and state governments (UP, Bihar, Haryana, Punjab)
items.quote: We are empaneled with CGHS, CAPF, ECHS, Air India, and Air Asia. All major health insurance companies are empaneled with us on a cashless and reimbursement basis.

items.statement: UP government launched UPSS scheme with cashless Ayurveda; Ayushman Bharat draft rates INR8,800-9,400/day expected in 1-2 months
items.quote: The new draft from the Government of India for the Ayushman scheme, which God willing will be implemented in a month or a month and a half, is also coming in at a rate of INR8,800 to INR9,400.

items.statement: Grant Thornton audit completed; first Big 4 audit; resulted in one-time provisions for lease accounting, ECL, loyalty points
items.quote: For the first time, our balance sheet has been audited through Grant Thornton, one of the world's top four companies.

items.statement: Revenue recognition changed: advances no longer booked as revenue; INR8 crore advance as of May 31 carried to June
items.quote: GT said in our practices that you should only book the patient once the bill is generated and they leave. Otherwise, my fourth quarter is INR6 crores higher than the third quarter in terms of collections.

items.statement: Luxury wellness centers opening in Panchkula (June) and Manali (July); 108 rooms, 22 villas, helipads, forest bathing
items.quote: Sir, mostly, I am starting two luxury wellness centers this month in June one in Panchkula, Chandigarh and one I am starting in Manali in July.

items.statement: Repeat rates: 26% for hospital admissions, 34% for products (last quarter)
items.quote: In the last quarter's data, in our hospital business, if I take the admitted business, there was a 26% repeat business. And on our product side, there was a 34% repeat business.

items.statement: Cost ratios improved YoY: direct cost 12%->11%, manpower 21%->19%, advertising 12%->8%, rent 7%->6%, other opex 15%->9%
items.quote: In FY25, our direct cost was 12%, but in FY26, it became 11%, it decreased by 1%. Manpower cost was 21% in FY25, which decreased to 19% this year.

items.statement: International expansion started from UAE; foreign health insurance policies accepted for cashless treatment
items.quote: International expansion has also started from the UAE, where demand for authentic, evidence-based Ayurveda care is increasing.

items.statement: INR9-10 crore one-time bonus to junior staff; ESOP provisioning; new hospital managers appointed for each facility
items.quote: Plus, we gave an extra bonus to our team, our junior staff whose salaries are low; that was about INR9 crores to INR10 crores.

items.statement: Swadeshi Health Card launched with referral benefits, diagnostic discounts, loyalty points; trial phase ongoing
items.quote: In this quarter, the Jeena Sikho Swadeshi Health Card was successfully launched. This is a swadeshi initiative designed to strengthen pati ent loyalty through referral benefits, diagnostic discounts, and seamless service integration across the entire

items.statement: Research credibility: 550 papers written, 400 accepted, 180+ published; 7 Nobel Prize studies referenced in treatment protocols
items.quote: We have written about 550 papers last year, of which about 400 have been accepted, and more than 180 are already published and documented in peer-reviewed research papers.

items.statement: Management projects 12-15% consolidated revenue growth for FY27 and targets crossing INR500 crore revenue within the financial year.
items.quote: So our projection is, from my end, it would be around something between 12% to 15% at a consolidated level. Debajit Choudhury: Actually we have achieved at the consolidated level something around INR436 crore s and we have a target of achieving INR500 crores within the financial year and it seems that we shall be able to achieve it even po ssibly maybe some time to spare

items.statement: Management expects strong growth tailwinds in West Bengal due to new government investments and sees pent-up demand in CCTV segment as STQC certification eases and tenders pick up.
items.quote: We are expecting a lot of investments in West Bengal due to the change in the government and our Chief Minister has already announced that. And we being a very established operator in this state for different kinds of industries and commercial activities and government infrastructures, we do see a very strong uptick on our business vertical once these projects get sanctioned and they take up.

items.statement: One-time exceptional provision of INR27.82 crore taken in FY26 for new Labor Codes implementation (standardized wage definition impacting employee benefit obligations); impact is non-cash and transitionary.
items.quote: Based on this assessment, we recognized a one -time exceptional provision of INR27.82 crores during FY26. This impact i s non -cash, accounting -led and transitionary in nature, reflecting alignment with statutory

items.quote: in the security and facility management industry, all costs which are related to the contract labor is passed through to the client. Mulesh Savla: Okay. Kanad Mukherjee: So everything is passed through to the client. We undergo minimum wage hikes during the year. Different states have it at different times , but it happens every year, twice a year. So that is passed through to the client. PF, ESIC

The reason for that increase in INR5 crore s is because we kind of suffered colle ction issues with four contracts. One is Haldia Dock, because of certain operational issues, the bills for five months were stuck. Which has now been cleared in the months of April and May

items.statement: Top clients: Reliance Retail (~INR30-36 crore), DTET (~INR24 crore), Airport (~INR22-23 crore), HDFC Bank (~INR19 crore), Anjali Jewellers (~INR12-13 crore); average client tenure 4.5-5 years.
items.quote: Ma'am, the largest revenue contributor is currently Reliance Retail at around INR30 crores. It will be slightly more, couple of purchase orders are yet to come. So this year it should be around INR35 crores, INR36 crores. And after that there is the Directorate of Technical Education and Training which contributes around INR24 crores.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR36.91 crore remain unutilized as of FY26 end; cash & equivalents INR67.13 crore; management expects significant deployment in FY27 and full deployment within 2 years.
items.quote: Sir, currently INR36.91 crores is unutilized. And if you look at, sir, our consolidated balance sheet, whatever we had deployed during the year has come back. So if you look at our cash and cash equivalents, it's around INR67.13 crores and other non-current assets is around INR16.22 crores.

items.statement: CCTV rental business (INR12 crore revenue, ~INR7 crore rental) generated ~INR4 crore EBITDA in FY26 as prior capex matured; expects CCTV revenue pickup within 6 months as STQC licensing expands and tenders convert.
items.quote: Although the CCTV business did not show much growth compared to last year, because around INR7 crores of the INR12 crores was rental. So whose capex was done in '24, '25, we saw an EBITDA of around INR4 crores coming just from there. So that will continue this year also.

items.statement: Security services revenue INR199.49 crore (46.03% of total); Housekeeping & Payroll INR171.01 crore (39.46%); IFM, Electronic Security & CCTV INR56.91 crore (13.31%); Other INR5.99 crore.
items.quote: From a segment perspective, security services remained our largest vertical contributing INR199.49 crore s and accounting for 46.03% o f total revenue. Housekeeping and payroll contributed INR171.01 crores representing 39.46% of revenue. Integrated facility management, electronic security and CCTV rentals contributed to INR56.91 crores or 13.31% of revenue

items.statement: Labor Code formalization expected to pressure informal operators; NIS benefits as larger clients prefer compliant, audit-ready partners; industry formalization historically boosted NIS.
items.quote: Smaller and informal operators may face increased pressure due to higher compliance requirements, while larger corporate and government clients are likely to prefer organized, audit-ready and compliant service partners who can manage workforce scale with proper systems and documentation.

items.statement: ICRA reaffirmed short-term rating at A2 and upgraded long-term rating outlook to positive from stable (BBB+).
items.quote: During the period, ICRA also reaffirmed our short-term rating at ICRA A2 and upgraded the outlook on our long-term rating of ICRA BBB+ from stable to positive.

items.statement: Skill development (DDU-GKY, PMKVY) projects restarting after 2-3 year lull; Keertika Academy revenue fell from INR4 crore to INR2 crore as projects ended; expects Odisha award by June, Maharashtra and West Bengal under evaluation.
items.quote: The different government schemes like the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana which is DDU-GKY or the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana. These had been very slow in coming. And in fact over the last two-three years there had been no new projects which had come about in the DDU-GKY or PMKVY area. But now these have started coming in.

items.statement: Targeting revenue of approximately Rs.500 Crores in FY2027 with PAT margin of 12% to 13%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are targeting a revenue of approximately Rs.500 Crores in FY 2027 while maintaining PAT margin in the range between 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of Rs.486.9 Crores as of May 2026 and active bid pipeline of Rs.1200 Crores
items.quote: As of May 2026, our unexecuted order books stood at approximately Rs.486.9 Crores providing healthy visibility for FY2027. In addition, we have an active bid pipeline of approximately Rs.1200 Crores across railways, metro systems, defence and aerospace opportunities.

So, we include that product as goodies.

items.statement: Positioned as affordable luxury / mass premium; benchmark against international brands, not Indian brands; quality is key differentiator
items.quote: We compare ourselves with international brands. We do not compare ourselves with any Indian brand. We say we are affordable luxury. Recode is a replacement for international brands. items.quote: We had one previously, but currently there is no brand ambassador as we are in a growth model and do not want to spend on that right now.

items.quote: Like I said, approximately 5 % to 6% on the current tanks that are leased out, that is what we hope to achieve every year.

items.quote: EBITDA margin, see EBITDA margin , what we are looking at is in the band of, you know, 9 to 11% kind of thing.

items.quote: That should be anywhere around, you know, ₹50 -60 crore. Around ₹50 crore at least from last year's ₹36 crore, we should target at least ₹50 crore from Pune.

items.quote: So, I would say anywhere between ₹5 to ₹10 crore is our current year target.

items.quote: As of today, the Malur plant is fully operational. The tooling required for our target product mix, medium and heavy fabrication for the construction equipment segment, is in place and validated.

items.statement: Pune plant FY26 revenue ₹36-38 crore; optimal capacity ~₹50-60 crore at 80% utilization
items.quote: That should be anywhere around, you know, ₹50 -60 crore.

items.quote: All the products' approvals are in place, and the billing has started, which means invoicing from that plant has also started.

items.statement: Export contribution 14.2% of FY26 revenue (₹22.83 crore); Malur designed to international export standards
items.quote: Our export contribution reached 14.2% of revenue in FY26, ₹22.83 crore.

items.statement: Finance costs expected to remain at Q4 FY26 level; no significant reduction guided
items.quote: Yeah, that should be, should be around the same level as it is in the Q4.

items.quote: Total assets at ₹148.7 crore, property, plant and equipment at ₹94.7 crore, debt-to-equity at a disciplined 0.29x.

items.quote: The fourth quarter continued the momentum. Revenue from operations increased 22.2% year-on-year to INR243.5 crores. Liquid terminaling was INR121.1 crores, up 31%, driven by higher volumes, capacity additions, and a more favorable product mix. Gas terminaling was INR122.4 crores, up 14.6%, with quarterly gas throughput reaching 1 million metric tons.

items.statement: Raised INR660 crores via Series 1 NCDs and INR1,030 crores via Series 2 NCDs (both NSE listed) to diversify funding base and lock in long-term capital at competitive rates
items.quote: During the year, we raised INR660 crores through Series 1 non-convertible debentures and INR1,030 crores through Series 2 NCDs, both were NSE listed. These issuances reflect strong investor confidence in our growth strategy and have enabled us to diversify our funding base, lock in long-term capital at competitive rates, and further strengthen our balance sheet.

items.statement: No formal guidance given, but historically target 30-40% YoY throughput growth; expect similar 30-40% throughput growth in current year
items.quote: No, we don't give guidance, but I think what we have always said, generally we do a 30% to 40% growth as far as throughput is concerned year-on-year. We continue to say so. So, I think we should do between 30% to 40% growth as far as throughput is concerned in this year also.

items.statement: FY27 capex to reach USD1.2 billion; FY28 capex expected generally in range of close to INR5,000 crores
items.quote: FY27, of course, we have already said we'll reach USD1.2 billion capex. '28, there are still some things to be summed up. We will soon come up with the numbers for FY28, but I think it will definitely be generally in the range of close to INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: JNPT liquid expansion expected to achieve good realization from commissioning, not gradual ramp-up, due to strong demand at JNPA
items.quote: No, full. I think JNPA, unlike other ports, has more demand. So, we don't expect it to gradually increase realization; it will be quite a good realization from the time it commissions. It will start commissioning from probably next month onwards, and you will see by H1 most of the capacity operative. Probably by October, we should finish.

items.statement: Most leases not near maturity; lessee has last look under land policy; only Pipavav Port lease dependent on concessionaire in 2029
items.quote: So, lease -- most of our leases are not very old. So, we have still long time to go before the lease maturity happens. But as you are aware, under the land policy, the lessee has got a last look. So, we are not -- I mean, we don't have to be unduly worried when the lease is mature. There is only one lease of Pipavav Port which is dependent on the concessionaire, which is in 2029. Otherwise, I thin

items.statement: LPG imports affected by Middle East conflict (50% down in March, 30-35% down in May); vertical integration with Aegis Logistics distribution helped utilization; expect normalization from Q2 FY27
items.quote: Yes, so of course, in LPG, the national oil companies had a supply source problem when the ships were stranded in Strait of Hormuz since the war began in March. Volumes were affected from March where it was generally a 50% down. But from May onwards, I think things are getting much better. Now it's no more 50%, but 30% to 35% as far as May is concerned. We expect the things to get normalized soon.

items.statement: Temporary ups and downs like Middle East conflict create opportunities for infrastructure business; believe investors and stakeholders see it that way
items.quote: There will always be temporary ups and downs like we saw with the situation with the Middle East conflict, but in fact, we believe that, that has opened up enormous opportunities for infrastructure business like ours. And we hope that all the investors and stakeholders see it that way as well, and we look forward to going on this exciting journey.

items.statement: Management reiterated revenue target of INR600-700 crores in next 2.5-3 years but declined to give FY27 guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: we are very strongly seeing our vision and target of INR600 to INR700 crores of revenue in the next 2.5 to 3 years, which we also guided in the previous earnings call

items.statement: Demand for construction and mining equipment remained resilient driven by infrastructure spending, industrial capex, and replacement demand across emerging markets
items.quote: demand for construction and mining equipment remained resilient, driven by infrastructure spending, industrial capex, and replacem ent demand across emerging

items.statement: Profitability impacted by higher employee costs, HexL brand investment, and elevated logistics expenses from geopolitical disruption
items.quote: profitability was impacted by a number of factors. This included higher employee benefit expenses and organizational costs, continued investment in product development, dealer network expansion, and market development activities relating to the HexL brand, and elevated logistic expenses arising from geopolitical disruption

items.statement: No order pipeline as business follows inventory-led sales model; 70% of overseas inventory available for retail, 30% allocated for pending orders
items.quote: we don't have an order pipeline as such and it is an inventory-led sales model. So, we have found the balance wherein we refurbish machines, keep our stock ready, and either it gets sold through retail channels by stocking them as inventory or else our B2B cust omers immediately pick them

items.statement: IPO proceeds deployed towards international market development, inventory positioning, team building, organizational strengthening, and brand building activities
items.quote: IPO proceeds have been deployed purposefully towards international market development, inventory positioning, team building, organizational strengthening, and brand building activities

items.statement: Strategically positioned overseas inventory in excess of INR50 crores as of March 31, 2026 to improve delivery timelines and customer responsiveness
items.quote: The group continues to maintain strategically positioned inventory in excess of INR50 crores as at 31st of March 2026

items.statement: Higher logistics costs from geopolitical disruptions absorbed by P&L, identified as primary reason for profitability degrowth
items.quote: the freight cost impact has been absorbed by our P&L, which is why -- which has been the only and only reason for our degrowth in profitability, I would say

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: 5% HexL brand (consolidated), 62% customized machines of other brands, 35% used refurbished equipment
items.quote: 5% from Hexcel brand on consolidated basis, 62% from the customized machines of other brands, and I believe 35% or something like this from the used construction equipment that we refurbished and sold

items.statement: Large majority of customers are repeat customers; targeting new customer acquisition for diversification with every extra crore of working capital
items.quote: a large portion of our customers are repeat customers still. And I would say a large majorit y is coming from repeat orders. We are able to just cater to them and with every extra crore of working capital, we definitely are targeting and eyeing to get new customers on board as well for further diversification

items.statement: Competitive advantage cited as 50+ year family legacy in mining/construction equipment, mechanical engineering background, and trust built over decades
items.quote: Well, I think it's the family legacy of 50-plus years of being in the mining construction equipment space, our mechanical engineering backgrounds of myself, my father, my family. And I think the trust that we really export in form of our products, which ha s been established, proven, appreciated, rewarded

items.statement: FY26 geographic revenue mix: Mexico 46%, UAE 19%, South Africa and Australia ~10% each, rest single-digit percentages
items.quote: Mexico was about 46%, then UAE was 19%, South Africa [Inaudible 0:35:33] and Australia, I think, was about 10% or so

items.statement: Working capital increased due to higher volumes, overseas inventory positioning, and longer export operating cycle; currently at INR300-350 crores, churning 2-2.5x
items.quote: The increase in working capital is primarily attributable to higher business volumes, overseas inventory positioning, and the longer operating cycle inherent in export markets

items.statement: Consolidated net worth increased from INR86 crores to INR194 crores following IPO, significantly strengthening capital base and financial flexibility
items.quote: Consolidated net worth increased from INR86 crores to INR194 crores following the IPO, significantly strengthening the company's capital base and financial flexibility

items.statement: IPO listing on BSE and NSE strengthened balance sheet, enhanced banking relationships, improved working capital access, and increased ability to support larger transaction volumes
items.quote: The funds raised through the IPO have strengthened our balance sheet, enhanced banking relationships, improved access to working capital resources, and increased our ability to support la rger transaction volumes across international

items.statement: HexL brand targets: 11-12% revenue share in FY27 (from 5% in FY26), 150 units sales target in FY27, long-term PAT margin target 12-14%
items.quote: the target would be to make it all the way up to 11% to 12% in FY27. And number of units for FY27 would be close to 150 units

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East conflicts, Strait of Hormuz) makes revenue visibility difficult; currency volatility, freight costs, and war insurance risks are macro factors beyond control
items.quote: It will be very difficult to give any kind of statement on revenu e visibility given the fact that Strait of Hormuz is going to be open or closed

items.statement: Onboarded experienced senior professionals across global operations, international sales, and regional leadership roles; CEO elevated to Managing Director
items.quote: We onboarded experienced senior professionals across global operations, international sales, and regional leadership roles. As the business has grown in complexity and geographic reach, the board elevated me to the position of Managing Director and CEO

items.statement: No immediate plans for new overseas inventory hubs or subsidiaries; will expand to new geographies as opportunities arise (targeting 80-100 countries)
items.quote: Currently, I think we are very well placed and covered. We do not have any immediate plans to expand to new geographies immediately. However, as and when business opportunities come, we are ready to take them up

items.statement: Medium-term target: revenue INR600-800 crores with 5-7% PAT margin on consolidated level before focusing on cash conversion cycle improvement
items.quote: we would really like to see our revenue grow to INR600 crores to INR800 crores first with decent profitability, which means around 5% to 7% of PAT on a consolidated level

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle expected to improve next year as brand establishes; working capital requirement scales at 2-2.5x revenue (every INR100 cr revenue adds INR200-250 cr working capital)
items.quote: I think next year we'll see a better cash conversion cycle

items.statement: HexL brand PAT margin target 12-14% over few years (currently lower due to low volumes, marketing, inventory costs); used equipment refurbishment also targets 12-14% PAT; new equipment of other brands at 2-4% margins
items.period: over the period of few years
items.quote: over the period of few years, I believe 12% to 14% will be targeted in HexL brand. And similarly, 12% to 14% PAT level are targeted in used construction equipment which we refurbish as well. New construction equipment of other brands are usually at like 2% to 4% margins

items.statement: Middle East reconstruction expected to be strongest demand driver; South Africa, Africa, Mexico, Australia, UK, Europe provide diversification against geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: Middle East will be the strongest demand driver with the reconstruction activities as you pointed out, and after every destruction, I think the growth becomes really good, I would say

items.statement: Limiting factor for multi-fold expansion is capital availability; professional-led corporate growth structure being built to unlock next growth avenue
items.quote: I think availability of capital because it's as simple as that. If there is a market size of INR1 lakh crores, then if INR1000 crores --- in a day, we can purchase, we can start the refurbishment operations

items.statement: FTAs with UAE, Australia, UK may contribute to export growth but impact timing uncertain due to geopolitical situations and policy implementation timelines
items.quote: It may contribute to the export growth. However, with the current geopolitical situations and various timelines of these policies being implemented, it is yet to be seen how and when will they start impacting our business

items.statement: Global used construction equipment market size INR1 lakh crore (USD133 billion) in 2024, expected to grow to INR16 lakh crore (USD177 billion); company claims largest Indian exporter share
items.quote: there is a total totality of INR1 lakh crores or USD133 billion market size of used construction equipment as per CareEdge reports, which was in 2024 and expected to grow to INR16 lakh crore s or USD177 billion globally

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 1,000 crores by FY29 and approximately 40% turnover growth target for FY27
items.quote: We have decided that we will achieve this goal in the next three years.

items.statement: FY27 turnover growth target of approximately 40%
items.quote: The target we have set for this year is to increase our turnover by approximately 40%.

items.statement: IPO proceeds to be deployed for working capital expansion and business growth
items.quote: We will focus on deploying IPO proceeds for working capital expansion, accelerating our transition towards the pay-and-collect model, expanding into new geographies and industry segments.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy focused on staffing, workforce management and payroll companies with strong client bases
items.quote: Our focus is on acquiring companies related to workforce management, staffing, and payroll services. We are looking at companies whose work matches our company's profile.

items.statement: Group consolidation to add new clients and reduce infrastructure costs through shared infrastructure
items.quote: The benefit we will get from group consolidation is that new clients will be added. When we acquire any group, we also get its client database and infrastructure.

items.statement: Strong demand from e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics, manufacturing and infrastructure sectors
items.quote: We are primarily focused on e-commerce, quick commerce, and the logistics sector. Now, with the investment from the IPO, we are going forward to the manufacturing and infrastructure sectors also.

items.statement: Balanced approach targeting profitable growth with sustained improvement in return ratios
items.quote: Right now, PAN HR is working on a balanced approach. While certain contracts do come with lower margins, they create a significant operating leverage for us.

items.statement: Transition from collect-and-pay to pay-and-collect model and expansion into higher-margin services like payroll outsourcing and compliance management
items.quote: Second focus will be on the pay-and-collect model earlier we were working on the collect-and-pay model, now our effort will be to participate in those businesses which are in the pay-and-collect model.

items.statement: Expansion into 3PL model and white-collar hiring services within existing client base
items.quote: Our business has started in the West as well. And currently, our manpower deployment has increased from 10,000 to 11,000. And our job is to participate in the 3PL model and B2B model.

items.statement: Workforce deployment increased from 10,000 to 11,000 personnel post-IPO with geographic expansion to South and West regions
items.quote: Earlier our manpower deployment was 10,000 when we brought the IPO, our workforce strength was 10,000. As of today, I have crossed 11,000, who are currently on our payroll.

items.statement: Client base expanded to over 17 clients with focus on deepening relationships and cross-selling 3PL services
items.quote: Today we have more than 10,000 deployments, more than 17 clients, and we have a very strong presence in the logistics, warehouse, and industrial sectors.

items.statement: Virtually debt-free balance sheet with no liabilities before or after IPO
items.quote: Today we are a debt-free company, we don't have any liability, nor was there any before, and even now we don't have any liability.

items.statement: Transition to pay-and-collect model to improve working capital efficiency
items.quote: Accelerating our transition towards the pay-and-collect model.

items.statement: Focus on maintaining healthy ROE and ROCE with temporary fluctuations expected during capital deployment
items.quote: Management's high focus is on maintaining healthy return ratios completely. Yes, there will be some temporary fluctuations because we will deploy our capital for growth and expansion purposes.

items.statement: Compliance credibility as key differentiator with 100% compliance structure since 2015
items.quote: First is compliance credibility. Having an experience from 2015, we are working continuously with a 100% compliance structure.

items.statement: White-collar hiring and one-time staffing services started using existing infrastructure
items.quote: We didn't do white-collar hiring along with this, we have started working on his. With this same infrastructure, our costing will be less there.

items.statement: Focus on technology, operational excellence, HRMS platform, automation and compliance infrastructure
items.quote: Fifth, which will be a very important focus, will be on technology, operational excellence, HRMS platform, and automation, and on compliance infrastructure.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue grew 28% YoY to INR 12,656.59 lakh and PAT grew 158% YoY to INR 432.20 lakh
items.quote: We reported total income of INR12,656.59 lakh, representing a growth of 28% year-on-year, while net profit increased by 158% year-on-year to INR432.20 lakh.

items.statement: Expect normalized EBITDA margin of 12-13% after one-off costs
items.quote: We expect a normalized margin in the range of 12-13%.

items.statement: Expect PAT margins of 4-5% for FY26 and above 5% for FY27
items.quote: They should be around 4-5% for FY26 and move above 5% for FY27.

items.statement: Expect production of 40,000 tons annually at steel price of 100 per kg for sales
items.quote: In terms of production levels, we expect to hit about 40,000 tons on an annual basis, with steel prices at about 100 per kg for sales.

items.statement: Target full capacity utilization of 54,000 tons in FY27
items.quote: For the following year, we intend to reach the full capacity of 54,000 tons.

items.statement: Aspire to reach 7-8% PAT margins going forward
items.quote: Our aspiration is definitely 7-8% margins going forward.

items.statement: Expect finance costs around 4% of turnover in FY26
items.quote: We expect finance costs to be around 4% of turnover.

items.statement: Solar plant capex estimated at 3-3.5 crores at 25-29 per KVA
items.quote: The cost is about 25 to 29 per KVA, so we expect the total cost to be about 3-3.5 crores for the solar expansion.

items.statement: 54,000-ton expansion has 21 crores WIP, additional 10-15 crores capex next year for automation
items.quote: We have 21 crores in work-in-progress, and in the next year, we will invest another 10-15 crores in capex.

items.statement: Future expansion post-FY27 to reach 800-1,000 crores revenue funded by internal accruals and equity
items.quote: We have open land available to build further capacity. To reach 800-1,000 crores in revenue and produce 7,000-8,000 tons a month, we will need more expansion post-FY27. This would be funded through internal accruals and equity.

items.statement: Expanding Umargam capacity from 30,000 to 54,000 tons, completion by October 2025
items.quote: We are expanding our current capacity at Umargam from 30,000 tons to 54,000 tons. This expansion is underway, with a revised completion timeline of October 2025.

items.statement: Sheds 1 and 2 construction 60% complete, full machinery installation by October 2025
items.quote: Our 54,000-ton expansion is progressing. Sheds 1 and 2 are under construction, with 60% completed. We expect to finish everything, including machinery installation, by October 2025.

items.statement: Expect 80-90% utilization of new capacity in FY26, manufacturing over 40,000 tons
items.quote: For FY26, we expect it to be around 80-90%. We anticipate manufacturing over 40,000 tons this year at a price of approximately 100 per kg.

items.statement: Order book grown from 200 crores to approximately 350 crores as of May
items.quote: In terms of our order book, we have grown from close to 200 crores to approximately 350 crores as of May.

items.statement: Order pipeline of 150 crores expected to convert around September or October
items.quote: Around September or October. We have received approval and are waiting for confirmation.

items.statement: Signed MOU for 15,000 tons specifically for data centers
items.quote: We recently signed an MOU for 15,000 tons specifically for data centers.

items.statement: Target order book to revenue ratio of 500 crores orders for 400 crores revenue, carrying 100 crores over
items.quote: We target an order book to revenue ratio where we have at least 500 crores in orders for a 400 crore revenue target, carrying 100 crores over.

items.statement: Maintained 10.86% EBITDA margin in FY25 despite input cost pressure
items.quote: Despite input cost pressure, we maintained a healthy 10.86% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA for H2 FY25 should have been around 14%
items.quote: Normalized EBITDA for H2 should have been around 14%.

items.statement: Automation expected to bring 15-20% efficiency and 1% EBITDA margin improvement by FY28
items.quote: That 1% increase is specifically attributed to automation alone. There will be other improvements beyond that factor.

items.statement: Conversion margin around 30-45 per kg depending on job complexity
items.quote: Our usual play is around 30 to 45 per kg depending on the complexity of the job.

items.statement: Steel price increases passed through via price variation clauses, steel rose from 50-55 to 65-70 per kg
items.quote: This year, steel rose from 50-55 per kg to 65-70. Without this principle, the company would have faced losses. We do not speculate in steel.

items.statement: Could not pass on costs like gas, transport, consumables, paint; took impact in Q1
items.quote: However, there is a fixed portion involving conversion and transport that we are gradually getting clients to accept. We took an impact on this during the first quarter.

items.statement: LPG supply force majeure from sole supplier in March affected cutting operations and caused labor migration
items.quote: Cost inflation, specifically a force majeure from our sole LPG supplier starting in early March, affected cutting and cooking gas operations. This led to issues in completing projects during March, which is a critical month. Additionally, labor unrest led to some migration back to hometowns.

items.statement: Solar plant to reduce energy bills by over 50%, eventually 100% power from solar
items.quote: It should reduce our bills by over 50%. We expect 100% of our power eventually to come from solar.

items.statement: Energy costs were approximately 25-30 lakhs per month in FY25
items.quote: Approximately 25-30 lakhs per month.

items.statement: 70-80% of 34,900 tons production from complex projects
items.quote: Approximately 70-80% is complex work.

items.statement: PEB segment revenue contribution down to 0%, focusing on heavy fabrication over erection
items.quote: We are getting better projects than PEB. We prefer to play a major role where we see more traction. Also, we prefer to concentrate on production rather than erection, so PEB will remain a small part of our portfolio.

items.statement: 90-95% repeat business due to custom heavy fabrication capability
items.quote: Because of this, 90-95% of our orders are repeat business.

items.statement: Added two of India's largest business houses and a major power plant company after audits
items.quote: This year, we also finished audits for two of India's largest business houses and a major power plant company. These clients will be added starting this year.

items.statement: Two more girders orders of similar value under negotiation for power plants
items.quote: We have already uploaded one order, and two more of similar value are under negotiation.

items.statement: Using TReDS, bill discounting, LC of 80 crores, channel financing, and client advances against bank guarantees
items.quote: We have limits for TReDS and bill discounting of MSME invoices, a letter of credit for 80 crores, and channel financing. Since our listing, we have started taking advances from clients against bank guarantees, which helps our cash flow cycle and reduces overall interest costs.

items.statement: Reduced long-term borrowings by 5 crores and short-term borrowings by 10 crores in FY25
items.quote: Regarding the balance sheet, we reduced long-term borrowings by 5 crores and short-term borrowings by 10 crores.

items.statement: Remaining debt mostly between 8% and 11% interest after paying off high-interest unsecured loans
items.quote: We paid off some high-interest unsecured business loans. Most of our remaining debt is between 8% and 11%.

items.statement: Labor migration in March-April due to LPG crisis, expect normalization by end of June
items.quote: We see labor returning, and we expect the situation to normalize by the end of June.

items.statement: Skilled manpower from MP, Jharkhand, Bihar required; automation push to mitigate constraint
items.quote: We do require skilled manpower from regions like MP , Jharkhand, and Bihar. The automation push is intended to mitigate this.

items.statement: Technical Director Satis (chemical engineer, 20 years exp) and Sunil Kataria (1 lakh tons erection for JSW) joined guiding team
items.quote: Satis, a chemical engineer with 20 years of experience, joined as Technical Director. Ganesh, our CFO, is also here. Mr. Sunil Kataria, who has overseen over 1 lakh tons of structural erection for JSW, is part of our guiding team.

items.statement: Khopoli facility exit caused 5,000-6,000 tons capacity reduction and 40 crores revenue impact from labor job
items.quote: We exited the Khopoli facility, which reduced our overall capacity by 5,000-6,000 tons. Additionally, for labor jobs, we do not invest in material, so the revenue looks lower because material prices aren't included. A labor job might be 30 per kg while full fabrication is over 100 per kg. We had about 40 crores less revenue due to this labor work.

items.statement: NCLT case resulted in 1.65 crore bad debt write-off in FY25
items.quote: Last year, we also performed a conversion job for an important client while expecting a large order. This compressed our revenue by about 40 crores because we had to accommodate the relationship and the fact that they had already purchased the material. Our expansion will be finished by October this year. We also had an NCLT case decided in FY25, resulting in a 1.65 crore bad debt write-off.

items.statement: Revenue crossed 300 crores for first time in FY25, up from 273 crores in FY24
items.quote: As you can see, we crossed 300 crores for the first time. In FY24, we achieved 273 crores, and we have surpassed 300 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Normalized PAT around 16.56 crores after adding back 1.65 crore bad debt and 2.4 crore rental costs
items.quote: The normalized PAT should be around 16.56 crores when these one-time costs are added back.

items.statement: ROE expected in range of 17-19% on 115 crore net worth
items.quote: On a 115 crore net worth, our ROE should be in the range of 17% to 19%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at 565 crores plus/minus 5%
items.quote: Last is we have guidance of 565 plus minus 5% for FY27 in Q3. So many developments will be coming in. So are we revising any guidance? At the moment, we are not because this plus minus 5 is a flexibility which we will keep.

items.statement: Budgeted capex for FY27 is 77.45 crores with corresponding bank debt to be availed
items.quote: As I have shared in last conference call also that our budgeted CAPEX plan for financial year 2026 -27 is 77.45 crores and our corresponding bank debt will be availed accordingly.

items.statement: Royal Enfield project won in January 2026 for 350cc motorcycle engine gears; commercial production expected August-September 2026
items.quote: We are very proud to share that now we are revealing the name of the customer, which we bagged in January 2026. So as you know, we informed you, we got a big high volume project from a domestic premium motorcycle customer and that customer I'm proud to share is Royal Enfield.

items.statement: Kawasaki Japan awarded high-volume project with 15 parts; one part started, pilot lots submitted, mass production expected January 2027
items.quote: We are very happy to share we have received a very high volume, huge project from Kawasaki Japan wherein there are 15 parts which will come to us and one part has already started. It's small, but the 9 pilot lots which will be submitted now will result in the start of production we are anticipating early next year.

items.statement: Project Titan and Venus (BMW electric car reduction gearbox) final sign-off in August 2026; mass production start October-November 2026
items.quote: Project Titan, which goes to BMW electric car, the final sign off is in August. The customer is visiting and then October '26, we can start the mass production, October or November, depending on how it is, but as of now it is October.

items.statement: Project Crystal (electric power steering for US market with ZF Rane) sampling 600 sets under validation in Mexico and US; focus for prototyping with huge capacity investment planned next year
items.quote: Project Crystal, as we told you, is for electric power steering system for the US market to be developed in India with ZF Rane, that sampling of 600 sets is already under validation in Mexico and US at our end customer end, which is our American OEM.

items.statement: Commercial track segment (electric power steering for truck with ZF) samples submitted; SOP expected September-October 2026
items.quote: This commercial track segment, as we told you, it's an electric power steering for the truck segment for ZF, again. They have already asked us to submit the samples. Samples should be leaving, I think, next week or end of this week. Moment the samples are validated, this is, though a small volume, but the SOP should start from September-October of this year.

items.statement: Shift drum project (non-gear transmission component) SOP next month; 150,000 per annum volume with 6-7 part numbers to add over next year
items.quote: Another project which we gave update to you last year was this shift drum. As we told you, this is outside of our prod uct portfolio. This is not a gear. This is something which enables a gear to be shifted. It is a shift drum. It is mounted on the transmission assembly. This also, despite the US Mexico issue is happening. Our start of production is next month and around 1 50,000 per annum volume

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved from 22.34% to 25.21% in FY26; standalone EBITDA margin improved from 22.52% to 25.26%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins have grown from 94.94 crores, which was 22.34% to 229.16 crores, which is 25.21%, representing a growth of almost 36%.

items.statement: Total debt reduced from 297 crores to 221 crores in FY26; debt-equity improved from 1.3x to 0.63x; current ratio improved from 1.05 to 1.38
items.quote: Our total debt from financial year 2024-25, which was almost 297 crores, has come down to 221 crores. But this is because of the equity infusion, which was done last year, which doesn't mean that we have stopped growing or we have stopped investing.

items.statement: No slowdown witnessed in European demand; commercial vehicle demand robust due to EU infrastructure and defence spending; road transport demand increasing
items.quote: So far we are not witnessing any slowdown. Demand is really robust. So, I'll sum up in a big way, and as far as tariffs and all, you know, as you had already seen our pie chart, our dollar exports to U.S. is hardly 2 -3%.

items.statement: Passenger car segment grew from 0% to 13% of revenue since 2022-23; commercial vehicle grew from 7-8% to 20%; two-wheeler share reduced from 40-45% to 30%; tractor agriculture from 18% to 10%
items.quote: We started PAS Car business in 2021. I'm sorry, not 21, 2022-23, it was 0. Now 13% of our total revenue comes from PAS Car. This has been the, I would say new entrant for us and the next league of growth, we believe in next two to three years, you see this will change further. Similarly, commercial vehicle 2022 -23 was maybe 7% to 8%, which is now 20% of our total revenue. Two wheeler was 40-45% n

items.statement: Digital smart factory Industry 4.0 implemented for BMW projects with zero paper documentation and end-to-end traceability from steel mill to finished product
items.quote: We are very proud to share, both of these projects will be having zero paper for any kind of documentation. Everything is digital. It will have end -to-end traceability right from the steel mill to t he finished product condition, each and every process , product, when it was made, who made it, what is the dimensional aspect

items.statement: Exports 75% of turnover (69% Europe, 29% India/Asia-Pacific, 2% US/Canada); USD exports to US only 2-3%; rupee depreciation helping absorb input cost inflation
items.quote: Our overall turnover, 75% of our overall turnover was exports and 25% was domestic. On geographical distribution, around 69% of our turnover is in Europe, 29% is in In dia and other Asian Pacific countries and about 2% is going to US and Canada

items.statement: Input cost inflation pressures being managed; speaking aggressively to export customers for price support; rupee depreciation partially offsetting inflation
