items.statement: Successfully developed electric Heavy Commercial Vehicle (e-HCV) platform; first vehicle delivered to customer in Q4 FY26; certification/homologation expected in FY27; commercial deployment from April next year
items.quote: Turning to our e-mobility business in India, I am pleased to share that we have successfully developed our electric heavy commercial vehicle platform and have already delivered the first vehicle to our customer in this quarter.

items.statement: MOU signed for e-HCV with one customer targeting INR60-70 crore annualized revenue; addressing niche 10-30 ton MCV/HCV segment for public services, infrastructure, utilities
items.quote: Just I think if I have to quantify with one customer, we have an MOU already signed where we are looking at an order book of INR60 crores to INR70 crores annualized revenue of that much just from one customer and one product.

items.statement: EMOSS Netherlands revenue INR29.47 crore in Q4 vs INR23.9 crore in Q3; Europe volatile with wars and subsidy issues; stable operations but no great growth expected this year or next; new customer programs scaling in 1.5 years
items.quote: Our e-mobility subsidiary, EMOSS in the Netherlands reported a revenue of INR 29.47 crores during the quarter compared to INR23.9 crores in the previous quarter. And while market conditions remain challenging in Europe, the business has maintained operational stability and continues to pursue new opportunities in electric commercial vehicle applications.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility across India, North America and South America; assembled camshafts and precision engineered products opportunities expanding
items.quote: Demand visibility remains strong across India, North America and South America, while opportunities for assembled camshafts and precision engineered products continues to expand.

items.statement: No international acquisition plans; actively looking at M&A opportunities in India for defense, aero and other businesses
items.quote: Not at all, not internationally, but we are actively looking in India.

items.statement: Solar power phase 2 commissioned in FY26 taking total capacity to 29 MW; expected annual saving ~INR24 crore; reduces conventional power dependence
items.quote: During FY '26, the second phase of our solar power project was successfully commissioned, taking the total capacity to 29 megawatts. This investment is expected to generate an annu al saving of approximately INR 24 crores while reducing dependence on conventional power sources and supporting sustainability objectives.

items.statement: MFT step-down subsidiary in Germany undergoing insolvency proceedings; exceptional impairment charge of INR48.8 crore in FY26
items.quote: This performance includes an exceptional charge of INR48.8 crores related to the impairment of investment in our step-down subsidiary, MFT, which is currently undergoing insolvency proceedings in Germany.

items.statement: EV retrofitting business dependent on compliance and regulatory frameworks becoming easier; Tata Ace retrofitting not pursued due to compliance/RTO issues
items.quote: And we just hope that compliance and regulatory frameworks become easier over the coming years so that this retrofitting business can actually take off. So I think it's a lot is subject to that and depends on that.

items.statement: Revenue and capacity utilization expected to grow 15-20% in FY27
items.quote: According to me, it seems that it will increase by around 15–20%.

items.statement: Targets 60-70% capacity utilization over next few years
items.quote: Management remains confident of improving utilization level gradually over the next few years towards 60 to 70%.

items.statement: Plans 60-80% growth over next 4-5 years
items.quote: We are planning to achieve growth of around 60% to 80%, or even 70% to 80%, over the next four to five years.

items.statement: Two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur by Dec 2026 funded internally
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are also setting two new biodiesel manufacturing facility a t Jhajjar in Haryana and Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, each with a capacity of 200 KLPD. These facilities expected to be commissioned by December 2026, will add 400 KLPD of capacity

items.statement: Plant setup cost at ~30% of peers' investment
items.quote: Compared to other biodiesel manufacturing units in India, I am able to set up a plant at around 30% of their investment cost, and that is my biggest strength.

items.statement: Expanded Rajasthan capacity from 500 to 1500 KLPD; total annual capacity ~480,000 KL
items.quote: We proactively expanded our biodiesel production capacity at our Rajasthan facility from 500 KLPD to 1500 KLPD, taking our cumulative annual biodiesel production capacity to approximately 4,80,000 KL.

items.statement: Current utilization 7-8%; expects increase from Q1 FY27
items.quote: Sir, it will increase. You will see it increasing from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Executable order book ~Rs 80 crore; pipeline ~Rs 215 crore
items.quote: From a growth standpoint, we currently have an executable order book of approximately 80 crore, comprising orders from OMCs and other custo mers with execution expected over the next three months. In addition, we have actively pursuing a pipeline of nearly 215

items.statement: Raw material prices move with OMC tender rates; margins stable
items.quote: Sir, the raw material prices depend on the rates given by the OMCs. So, if the OMCs offer lower rates, the margin remains the same. Similarly, if the rate s increase, the raw material prices also go up

items.statement: Sells biodiesel to Modern Insulators; semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels
items.quote: We sell biodiesel to Modern Insulators, and we sell semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels.

items.statement: Glycerin byproduct monetized across pharma, food, cosmetics, paints
items.quote: Our glycerin business reinforces our circular economy approach and creates additional monetizing opportunity across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetic, personal care and paint industry.

items.statement: ARAI certifications driving industrial sales growth
items.quote: Absolutely, absolutely. The increase that we are seeing in our industrial sales is happening because of that itself, sir.

items.statement: FMCG products performing well across all markets
items.quote: Absolutely, absolutely. It is doing well everywhere, across all markets.

items.statement: Isobutanol 70-75% more expensive than biodiesel; limited plants in India
items.quote: But sir, according to me, isobutanol is 70% to 75% more expensive than biodiesel. So, if they are n ot doing it with biodiesel, then how will they do it with isobutanol

items.statement: Biodiesel export banned; pursuing license and ISCC certification for exports in 4-6 months
items.quote: Actually export of biodiesel is banned. Ashish Thakur: Okay. Gaurang Shah: But we are obtaining a license, and through that we will be able to do it. It will take around four to five months, or six months, for the license to be obtained

items.statement: Stay order received on personal case; permitted to sell to OMCs and industrial customers
items.quote: Sir, regarding my case, we have received a stay order, and we have been permitted to sell to OMCs as well as industrial customers.

items.statement: Promoter sales fully reinvested; targeting zero-debt company
items.quote: Whatever promoter group sale has happened, 100% of it has come into Kotyark Industries itself; I have not taken any money home.

items.statement: No plans for additional storage; own vehicles for logistics
items.quote: Sir, we do not need any additional storage. We already have sufficient storage capacity for that quantity. As of now, there are no plans for additional storage.

items.statement: Yield >99% vs industry 97-98%
items.quote: Kotyark Industries achieves a yield of more than 99%, and that is also one of our strengths.

items.statement: Generated 57,000+ carbon credits; first Indian biodiesel company with Vera certification
items.quote: Our sustainability initiative have enabled Kotyark to become the first Indian biodiesel company to receive Vera carbon certification and generate over 57,000 carbon credits.

items.statement: Legal cases ongoing; Supreme Court case on penalty from Revenue Dept gazette notification
items.quote: The association approached the Supreme Court regarding the penalty that was imposed through the gazette notification by the Revenue Department. That case is also ongoing.

items.statement: Export revenue expected in FY27 after license and ISCC certification
items.quote: It will come in this year itself, sir.

items.statement: Working on employee additions and talent for multi-location operations
items.quote: We are working on that, sir.

items.statement: Plant visit inside facility not possible due to low capex vs peers
items.quote: We have made our investment at roughly one-fourth of that amount. Therefore, we will not be able to arrange a factory plant visit; we can arrange an office visit instead.

name: Denta Water and Infra Solutions Ltd

items.statement: Management projects minimum 20% revenue growth for FY27.
items.quote: There will be 20% growth in revenue, that is the minimum revenue projections which we are having.

items.statement: Management hopes to achieve 20-25% revenue growth in FY27.
items.quote: We hope to achieve a good revenue projection of around 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 7,278 million across 38 projects as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, our outstanding order books stood at approximately 7,278 million across 38 ongoing projects providing strong revenue visibility for the coming years.

items.statement: Company is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders soon.
items.quote: we are agg ressively bidding for five to six tenders. In coming quarter, we will try to announce new order books

items.statement: Current bidding pipeline comprises 5-6 projects valued around Rs 600 crore.
items.quote: Around 5 to 6 projects valued at around Rs. 600 crores.

items.statement: New Karnataka government is pushing infrastructure projects aggressively after six months of inactivity.
items.quote: And sin ce last 6 months, due to some political equation, the government was not under active mode and now the new government is taking all initiatives to push up infrastructure projects

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT 2.0 schemes are being pushed aggressively by the government.
items.quote: The Jal Jivan Mission has been pushed aggressively by the government in its latest budget speech. And our project mix is Jal Jivan Mission and Amrut 2 scheme and also under Swachh Bharat, we have banked new establishment of new ST Ps.

items.statement: Price escalation clauses exist in projects over Rs 100 crore; smaller projects lack escalation protection.
items.quote: Yes, almost all projects more than 100 crores we have got price escalation. Less than 100 crores, we don't have price escalation.

items.statement: Raw material costs (UPVC/HDPE pipes) rose in Q4 and April-May due to petroleum price increases; company pre-ordered supplies and negotiates hard to mitigate.
items.quote: Our 20% to 30% of the raw material is UPVC pipe and HDP pipe, which are dependent on petroleum products. And the prices have got increased in the 4th Quarter and also in the month of April and May.

items.statement: Company maintains zero-debt profile except for small NBFC borrowings for daily operations.
items.quote: And our company is again maintaining a zero-debt profile except for few funds taken from NBFC for our day -to-day operation.

items.statement: Government may provide price escalation concessions for HDPE/PVC pipes and additional funds in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: I think the government now has given some concession of the HDP and PVC thing, the price escalation terms and another extra additional fund they might give for PVC and UPVC items. Hopefully, we might get it in July or 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Key risks are petroleum-driven raw material cost increases and government fiscal rationalisation; monsoon disruption risk is low.
items.quote: Actually, business risk is not much since we have all committed projects. And probably there will be the risk which we are foreseeing i s due to Iran -US war, there was shortage of petroleum

items.statement: Adopting NEBR and CAMUS technologies for STPs achieving 95% purity; work subcontracted to patent holders.
items.quote: In this field, we are adopting new technologies like NEBR technology and CAMUS based technologies with which we will be able to achieve almost 95% purity in treatment of sewage water.

items.statement: Order book dominated by government water projects; 90% of future orders expected in water sector including STPs and tank regeneration.
items.quote: But 90% of our water books will be in the water sector only. That is our main business, and we are more expertise in the water segment, STP treatment as well as regenerating the tanks.

items.statement: Completed 40 projects to date; 38 projects currently ongoing.
items.quote: Our execution track record remains strong with 40 projects successfully completed as on date.

items.statement: Exploring biogas project with partner having GAIL/BPCL contracts; also evaluating entry into industrial water (data centres, green hydrogen) but no firm plans yet.
items.quote: Actually, we have identified one or two projects in biogas where we plan to identify the land where grass can be grown and that can be used as biogas fuel. One of our partners is having a long-term contract with GAIL and also with BPCL and we are t rying to explore that project

items.statement: No current export activity; management open to exploring high-purity water technology exports in future.
items.quote: And your suggestion is most welcome. I will put my team there also in the con-call. I will put my team on the job and ensure that if we are able to export such kind of high technology p rojects, they are also hearing me

items.statement: Two senior personnel dedicated to hard negotiation with suppliers to contain raw material cost increases.
items.quote: I have got two senior personnel in my organization who do bargain very hard and ensure that the company does not get burdened with huge amount of increase in prices of raw materials.

items.statement: Strategy balances large long-margin projects (Rs 100-300 cr) with smaller quick-execution projects (Rs 10-50 cr) to grow absolute profit volume.
items.quote: We try to balance both the type of projects, value of work up to Rs. 50 crore and value of work up to Rs. 300 crore, so that volume will grow and we want to reward our investors so that we can show healthy increase in profit in absolute terms.

items.statement: Inventory investment of Rs 129 crore and other assets Rs 126 crore deployed in ongoing projects; liquidation expected by Dec-Jan FY27.
items.quote: Yes, your figures are correct. And we are investing all this money on the new project. Probably in the month of December and January, we hope to liquidate majority of the amount which is available in these heads, inventory and all.

items.statement: Karnataka reservoir levels at 20-25%; no acute drinking water shortage currently affecting project execution.
items.quote: There is as such no acute shortage in the state of Karnataka. All our reservoirs are filled to the level of 20% to 25%.
